## Symptom

Desktop app (macOS) shows a notification banner and error window:

> Hermes update — Update failed (exit 1). Run hermes debug share in a terminal to send a report.
> Failed to update.

The prompt recurs on every update check and cannot be satisfied: the offered update is, by git ancestry, a **downgrade** of the current checkout, so it always exits 1.

## Repro

1. Install via git on `main` (`hermes update --branch main` / desktop on the **stable** channel).
2. Let local main advance past the latest stable tag. Here: local HEAD `ecac27c` (v0.22.1+104), stable release `v0.22.2` = `d923a5eb487a` — and `git merge-base --is-ancestor d923a5eb487a HEAD` → **true** (release is 104 commits behind local HEAD).
3. Desktop updater compares **version numbers** (v0.22.2 > v0.22.1) → offers the update.
4. The update then hits the ancestry/downgrade guard and refuses.

## Log (from `~/.hermes/logs/update.log`, three identical refusals 2026-10-15)

```
→ Update channel: stable
→ Latest release: stable v0.22.2 (d923a5eb487a)
→ Fetching updates...
✗ Refusing to move this install to d923a5eb487a: that release predates the gateway runtime these session stores now use. Downgrading is unsupported.
  /Users/adriel/.hermes/state.db has gateway runtime history.
  The older release could not delete or prune those sessions.
  ... No update was applied; your install is unchanged.
```

Repeated at 17:18:48, 17:19:37, and 19:49:13 (desktop-initiated attempts, all exit 1). A manual `hermes update --branch main` (fast-forward of +32 commits) completes fine — this is purely a channel-selection / version-comparison problem, not a fetch problem.

## Expected behavior

1. For git installs whose HEAD is at or ahead of the stable release commit (`merge-base --is-ancestor release HEAD`), the updater should report **already up to date** — no offer at all. Version-number comparison (`v0.22.2 > v0.22.1`) is the wrong test for git checkouts; ancestry is the right one.
2. If a refusal does happen, the desktop surface should show the **refusal text**, not a generic 'Update failed (exit 1)' — right now the banner gives zero actionable signal.
3. The nag should be dismissable or stop recurring once the install is provably ahead of the offered release.

## Env

- macOS Darwin 27.0.0 arm64, Hermes Desktop + `hermes` CLI, git install on `main`
- Before: v0.22.1+72.g450ad50 → after manual update: v0.22.1+104.gecac27c (main @ ecac27c0af)
- Stable release offered: v0.22.2 (d923a5eb487a), an ancestor of local HEAD
title: Desktop updater: stable channel always offers v0.22.2 to git installs on main, then fails with exit 1 (refusal surfaced as 'Failed to update')

body:
### Problem
We deploy skills to a gateway from a pinned list (`hermes skills install <source>@<rev>`), with one profile per lane. After a deploy, we need to verify what is actually installed: which source, which revision, which files, and where. That lets us catch drift and duplicates. In one recent incident, a stale duplicate of a skill made every worker spawn fail with `Unknown skill(s): …`.

Today that data seems to exist only in the internal hub cache (`.hub/lock.json`). Agents are deliberately blocked from reading it, and that is a good safety boundary we don't want to bypass. The supported surfaces, `skills list`, the snapshot export and `skill_view`, return name, source, identifier and category. They do not return the source URL, source revision, file list or install path.

### Proposal
A supported, read-only export of installed-skill provenance, per profile. For example:

```
hermes skills list --json [--profile <name>]
hermes skills show <identifier> --json
```

Each entry would include:
- `identifier`, `name`, `category`
- `source_url`, `source_revision` (commit or tag)
- `install_path`
- `files`: `[{ "path", "sha256" }]`
- `installed_at`, plus `enabled` / `disabled`

The command would never expose secrets, and would read from the same lock data the hub already keeps.

### Why it helps
- Deploy tools can verify installs exactly (source, revision and file hashes) without touching internal caches.
- Duplicate or stale installs become detectable before workers crash.
- It is useful for any multi-profile or CI-driven setup that pins skills.

### Alternatives considered
- Reading `.hub/lock.json` directly. This bypasses a safety boundary and depends on an internal format.
- Recording our own manifest at install time. This is what we're doing for now, but it can drift from Hermes's real state.

Happy to test a preview build.

### Related
#71274 asks for `skills list --json` with the name, category, source, trust and enabled fields. This request would add the provenance fields to that same output, or to a `skills show --json`.
title: [Feature]: Supported read-back of installed-skill provenance (source URL, revision, files, install path)

## Bug Description

`hermes update` on the default `stable` channel aborts **before any fetch or checkout** with:

```
→ Update channel: stable
✗ Could not resolve the stable source channel: Command '['git', 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', '<release-sha>', '<HEAD>']' timed out after 10 seconds. No update was applied.
```

This is the same user-visible failure as #137646 / #138404 / #138938, but **not** the missing-object / lazy-fetch case those issues describe.

On this host **both SHAs were already in the object store**. `git cat-file -t` returned `commit` for the new stable tip and for HEAD. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` then ran to completion in **12.1 s, exit 1** (release is not an ancestor of HEAD — we were behind). The updater's `timeout=10` killed the probe first, `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` escaped `_head_containing`, and `select_apply_target` reported an unresolvable channel (`stop_class: channel_unresolved`).

Hermes itself makes this likely: a `blob:none` partial clone gets commit-graph **writes** turned off on every update (`gc.writeCommitGraph=false`, `fetch.writeCommitGraph=false` via `disable_tree0_auto_maintenance`). Without a graph, proving the common “behind” answer (walk every ancestor of HEAD looking for a commit that is **not** in that set) is a ~12 s CPU walk on this repo (~54k commits, 59 packs, `.git` ~1.3–1.4 GB).

A one-shot `git commit-graph write --reachable` dropped the same command from **12.1 s → 3 ms**. `hermes update -y` then applied `v0.21.7` → `v0.22.2` cleanly.

#139079 / #137649 (treat an unanswered probe as unknown relation, fall through to GitHub compare) would **also unblock** this host, because the timeout would no longer refuse the run. It would not make the local probe cheap: every update would still burn 10 s of git CPU then hit the network fallback, unless a commit-graph exists.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Git install, `stable` channel (unchosen default → `forward_only=True`).
2. `blob:none` partial clone (`remote.origin.promisor=true`, `partialclonefilter=blob:none`).
3. Hermes-managed keys: `gc.writeCommitGraph=false`, `fetch.writeCommitGraph=false`. No current commit-graph (or a stale one).
4. HEAD **behind** the latest published `vX.Y.Z` release, **and** both commits already present locally (`git cat-file -t <release>` and `git cat-file -t HEAD` both print `commit`).
5. `hermes update` (or `hermes update --check`).

Direct probe (this host, before writing a graph):

```
$ git cat-file -t d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8   # v0.22.2
commit
$ git cat-file -t 0e161737d2a5982a481d2d340434f9eac25d9f10   # HEAD v0.21.7+179
commit
$ time git merge-base --is-ancestor d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8 0e161737d2a5982a481d2d340434f9eac25d9f10
# real 0m12.112s  user 0m10.617s  sys 0m3.883s  exit 1
```

After `git commit-graph write --reachable`:

```
$ time git merge-base --is-ancestor d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8 0e161737d2a5982a481d2d340434f9eac25d9f10
# real 0m0.003s  exit 1
```
title: [Bug]: stable update 10s merge-base probe times out even when both commits are local (partial clone, commit-graph writes disabled)

body:
## Bug Description

While updating, the package manager publishes a new tools entry by renaming the existing directory
aside. On Windows, if a **running Hermes copy still holds that directory** (a live gateway/Desktop
process), the rename is refused with `WinError 5` and the whole update run ends as a python-deps
failure — even when the installed copy already satisfies the update's target (same version /
digest), i.e. when the "failure" is only about not being able to replace a directory with an
identical one.

**Environment**: Windows 10 (10.0.19045, zh-CN) · console cp936 · Python 3.14.7 ·
hermes v0.22.1+99.g3dd9e4e (upstream `3dd9e4ed`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, keep a Hermes instance running (gateway/Desktop) whose install tree contains the
   tools directory the update is about to replace.
2. Run the update so the same tools entry is republished (even at the same version/digest).
3. The rename of the in-use directory fails with WinError 5; the run aborts.

## Expected Behavior

A directory that already satisfies the target does not need to be replaced; the run should keep the
live copy (with a warning) and continue. A genuinely different target still fails loudly.

## Actual Behavior

`OSError` (WinError 5) propagates out of `_publish_entry` and the update ends unsuccessfully.

## Root Cause Analysis

`pm/install.py :: _publish_entry` (~line 324): `retry_held(lambda: entry.rename(previous_entry))`
has no fallback for "held by a live process, but already equivalent". Windows refuses the rename
for as long as any process has the directory open, and the updater itself keeps such a process
alive by design.

## Proposed Fix

On `OSError` from the rename: if `package.verify(entry, target)` shows the installed copy already
satisfies this run's target, keep it and warn; otherwise re-raise (unchanged behavior):

```python
try:
    retry_held(lambda: entry.rename(previous_entry))
except OSError:
    if package.verify(entry, target):
        raise
    print(f"  ⚠️ {getattr(package, 'name', 'package')}: already installed and in use; keeping the live copy")
    keep_live = True
```

Verified locally: updates proceed while Desktop stays open; a genuinely different target still
fails loudly.

Reported by srymak1r (from CN)
title: [Bug]: on Windows, an update fails when the live Hermes holds a tools entry directory (WinError 5 on rename)

body:
## Bug Description

The update check talks to the GitHub API. Its credentials live in `<hermes home>/.env`
(`GITHUB_TOKEN`) — that is where this install's token is configured and where the rest of the
codebase reads configuration from. But when the check runs in an environment that does not inherit
that file (the Desktop app's probe inherits a minimal environment), no token is read, the request
runs on the **anonymous 60/hour quota**, and the check intermittently fails with 403 /
"could not resolve".

**Environment**: Windows 10 (10.0.19045, zh-CN) · console cp936 · Python 3.14.7 ·
hermes v0.22.1+99.g3dd9e4e (upstream `3dd9e4ed`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure no `GITHUB_TOKEN` is exported in the environment (a minimal inherited env, as Desktop's
   probe has), while `<hermes home>/.env` contains one.
2. Trigger the update check from that environment.
3. Observe unauthenticated-quota behavior (rate-limit 403s) where an authenticated request
   succeeds.

## Expected Behavior

The check uses the credentials configured in `<hermes home>/.env` — the project's own dotenv
loader exists for exactly this — so it runs on the authenticated quota (5000/hour), whatever the
inherited environment looks like.

## Actual Behavior

No credential is loaded; the check runs anonymously and hits 403s / unhelpful failure states.

## Root Cause Analysis

`hermes_cli/source_check.py :: _request` (~line 135) reads the token through
`hermes_cli.github_api.github_token`, but never loads the home dotenv first; on the CLI path the
env happens to carry it, on the probe path it does not. The tree contains an official loader
(`hermes_cli/env_loader.py :: load_hermes_dotenv`) which this path does not call.

## Proposed Fix

Call `load_hermes_dotenv()` once (module-level guard) before reading the token, fail-open:

```python
def _load_home_dotenv() -> None:
    global _dotenv_loaded
    if _dotenv_loaded:
        return
    _dotenv_loaded = True
    try:
        from hermes_cli.env_loader import load_hermes_dotenv
        load_hermes_dotenv()
    except Exception:
        pass
```

Verified locally: the probe path now runs on the authenticated quota.

Reported by srymak1r (from CN)
title: [Bug]: the update check reads no credentials when its environment doesn't carry <hermes home>/.env — anonymous quota, 403s

body:
## Bug Description

`hermes update` performs its `git fetch` once. On a link whose reachability to the git remote
flips on a seconds-to-minutes scale, a single transient failure ends the entire update run; a
second attempt seconds later usually succeeds. This is not distance-specific: any flaky egress
(Wi-Fi roaming, VPN rekey, captive portal, CDN transient) has the same shape.

**Environment**: Windows 10 (10.0.19045, zh-CN) · console cp936 · Python 3.14.7 ·
hermes v0.22.1+99.g3dd9e4e (upstream `3dd9e4ed`)

## Steps to Reproduce

Measure single-attempt success from a flaky link instead of trusting a number:

```bash
ok=0; for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  git -C "$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent" fetch origin main >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok=$((ok+1)); sleep 5
done; echo "$ok/20"
```

(Measured on this host -- 2026-09-26: ~1/3 single-attempt success, the same IP going from dead to live
seconds later; re-measured 2026-10-15: 10/10. The point is that a single failure must not end the run.)

## Expected Behavior

One transient failure is absorbed; the run completes when a later attempt succeeds, and only a
persistent failure surfaces — with the original error text.

## Actual Behavior

The first failed fetch ends the update immediately; the user sees a generic update failure.

## Root Cause Analysis

`hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` — the fetch call sites in `_pull_updates` go through `_git_run`
(`network=True`), which performs exactly one attempt. There is no time-dimension retry anywhere on
this path.

## Proposed Fix

A bounded retry around fetch calls: `attempts=4, delays=(5, 10, 15)` seconds, returning the last
result unchanged when all attempts fail (the caller's existing error path still fires — nothing is
masked). No-op on a healthy link (first attempt wins).

Reported by srymak1r (from CN)
title: [Bug]: hermes update aborts the whole run on a single transient git fetch failure

body:
## Bug Description

A gateway worker started by the 3.14 runtime crashed during import because `sys.path` carried
`<install>/hermes-agent/venv/Lib/site-packages` — a leftover from an **older cp311 install** on the
same tree. The ABI-mismatched binary extension took the worker down before it could start, and the
gateway either exited or restart-looped.

**Environment**: Windows 10 (10.0.19045, zh-CN) · console cp936 · Python 3.14.7 ·
hermes v0.22.1+99.g3dd9e4e (upstream `3dd9e4ed`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an editable install whose tree still contains a legacy `venv/` built for an older Python
   (here cp311) while the PM-managed runtime is a different minor (3.14).
2. Let a gateway worker start (`gateway/run_startup.py` path, e.g. the local Group Chat worker).
3. The worker's import chain resolves binary extensions against the legacy venv and crashes
   (`pydantic_core._pydantic_core`), instead of against the runtime's own environment.

## Expected Behavior

The worker resolves its dependencies against the runtime it was launched with (the PM-managed
environment), regardless of any leftover venv directory in the install tree.

## Actual Behavior

Worker start dies on a binary-extension import; gateway startup does not complete.

## Root Cause Analysis

Nothing should deliberately add that venv to a PM-managed runtime's `sys.path`, so the entry (and
anything injecting it — launcher `.pth`, shell hooks, a cached `PYTHONPATH`, …) is pollution the
runtime must tolerate. The upstream tree has no `sys.path` cleanup on this path.

## Proposed Fix

Before `import tui_gateway.server` in `gateway/run_startup.py` (`GatewayStartupMixin`, ~line 818),
purge any `sys.path` entry under `<install>/venv/Lib/site-packages`, whatever injected it:

```python
_legacy_sp = str((Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "venv" / "Lib" / "site-packages").resolve()).lower()
sys.path[:] = [p for p in sys.path if not str(p or "").lower().startswith(_legacy_sp)]
```

Best-effort, wrapped so it can never block the worker. Verified locally: the crash loop ends and the
worker starts.

Reported by srymak1r (from CN)
title: [Bug]: a gateway worker under a Python 3.14 runtime inherits a legacy hermes-agent/venv (cp311) site-packages from sys.path and dies on pydantic_core

body:
## Bug Description

On Windows the gateway control path is the named pipe in `gateway/runtime_bootstrap_windows.py`.
Desktop's boot-time auto-start spawns a **one-shot, very short-lived `ensure` child** which creates
the pipe and exits. When the server-side peer check runs after that child has exited,
`OpenProcess` can no longer read its SID, `_peer_subject(..., server=True)` raises

```
PermissionError('named-pipe peer belongs to another user')
```

and the same-user client is refused. Callers fold this into the
`authorization` / `inaccessible` path — so on this host **every boot-time auto-start** was
misdiagnosed, not occasionally.

**Environment**: Windows 10 (10.0.19045, zh-CN) · console cp936 · Python 3.14.7 ·
hermes v0.22.1+99.g3dd9e4e (upstream `3dd9e4ed`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Boot the machine with the gateway installed as a Scheduled Task (Desktop auto-start enabled).
2. Desktop's ensure connects to `\\.\pipe\hermes-gateway-<hash>` in the window where the spawning
   child has already exited.
3. Observe the refusal folded into `authorization` / `inaccessible`.

## Expected Behavior

A same-user connection is accepted. The pipe's DACL already restricts it to the owner
(`D:P(A;;GA;;;<owner>)`, same-user only), so "could not read the peer's SID" is not evidence of a
different user.

## Actual Behavior

```
PermissionError('named-pipe peer belongs to another user')
  -> ensure reads "authorization" / "inaccessible"
```

## Root Cause Analysis

`gateway/runtime_bootstrap_windows.py :: _peer_subject(handle, *, server: bool)` (~line 75):

```python
sid = _process_sid(pid.value)
if sid != _process_sid(os.getpid()):
    raise PermissionError('named-pipe peer belongs to another user')
return 'sid:' + sid
```

`_process_sid` opens the pid with `OpenProcess`; for an exited process that fails, and its
`PermissionError('cannot identify named-pipe peer')` is indistinguishable from "the SID differs" at
the caller. The exit is normal by design (desktop spawns a disposable ensure child), so the check
must treat "unreadable" differently from "different".

## Proposed Fix

Degrade "SID unreadable" to **allow + WARNING** (`sid:unresolved`), keeping an explicit
different-SID refusal unchanged:

```python
try:
    peer_sid = _process_sid(pid.value)
except PermissionError:
    logger.warning('named-pipe peer pid %s unreadable (likely exited); allowing, DACL still enforces same-user', pid.value)
    return 'sid:unresolved'
if peer_sid != _process_sid(os.getpid()):
    raise PermissionError('named-pipe peer belongs to another user')
```

Verified locally: after this change the boot-time auto-start attaches instead of being refused;
an explicit different-SID case still refuses.

Reported by srymak1r (from CN)
title: [Bug]: the Windows named-pipe peer check refuses a short-lived ensure child — OpenProcess can't read an exited peer's SID, so boot-time auto-starts are rejected

body:
## Bug Description

On a localized Windows host (zh-CN, console code page cp936), `hermes gateway ensure` — the path the
Desktop app calls at boot — reports `Gateway inaccessible (service_identity_unverified)` **every time
the gateway was started by the installed Scheduled Task**. Desktop cannot attach until the user
replaces the instance from a shell (an unmanaged spawn, which the client does attach to).

Three independent defects in the same discovery path make a healthy install look broken.

**Environment**: Windows 10 (10.0.19045, zh-CN) · console cp936 · Python 3.14.7 ·
hermes v0.22.1+99.g3dd9e4e (upstream `3dd9e4ed`)

## Steps to Reproduce

Minimal repro of defect 1:

```python
import subprocess, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
raw = subprocess.run(["schtasks.exe", "/Query", "/TN", "Hermes_Gateway", "/XML"],
                     capture_output=True).stdout
ET.fromstring(raw)                  # ParseError: encoding specified in XML declaration is incorrect
ET.fromstring(raw.decode("utf-8"))  # parses
```

Encodings observed on the same bytes:

```
b'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?>\r\r\n<Task version="1.4" xmlns="h'
utf-8 -> OK   utf-16 -> FAIL (truncated data)   cp936 -> OK
```

Defect 2 (CSV / `whoami` reads under an UTF-8-mode Python):

```
b'"\\CCleanerSkipUAC","N/A","\xbe\xcd\xd0\xf7"\r\n...'   # "就绪" in cp936
utf-8 -> FAIL UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xbe in position 26
```

## Expected Behavior

A healthy, this-app-installed task resolves as an owner:

```
RESULT: ExistingService(backend='windows', start_argv=('schtasks.exe', '/Run', '/TN', 'Hermes_Gateway'), running=False)
```

## Actual Behavior

```
xml.etree.ElementTree.ParseError: encoding specified in XML declaration is incorrect: line 1, column 30
  -> ValueError: service_identity_unverified
```

and on the CSV path the `UnicodeDecodeError` (a `ValueError`) is caught by
`discover_existing_gateway_service`, which reports `service_manager_unavailable` — the task list is
never even read.

## Root Cause Analysis

**1. Raw bytes whose XML declaration lies.**
`hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_service.py :: _windows()`:

```python
definition = _run(["schtasks.exe", "/Query", "/TN", name, "/XML"], deadline, encoding=None)
...
_verify_binding(verify_windows_task, definition.stdout, home, *accounts[0])
```

`encoding=None` yields `bytes`; `verify_windows_task`
(`hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_service_identity.py:276`) passes them to `ET.fromstring`, and
`schtasks` writes an XML declaration naming **UTF-16** over bytes that are the OEM code page.
The same content as `str` parses fine (three variants tested above) — decoding before verifying is
the fix.

**2. CSV / `whoami` reads use the locale encoding, not the console code page.**
Same call site: `_run([...], deadline, encoding=_schtasks_encoding())`, where
`_schtasks_encoding()` is `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)`. Under Python's UTF-8 mode
(`utf8_mode: 1`) that returns `utf-8` while the tool emits cp936. `subproces
title: [Bug]: gateway ensure can never verify an installed Scheduled Task on a localized Windows host (cp936 XML/CSV + XML default elision)

body:
# [Bug]: profile-scoped /api/status reports a multiplexed profile's Telegram as disconnected (Desktop shows "telegram down")

## Bug Description

On a host where one shared gateway serves `default` plus a named profile (`gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`), the Desktop status panel for the named profile shows Telegram as **Disconnected** and the status bar reads "Backend telegram down", while that profile's bot is actually connected and sending/receiving normally.

`GET /api/status?profile=<profile>` fills `gateway_platforms` from the profile's **own** `gateway_state.json`. On a host that was migrated from per-profile gateways, that file is a leftover from the retired process: it still says `"gateway_state": "stopped"` with `telegram: disconnected` stamped the day it exited. The liveness ladder used by the same handler resolves the profile's PID from `gateway.lock` (held by the shared gateway) and returns at that rung with `runtime=None`, so the re-key step that would have pulled the live `"<profile>:telegram"` entry out of the shared record never runs. The endpoint therefore reports live liveness with a dead platform map.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Host with `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`: one shared gateway on `default`, one named profile served by it. The shared record has `served_profiles: ["default", "<profile>"]` and `"<profile>:telegram": {"state": "connected"}`.
2. Arrive at that state by migrating an older per-profile install (`hermes gateway migrate --multiplex`) and leave the retired profile's `gateway_state.json` in place. Nothing invalidates it afterwards; the file keeps the shutdown-time platform states.

### Problem or Use Case

Catalog rule 11 says a plugin gets credentials only through Hermes and "never refreshes, rotates or
writes OAuth tokens", and that a plugin needing a missing route should ask for one. This is that
request.

A platform or tool plugin that talks to a third-party API on the user's behalf with the user's own
OAuth client (Google, Microsoft, Notion, Spotify...) has no route today:

- `credentialed_provider_request` with `requires_auth` covers subscription sign-ins (Codex / ChatGPT)
- the PKCE helpers and the credential pool serve model providers through `ProviderProfile`, which would
  put Google into `hermes model`
- `requires_env` holds static secrets, so an OAuth refresh token stored there still has to be exchanged
  by the plugin itself

Concrete consumer: [gemini-voice](https://github.com/bablobanov/hermes-agent-gemini-voice), a gateway
platform that turns Google Calendar events, Docs and Sheets created by voice in the Gemini app into
tasks for Hermes. It needs four Google scopes. Today it reads its own client ID, client secret and
refresh token through `get_secret` and exchanges the refresh token for an in-memory access token, which
is exactly what rule 11 now rules out. The catalog entry discloses this and points here.

### Proposed Solution

Let a plugin declare an OAuth client in `plugin.yaml`, and let Hermes own the token:

    oauth:
      - id: google
        authorize_url: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth
        token_url: https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
        scopes: [https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.owned, ...]
        client_id_env: GEMINI_VOICE_CLIENT_ID
        client_secret_env: GEMINI_VOICE_CLIENT_SECRET
        hosts: [www.googleapis.com, docs.googleapis.com, sheets.googleapis.com]

1. `hermes auth plugin <plugin> <id>` runs the consent flow in a terminal (PKCE, loopback or paste-back
   redirect) and stores the refresh token in Hermes's credential store, per profile
2. Hermes refreshes it; a revoked grant is reported as the plugin's auth status, never as a browser
   flow under the gateway or cron
3. The plugin calls an API through Hermes, the same shape as `credentialed_provider_request`: a request
   helper that attaches the bearer only for the declared `hosts`, so the plugin never holds a token.
   A smaller first step would be `get_access_token(plugin, id)` returning a short-lived token, with the
   refresh token never leaving Hermes

`hermes plugins validate` can then check that a plugin with `oauth:` makes no direct calls to the
token URL.

### Alternatives Considered

- Reading another tool's token file (for example the Google Workspace skill's `google_token.json`):
  broader scopes than the plugin needs, a race with the skill's own refresh, and rule 11 forbids it
- `ProviderProfile` and the credential pool: built for model providers; the third-party service would
  show up as a model provider
- The plugin keeps exchanging its own refresh token (gemini-voice today)
title: [Feature]: OAuth route for plugins that call a third-party API with the user's own OAuth client

## Bug Description

Bot sessions no longer appear in the desktop **Sessions sidebar**, so they can't be seen or managed from there anymore — this worked in earlier versions. The only remaining surface is the **Bots tab**, which offers very little per-session management (open the canonical chat; rename/disband for group chats — no per-session listing, history access, delete, or cleanup).

I did some archaeology before filing, and **this looks intentional, not an accident** — filing anyway because the replacement management surface is missing.

## Investigation: it's by design

- `5ab74737e0a` (2026-08-20, PR #90732, "kill the canonical-chat infinite-fork loop; drop the per-bot Sessions browser") removed the per-bot Sessions browser, stating "Bot Mode's product contract is ONE forever-chat per bot; a browser listing every hidden plumbing session contradicts that and confused users into opening dead forks."
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/hide-bot-chats.test.ts` pins the current contract verbatim: *"Bot Mode sessions are ALWAYS hidden from the global Sessions sidebar. … There is no user pref: `session.create` passes `hidden: true` unconditionally … and this reconciliation sweep pushes rows born visible under the old pref — or minted outside the plugin entirely — back to hidden on load and on every reconnect."*
- `canonical-chat.ts` (`hidden: true` at creation, "Always born hidden from the global sidebar — Bot Mode sessions are plugin-owned") and `session-sweep.ts` (an **always-hidden reconciliation sweep** that re-hides rows on every load/reconnect) enforce it actively — so even a manually un-hidden row gets pushed back.

So the fork-loop fix is fair, but the pendulum went all the way: bot sessions went from "manageable in the sidebar" to "invisible everywhere except the Bots tab, with no opt-in and no per-session management at all."

## What's actually lost

- No way to see a bot's past sessions/history from the Sessions sidebar (or anywhere)
- No way to delete/reset/clean up a bot's sessions — including stray drafts and dead forks the sweep itself mentions
- No way to rename or archive a bot's canonical chat from a session context
- The Bots tab is now the only surface, and it has no session list — the per-bot browser that at least showed *something* was removed in #90732

## Expected Behavior

Hiding plumbing sessions from the sidebar by default is reasonable. But there should be a management affordance that respects the design, e.g.:

- An **opt-in "show bot sessions" toggle** for the Sessions sidebar, or
- A **per-bot session manager** in the Bots tab (list a bot's sessions with open/rename/delete), or
- At minimum, right-click actions on the bot's canonical chat entry (open/clear/delete history)

## Actual Behavior

Bot sessions are unconditionally hidden and actively re-hidden by a sweep; the Bots tab exposes no session listing or destructive/manage actions for them. Users who relied on the Sessions sidebar to manage bot sessions have
title: [Bug]: Bot sessions can no longer be seen or managed from the Sessions sidebar — hiding is intentional (always-hidden sweep), but no replacement management surface exists

In ACP mode (`hermes acp`, 0.21.5) file edits go through `session/request_permission`, but terminal commands only ask when they match the dangerous-command patterns (`approvals.mode` manual/smart/off).

Clients that must mediate every side effect (policy engines, audited runners) cannot use Hermes without an "ask for every tool" mode, or a way to pass the enabled toolsets per ACP session (e.g. in `session/new` `_meta`). Either would let such clients gate shell use through ACP instead of disabling it.

**Observed (Hermes 0.21.5, empty scratch workspace, client advertising `terminal: true` and `fs`):**
- a `write_file` arrived as `session/request_permission` (`kind: edit`, options `allow_once` / `reject_once`); rejecting it left the workspace unchanged;
- `touch shell-ran.txt` ran with no permission request.

**Request (either would work):**
1. an ACP option (config or `session/new` `_meta`) under which every tool call, terminal included, goes through `session/request_permission`; or
2. a way for the ACP client to pass the enabled toolsets per session, so a client can disable the terminal toolset for that session only.

Thanks!
title: ACP: option to request permission for every tool call (terminal included)

## Summary

Voice chat with Chinese input produces nonsensical, off-topic results (Chinese idiom: 牛头不对马嘴 — "horse's head, horse's tail": completely incoherent). A Chinese-speaking user running the desktop voice flow gets STT transcripts and TTS playback that do not match what was actually said/answered, making Chinese voice chat effectively unusable.

## Root-cause analysis (reproduced locally)

On a clean Windows 11 install, the default configuration bakes English into both halves of the voice pipeline, with no language detection anywhere:

```yaml
stt:
  enabled: true
  language: en          # <-- hard-locked to English; Chinese speech is mistranscribed
  local:
    model: base
  openai:
    model: whisper-1
    language: ''        # no override
```

- There is **no `language: auto` / auto-detect option** — a Chinese user must manually edit `config.yaml` to `stt.language: zh` to get any usable transcript.
- The **TTS side has no language setting at all**; the default edge-tts voice is en-US, so Chinese text is either mispronounced or fails outright. The setup wizard / onboarding never offers a Chinese voice.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh install on Windows 11 (Hermes v0.22.0), default config.
2. Enable voice chat (STT on, TTS on) in the desktop app.
3. Speak a normal Chinese sentence, e.g. "今天天气怎么样？".
4. Observe: the transcription is garbled/English-mangled, and the synthesized reply (if any) is voiced by an en-US speaker.

## Expected behavior

- STT should auto-detect the spoken language (or offer language selection during onboarding), so Chinese input transcribes correctly out of the box.
- TTS should select a voice matching the answer language (at minimum, zh voices available and selectable in desktop Settings → Voice).

## Related issues

- #128149 — edge TTS fails with "No audio was received" on Chinese text (en-US default voice, setup never offers a voice)
- #9535 — TTS does not handle multilingual input properly (no language detection)

This issue covers the **STT half** of the same gap (locked `language: en`, no auto-detect) plus the end-to-end Chinese voice-chat experience. Happy to consolidate if maintainers prefer.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.0 (2026.9.24), local commit e06df9c2eae6
- Windows 11, desktop app
- STT: whisper-1 / local `base` model, `stt.language: en`
title: [Bug] Chinese voice chat is unusable: STT hard-locked to language=en with no auto-detect, and TTS defaults to an en-US voice for Chinese text

## Summary

AWS Bedrock Converse/ConverseStream rejects any tool whose `input_schema` has a top-level combinator:

```
ValidationException: ... The model returned the following errors:
tools.33.custom.input_schema: input_schema does not support oneOf, allOf, or anyOf at the top level
```

Core tool definitions are protected by `sanitize_tool_schemas` / `_strip_top_level_combinators` (`tools/schema_sanitizer.py`, applied in `model_tools._compute_tool_definitions`). But **plugin-registered and MCP tool schemas reach the provider without that pass**, so a single plugin tool carrying a top-level combinator (in our fleet: a Pydantic-generated `allOf: [{if/then}]` conditional-required hint) kills every Bedrock call, not just that tool.

## Repro

A toolset of N core tools + 15 plugin tools, one of which has top-level `allOf`:

```python
import boto3
from agent.bedrock_adapter import convert_tools_to_converse
tools = [...]  # one tool: {function: {name: t, parameters: {type: object, properties: {...}, allOf: [{if: {...}, then: {...}}]}}}
client = boto3.client(bedrock-runtime, region_name=eu-north-1)
client.converse_stream(modelId=eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6,
    messages=[{role: user, content: [{text: hi}]}],
    toolConfig={tools: convert_tools_to_converse(tools)})  # ValidationException
```

Measured on eu-north-1 / eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 (2026-10-15): raw toolset → `ValidationException` naming the exact tool index; same toolset with the top-level combinators stripped → HTTP 200 stream completion. Nested combinators inside properties/items are accepted fine; only the top level of `input_schema` is the wall.

## Impact

When Bedrock is a fallback provider, one plugin tool schema turns a primary-provider blip into a hard outage: 3 retries of the same ValidationException, then the whole arm is down while every other provider tolerates the schema.

## Proposed fix

Sanitize at the adapter boundary, where every provider path converges — in `agent/bedrock_adapter.convert_tools_to_converse`, apply the existing core helper per tool:

```python
from tools.schema_sanitizer import _strip_top_level_combinators

def convert_tools_to_converse(tools):
    out = []
    for t in tools or []:
        fn = t.get(function, {})
        params = fn.get(parameters)
        if isinstance(params, dict) and any(k in params for k in (allOf, anyOf, oneOf)):
            fn = {**fn, parameters: _strip_top_level_combinators(params)}
            t = {**t, function: fn}
        out.append(t)
    ...
```

Validity is unchanged (top-level combinators are conditional-required hints; handlers re-validate), consistent with the rationale already in `_strip_top_level_combinators` for the Codex backend. The Moonshot/Gemini adapters already do provider-specific schema repair; Bedrock has none.

Config-side mitigation we run in the meantime (works without touching the clone): a local plugin that wraps `convert_tools_to_converse` the same way; verified live with a 200 completion on t
title: Bedrock Converse/ConverseStream: plugin-registered tool schemas with top-level allOf/anyOf/oneOf fail ValidationException

**Summary**

A tool call issued from inside an `execute_code` cell (through the RPC bridge) is not cancelled when that cell times out and its kernel is killed. If the call is waiting for an approval at that moment, it keeps waiting; when the approval resolves, the tool completes and applies its write, while the agent has already been told the cell died and its state was lost. Nothing in the transcript - and nothing in `agent.log` - links the applied write to any tool call.

**What was observed** (Hermes Agent `0.21.7+495.g6e7b83a`, Windows 11, desktop platform)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 16:34:52 | `execute_code` cell issued. Its code did `from hermes_tools import patch` and called `patch(...)` on a project's `CLAUDE.md` (a protected agent-instruction file). |
| 16:39:53 | `agent.log`: `WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool execute_code returned error (301.26s): {"status": "timeout", "output": "Cell timed out after 300s; the session kernel was killed and its state was lost."}` |
| 16:40:59 | `git status --short` in that repo: **clean** - only an untracked `?? .hermes-tmp.6bC0pl` (the atomic-write temp of `ShellFileOperations`, `tools/file_operations.py:582`) |
| 16:41:02 | same command: ` M CLAUDE.md` |
| 16:41:08 | `git diff --stat CLAUDE.md` -> `1 file changed, 44 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)`, and the patch had landed with a duplicated bullet - exactly the shape of that cell's `new_string` |

There is **no** `agent.tool_executor` line anywhere for that write, and **no** approval-prompt timeout was logged for it either (the only protected-file gate event logged that day is `13:53:14`, which belongs to a separate direct `patch` call made at `13:48:14`).

**What is NOT the bug (checked, with a live probe)**

The protected-instruction gate is strictly pre-write and does not leave anything behind on a timed-out approval: `tools/file_tools.py:977` (`patch_tool`) and `:872` (`write_file_tool`) run `_write_precheck_error` before any file operation, and `_request_protected_instruction_approval` (`tools/file_tools_write_guards.py:260-343`) returns the error string instead of writing. Verified headless with a scripted approval channel (`approvals.timeout: 300`):

```
write_file to a new CLAUDE.md, prompt times out -> file does not exist
patch on an existing AGENTS.md, prompt times out -> file unchanged
the same patch, answered "once"                 -> applied
write_file to SOUL.md, answered "deny"          -> file unchanged
write_file to a plain notes.md                  -> applied, no prompt
```

So the defect is not "a timed-out approval leaves a partial write". It is the **lifetime of the nested call**.

**Where it lives (read while diagnosing, not fixed here)**

* `tools/code_kernel.py` - `_await_cell` and the timeout branch (~760-830): *"No safe way to interrupt one cell in place: kill the kernel, report the loss, respawn next call."*
* `tools/code_execution_rpc.py` - `_rpc_server_loop` (line 139; `conn.settimeout(300)` at 160) serves requests sync
title: execute_code: a nested tool call outlives its cell and applies a protected-file write after the cell timed out

### Summary

Pasting an image into the composer of a desktop session that belongs to a **non-default profile** fails to
send. The desktop only shows `提示词发送失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: invalid_params`
(EN: prompt send failed: `JsonRpcGatewayError: invalid_params`). Sending the same prompt as plain text
succeeds.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.22.1+72.g450ad50.dirty` (`450ad5055eb3`, stable, git install)
- Windows 11, Hermes desktop, multi-profile gateway hosting (6 servable profile homes)
- Session profile: `novel-writer` (non-default), session platform `local`
- No Docker backend (local terminal backend)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a desktop session owned by a non-default profile.
2. Paste a PNG into the composer and send.
3. → `提示词发送失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: invalid_params` (fails on every retry).
4. Remove the image and send the same text → succeeds.

### Root cause

The upload endpoint persists the bytes under the ambient (launch/default) profile's image cache, because
`profile` is optional and defaults to `None`:

- `hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py:471` `async def upload_chat_image(payload: ChatImageUpload, profile: Optional[str] = None)`
- `:481` `with _profile_scope(profile)` — a `None` profile does not override `HERMES_HOME`
- `:483` `img_dir = get_image_cache_dir()`

At submit time the attachment is admitted inside the **session** profile's scope:

- `gateway/session_ingress_media.py:90` `def admit_attachments(attachments, *, admitted=None)`
- `:103` `staging = get_image_cache_dir().resolve()`
- `:105-106` `if any(not path.is_absolute() or path.resolve().parent != staging ...): raise RuntimeStoreError('invalid_params')`

So the staged path's parent is the default profile's `cache/images`, while admission resolves
`cache/images` under the session's profile → mismatch → `invalid_params` (rejected before any model call).

### Evidence

Five consecutive failures in the desktop renderer log (`logs/desktop.log`, local time CST):

```
2026-10-15 16:17:55,085 [hermes] [renderer error:main] 提示词发送失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: invalid_params
2026-10-15 16:17:57,371 [hermes] [renderer error:main] 提示词发送失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: invalid_params
2026-10-15 16:18:13,544 [hermes] [renderer error:main] 提示词发送失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: invalid_params
2026-10-15 16:18:16,647 [hermes] [renderer error:main] 提示词发送失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: invalid_params
2026-10-15 16:18:41,205 [hermes] [renderer error:main] 提示词发送失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: invalid_params
```

The pasted images landed in the **default** profile's cache, their mtimes matching the errors above
(4 copies of the same paste, 75419 bytes each; the session profile's own directory is empty):

```
D:\hermes\cache\images\dashboard_20261015_161755_21f50292_image_748a95.png   75419 bytes   16:17:55
D:\hermes\cache\images\dashboard_20261015_161813_6a260ea6_image_748a95.png   75419 bytes   16:18:13
D:\hermes\cache\images\dashboard_20261015_161816_666b7016_image_748a95.png   75419 bytes   16:18:16
D:\hermes\cache\imag
title: [Bug]: Pasting an image fails with invalid_params in a non-default profile (attachment staged in the default profile's cache)

### Bug Description

Under `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`, a Desktop chat in a secondary profile stops honouring its model pick as soon as the primary profile has had any local session in the running gateway. Every turn of that chat then runs the secondary profile's default model. The pick is stored: the chat's frozen policy holds it. The gateway looks it up in the wrong adapter and does not find it. It stays broken until the gateway restarts.

First reported as item 1 of https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6181158031. Filed separately so it can be tracked. It is not the same as #138879, #138790 or #138814: there the model switch itself fails, here the switch commits and the turn ignores it. Related: #135763.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a multiplexed gateway (`gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`) with the primary profile `default` and a secondary profile, here `desktop-local`. The secondary profile has default model A.
2. Restart the gateway, so the primary profile has no local session yet.
3. Open any local session in the primary profile. Here these were test chats over the TUI websocket. By my reading of the code, `hermes chat` without `-p` does the same.
4. In the Desktop, open a chat in the secondary profile, pick model B and send a message.

### Expected Behavior

The turn runs model B.

### Actual Behavior

The turn runs model A, and its turn line in the secondary profile's `agent.log` says `platform=cli` instead of `platform=desktop`. A gateway restart fixes it until step 3 happens again.

Evidence from `desktop-local/logs/agent.log` on `eb75627faf` (chat ids and message text removed; times UTC-3):
```
18:15:45 conversation turn: ... model=claude-opus-5-5 provider=custom platform=cli          # CLI chat, runs its requested model
18:16:51-18:22:51  local sessions in profile `default` (root logs/agent.log)
18:30:06 conversation turn: ... model=gpt-6.1-sol provider=openai-codex platform=cli       # Desktop chat, stored pick claude-opus-5-5
18:54:07 conversation turn: ... model=gpt-6.1-sol provider=openai-codex platform=cli       # Desktop chat, stored pick claude-opus-5-5
20:42:02 hermes gateway restart
20:45:44 conversation turn: ... model=claude-opus-5-5 provider=custom platform=desktop      # new Desktop chat, profile default (by then Opus)
20:47:33 conversation turn: ... model=claude-sonnet-5-5 provider=custom platform=desktop    # Desktop chat created on gpt-6.1-sol, Sonnet picked: honoured
```
The gateway ran from 18:03 to 20:42 without a restart. The profile default was `gpt-6.1-sol` until 18:56.

Side effect: for one affected chat, an async delegation completion was requeued about every 2 s (`WakeNotAccepted`, `gateway/run_notifications.py:877-898`). That made about 3,750 `Watch pattern notification — injecting` lines in two hours. It was delivered right after the restart.

Workaround: `hermes gateway restart`, then keep the primary profile free of local sessions.

### Affected Component

Othe
title: [Bug]: Multiplexed gateway: a secondary profile's Desktop chat runs the profile default instead of its model pick once the primary profile has a local session

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.1 (2026.9.24), code 297552a9d64
- Linux (Manjaro), Python 3.14.7
- Interactive CLI chats running through the local gateway (the default thin-client mode)

## What happened

After updating to 0.22.1, every interactive chat gets a `local-<64 hex>` session id. Any launch
that ends without sending a message (quit before the first turn, or a launch used only for a
failed `/resume`) leaves an empty 0-message session row behind. `hermes -c` (and
`hermes --resume latest`) then resolves to the most recent of these empty stubs and prints:

    ↻ Resumed session local-…— no messages, starting fresh.

The real conversations are never picked. Worse, each failed attempt leaves another empty stub on
top of the MRU list, so the problem reproduces on every retry — it cannot self-heal. Today this
accumulated 6 empty stubs interleaved with 4 real chats in `hermes sessions list`, all
indistinguishable (same `local-…` id format, stubs just show "—" as title).

The data itself is fine: `get_resume_conversations` and the `session.resume` gateway RPC both
return the full history for every real session, so `hermes --resume <full id>` works.

## Repro

1. On 0.22.1 with the gateway running, launch `hermes` and quit without sending a message.
   An empty row appears (`source='cli'` or `'local'`, 0 messages, no title).
2. Have a real chat in another launch (row: `source='local'`, `created_source='unknown'`).
3. Run `hermes -c` in the same workspace. It resolves to the empty stub from step 1, not the
   chat from step 2.

SQL view of the state after a morning of this (real chats marked):

    source | created_source | msgs | note
    local  | unknown        | 34   | real chat
    cli    | (null)         | 0    | stub from a failed resume attempt
    local  | cli            | 20   | real chat
    cli    | (null)         | 0    | stub
    local  | unknown        | 30   | real chat

### Summary

Two related gaps on the Desktop + host-gateway setup (Windows 11, v0.22.1+83.gdb44c46, main @ db44c46208):

1. A failed session delete shows the user a bare `删除失败: Error: 404: {"detail":"not_found"}` — **no session id anywhere**, and the 404 path is not logged by the main process either, so nobody can tell which entry failed.
2. `gateway_routing` keeps entries whose session row is gone, forever, with **no supported way to drop them** — and no safe window to run an offline repair while a gateway owns the store.

### 1) The unattributable 404 delete failure

`logs/desktop.log`, one session, 9 occurrences of:

```
[renderer error:main] 删除失败: Error: 404: {"detail":"not_found"}
```

The *same day's* 409s do carry the target and are logged by the main process:

```
[hermes:api DELETE /api/sessions/<id>?profile=default&request_id=<uuid>&expected_revision=1&expected_generation=2] Error: 409: {"detail":"unknown_execution"}
```

So the 404 path differs in two ways: the renderer error has no id and no service context, and no `[hermes:api ...]` line is emitted for it (different transport). A user who sees 删除失败 cannot report which entry, and neither can we from logs.

**Ask:** log the target (session id / route key) and the originating call for *every* failed delete, not only the `hermes:api` path. The 404 → `not_found` mapping comes from `hermes_cli/web_server_sessions.py::_mutate_session_request` (`RuntimeStoreError` → 404), so the id is known at that point.

### 2) Orphan routing rows are permanent

Routing rows whose `session_id` has no `sessions` row:

```sql
SELECT r.scope, r.session_key, json_extract(r.entry_json,'$.session_id') AS sid
FROM gateway_routing r
LEFT JOIN sessions s ON s.id = json_extract(r.entry_json,'$.session_id')
WHERE s.id IS NULL;
```

On this machine: 3 rows (2 platform group chats, 1 platform dm), plus 1 more present only in the legacy mirror `sessions/sessions.json`. Opening or deleting those chats fails with 404.

Why they can never be cleaned:

- `gateway/session_persistence.py::_prune_stale_sessions_locked` states the intent explicitly: *"Stale == `end_reason IS NOT NULL`; rows absent from the DB are kept."* An absent row is therefore never pruned, on any startup.
- The whole index is rewritten from the in-memory snapshot — `_persist_routing_data` → `replace_gateway_routing_entries` (+ `_save_sessions_json`) — on structural saves **and on graceful shutdown**. So editing `gateway_routing` / `sessions.json` while a gateway is running is silently undone by the next save.
- `hermes sessions repair-routing` fixes the opposite case (sessions with no routing identity; 81 reported here) and has no orphan-dropping option.
- `hermes sessions repair-profiles --apply` refuses while a gateway is running, and targets cross-profile state, not orphans.
- Stopping the gateway from an agent tool call is unsafe on Windows (see #99215: stops without relaunching).

Net effect: the only path today is a manual `hermes gateway stop` → han

### Bug Description

On a host serving two profiles (a default profile plus one named profile) with `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`, every plain-text Telegram message sent to the **default** profile's bot is refused. The user sees "Sorry, I encountered an error (RuntimeStoreError). invalid_params. Try again or use /reset to start a fresh session." The named profile's bot on the same gateway keeps working. `/reset` does not help, because the refusal happens before any session loads.

This is the same refusal at the same raise site (`gateway/session_envelope.py:69`) as #139040, which reports it for `/retry` and says plain messages work. Here ordinary messages fail too. Possibly related to the session-ownership refactor tracked in #134889.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a gateway with a default profile and a named profile, with `gateway: {multiplex_profiles: true}`. Each profile has its own Telegram bot.
2. Start the gateway on `v0.22.1`. In my case this was a restart after the daily auto-update had moved the checkout from v0.22.0 to v0.22.1.
3. Send any plain-text message to the default profile's bot.

### Expected Behavior

The message is admitted and answered, as on `v0.22.0` (`e06df9c2ea`) with the identical config. `gateway/session_envelope.py` does not exist at that commit.

### Actual Behavior

Every message to the default profile is refused with `RuntimeStoreError('invalid_params')`. The named profile's bot is unaffected.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram)

### Root Cause Analysis (from reading the code; not verified by a fix)

- `gateway/session_envelope.py:_validate_native` raises `invalid_params` when `runner.config.multiplex_profiles` is true and `provenance is None` (and also when `source._authorization_profile_home is not None and provenance is None`).
- `session_authority._admit_native` calls `prepare_native(self.runner, event)` without passing any provenance.
- So under multiplex, a message that reaches the native path with no provenance is always refused.
- A temporary local debug print at the raise site (not upstream code) showed both conditions true: `['auth_home_no_prov', 'multiplex_no_prov']`, with `profile=None provenance=False role_authorized=False relay=False internal=False text_type=str`.
- `profile=None` plus the fact that only the default profile fails suggests the named profile's messages arrive with provenance and the launch/default profile's do not. That part is my inference.

### Timeline

- The daily `hermes update` moved the checkout from `e06df9c2ea` (v0.22.0) to `297552a9d6` (v0.22.1) at 08:24.
- The running gateway kept the old code in memory. The first restart that loaded the new code failed on the first message.
- Rolling back to `e06df9c2ea` and restarting fixed it, with no config change.

### Traceback (trimmed)

```
gateway/run_inbound.py:1225 _handle_message
gateway/run_inbound.py:1188 _hm_authority_admission
gateway/session_ingress.py:24 admit_message
gateway/session_authority.py:332 admit_nati

## Summary

A graceful gateway restart (SIGUSR1 from Desktop's code-SHA mismatch check, or the drain before `hermes update --gateway`) waits for in-flight chat turns. A turn that is blocked waiting for the user — a terminal command approval or a `clarify` question — counts as active work for the whole wait. Meanwhile the gateway refuses Desktop connections (`hermes gateway ensure` → `state: draining`, exit 6), so the only surface that could answer the prompt cannot connect. Desktop sits at "Hermes couldn't start: Gateway draining (ensure_failed)" until the drain cap (1800s) expires.

## Observed (macOS, launchd, main merged up to 30463589eb)

Case 1 — Desktop relaunch after the on-disk checkout changed:

```
[gateway] owner runs 62aad49... but this Hermes is e3d035f...; restarting it
SIGUSR1 received ... performing a graceful gateway restart — drain active turns
Restart deferred: waiting on 1 active work unit(s) (0 wedged and excluded, 0 restart-safe and excluded; 1470s remaining before force drain):
  [{'kind': 'chat', ..., 'current_tool': 'terminal', 'idle_s': 3.2}]
```

Desktop meanwhile: `Desktop boot failed: Gateway draining (ensure_failed). Use hermes gateway status for recovery.`

After forcing a stop, the turn reported:

```
Tool terminal returned error (718.04s): ... "BLOCKED: Command approval was withdrawn before the user answered (gateway shutdown)."
```

So the turn had been sitting at an approval prompt the whole time; `idle_s` stayed at a few seconds.

Case 2 — Desktop "Update" button (`hermes update --yes --gateway`):

```
⏳ Waiting up to 1885s for in-flight turns on ai.hermes.gateway to finish before the update...
   • chat turn ... running 6m21s [model ..., tool clarify]
```

`hermes gateway ensure --json` → `{"reason_code":"update_paused","state":"draining"}` (exit 6). The Desktop window is already closed for the update, so the `clarify` question cannot be answered.

## Why the wait never excludes these turns

- `gateway/run_shutdown.py:1536` `_wedged_chat_agent_count` excludes a chat turn only once `seconds_since_activity >= HERMES_AGENT_TIMEOUT` (default 1800).
- While waiting on the user, the activity clock keeps being refreshed:
  - `tools/clarify_gateway.py:91` — `touch_activity_if_due(activity_state, "waiting for user clarify response")`
  - `tools/approval_human_wait.py:105` — `return lambda: touch_activity_if_due(state, label)`
- So a turn blocked on the user is never "wedged", never "restart-safe", and holds the drain until the force-drain cap.

The stop path already handles this cleanly: on SIGTERM the pending approval is withdrawn immediately (`Command approval was withdrawn before the user answered (gateway shutdown)`).

## Expected

A turn whose current tool is blocked on human input (approval, clarify) should not hold a restart/update drain — that wait cannot complete while the gateway refuses the clients that would answer it. Possible approaches:

1. Exclude such turns from the restart wait set and withdraw the pe
title: fix(gateway): restart drain waits the full cap on a turn blocked on user approval/clarify while Desktop is refused

### Bug Description

On a gateway that resolves `gateway.multiplex_profiles` to `true` at boot (a host with more than
one profile to serve), `/retry` from a messaging platform fails **every time**:

```
RuntimeStoreError: invalid_params     # raised at gateway/session_envelope.py:69
```

The user sees the generic turn-error notice (`locales/en.yaml:637`: "Sorry, I encountered an
error ({error_type}). {error_detail} Try again or use /reset to start a fresh session."), and no
retried turn runs.

There is a second, worse half to it: the refusal happens **after** the transcript rewrite, so the
last user turn has already been removed from the active transcript by the time admission refuses.
A failed `/retry` therefore loses the turn it was supposed to repeat, and the user has to retype
it.

Reproduced on `main` @ `7bda2a3368` (`v0.22.1+66.g7bda2a3`) and on `v0.22.1`. Not present on `v0.22.0` or
older: `gateway/session_envelope.py` (the native-admission layer this path now goes through)
first appears in `v0.22.1`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a gateway that resolves `multiplex_profiles` to true at boot — i.e. a host with more than
   one profile to serve, or an explicit `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`. (A single-profile
   install is settled standalone at boot by `implicit_multiplex_blocker()` and is unaffected.)
2. From any messaging platform, send a plain-text message and let it be answered.
3. Send `/retry`.
4. `gateway.log` logs the slash invocation, then
   `ERROR gateway.platforms.base: [Discord] Error handling message: invalid_params`, with the
   traceback in *Additional Logs* — and no turn is dispatched.

The last user turn is gone from the active transcript at that point (the rewrite in
`slash_commands_session.py` runs before the re-dispatch).

### Expected Behavior

`/retry` re-sends the last user turn and it runs — as it does on a standalone (single-profile)
gateway, and as it did on `v0.22.0`.

### Actual Behavior

Every `/retry` on such a host is refused with `RuntimeStoreError('invalid_params')` from
`gateway/session_envelope.py:69`, and the turn is not re-run (and has already been dropped from
the transcript).

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform

Discord (reported), but the failing code is the shared messaging `/retry` handler, so any platform
that goes through native admission is affected. CLI / TUI / Desktop `/retry` are *not* affected:
they re-submit through `prompt.submit` / `session.mutate`, not through native admission.

### Hermes Version

`main` @ `7bda2a3368` = `v0.22.1+66.g7bda2a3`. Also reproduced on `v0.22.1` (`5575a085`); absent on `v0.22.0`.

### Debug Report

Collected with `hermes debug share --local` (prints locally — **no upload**, no paste URL) on a
throwaway isolated repro host: a fresh Linux box on `main` @ `7bda2a3368` with the candidate fix
applied locally (hence the `.dirty` version string). No platform adapter is configured there and
no API key is set,
title: [Bug]: /retry from a messaging platform fails with RuntimeStoreError(invalid_params) when multiplex_profiles is on

We need a supported way for a trusted plugin to deliver automated work to one exact Hermes session, recover a lost acknowledgement without starting it twice, and know when the attempt can no longer write to its transcript. Would you accept a native contract for this, building on the plugin-author work in #130622?

A concrete consumer is a collaboration plugin that delivers a question or task to an agent. Its local supervisor can journal requests and enforce owner consent. It cannot tell whether Hermes admitted input if the host crashes between enqueue and acknowledgement, or stop another native input path from competing for the same transcript.

### Existing work and evidence

#130622 covers plugin input being attributed to the human by memory providers. Its proposed `turn_author` path is a useful foundation. Please keep that repair independently shippable. #110031 proposes authorized same-session completion events; we would prefer extending suitable host-owned admission, typed-event and session-lease machinery from that work over creating another queue.

Our source review and no-model probe used v0.22.0, commit `e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8`:

- [`inject_plugin_message`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8/hermes_cli/plugins_injection.py#L12-L62) returns a Boolean and converts a non-user role into a text prefix. In a probe using the real functions with disposable in-memory host collaborators, duplicate calls retained both copies. A deliberately injected exception after enqueue returned `False` while the input remained queued. This is a synthetic failure case, not a production incident or a native crash/restart test.
- [TUI/Desktop injection](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8/tui_gateway/plugin_inject.py#L24-L66) drops `plugin_id` and may start draining immediately. That route exposes no retained attempt-to-turn receipt.
- [Deferred active-session leases](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8/tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py#L598-L668) include an age-based concurrency-slot reaper. That slot's release does not prove every writer has stopped. We are not claiming Hermes has no transcript locks.

These findings are pinned to that release and route. We have not run a complete native conformance suite or established the absence of an equivalent on every current surface.

The operation names below describe semantics, not a required Python or RPC API. We call the complete bundle handshake v1; this is a proposed integration contract, not a claim that Hermes already defines it.

[Bug]: Desktop treats messaging-channel sessions as local: WeChat completions count as unread, and opening a WeChat session raises "Session controls unavailable: stale_generation" (v0.22.1)

## Summary
On the unified gateway runtime, Desktop's session list now includes messaging-channel (WeChat) sessions — listing them is presumably intended — but two local-only behaviors leak onto them:

1. **Unread badges**: every completed WeChat turn raises the Desktop's unread-session count and dots the row, as if it were a local completion the user hasn't seen.
2. **stale_generation banner**: opening a WeChat session shows a persistent red `Session controls unavailable: stale_generation` banner. The desktop polls `session.control.read`; the gateway's `_require_current_route` (`gateway/session_ancillary.py:304`) raises because the live route's entry no longer points at that conversation (messaging sessions rotate routes on /new), so the control snapshot can never be served for these sessions. Same error family as #138952 (mutate path), different trigger (read-only poll on a messaging session).

For 1: `lightUnreadCompletion` only exempts the focused session; it does not consider the session's source platform, and unified fanout delivers every session's busy→idle edge to every subscriber (`LocalSessionAdapter` viewers read one canonical stream by design).

## Expected
Either exclude messaging-platform sessions from the Desktop unread accounting (or mark them read-by-default), and let `session.control.read` answer "no controls" instead of raising for sessions whose route rotated — the banner is permanent and unactionable otherwise.

## Notes
- The two referenced sessions: 20261015_145005_97380a93 and 20261015_095001_53a3467c (both source=weixin, ended via session_switch). A local session with queue/steer activity shows no banner, consistent with the route-rotation reading.

[Bug]: Desktop statusbar context gauge / cache-hit / tokens-per-second never populate on unified-gateway sessions — session.usage payload shape mismatch (v0.22.1)

## Summary
On the unified gateway runtime, the Desktop statusbar's context-usage, cache-hit-rate and tokens-per-second items never populate: the gauge reads "0 / 0 Tokens · No context data yet", the other two stay "—". The one number that does appear (e.g. "160.9k tok") is the label's fallback to the session's cumulative OUTPUT tokens (`usageContextLabel` shows `usage.total` when `context_max` is absent) — not context occupancy, and misleading next to the empty gauge.

## Root cause (payload shape mismatch)
- Gateway publishes the frame as the bare stats dict: `gateway/session_usage.py::publish_usage` → `turn._publish_execution("session.usage", stats)`.
- Desktop consumes a NESTED field: the message-stream `session.usage` handler reads `payload?.usage` and merges it (`apps/desktop/.../gateway-event/session-info.ts:534`). With the bare-dict payload, `payload.usage` is always undefined → the merge never runs → `$currentUsage` keeps its initial zeros → all three labels render their empty forms.
- The pre-0.22 sidecar emitted `session.usage` from `tui_gateway`'s usage ticker with the `{usage: ...}` envelope the desktop handler was written for; the canonical port kept the desktop consumer but changed the producer's shape.

## Secondary gaps (same frame's consumers)
- `message.complete.usage` DOES arrive (its handler merges `payload.usage` from the complete payload — that path works, which is why the gauge partially appears after running a NEW turn in the session). But a freshly OPENED session never gets a hydration read: the legacy `session.usage` RPC fallback in the resume path only fires when `session.activate` is missing; on the canonical path it isn't called, so pre-turn context figures (`last_prompt_tokens`, `context_length` of the session's last turn) never reach the desktop.
- `cache_hit_pct` / `avg_tps` are only included when the producing agent has the counters; a resumed/lazy session has no agent, so `session.stats` can't backfill them either.

## Expected
- Publish `session.usage` with the `{usage: stats}` envelope (or make the desktop handler read the bare dict) so live ticks land.
- Hydrate usage on session attach on the canonical path (the `session.stats` RPC exists for exactly this), so an opened session shows its context occupancy before any new turn.

## Repro
v0.22.1 desktop, local gateway, `display.show_reasoning: true`. Open any session that ran turns pre-update: statusbar shows `<n> tok` (cumulative output) while the Context Usage panel reads 0/0 "No context data yet", cache-hit and t/s stay "—". Send one message: the gauge fills in (complete.usage path works); cache-hit and t/s still "—".

Related: #134889 (unified gateway tracking), #138852.
title: [Bug]: Desktop statusbar context gauge / cache-hit / tokens-per-second never populate on unified-gateway sessions — session.usage payload shape mismatch (v0.22.1)

[Bug]: Desktop model picker loses the current-model checkmark on unified-gateway sessions — session.info carries no provider field (v0.22.1)

## Summary
On the unified gateway runtime, opening an existing Desktop chat leaves the model picker with no row checked, and the composer pill shows only the profile default. The session's actual model is never reflected until the user re-picks.

## Root cause
- The canonical `session.info` payload (`gateway/session_local.py::local_session_info`) includes `model`, `cwd`, `reasoning_effort`… but **no `provider`**.
- The Desktop session-info handler deliberately does NOT write composer `$currentModel`/`$currentProvider` from `session.info` (comment: heartbeats would revert manual picks) — the per-session runtime state is the only intended channel, and it is fed from session.info's model/provider fields.
- With `provider` absent from the payload, the picker's is-current predicate (`catalogProviderMatches(row.provider, current.provider) && row.family.id === current.model`) can never be true for a resumed session.

## Repro
v0.22.1 desktop (local gateway). Open any session that already ran turns with a non-default model → open the model menu → no checkmark on any row; the session chip/thinking pill shows the model name correctly (it comes from the same payload's `model`), proving the data exists but provider never arrives.

## Expected
session.info carries `provider` (agent's provider when built; the policy's route provider when lazy), so the picker can mark the current row on resumed sessions like it did pre-unification.

Related: #134889 (unified gateway tracking), #138852.
title: [Bug]: Desktop model picker loses the current-model checkmark on unified-gateway sessions — session.info carries no provider field (v0.22.1)

## Version / environment

- Hermes `v0.22.1+13.g8f0367c` (upgraded from `v0.21.6+607.gc573316`), Windows 11, native, gateway hosted by a Scheduled Task.
- Present in `main` @ `db44c46208f1`: `hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_service_identity.py:294,296`.

## Symptom

After the upgrade, every launch of the desktop app fails with `Desktop boot failed: — Gateway inaccessible`, and:

```
$ hermes gateway ensure
… "reason_code": "service_identity_unverified"   → exit code 7
```

There is no user-level way back into the app: the check is not a warning, and the UI boots through the gateway path. (Clicking "Repair install" does not help — the install is fine.) Naming the module explicitly:

```
$ hermes gateway ensure      # HERMES_HOME = D:\Hermes
state=ready? no — reason_code=service_identity_unverified, exit 7
```

## Root cause — two judgments in `verify_windows_task`, both unsatisfiable/incorrect

```python
294:  if principal.findtext("t:RunLevel", "", ns) != "LeastPrivilege" or actions.get("Context") != principal.get("id"):
296:  if task.findtext("t:Settings/t:Enabled", "", ns) != "true":
```

**1. `RunLevel` is compared against the XML *schema* spelling, against a value that does not survive registration.**

- The XML schema's spelling is `LeastPrivilege`; the object model reports the same setting as **`Limited`** (`(Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName <task>).Principal.RunLevel` → `Limited`).
- More decisively, **`schtasks /Create /XML` drops the `<RunLevel>` element on registration.** Reproduced here: register a task XML that contains
  ```xml
  <Principals><Principal id="Author"><UserId>…</UserId><RunLevel>LeastPrivilege</RunLevel></Principal></Principals>
  ```
  then re-export the registered task (`Export-ScheduledTask` / `schtasks /Query /XML`) — there is no `<RunLevel>` element in the output. So there is no XML-side fix: whatever the generator writes, the read-back is empty, and `"" != "LeastPrivilege"` is permanently true.

**2. A missing `<Enabled>` element is treated as "disabled", but absent is the schema default (enabled).**

`<Settings><Enabled>` is optional and defaults to enabled; an empty `findtext` result therefore means "enabled" and must not fail the check. (The task this ran against had no `<Enabled>` element and was very much enabled — the gateway process was running.)

Net effect: on this platform the identity check **cannot** pass, and because it is a hard gate rather than a degradation, an otherwise-healthy Windows install cannot start the desktop app at all.

## Second-order problem: the module exists in two copies, and the one that runs is not the repo one

On this install the module is present twice:

```
D:\Hermes\hermes-agent\hermes_cli\gateway_runtime_service_identity.py                                     (repo tree)
D:\Hermes\installs\<hash>\environments\<env>\workspace\hermes_cli\gateway_runtime_service_identity.py      (PM environment snapshot)
```

The **snapshot copy is the one the running code loads**; patching the repo copy

### Summary

Every WebSocket accept on the gateway runs a synchronous file write on the event loop. When the filesystem is slow for a few seconds, the whole gateway loop stalls. Managed workers that need the owner during that window fail fast with `WorkerPersistenceError: owner_unavailable` and exit. Each persistence RPC opens a new WebSocket, so the busier the workers are, the more often the loop runs the blocking touch.

Version: v0.22.1 (2026.9.24), local 297552a9d6. The relevant code is unchanged on `main` at db44c46208.

### Where

1. `tui_gateway/ws.py:417` calls `_note_dashboard_client_activity(force=True)` on every accepted socket, which bypasses the 5-second debounce at line 29. Line 457 calls it again for received frames, with the debounce.
2. That calls `gateway/scale_to_zero.py:100` `touch_dashboard_client_heartbeat()`. It runs `os.makedirs`, `open(..., "a")` and `os.utime` (line 106) directly on the event loop thread.
3. `agent/runtime_session_store.py:66-80` `WorkerRPC.__call__` gives the owner 5 seconds for discovery and 5 seconds to open the connection. It opens a new connection per call and doesn't retry. A stalled owner becomes `owner_unavailable` (line 70), and the store latches that as `self.failure`, so every later call in the worker raises it too.

### What we observed

This is one machine (Linux aarch64, btrfs `/home` at about 85% full), with a gateway serving several profiles and 5 to 8 concurrent Kanban workers running builds and tests.

- Over about 4.5 hours, the gateway logged 6 loop stalls of 10 to 20+ seconds. The detector is discord.py's "heartbeat blocked for more than N seconds". Every captured loop traceback ends in the same frame:

  ```
  tui_gateway/ws.py, line 44, in _note_dashboard_client_activity
    touch_dashboard_client_heartbeat()
  gateway/scale_to_zero.py, line 106, in touch_dashboard_client_heartbeat
    os.utime(p, None)
  ```

- In the same window, there were about 9 `Managed worker lost: managed_worker_failed` events. Each was preceded by `ws ready frame send failed` and followed by worker tracebacks ending in `WorkerPersistenceError: owner_unavailable` (from `acquire_session_turn_lease`, `append_message`, `flush_token_counts` and `release_session_turn_lease`). One stall at 09:39 was followed by four worker losses within 30 seconds.
- Kanban then sometimes refused the respawn ("Kanban owner refused: Kanban execution unknown; retained by owner") and gave up on the card, which needed a manual unblock.

Stalls shorter than 10 seconds aren't logged by the heartbeat detector, but they still exceed the worker's 5-second budget. That likely explains the losses with no logged stall. We have not reproduced this in isolation: a 3-minute `os.utime` timing probe on the same filesystem in a quiet period stayed under 1 ms. The trigger is intermittent filesystem latency under heavy write load. The amplifier is a blocking call on the loop.

1. Move the heartbeat touch off the event loop (`async

The Claude "Current session" usage shows 100% when the real usage is around 1%.

I noticed it because the dashboard (reading hermes model options) said 100% while the Claude VS Code extension, same profile, said 1%. Weekly matched in both (29-30%), so it's only the session bar, and only right after a session reset when usage is very low.

Looks like it comes from `_usage_windows` in `agent/account_usage.py`:

```python
used = float(used)
if fraction and used <= 1:
    used *= 100
```

`_fetch_anthropic_account_usage` calls it with `fraction=True`, so any `utilization` of 1 or below gets multiplied by 100. As far as I can tell `/api/oauth/usage` already returns a percentage, so 1.0 means 1%, not 100%. I ran the function with a few values:

| utilization | shown |
|---|---|
| 0.5 | 50.0 |
| 1.0 | 100.0 |
| 1.1 | 1.1 |
| 29.0 | 29.0 |

So the bar jumps from 100% down to ~1% as soon as usage passes 1%, which is why it looked fine most of the time.

I couldn't confirm the raw API value, the endpoint rate limited me (429) when I tried to call it directly. The weekly number matching VS Code is what makes me think it's percent and not a fraction.

This only seems to affect Claude. The Anthropic call is the only place that passes `fraction=True`, the other providers (codex etc.) don't use it, so they look fine. Probably the fix is just to drop `fraction=True` for Anthropic.
title: Anthropic "Current session" usage shows 100% when real usage is ~1%
