[Bug]: Desktop group creation always fails with `invalid_params` — `CanonicalHostedRoomService.local_profiles()` only knows the own profile

## Summary

On a fresh Windows install (v0.22.1, stable), creating **any** canonical Bot Mode group chat (Desktop → Bots → New Group Chat, 2–6 local bots) always fails with a bare `invalid_params` toast, regardless of the active profile. No detail is logged anywhere (`desktop.log`, `gateway.log`, `errors.log` are silent).

Root cause: `CanonicalHostedRoomService.local_profiles()` (`gateway/session_hosted_service.py`) returns only the authority's own profile plus `hosted_rooms.profiles` from the gateway config. A default config contains no `hosted_rooms` key at all, so the known set is a single profile (e.g. `('default',)`). `validate_roster` then rejects every member with a different profile (`member 0 local target does not match a local profile` → `invalid_params`). Since members must have unique profiles, **no** multi-profile group can ever be created out of the box.

## Repro

1. Fresh install, 2+ local profiles (e.g. created via Desktop New Agent dialog).
2. Desktop → Bots → New Group Chat → pick 2 bots → Create.
3. Result: `invalid_params`, no group. Active profile is irrelevant.

Verified server-side with the isolated runtime against the real code:

```python
svc = CanonicalHostedRoomService(authority, loop)  # authority = default home
svc.local_profiles()   # -> ('default',)  -- siblings missing
svc.create_room(room_id=..., name=..., members=[...two other profiles...])
# -> DiscussionValidationError: member 0 local target does not match a local profile
```

After adding all profiles to `hosted_rooms.profiles` in `config.yaml`, the same call succeeds and UI group creation works.

## Expected

Either the multiplexed gateway auto-registers its served profiles as valid group members, or the Desktop surfaces the real validation message (which member/field failed) instead of bare `invalid_params`.

## Workaround (verified)

In `<HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml`:

```yaml
hosted_rooms:
  profiles:
    default: C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/hermes
    <each-profile>: C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/hermes/profiles/<each-profile>
```

then `hermes -p default gateway restart`.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (native)
- Hermes Desktop v0.22.1 (2026.9.24), stable, git install
- Gateway 0.22.1, multiplexed, profiles served from one host gateway

## Related

Likely a post-merge gap of #106742 (unified runtime owns every local session) — see tracking #134889. Same bug family as #138761 (`profile_scope_mismatch` on cross-profile operations).
title: [Bug]: Desktop group creation always fails with `invalid_params` — service only knows own profile

### Bug Description

For inference providers that authenticate with a dedicated HTTP header (e.g. a literal `api-key`
header, Azure-style or gateway routing tags configured via a named custom provider's
`extra_headers`), the main agent's chat calls succeed because the main client lifts the
provider's header block onto its requests. **Auxiliary session-title requests do not carry
those headers**, so title generation fails with an auth error (401/403) on every session:

```text
Title generation failed: Error code: 401 - {"error": {"message": "...missing required header 'api-key'..."}}
```

Sessions fall back to the provisional/derived instant title forever. This is the same failure
family as **#109595** ("named custom provider `extra_headers` dropped on aux clients"), which
was fixed in the _named-custom_ resolution branch but **not** in the _main-runtime-reuse_
branch — and main-runtime-reuse is exactly the branch `task="title_generation"` resolves
through.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a named custom provider whose endpoint requires an `api-key` header, e.g. in
   `config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   custom_providers:
     - name: my-gateway
       base_url: https://gateway.example.com/v1
       key_env: MY_GATEWAY_KEY
       extra_headers:
         api-key: '${MY_GATEWAY_API_KEY}' # required by the gateway; 401 without it
   model:

   ```

`call_llm(task="title_generation", main_runtime=...)` authenticates identically to the main
agent client for the same endpoint — the provider's `extra_headers`/`default_headers` block
(`api-key` included) is present on the title request, and titles are generated successfully.

### Actual Behavior

The title request is sent **without** the `api-key` header and the provider rejects it. The

### Bug Description

Since the Kanban worker became a thin client of the profile owner (`hermes_cli/kanban_worker_client.py` → `kanban.run`), `gateway/session_kanban.py::run_task` submits the card's turn as

```python
Submission(request_id, ref, {'text': f'work kanban task {params["task_id"]}'}, 'queue')
```

without `'finite': True`. Inside the card's turn `finite_turn_required()` is therefore `False`, and everything the old `hermes chat -q` worker got from single-query mode is gone:

- `approvals.single_query_mode` no longer applies (`tools/approval_context._is_single_query_approval_context()` is `False`). Any approval request in a card (`execute_code`, a command the gate flags) parks a pending approval nobody can answer, waits the full `approvals.timeout` (300 s by default), returns "timed out without user response … Silence is not consent", and the worker then blocks the card.
- `clarify` is not answered headless (the finite branch in `gateway/run_turn_runner.py`).
- `delegate_task` does not take the synchronous fallback that `tools/delegate_tool_dispatch.py` explicitly intends for "one-shot Kanban workers (#63169)".
- The codex app-server child is not closed after the turn (finite branch in `run_turn_runner.py`, ~L1265) and lingers until the idle-TTL sweep.
- The post-turn background review runs after every card turn (`agent/background_review.py`).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Hermes v0.22.1 with the gateway as a systemd user service; a headless profile with `approvals.mode: smart`, `approvals.single_query_mode: deny`, `approvals.timeout: 300`, and `code_execution` in its toolsets.
2. Create a Kanban card for that profile whose work leads the model to call `execute_code` (or any command the approval gate flags).
3. Let the dispatcher run it.

### Expected Behavior

Same as the pre-owner `chat -q` worker: `single_query_mode: deny` resolves the approval immediately and the agent continues by other means (or blocks with a real reason).

The tool call blocks for 300 s and then returns `BLOCKED: execute_code script timed out without user response. 1. `hermes_cli/web_server_gateway.py::_spawn_hermes_action` (line ~475) builds the child with `hermes_cli/_launchers.py::runtime_command` (line 38) → `<store python> -I -c <bootstrap>`. The store Python comes from `/opt/hermes/tools/facts.json` (`packages.python.entry`) = `/opt/hermes/tools/python-3.14.7+…/bin/python3`. That interpreter is not a venv (`sys.prefix == sys.base_prefix`).
2. `hermes_bootstrap.py:613` → `pm/environments.py::activate_dependencies` → `committed_venv()`:
   - `_recorded_venv()` → no `$HERMES_HOME/installs/351f81cc06284494/facts.json` on the volume (only `bootstrap/default.json` and `.install.lock`).
   - `payload_venv()` → `None`: `_payload_manifest()` (line 150) reads `root.parent / "manifest.json"`, i.e. `/opt/manifest.json`, which the image does not ship — unlike every packaged/desktop payload. The image's `install-stamp.json` carries `payload: bootstrap` and `pmRuntime` but no manifest, and nothing else supplies the venv.
3. `_require_own_dependencies` (line 435) then refuses at line 446, and `hermes_bootstrap.py:619` prints the message.

There is no self-healing path either: `pm/recovery.py::refresh_dependencies` returns `"base"` when `runtime_facts_path()` is absent (line 111-112), so the stage2-hook refresh step can never commit a first generation. `/opt/hermes/.venv` is the correct environment (482 MB, `hermes-agent.pth`; its `python` has `prefix=/opt/hermes/.venv`, `base_prefix=/opt/hermes/tools/python-3.14.7+…`, so the same guard returns early there) — the image just never declares it to PM.

### Workaround (confirmed in production)

Mount the missing manifest. It must be `/opt/manifest.json`, because `_payload_manifest` reads `root.parent/"manifest.json"` with `root=/opt/hermes`, so entries are relative to `/opt`:

```yaml
services:
  agent:
    image: nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
    command: gateway run
    volumes:
      - ./manifest.json:/opt/manifest.json
```

```json
{"schema":1,"repo":"hermes","venv":"hermes/.venv","store":"hermes/tools","runtime":{"commands":{"hermes":"hermes/bin/hermes"}}}
```

After that, hub actions run on `/opt/hermes/.ven
title: Docker image ships no payload `manifest.json`, so every `runtime_command`-spawned action (skill install, MCP install, doctor, backup) dies with "no dependency environment is committed for this install"

Found while independently re-verifying PR #131755 (which fixes the `max_spawn` / `max_in_progress` form of this class), at its head `1fc5069b3f8343aa528773c663cfe120f50b1d7d`, base `origin/main` @ `5d3c05977bb3`.

## Observation

At the PR head, `capacity_full` is set **only** at the `max_spawn` and `max_in_progress` gates (`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py`, `_tick_spawn_budget`, L2296 and L2303). The per-profile cap (`kanban.max_in_progress_per_profile`) defers ready work in `_dispatch_lane_task` (L2132) by appending to `skipped_per_profile_capped` and returning `False` — it never touches `result.capacity_full`. `any_genuine_stall` (L216-244) excuses only `res.spawned` or `res.capacity_full`, so a board whose ready work is deferred solely by the per-profile gate still counts as a genuine stall → `bad_ticks` keeps incrementing in the gateway watcher (`gateway/kanban_watchers.py` L318-330; `_HEALTH_WINDOW = 6` at L37) → the false `kanban dispatcher stuck: ready queue non-empty for N consecutive ticks but 0 workers spawned.` fires with **no `held` suffix** (`describe_suppression`, L163-193, doesn't count this bucket either).

The bucket's own docstring says it exists "so dashboards show 'profile busy' vs 'stuck'" (L128-131) — the telemetry flag that would make that true is exactly what's missing.

## Repro (real dispatch tick, real sqlite boards; synthetic test profiles)

`max_in_progress_per_profile=1`, one running worker for profile `alice`, two ready tasks assigned to `alice`, no other cap hit:

```
spawned:                     []
skipped_per_profile_capped:  [('t_31d2d31d', 'alice', 1), ('t_124ed1c7', 'alice', 1)]
capacity_full:               False
board_ready_flag:            True
stuck (any_genuine_stall):   True
held (warn suffix):          ''
```

After six consecutive such ticks the watcher fires the false alarm. Same class as #46800 / #80513, different gate.

## Suggested fix

Set `capacity_full=True` when a tick's zero-spawn of ready work is fully explained by the per-profile gate (e.g. a per-tick "every deferred task was per-profile-capped" flag), or extend `any_genuine_stall` to treat `skipped_per_profile_capped` as an excusing condition on a per-board basis. Nuance worth an explicit call: the per-profile cap counts across boards (#118499, #135515, #135600), so "excused" means "the only reason this board held work back is a saturated profile", preserving the per-board judgment design from the PR. Also consider adding `per_profile_capped=N` to `describe_suppression` so the warning suffix can name it.

## What happens

A compaction (or a committed tool-result prune) is a content-loss boundary: old tool results are
replaced by a summary or a one-line marker, and the boundary re-arms the repeat-read dedup caches so
the model can fetch that content again. The comment at the preflight site states the intent:

> A committed prune is a content-loss boundary like compaction: demoted skill_view / read_file
> bodies survive only as one-line markers, so the repeat-read dedup must stop answering "unchanged"
> for them or the reload the marker asks for is refused.

The tool-call guardrail is not re-armed at the same boundary. If the model read a file (or viewed a
skill) twice earlier in the same turn, `ToolCallGuardrailController` is holding that as a repeated
identical/no-progress call, and a third identical read is refused with
`idempotent_no_progress_block`. The boundary un-blocks the read and a sibling mechanism re-blocks
it — so the model cannot recover content the boundary removed, which is the one thing the boundary
exists to allow.

## Where it manifests

- `agent/conversation_compression.py::_reset_read_dedup_caches` — the seam every content-loss
  boundary shares. It re-arms file-read, skill_view and computer-use frame dedup; nothing re-arms
  the guardrail that can refuse the same call.
- Callers: `_finish_compaction_boundary` (compaction) and
  `agent/turn_preflight.py::compress_after_tool_results` (committed prune).
- `agent/tool_guardrails.py::ToolCallGuardrailController` — `reset_for_turn()` runs at turn start
  (`agent/turn_context.py`), so the exposure window is a single turn — which is precisely when
  compaction is triggered by tool results and when the model is being asked to re-read.

## Reproduce

```python
from agent.tool_guardrails import ToolCallGuardrailConfig, ToolCallGuardrailController

config = ToolCallGuardrailConfig(hard_stop_enabled=True, no_progress_block_after=2)
controller = ToolCallGuardrailController(config)
args = {"path": "C:/example/data.txt"}
result = '{"content":"1|contents","total_lines":1}'

for _ in range(2):
    assert controller.before_call("read_file", args).action == "allow"
    controller.after_call("read_file", args, result, failed=False)

assert controller.before_call("read_file", args).code == "idempotent_no_progress_block"

# Boundary runs: content is now only a marker, the read must work again.
from agent.conversation_compression import _reset_read_dedup_caches
_reset_read_dedup_caches("task", session_id="session")

# Current main: still blocked -> "idempotent_no_progress_block"
assert controller.before_call("read_file", args).action == "allow"
```

## Expected

A boundary that re-arms reads also re-arms the guardrail's success-repeat state, so the re-read is
allowed. Failure state should NOT be re-armed: a boundary does not make a failed call safe to retry.

## Fix

Proposed fix (PR to follow): `ToolCallGuardrailController.reset_for_compaction()` clears the
success-repeat state (`_no_progress`, the i

## Summary

Repeated `Path.resolve()` calls (realpath syscalls, one `lstat` per path component) are the single largest CPU cost in the classic CLI's redraws and in tool-heavy turns. The inputs (`HERMES_HOME`, the profiles root, the managed runtime dirs) don't change during a session, so the results can be memoised on the input strings.

## Measurements (a9109b07, Linux, Python 3.14.7)

Throwaway profile, a resumed session of ~400 active messages (~140k tokens, ~560 KB request bodies), a local fake OpenAI-compatible model, so only Hermes's own CPU counts. A turn that makes 30 `terminal` tool calls (`echo hi`) took **8.2 CPU-seconds in 15.6 s of wall time, about 0.26 CPU-seconds per tool round trip**. In-process sampling of threads in the running state during a 40-call turn:

| share | hot path |
|---|---|
| ~21% | `pathlib.Path.resolve` → `posixpath.realpath`, from `tools/environments/local.py` `_make_run_env` → `_managed_runtime_path_entries` / `_append_missing_sane_path_entries` (per terminal call), `hermes_cli/plugins.py` `_plugin_home_key` (per `get_plugin_manager()` call), `hermes_cli/profiles.py` `get_active_profile_name` (per prompt render) |
| ~7% | session DB writes: `_flush_messages_to_session_db` → `append_messages_batch` → `_execute_write`, plus `_try_wal_checkpoint` |
| ~7% | imports on the hot path: `agent/relay_llm.py` `_start_unmanaged` reaching `importlib` per call |
| ~5% | `agent/usage_anchor.py` `message_fingerprint` |

In the redraw path, `_get_tui_prompt_symbols` → `get_active_profile_name()` runs several times per frame and accounts for ~75% of each redraw (three `resolve()` calls per invocation). That makes every spinner tick during a turn (10 Hz) cost more than it should, and it amplifies the idle redraw loop in #138982.

## Suggested fix

Memoise on the string inputs, e.g.

```python
@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8)
def _active_profile_name_for(home: str) -> str: ...

def get_active_profile_name() -> str:
    return _active_profile_name_for(str(get_hermes_home()))
```

and the same pattern for `_plugin_home_key` and the managed-runtime PATH entries (keyed on the env/HOME values they read). A profile switch changes `HERMES_HOME`, so it misses the cache naturally.
title: perf: memoise Path.resolve() in get_active_profile_name / _plugin_home_key / local env PATH (≈21% of CPU in tool-heavy turns, ≈75% of each CLI redraw)

## Summary

The classic CLI (`hermes chat`) pins one CPU core at ~100% **while idle** whenever its terminal is 3 rows tall or less. It never stops until the terminal is made taller. We found it on a long-running orchestrator session in a multiplexer pane that had been squashed to 4 columns × 2 rows: its main thread used ~96–100% of a core for hours with no turn running.

## Cause

`hermes_cli/cli_footer_split.py`, `FooterSplit._divide_heights` (unchanged on `main` as of db44c462):

```python
sizes = super()._divide_heights(write_position)
if sizes is not None:
    return sizes
...
get_app().invalidate()        # every overflowing frame
return clipped[::-1]
```

The heal-redraw from #57393 assumes the overflow is transient (a row appearing between the two measuring passes). When the terminal is simply shorter than the footer's minimum height (composer + rules + status bar ≥ 4 rows), **every** frame overflows, so every paint schedules another paint: an unthrottled redraw loop.

Each of those redraws is also expensive because `_get_tui_prompt_symbols` calls `hermes_cli.profiles.get_active_profile_name()` several times per frame, and that does three `Path.resolve()` calls (realpath syscalls) each time (separate issue to follow).

## Repro

1. `tmux new -d -s t -x 200 -y 50 'hermes chat'` and wait for the prompt.
2. `tmux set -g window-size manual; tmux resize-window -t t -x 200 -y 2`
3. Watch the hermes main thread: `top -H -p <pid>` → ~100%.
4. `tmux resize-window -t t -x 200 -y 50` → back to ~0%.

Measured on a9109b07 (Linux, Python 3.14.7), idle session, main-thread CPU over 5–10 s:

| terminal | CPU |
|---|---|
| 200×50, 40×10, 10×4, 200×4, 200×5 | 0.1–0.2% |
| 200×3, 200×2, 200×1, 4×2 | 99.7–101% |

In-process stack sampling of the main thread during the spin: 92% inside `Application._redraw` (via `_redraw_unless_resizing`), of which 75% is `realpath` under `get_active_profile_name` and 15% is `flush_stdout`.

## Suggested fix

Heal once per geometry instead of on every overflowing frame:

```python
def _divide_heights(self, write_position):
    sizes = super()._divide_heights(write_position)
    if sizes is not None:
        self._overflow_size = None
        return sizes
    budget = write_position.height
    clipped = []
    for child in reversed(self._all_children):
        rows = min(child.preferred_height(write_position.width, budget).min, budget)
        budget -= rows
        clipped.append(rows)
    size = (write_position.width, write_position.height)
    if getattr(self, "_overflow_size", None) != size:  # a too-short terminal stays clipped, not repainted forever
        self._overflow_size = size
        get_app().invalidate()
    return clipped[::-1]
```

The #57393 case (a row flips mid-turn on a full-size pane) still gets its one healing repaint, because the next good frame resets `_overflow_size`. With this patch applied at runtime, the same 4×2 terminal idles at ~0% and the prompt still repaints correctly when the terminal grows
title: CLI pins a CPU core at 100% while idle when the terminal is 3 rows or fewer (FooterSplit heal-redraw loop)

### Background review fork inherits the turn's *fallback* runtime, so a one-off failover keeps billing the fallback provider after the turn ends

**Summary**
When a turn finishes on `fallback_providers` (the primary failed mid-turn), the end-of-turn background review is spawned **before** `_restore_primary_runtime()` runs (that only happens at the start of the next turn, `agent/turn_context.py`). `_resolve_review_runtime()` (`agent/background_review.py`) takes the parent's *live* runtime (`agent.provider`, `agent._current_main_runtime()`) when `auxiliary.background_review.provider` is `auto`/unset. As a result, the review fork runs entirely on the fallback provider.

**Why it matters**
A fallback is usually a paid API key backing a subscription primary. The review fork replays the whole conversation (~150K tokens per call here) and makes several calls. One transient primary failure therefore turns into a burst of paid calls that the user never sees and that are not part of their turn. It also confuses route monitoring: the main session is back on primary while the fork is still on fallback, so "now on fallback" and "back on primary" interleave.

**Observed** (macOS gateway, Hermes v0.21.7 source install, primary = a subscription model-provider plugin, fallback = `anthropic`)
- 08:57: the primary failed 3× in one turn, then failed over to `anthropic`, and the turn finished there.
- 09:00:25–09:01:17: background review `thread=bg-review calls=6`, every call `provider=anthropic`, `cache_read=991844`.
- Other sessions were on the primary the whole time, so route alerts flapped 7 times in ~2 minutes.

**Still present on `main`**
Checked at `origin/main` 2026-10-15: `_resolve_review_runtime` still returns the live parent runtime when unrouted; `_restore_primary_runtime()` is still called only from turn setup.

**Workaround**
Pin `auxiliary.background_review.provider` / `.model` to the primary.

**Suggested fix**
When `agent._fallback_activated` is set and `auxiliary.background_review` is unrouted, resolve the fork from `agent._primary_runtime` (the runtime the next turn will restore to) rather than the live fallback runtime. If primary resolution fails, skip the review rather than spending fallback budget on it, or make that behaviour configurable.
title: Background review fork inherits the turn's fallback runtime, so a one-off failover keeps billing the fallback provider after the turn ends

body:
### Bug Description

When the LLM provider returns an error during an ACP session (for example HTTP 429 after retries are exhausted, or a connection failure), the Hermes ACP adapter never reports the failure to the client. In `acp_adapter/server.py` (main, commit c858fb07ab), an agent exception is caught in `_run_agent_turn` and converted into a plain `final_response` of the form `"Error: {e}"` ([server.py:814–816](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/acp_adapter/server.py#L814-L816)). The client receives it as an ordinary agent message: no error state, no provider name, no HTTP status, and the turn ends with a normal stop reason. An executor-level exception is caught in `prompt` and returns `PromptResponse(stop_reason="end_turn")` with no message at all ([server.py:876–881](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/acp_adapter/server.py#L876-L881)), so the client sees a silent end of turn.

A user pairing in an IDE therefore sees the agent either finish "normally" with a bare `Error: …` line, or stop silently, while the actual cause (rate limit, provider outage, misconfiguration) is only in Hermes logs.

Observed live (2026-10-15, Hermes v0.21.7+310.gc858fb0 with agent-client-protocol 0.9.0, ACP client: acp-patchbay 0.86.0): during a provider 429 the client shows only a spinner for the whole turn; the cause is visible exclusively in the gateway logs.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes acp` and connect an ACP client (e.g. an editor extension).
2. Point the active provider at an endpoint that returns HTTP 429 (or interrupts the connection) and send a prompt.
3. Observe the client UI: the turn ends with a normal stop reason and either no message or a plain `Error: …` text line; no error indication is sent through ACP.

### Expected Behavior

A failed turn is distinguishable from a successful one in the client: the adapter surfaces a readable failure (provider error text, at minimum the exception message) through the ACP session stream, and the turn's stop reason reflects the failure instead of `end_turn`.

### Actual Behavior

- Agent-level exception → `Error: {e}` arrives as a normal agent message; stop reason is normal.
- Executor-level exception → turn ends with `end_turn` and no message.

### Affected Component

acp_adapter
title: ACP: provider errors (e.g. HTTP 429 after router retries) are not surfaced to the client

### Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.22.0+119.g0e427d7` (2026.9.24) · channel `stable` · install method `git`
- Upgraded from `v0.21.3` on 2026-10-14
- Windows 11 (x64), user profile `C:\Users\<user>`
- Python runtime: `tools\python-3.14.7+<build>-win32-x64\python.exe`
- Desktop app launched from source (`Using Hermes source at ...\hermes-agent`)

### Summary

After the upgrade, the desktop app failed to start its own backend **on boot** — the
backend child died immediately and the app fell back to "no backend". Manually
running `hermes serve` afterwards worked, which made it look like a process-lock
problem. The actual cause is unrelated: the upgrade **replaced the inherited ACLs
of every directory under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\tools\`** with metadata from the
extracted archives, removing the current user's access to the tool executables.

### Symptoms

`logs/desktop.log`:

```
Hermes backend (PID 8532) died before its identity could be recorded: Command failed: powershell.exe ...
Recent backend output:
did not find executable at 'C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\tools\python-3.14.7+<build>-win32-x64\python.exe': ?????
```

Note the `?????` — 5 characters, i.e. the **localized** Windows message
(`拒绝访问。` = "Access is denied."). On an English system this surfaces as
`Access is denied.` The message is misleading: the file **exists** and is a valid
executable — it simply isn't accessible to the current user.

Behavior is intermittent and easy to misdiagnose:

- fails for the first ~10 minutes after boot
- works if the backend is started manually a bit later
- works if the user runs with an elevated context

### Root cause

`icacls` on the parent directory is healthy, but **every tool subdirectory** has
lost its inherited ACEs and gained an `OWNER RIGHTS` entry:

```
C:\...\hermes\tools                       <-- OK
    <user>\CodexSandboxUsers:(I)(OI)(CI)(RX)
    NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(I)(OI)(CI)(F)
    BUILTIN\Administrators:(I)(OI)(CI)(F)
    <user>\<user>:(I)(OI)(CI)(F)

C:\...\hermes\tools\python-3.14.7+...\python.exe    <-- BROKEN
    NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(I)(F)
    BUILTIN\Administrators:(I)(F)
    OWNER RIGHTS:(F)              <-- appears out of nowhere
                                  <-- current user ACE GONE
```

Same for `python314.dll`, and for **all 10 tool directories**
(`python-*`, `node-*`, `git-*`, `ripgrep-*`, `ffmpeg-*`, `uv-*`, `npm-*`, …).

- `tools\` directory mtime == the exact upgrade timestamp (2026-10-14 18:06)
- the `OWNER RIGHTS` placeholder is what Windows writes when an object's

body:
## Problem

The stale-checkout guard on gateway surfaces refuses mutating slash commands (`/model`, `/retry`, …) with copy of the shape:

> This gateway is running code from `<old-sha>` but the checkout on disk is now `<new-sha>`. Restart the gateway to load the new code — switching models would risk a stale-module crash.

On chat surfaces the named remedy is **unreachable**: a Telegram/Slack user cannot run `hermes gateway restart`. Every retry bounces identically — observed 4 consecutive refusals over two days on a messaging-controlled deployment.

Related: PR #138972 (same audit; that PR stops error copy from advertising advice that cannot change the outcome — this issue is the structural counterpart giving the chat surface a real remedy).

## Proposal

An owner-facing `gateway-restart` slash command (name TBD), listed in `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` so it works mid-run:

1. Run the stale-check import probe on the checkout; on failure, refuse and surface the error (never restart onto a broken tree).
2. Write a pending-ack marker `{chat_id, message_id, old_sha}`.
3. Acknowledge in-chat ("restarting"), then hand off to the supervisor via the existing `gateway_supervised_restart` SIGUSR1 drain path — never tear down from inside the process being torn down.
4. Drain releases the Telegram `getUpdates` lease before exit (observed: a fresh boot's first poll can 409 against the old session for ~10s).
5. New process reads the marker on boot and posts "back on `<sha>`" to the originating chat.
6. The stale-guard message copy names `/gateway-restart` on chat surfaces instead of the bare `hermes gateway restart` instruction.

## Open design questions for maintainers

- Ownership/placement: gateway mixin vs reuse of `hermes_cli/gateway_supervised_restart.py` primitives.
- Authorization scope for chat-triggered restarts (paired DM only? admin gate?).
- Interaction with fleet-wide restart rules when multiplexed (per-profile vs all-served).
title: Gateway surfaces: a chat-executable restart command so the stale-guard refusal has a reachable remedy

**What happens**

On the OpenCode **Go** relay, `hy4-preview` is served live and the `/model` picker offers it, but
creating a session with it is refused by the offline model×provider coherence gate — the chat is
dead until the model is switched back. The desktop (Chinese UI) shows `会话不可用` plus the gate's
message:

```
Model `hy4-preview` is not served by provider `opencode-go` (OpenCode Go).
Closest OpenCode Go models: `hy3-preview`.
```

**Live, it is served** (`OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` + an `x-opencode-session` header):

- `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/models` lists `hy4-preview`.
- `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` with `{"model":"hy4-preview", ...}` → 200,
  normal completion. Routing is already right: `_OPENCODE_API_MODE_PREFIXES` sends every id that is
  not `gpt-`/`grok-`/`muse-spark-`/`claude-`/`minimax-`/`qwen*` to `chat_completions`, and
  `agent/model_metadata.py` already carries `hy4-preview: 1_048_576`.

**Offline repro** — the whole bug, no network:

```python
from hermes_cli import models as m, models_validate as v
'hy4-preview' in m.provider_model_ids('opencode-go')           # True — the picker offers it
v.static_model_provider_conflict('hy4-preview', 'opencode-go')  # conflict — session.create refuses it
```

```
{'model': 'hy4-preview', 'provider': 'opencode-go', 'suggestions': ['hy3-preview'],
 'message': 'Model `hy4-preview` is not served by provider `opencode-go` (OpenCode Go). Closest OpenCode Go models: `hy3-preview`.'}
```

Desktop path: `tui_gateway/methods_session_model_guard.py::model_override_conflict` →
`static_model_provider_conflict` (#96817's offline gate); the string above is what the user sees.

**Why it rejects**

The gate checks membership in the curated `_PROVIDER_MODELS['opencode-go']`, whose family stops at
`hy3` / `hy3-preview`. `_static_catalog_matches("hy4-preview", "opencode-go")` then finds the slug in
`tencent-tokenhub` / `tencent-tokenplan`'s curated catalog, and because `hy4` is not a family head of
the opencode-go list the id is classified as a cross-vendor conflict — even though the same provider's
live listing (which `provider_model_ids` merges) contains it.

Adding `"hy4-preview"` to the `opencode-go` tuple clears it — verified in-process (verdict goes from
the conflict dict to `None`), after which a real `chat/completions` call with that id runs.

## Summary

In the desktop app, picking a reasoning effort (model menu → effort) fails with the toast **"模型选项更新失败 / Model option update failed: JsonRpcGatewayError: stale_generation"**. Once it has failed, every later pick of the same value fails the same way, sometimes several times within one second. Our reading of the code is that the desktop keeps the refused `session.mutate` request, along with its old `expected_generation`, and resends it unchanged. Nothing refreshes it until a prompt is submitted or the session is re-attached.

> Note: this analysis comes from reading the code at 297552a9. We have not reproduced it under a debugger. The log pattern matches it, but the exact trigger (which event advanced the session's generation without the desktop observing it) is not confirmed.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.22.1 (2026.9.24)**, stable, git install, commit **297552a9**. The desktop app is built from the same checkout; its status bar reads "0.22.0+2216".
- macOS (Apple Silicon), desktop app with a local gateway and multi-profile hosting (`primary-shared`, active profile non-default)
- Session model: a non-default provider/model chosen in the picker; effort changed from the menu (Med → other)
- `hermes update` finished cleanly (exit 0) before the errors started

## Bug Description

On 0.22.1, `hermes acp` can no longer run sessions when `HERMES_HOME` is a **per-task home** — a real directory that mirrors a profile home through top-level symlinks. This is the shape used by the self-hosted [Multica](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica) daemon for its Hermes-runtime agents (one home per task: `<workspace>/<task>/hermes-home`, with `gateway.lock` symlinked to the served profile's lock, plus mirrored `skills/`, `state.db`, `mcp-tokens/`, `logs/`, etc. — the repo calls these "Multica overlay homes").

Every ACP `session/new` / `session/load` (resume) now fails:

```
session/new: Internal error (code=-32603, data={"details":"Gateway inaccessible: not_ready"})
```

and each run dies in ~13 s (17 consecutive failures on one deployment). On 0.22.0 the same command ran sessions in-process and worked for weeks. The 0.22.1 adapter is a gateway *viewer* (`HermesACPAgent.__new__` → `GatewayACPAgent` when no `session_manager` is passed) that requires a gateway **owner** resolvable for its `HERMES_HOME`; for this home shape nothing resolves — and there is no fallback to local sessions.

## Steps to Reproduce

On an unpatched 0.22.1 install (we carry a local bridge patch since the incident, so the failure was captured from the affected deployment plus direct discovery probing immediately before patching):

1. Mirror the task-home shape for any profile served by your gateway:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p /tmp/task-home
   ln -s ~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/gateway.lock /tmp/task-home/gateway.lock
   cp ~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/config.yaml /tmp/task-home/config.yaml   # minimal config is enough to boot the adapter
   ```
2. `HERMES_HOME=/tmp/task-home hermes acp`
3. Drive ACP over stdio: `initialize`, then `session/new` with `{"cwd": "/tmp/task-home", "mcpServers": []}`.
4. Observe `-32603 Gateway inaccessible: not_ready` (`session/load` behaves the same).

Direct discovery evidence from the same install:

```
discover_gateway_endpoint(Path("/tmp/task-home"))
  -> GatewayDiscovery(state='inaccessible', reason_code=None)

discover_gateway_endpoint(Path("~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>"))
  -> GatewayDiscovery(state='ready', endpoint=GatewayEndpoint(profile_id='...', capabilities={'session-authority-v1', ...}))
```

## Expected Behavior

A consumer that sets `HERMES_HOME` to a per-task home can run ACP sessions — either by resolving the task home to the profile it mirrors (the symlinked `gateway.lock` names the serving owner), or through a supported local (in-process) session mode when no owner is reachable.

## Actual Behavior

`session/new` / `session/resume` fail with `Gateway inaccessible: not_ready`; there is no fallback path; `hermes acp` is unusable for t

**Environment:**
- Hermes Agent v0.22.1 (2026.9.24) · upstream 297552a9
- Install method: docker
- Python: 3.14.7

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Start Gateway/TUI/Dashboard and open a session so it is held live in `self.authority.sessions` (process memory).
2. While that process is still running, delete the same session's row from the DB via another path, e.g. `hermes sessions delete <id> --yes` (CLI, separate process, writes directly to `state.db`).
3. In the still-running TUI/Dashboard process, trigger any `session.list` call (e.g. open the session switcher, refresh dashboard).

**Expected Behavior:** The now-orphaned in-memory session is silently skipped from the list (as `session_controls.py::list_sessions` already does for `RuntimeStoreError` with `reason in {'not_found', 'permission_denied', 'profile_mismatch'}`).

**Actual Behavior:** The whole `session.list` call crashes, blocking session listing/deletion in TUI and Dashboard for every session of that process, not just the deleted one, until the process is restarted.

**Exact Traceback (from production errors.log):**
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/hermes/tui_gateway/ws.py", line 390, in _dispatch_loop
    resp = await _dispatch_request(authority_connection, req, req_method, transport)
  File "/opt/hermes/tui_gateway/ws.py", line 324, in _dispatch_request
    resp = await authority_connection.dispatch(req)
  File "/opt/hermes/gateway/session_controls.py", line 191, in dispatch
    result = await handlers[method](ref, params)
  File "/opt/hermes/gateway/session_controls.py", line 394, in list_sessions
    handle = await self.authority.resolve(self.actor, candidate)
  File "/opt/hermes/gateway/session_authority.py", line 209, in resolve
    return self._handle(ref)
  File "/opt/hermes/gateway/session_authority.py", line 204, in _handle
    return SessionHandle(ref, self.instance_id, self.epoch, row['runtime_revision'],
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```

**Root Cause:** `session_authority.py::_handle(ref)` (line 199-205) calls `self.db.get_session(ref.session_id)` and immediately subscripts the result (`row['runtime_revision']`, line 204) without a `None` check. If the session is still held live in process memory (`self.authority.sessions`) but its row was removed from `state.db` by another process/path, `get_session` returns `None` and the subscript raises an unguarded `TypeError`. `session_controls.py::list_sessions` (line 391-398) already anticipates exactly this class of failure and specifically catches `RuntimeStoreError` with `reason == 'not_found'` to `continue` past an unresolvable session — but `_handle` never raises that error for this case, so the catch is dead code for this path and the raw `TypeError` propagates uncaught through `resolve()` and crashes the entire `session.list` dispatch.

**Proposed Fix:**
```diff
--- a/gateway/session_authority.py
+++ b/gateway/session_authority.py
@@ -199,2 +199,4 @@
     def _handle(self, ref):
         ro

### Description
When a background command is spawned via `terminal(background=True, notify=True)` in a Discord session, after the background process completes execution with exit code 0, the completion notification is never delivered to the Discord channel. Instead, the gateway enters an infinite retry loop, continuously emitting injection log lines every few seconds and flooding the gateway log indefinitely without ever successfully delivering the notification or backing off.

### Environment
- **Hermes Version**: `v0.22.1 (commit 297552a9d646)`
- **OS / Environment**: Linux x86_64 (WSL2)
- **Active Model & Provider**: `gemini-3.8-flash` (via `github-copilot`)
- **Gateway Platform**: `Discord`

### Reproduction Steps
1. Connect Hermes gateway to Discord.
2. In a Discord channel, ask the agent to launch a long-running background command using `terminal(background=True, notify=True)`.
3. Wait for the background process to finish execution (e.g. exit code 0).
4. Observe the Discord channel and the gateway logs.

### Expected Behavior
Once the background process finishes, the gateway should inject the process completion notification into the conversation session, and the user should receive the completion notification in the Discord channel. If the notification cannot be admitted or delivered, it should fail with backoff or drop after bounded retries rather than retrying indefinitely every few seconds.

### Actual Behavior
- The completion notification is never delivered to the Discord channel.
- The gateway log gets continuously flooded every ~5 seconds with injection attempt logs indefinitely:

```log
INFO gateway.run: Watch pattern notification — injecting for discord chat=<REDACTED_CHAT_ID> thread=None
INFO gateway.run: Watch pattern notification — injecting for discord chat=<REDACTED_CHAT_ID> thread=None
INFO gateway.run: Watch pattern notification — injecting for discord chat=<REDACTED_CHAT_ID> thread=None

body:
## Summary
`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py` terminates a worker by the PID stored in the task row (`worker_pid`) without checking that the process behind that PID is still the worker it spawned. On Windows (and Linux), PIDs are recycled quickly; after a worker crashes and its PID is reused by an unrelated process (e.g. an interactive CLI session, `svchost.exe`, a terminal), `_pid_alive` reports it alive and the dispatcher's timeout / reclaim path calls `os.kill()` on it.

Observed on Hermes 0.21.3, Windows 10 (19045), during an infrastructure audit of a Windows-native deployment (no incident yet: our board has 0 `timed_out` events so far, 67 `crashed`).

## Where
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py` ~L2302-2319: `Popen(...)` for the worker, then only `proc.pid` is kept (the `Popen` handle is dropped).
- `~L450-461` (max_runtime handling): `pid = int(row["worker_pid"])` → `kill(pid, SIGTERM)` → `_sigkill(kill, pid)` — no start-time / cmdline check.
- `~L285-327` `_terminate_reclaimed_worker`: same pattern (only the host prefix in `claim_lock` is checked).
- Only the main process is killed, not the tree: a `claude -p` (or any tool subprocess) started by the worker survives as an orphan.

## Contrast
`gateway/status.py` ~L216-218 already has the right guard: *"Windows force REQUIRES a matching expected_start_time (taskkill on a recycled PID has killed svchost.exe)"*. The kanban dispatcher does not use it.

## Suggested fix
1. At spawn, persist `create_time` (e.g. `psutil.Process(pid).create_time()`) next to `worker_pid` (task_runs row or a sidecar file next to the worker log).
2. Before any `kill()` in the timeout and reclaim paths, require `create_time` match (±1 s) **and** a cmdline that looks like a Hermes worker (e.g. contains `--cli` / `--accept-hooks` or the worker entrypoint). On mismatch: log a refusal and treat the worker as dead instead of killing.
3. Kill the process tree (children with `create_time >= parent's`), not just the root, so tool subprocesses do not linger.

Happy to test a patch on Windows.
title: Kanban dispatcher kills worker PID from DB without verifying process identity (PID reuse can hit an unrelated process)

## Summary

On a `blob:none` **partial clone** (`remote.origin.promisor=true`), `hermes update` on the `stable`
channel fails **permanently and identically** on every run:

```
☤ Updating Hermes Agent...
→ Update channel: stable
✗ Could not resolve the stable source channel: Command '['git', 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor',
  '<new-release-commit>', '<HEAD>']' timed out after 10 seconds. No update was applied.
```

The only thing that changes between runs is the release SHA in the message. Observed three
consecutive nights (2026-10-13, -14, -15), never self-healing, always exit 1.

## Root cause — a self-deadlock

`select_apply_target()` (`hermes_cli/update_cmd_check.py`) resolves the update target **before** the
updater's own `git fetch`:

```
select_apply_target -> resolve_source_target(forward_only=...) -> source_releases._head_containing()
```

`_head_containing()` must **prove** whether HEAD already contains the new release commit, so it runs:

```python
# hermes_cli/source_releases.py
ancestry = run("merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, head).returncode   # hardcoded timeout=10
```

In a partial clone, a release commit the clone has never fetched is **absent from the local object
store**. So `merge-base` triggers a **promisor lazy-fetch of upstream history**, which cannot finish
inside 10 seconds — hence the timeout.

The deadlock: *the probe that fails is precisely the step that would have fetched the commit.* Every
retry repeats the identical timeout, so the failure can never self-heal. Once you are stuck, you are
stuck permanently.

`source_git_env()` does set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` via `NO_LAZY_FETCH_ENV` precisely to stop this
(the comment in `_subprocess_compat.py` describes this exact failure mode), but it is **not honoured
on this path**. Reproduced on **git 2.43.0**; `_subprocess_compat.py`'s own comment notes that
"older git ignores the variable".

## Reproduction

```
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git
cd hermes-agent
hermes update            # once a release lands after your last fetch
# -> merge-base --is-ancestor timed out after 10 seconds. No update was applied.
```

Environment: git 2.43.0, Hermes v0.21.6+529, `remote.origin.partialclonefilter=blob:none`.

**Workaround that unblocks immediately** — make the commit local first, then run the update:

```
git fetch --no-tags origin '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*' '+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*'
hermes update            # probe now answers in ~50 ms
```

## Suggested fixes (any one is sufficient)

1. **Fetch before resolving the target** — resolve the stable release, then fetch that specific
   commit/ref, then run the ancestry probe. The probe is only ever a few bytes of graph work once
   the objects are local.
2. **Fetch inside the probe's own budget** — replace the hardcoded `timeout=10` with a retry that
   first materialises the missing object (or raise the timeout and let the lazy-fetch complete, at
   least once, so the second ru
title: hermes update permanently fails on blob:none partial clone: stable channel probe lazy-fetches and self-deadlocks at its own 10s timeout

### Bug Description

On Hermes Desktop, entries in the composer queue (`hermes.desktop.composerQueue.v1`, Electron
localStorage) accumulate and **cannot be removed from the UI** — pressing delete appears to do
nothing.

Two distinct symptoms:

1. **Duplicate enqueue** — the same prompt is queued many times. The duplicates share the same
   `id` but carry different `queuedAt` values, so this is one prompt enqueued repeatedly, not
   several different prompts.
2. **Delete is a no-op** — every entry has `serverStatus: "queued"`, but the server has no
   matching record, so the delete request has nothing to act on.

Clearing the Electron storage directory fixes it only temporarily: new entries reappear within
minutes.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Desktop app, in a session that runs `terminal(background=true)` jobs (each completion notice
   is admitted as an automation turn and mirrored into the composer queue).
2. Leave the session / let it stay busy so the queue never drains.
3. Observe `hermes.desktop.composerQueue.v1`: the same `[IMPORTANT: Background process ...]`
   notice appears many times.
4. Try to delete the queued entries in the UI → nothing happens, they stay.
5. Quit the app, `rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/Hermes/Local Storage`, relaunch →
   the queue is empty, but new entries appear within minutes.

### Expected Behavior

- A prompt is enqueued once.
- Deleting a queued entry removes it.
- When the server has no matching admission, the entry is still removable locally, so the queue
  cannot get permanently stuck.
- Clearing local storage stays cleared.

### Actual Behavior

Measured 2026-10-15. All numbers below come from reading the storage directly (Snappy-compressed
LevelDB, UTF-16LE values), not from estimates.

- **97 entries across 3 sessions.** One session (`20261013_142935_61f770`) held **80 entries
  covering only 15 unique prompts**; a single background-completion notice repeated **x13**.
- Every entry has `serverStatus: "queued"`.
- `state.db` → `session_admissions` (read-only query): **91 completed, 11 interrupted, 2 started
  — zero queued.** The client treats each entry as server-owned, forwards the delete to the
  server, the server has no matching admission, and the delete silently does nothing.
- Cleared `Local Storage` at 14:41 → a new entry was back at 14:48 (a normal user message this
  time, not a background notice), same `serverStatus: "queued"`.

  drain are never collected (same conclusion as #68895).
- The desktop mirrors gateway-admitted automation turns (background-process completion notices)
  into the composer queue as pending prompts; when the session has no live runtime binding those
  never drain.

Body:
 markdown
 Summary

 The Hermes agent (execute_code / terminal codegen path) generates working code for
 single-loop / small-data tasks, but for long-running batch tasks it frequently changes
 execution strategy between the sample-size validation run and the full-batch run — and
 that drift is the dominant source of batch errors.
 Observed failure mode

 On batch workloads (e.g. processing a 100k-paragraph docx corpus, multi-sheet Excel
 ledgers, bulk column transformations), the typical loop is:

 1. Agent writes a script, runs it on a small sample → correct.
 2. Agent then re-writes / re-approaches the full-batch run with a different strategy
 (different data-access pattern, different chunking, a "faster" alternative path,
 different library call), because it decides the sample approach "scales poorly".
 3. The batch run fails in the middle. Re-work is 2-3 iterations.

 The sample run validates path A. The batch run runs path B. Path A being correct gives
 no evidence about path B. This makes sample-based validation structurally unreliable —
 which is why "run a sample first" as a user-side discipline does not fix it.
 Why this is a model-side / framework-side gap

 - The agent has no constraint that sample and batch share one code path (only the
 data-volume parameter differs). It will freely "optimize" the batch into a new strategy.
 - Codegen quality on non-trivial batch scripts is below what the task needs; errors are
 not caught pre-execution (no self-check / dry-run / strategy-stability guarantee).
 - This is not a "user discipline" problem — adding more rules on top of the agent makes
 it heavier and more brittle. The fix belongs in codegen behavior itself.
 Suggested directions (any of these)

 1. Strategy-stability contract: when a batch task extends a validated sample run, the
 agent must reuse the same code path (parameterized by data volume) unless the user
 explicitly approves a strategy change. Surface the proposed strategy diff before
 switching.
 2. Batch dry-run / canary: built-in pre-execution step that runs the batch code path on
 a small slice of the real data (same code, truncated input) and reports before
 committing to the full run.
 3. Codegen hardening for long tasks: pre-execution self-check / static sanity pass on
 generated batch scripts (off-by-one in chunking, data-source switch, missing termination
 condition) — the class of errors that recur across sessions.
 Repro context (one instance, full trace in our local logs)

 A docx clause-parsing batch: sample run used regex + sequential walk (correct). Batch
 run switched to a different parse strategy, produced garbage mid-file; required 3
 iterations (v1 → v2 → v3) to converge.
 Expected

 Batch tasks complete on the first full run at the same reliability as the sample run,
 because both exercise the same code.
title: Codegen: strategy drift between sample-size run and full-batch run makes batch tasks  unreliable

## Problem

The public lifecycle `result()` adds loss that vanilla `delegate_task` does not: `SubagentLifecycleService._run` clips the already-native-budgeted summary again at 32,000 characters and discards `summary_truncated` / `summary_full_path`.

The shared native worker already applies `delegation.max_summary_chars` and the parent's context-headroom budget, retaining the complete original in a safely created spill file. Its returned summary includes a recovery footer. The additional lifecycle clip can cut off that footer when the configured native cap exceeds 32k; with both native limits disabled it silently cuts an otherwise untrimmed answer. Even under the default cap, consumers lose the structured spill metadata.

Concrete consumer: `seppegadeyne/hermes-claude-agents`. This is distinct from image/schema inputs (#138828), ownership (#138860), and the progress/completion work in #72630.

## Reproduced

Against main `7bda2a3368024f7ae1c70cef16583e7c2c891674`, nine proposed lifecycle regression cases fail. They execute the real shared native worker/finalization path with only model conversation and child construction scripted:

- native static cap disabled and no parent headroom estimate: a long answer is silently cut to 32k;
- native caps of 24k and 40k: the public result has no truncation/spill fields; the 40k recovery footer is cut off;
- direct and plugin-host-wire result paths exhibit the same loss.

## Requested fix

Keep the native summary as finalized, carry optional `summary_truncated` and `summary_full_path` through the public result, and retain existing capability/owner gating. Do not expose raw conversations or hidden reasoning, bypass native context protection, auto-read model-supplied paths, or claim a spill succeeded when it failed. Preserve positional compatibility by appending defaulted fields. Document that the lifecycle adds no second summary cap.
title: Public subagent lifecycle re-truncates native summaries and drops spill recovery metadata

**Component:** `hermes_cli/web_server_sessions.py` (`_mutate_session_request` / `_mutate_offline_store`)
and `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py` (`_with_db`)
**Version:** Hermes Agent v0.22.1+39.g2823fbe (2026.9.24), stable, Windows 11
**Severity:** medium-high on an always-on install (dashboard + gateway both running, the normal setup
for remote/phone access) — the dashboard's write actions fail with a bare 409.

## Symptom

With a gateway running for the profile, a *separate* `hermes dashboard` process is not the store
owner, so its offline mutation path is refused the exclusive-maintenance reservation:

```
12:22:58 DELETE /api/sessions/empty?profile=default -> 409      # "Delete empty" always fails
13:05:50 DELETE /api/sessions/<id>?profile=default&request_id=<uuid>&expected_revision=0&expected_generation=0 -> 409
```

`_with_session_maintenance` turns that into `HTTPException(409, str(OwnershipConflict))`, and the SPA
shows "Failed to delete session" / "Failed to delete empty sessions". Under `uvicorn
log_level="warning"` a handled 4xx is not logged at all, so nothing lands in `logs/agent.log` or
`logs/errors.log` — the failure is invisible server-side, which is why it is easy to misdiagnose as a
UI bug.

## Root cause

Two paths exist and only one is owner-safe:

1. **Bulk** (`web_routers/sessions.py::_with_db`, non-read-only) → `_with_session_maintenance()` →
   `exclusive_maintenance([home])` → `OwnershipConflict` → 409. It never tries the owner.
2. **Single session** (`_mutate_session_request`) → when `_session_mutation_context()` reports no
   authority (the standalone dashboard case), the mutation goes to `_mutate_offline_store` →
   `_with_session_maintenance()` → same 409.

## Suggested fix (applied locally, verified)

Let the standalone dashboard hand the mutation to the live owner over the control socket instead of
writing `state.db` itself — the gateway already exposes the same owner-guarded, revision-fenced verb
(`session.mutate`):

```python
async def _mutate_via_gateway_owner(profile, params):
    """Forward a standalone dashboard mutation to the live gateway owner (control socket)."""
    home = Path(_cron_profile_home(profile)[1]) if profile else Path(_default_db_path()).parent
    discovery = await asyncio.to_thread(discover_gateway_endpoint, home, timeout=1.5)  # read-only
    endpoint = getattr(discovery, 'endpoint', None)
    if endpoint is None:
        return None                      # no owner -> caller falls back to the offline store
    call = {k: params[k] for k in ('session_id','request_id','expected_revision','operation','payload')
            if k in params}
    if params.get('expected_generation') is not None:
        call['expected_generation'] = params['expected_generation']
    try:
        async with connect_gateway(endpoint=endpoint) as client:
            return await client.rpc('session.mutate', **call)
    except GatewayClientError as exc:
        reason = str(exc)
        status = {'permission_denied

**Component:** `gateway/session_authority.py` — `SessionAuthority._handle()`
**Version:** Hermes Agent v0.22.1+39.g2823fbe (2026.9.24), stable, Windows 11
**Severity:** high — the session list is dead for every client until the gateway restarts.

## Symptom

`session.list` (WS RPC) fails for every client, repeatedly:

```
2026-10-15 12:45:xx ERROR tui_gateway.ws: ws dispatch crash peer=127.0.0.1:12086 id=r957 method=session.list
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable        # gateway/session_authority.py:204, in _handle
```

One crash every ~1.5 s (542 occurrences in a single hour of `logs/errors.log`). `runtime.describe`
and other methods keep working, so the gateway looks alive.

Client-visible consequences:

- TUI `/sessions` overlay renders **empty** (the live-list call fails and the component returns early,
  before parsing resumable history), so the delete affordance is unreachable — reported by the user as
  "I can't delete a session".
- Any panel that needs the live list (dashboard, desktop) loses the live half of its data.

## Root cause

A session stays in `SessionAuthority.sessions` (in-memory live registry) while its `state.db` row is
already gone, e.g. after the dashboard's "delete empty sessions" sweep deleted rows for sessions whose
gateway routes were still live. `_handle()` then does:

```python
def _handle(self, ref):
    row = self.db.get_session(ref.session_id)      # -> None
    pending = self._pending_rows(ref)
    ...
    ... row['runtime_revision'] ...                # TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```

Its own docstring already promises the safe behaviour ("a deleted/evicted live entry surfaces here as
`not_found`, not as a KeyError"), and `list_sessions` already skips `not_found` candidates — the guard
is just missing at the top of `_handle`.

## Suggested fix

Exactly the guard the docstring promises (5 lines, applied locally and verified):

```python
def _handle(self, ref):
    row = self.db.get_session(ref.session_id)
    if row is None:
        raise RuntimeStoreError('not_found')
    pending = self._pending_rows(ref)
    ...
```

Verification after the fix (gateway restarted): zero `session.list` failures in 10+ minutes of
steady-state traffic that previously produced one every 1.5 s; `session.list` returns the live
sessions again.
title: session.list crash-loops when a live session's DB row is gone (TypeError in session_authority._handle)

**Component:** web UI — `hermes_cli/web_dist/assets/api-*.js` (SPA mutation wrapper)
**Version:** Hermes Agent v0.22.1+39.g2823fbe (2026.9.24), stable, Windows 11, install=git
**Severity:** high for remote/phone users — every write action in the dashboard is dead, while the UI
reports a generic error (e.g. "Failed to delete session").

## Symptom

Over `http://<lan-ip>:9119` or `http://100.x.x.x:9119` (Tailscale IP):

- "Delete session" → toast `Failed to delete session`. The session is **not** deleted.
- The server never receives the request. Server-side log of a failed attempt shows the preflight
  snapshot landing and then nothing:

```
13:05:49 GET  /api/sessions/<id>/mutation-snapshot?profile=default -> 200
13:05:50 DELETE /api/sessions/<id>?... -> 409      <-- only when it DOES get sent; usually NO DELETE line at all
```

Reads (`GET /api/sessions`, `/api/status`, history) work fine from the same origin, which is why this
reads as a "delete is broken" bug rather than a client crash.

Same dashboard over `http://127.0.0.1:9119` works. Rename, pin, model change, branch — all affected.

## Root cause

The mutation wrapper (`_e` factory in `api-*.js`) resolves the request id with an **unguarded**
`crypto.randomUUID()`:

```js
a=n().then(e=>{
  if(typeof e?.exists!="boolean"||!Number.isSafeInteger(e.runtime_revision)||... )
    throw Error("Session mutation snapshot unavailable; refresh before trying again");
  return{request_id:crypto.randomUUID(),expected_revision:e.runtime_revision,
         ...e.exists?{expected_generation:e.runtime_generation}:{}}
})
```

`crypto.randomUUID` is **only defined in a secure context**. On a plain-HTTP origin that is not
localhost it is `undefined`, so the call throws `TypeError: crypto.randomUUID is not a function`
*inside the snapshot `.then()`* — before the DELETE fetch is ever built. The rejection bubbles to the
page's catch, which shows the generic toast. Verified on the failing origin itself:

```
http://192.168.x.x:9119  -> isSecureContext=false, typeof crypto.randomUUID = "undefined"
                            crypto.randomUUID() -> TypeError: crypto.randomUUID is not a function
                            crypto.getRandomValues -> "function"   (still available)
http://127.0.0.1:9119    -> isSecureContext=true,  typeof crypto.randomUUID = "function"
```

Note the sibling call site in `ChatPage-*.js` **is** guarded, which suggests the pattern is known:

```js
typeof crypto<"u"&&"randomUUID"in crypto?`${t}-${crypto.randomUUID()}`:`${t}-${Math.random()...}`
```

`api-*.js` simply missed the same guard.

## Suggested fix

One site, one expression — fall back to `getRandomValues` (available in insecure contexts):

```js
request_id: crypto.randomUUID ? crypto.randomUUID() : (() => {           // or a shared newRequestId()
  const b = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16));
  b[6] = b[6] & 15 | 64; b[8] = b[8] & 63 | 128;
  const h = [...b].map(x => x.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");
  return `${h

## Bug Description

After upgrading to `v0.22.1` (`297552a9d6`, post-#106742 unified gateway runtime), resuming a pre-upgrade local TUI/CLI session whose provider differed from `config.yaml`'s current `model.provider` / `model.base_url` routes the session's model ID to the wrong provider endpoint and fails every turn with HTTP 404 (`Your request was not processed. Send it again if you still want me to carry it out.`).

Specifically, `adopt_legacy_session()` in `gateway/session_local_migration.py` only copies `row['cwd']` and `row['model']` from the legacy `sessions` row and ignores `row['model_config']` (which holds `provider`, `base_url`, `api_mode`, `reasoning_config`, and `service_tier`).

Related to tracking issue #134889 (and adjacent to #138843 / #138856).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Prior to `#106742` (`v0.21.6`), create and run a TUI session on `provider: openai-codex`, `model: gpt-6.1-sol-900k`, `reasoning: xhigh` (`sessions.model_config` records `{"model": "gpt-6.1-sol-900k", "provider": "openai-codex", "base_url": "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex", "api_mode": "codex_responses", "reasoning_config": {"enabled": true, "effort": "xhigh"}, "service_tier": "priority"}`).
2. Have `config.yaml` configured with a different default provider/base_url, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   model:
     default: gemini-3.8-flash
     provider: gemini
     base_url: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta
   ```
3. Update Hermes to `v0.22.1` (`297552a9d6`), open TUI, and resume the pre-upgrade `gpt-6.1-sol-900k` session.
4. Send any prompt in that resumed session.
5. **Actual:** The turn fails after 3 retries and prints:
   ```text
   Your request was not processed. Send it again if you still want me to carry it out.
   ```
   (And if the user then tries to fix the route via the TUI `/model` picker and selects a reasoning level, they immediately hit #138856 `error: unsupported canonical model option: --reasoning`.)

## Evidence from `agent.log` and `state.db`

From `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log`:

```text

2026-10-15 12:13:24,984 INFO [20261012_122515_721bf6] agent.turn_context: conversation turn: session=20261012_122515_721bf6 model=gpt-6.1-sol-900k provider=gemini platform=tui history=242

### Bug Description

`groups.log` returns room events whose `actor` object carries keys its own declared result model forbids, so the handler's result fails contract validation on every call. Production logs an ERROR per call; under `HERMES_TEST_ISOLATION=1` this raises `ContractViolation`.

Every `groups.log` page that includes at least one member-authored event re-triggers it, because the actor dict is persisted verbatim in `state.db` and replayed on each page. The error count scales with the number of member events in the page.

### Environment

- Hermes `v0.22.1+66.g7bda2a3` (git install)
- macOS 15, Apple Silicon, Python 3.14.7
- Single gateway serving 7 multiplexed profiles

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a hosted room with at least one member-authored event.
2. Call `groups.log` (the Desktop Bot Chat / dashboard group view does this on poll).
3. Observe the gateway log.

Or reproduce without a gateway:

```bash
python -c "
from tui_gateway.contracts.groups_bot_relay import GroupsLogResult, RoomActor
producer_actor = {'kind':'member','id':'alice','display_name':'profile-a','profile':'profile-a'}
RoomActor(**producer_actor)"
```

```
model fields: ['kind', 'id']
REJECTED as expected ->
    ('display_name',) extra_forbidden input= 'profile-a'
    ('profile',)      extra_forbidden input= 'profile-a'
```

### Expected Behavior

`groups.log`'s handler result passes `check_result` against `GroupsLogResult`.

### Actual Behavior

```
ERROR tui_gateway.contracts.registry: result of 'groups.log' violates its wire contract: 15 validation errors for GroupsLogResult
events.0.actor.display_name
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value='profile-a', input_type=str]
events.0.actor.profile
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value='profile-a', input_type=str]
events.2.actor.display_name
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value='profile-b', input_type=str]
events.2.actor.profile
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value='profile-b', input_type=str]
```

Observed error counts in a single day on one host: 1, 4, 5, 8, 15. It fires roughly every 2–10 minutes while the group view polls, and accounted for the bulk of a 16 MB `gateway.error.log` (~2 KB/s sustained growth).

### Root Cause

The contract model declares two fields; the producer is explicitly sanctioned to write four.

| Location | Role |
|---|---|
| `tui_gateway/contracts/groups_bot_relay.py:31` | `class RoomActor(Result): kind: str; id: str` — `extra="forbid"` by default |
| `gateway/hosted_room_discussion.py:184` | `_member_actor()` always emits `profile`; conditionally emits `connection_id` and `display_name` |
| `gateway/hosted_rooms.py:59` | `_OPTIONAL_ACTOR_FIELDS = (("display_name", …), ("profile", …), ("connection_id", …))` — the writer validates against exactly these |
| `gateway/hosted_rooms.py:512` | `_event_from_row()` replays `actor_json` verbatim from `state.db` |

### Bug Description

Hermes Desktop installed directly from the **Microsoft Store on Windows** remains stuck on **“Connecting”** when using the default local connection (“This device”).

This report concerns the Microsoft Store bundled installation, rather than a source checkout or a manually installed CLI.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install **Hermes Agent from the Microsoft Store** (Store product ID: `9PMXK8CZC7KR`).
2. Launch the installed desktop app and use the local connection.
3. Observe that the GUI remains on “Connecting”.
4. Inspect `desktop.log`: the gateway reports ready, but subsequent desktop API requests fail with `Gateway ticket bootstrap failed`.

### Expected Behavior

The Store-installed desktop app should connect to its bundled local gateway without requiring a separate Python or CLI installation.

### Actual Behavior

Sanitized excerpts from the desktop log:

```text
[backend] Hermes gateway is ready
[boot] Hermes gateway is ready
[gateway] forgot stale canonical endpoint for primary "default"; re-ensuring
[fleet-roster] local: Gateway ticket bootstrap failed
[hermes:api GET /api/profiles] Error: Gateway ticket bootstrap failed
[hermes:api GET /api/config?include_defaults=false] Error: Gateway ticket bootstrap failed
```

### Environment

- OS: native Windows, x64
- Installation channel: **Microsoft Store**
- Store package version: `2026.6886.872.0`
- Bundled Hermes version: `0.22.1`
- Bundled source commit: `297552a9d646119871391d202509822cd86330df`
- Connection: local / “This device”
- WinGet reported no available upgrade for the Store product ID. Availability of a newer build was not independently confirmed in the Microsoft Store app.

### Root Cause Analysis

Inspection of the installed `dist/electron-main.mjs` suggests the bundled backend is incorrectly treated as a raw Python interpreter during ticket bootstrap:

1. The bundled branch of `resolveHermesBackend()` returns `kind: "python"`, `shell: false`, and `command: payload.shim`.
2. `payload.shim` resolves to the package-relative **`agent-payload/bin/hermes.exe`**, a Hermes CLI launcher.
3. `ticketRuntimeFor()` returns a non-shell `python` backend unchanged.
4. `TicketBridge` then spawns that command with `["-P", "-u", "-c", TICKET_SCRIPT]`.
5. Running the installed launcher with these interpreter arguments reproduces an immediate CLI parser failure:

```text
hermes: error: unrecognized arguments: -P -u
```

The reproduction used the installed `agent-payload/bin/hermes.exe` with `-P -u -c` and a small import/print probe. It exited with code 1.

The ticket bridge calls `this.child.stderr.resume()`, discarding the subprocess's error output. When the child closes, the UI receives only the generic `Gateway ticket bootstrap failed` error.

The inspected code and reproduced parser failure indicate a launcher/interpreter mismatch in the ticket bootstrap path. A corrected build has not been tested, so it remains unverified whether fixing this mismatch fully restores connectiv
title: [Bug]: Microsoft Store Windows install stuck on Connecting — ticket bridge passes Python flags to hermes.exe

## Bug Description
Desktop's legacy remote session interceptor routes /api/sessions/{id} and /messages, but not /api/sessions/{id}/mutation-snapshot. The renderer fences edits by reading that snapshot before PATCH. Without an explicit registry connection pin, the read can reach local primary while the write reaches a remote backend.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use legacy global-remote mode or a per-profile remote override, without a registry-pinned connectionId.
2. Archive a remote session using the current fenced renderer.
3. The snapshot GET does not match the Electron per-session interception regex and falls through locally.
4. If that local backend lacks the route, the renderer's intended old-server fallback sends an unfenced PATCH to the modern remote, which rejects it with mutation_identity_required. If the local route exists but the session does not, snapshot validation fails before the write.

## Expected Behavior
The mutation snapshot and mutation must reach the same remote backend and owner profile. Profile aliasing and revision/generation fencing must remain intact.

## Actual Behavior
The interceptor regex only accepts /api/sessions/{id} and optional /messages. The snapshot suffix falls through.

## Affected Component
Other: Desktop Electron remote REST routing. Pure-local and explicitly registry-pinned remote requests are not the affected path.

## Debug Report
No private config or logs uploaded. Reproduced against main 7bda2a3368024f7ae1c70cef16583e7c2c891674 by calling the real renderer archive function through the extracted production route with separate local/remote test stores. Removing snapshot interception causes both global and profile-override cases to emit an unfenced write; restoring it keeps request_id, expected_revision and expected_generation.

## Operating System / Versions
Reported from a macOS Desktop v0.22.1 installation; source-level reproduction/tests on Linux ARM64. The installed renderer already contained the snapshot flow. The original failed network request was not captured, so this report establishes a concrete source defect and failure mechanism, not a proven forensic attribution of that particular screenshot.

## Root Cause Analysis
apps/desktop/electron/main.ts interceptSessionRequestForRemote: /^\/api\/sessions\/[^/]+(\/messages)?$/ excludes mutation-snapshot. HTTP JSON serialization itself does not strip identity fields.

## Proposed Fix
Extend the existing per-session route to mutation-snapshot; extract only that routing block into its existing topic module so the renderer-to-routing boundary is behavior-testable. Do not weaken server identity enforcement or broaden older-server fallback.

## Follow-up: same-class remote reads
The same interceptor omission affects `/api/sessions/{id}/timeline` and `/api/sessions/{id}/messages/around` in the legacy remote path. The fork branch now includes both exact suffixes without accepting unrelated/deeper routes.

## Bug Description
A committed update can fail to restore a dashboard/serve backend even though the messaging gateway already runs the new code. The updater then reports `gateway_restart` and retains a gateway restart obligation, sending the user to a command that cannot restore that dashboard.

There are two connected problems:
1. On macOS, dashboard argv captured through `ps -o command=` and `shlex.split` loses argument boundaries around Python `-c` source. Replaying it can produce a `SyntaxError` and an immediate child exit.
2. Post-restart verification treats the aggregate `restart.incomplete` flag as gateway debt, even when the outstanding work belongs to a dashboard or serve runtime.

Related: #136159 reports the corrupted argv and contradictory gateway warning. Exact-argv proposals #136245 and #127204 address the capture problem; this issue also covers component-specific follow-up accounting.

## Steps to Reproduce
### Corrupted dashboard restart
1. Run a dashboard/serve backend through a Python inline bootstrap containing spaces or newlines.
2. On macOS, capture it with `_dashboard_cmdline_for_pid`, then replay the command as the updater does.
3. `ps` supplies display text, not an argv serialization; splitting it can turn the source into many arguments and make the child exit immediately.

### Wrong follow-up attribution
1. Have `_refresh_dashboard_after_update` report a dashboard that could not be restored.
2. Have the fleet probe show the messaging gateway as current, with no failed gateway unit or standing gateway obligation.
3. Inspect the emitted follow-up, receipt and marker-clear decision.
4. Repeat with simultaneous gateway failure, or an unaccounted serve/dashboard runtime whose PID is unavailable.

## Expected Behavior
- Capture exact argv; do not guess Python source or argument boundaries from lossy `ps` text.
- A dashboard-only failure records `dashboard_restart`, not a false gateway obligation.
- Simultaneous dashboard and gateway failures retain both follow-ups and recovery instructions.
- Genuine standing gateway debt is preserved.
- Unaccounted serve/dashboard rows retain a follow-up even without a PID, and are not labelled as stopped merely because reconciliation could not verify them.

## Actual Behavior

### Symptom

On a desktop / local session, every **write-form** `/memory` subcommand is refused with `error: unsupported_command`:

```
/memory                 → OK  (state + pending list)
/memory pending         → OK
/memory reject all      → error: unsupported_command
/memory approve <id>    → error: unsupported_command
/memory approval on     → error: unsupported_command
```

`/skills reject <id>` works on the *same* surface. The backend handler (`hermes_cli/write_approval_commands.py`) implements approve/reject/approval for **both** subsystems and already supports the `all` target (`_reject`, "Target ALL"), so this is a dispatch-layer gate, not a missing implementation — net effect: staged memory writes cannot be reviewed from the desktop at all.

### Root cause

`gateway/session_commands.py::command_verdict` returns `'refused'`, which `execute_command` turns into `RuntimeStoreError('unsupported_command')` (~L197-198):

```python
_READ_ARGUMENTS = {
    'skills': lambda arg: _first_token(arg) in {'', 'pending', 'diff'},
    'usage': lambda arg: not arg.strip(),
    'memory': lambda arg: arg.strip().lower() in {'', 'pending'},     # ~L63
    ...
}

_CONTROL_ARGUMENTS = {                                                # ~L72-74
    'skills': lambda arg: _first_token(arg) in {'approve', 'apply', 'reject', 'deny', 'drop', 'approval', 'mode'},
}
```

`/memory reject all` matches neither arm: the read gate only admits `''`/`'pending'`, and the control table has no `memory` key. `/skills` has both.

### This looks like an omission, not a deliberate restriction

The comment immediately above those tables (~L57-59) already groups memory with skills as *"a read command whose other subcommands write"*:

```python
# The read-only argument forms of a read command whose other subcommands write: ``/usage reset``
# redeems a credit, ``/memory approve|approval`` applies writes / edits config.yaml,
# ``/suggestions accept|catalog`` schedules cron jobs delivering to this (non-messaging) chat.
```

`skills` got its control entry; `memory` — explicitly named in that same sentence — did not.

### Proposed fix

One line, mirroring `skills`:

```python
_CONTROL_ARGUMENTS = {
    'skills': lambda arg: _first_token(arg) in {'approve', 'apply', 'reject', 'deny', 'drop', 'approval', 'mode'},
    'memory': lambda arg: _first_token(arg) in {'approve', 'apply', 'reject', 'deny', 'drop', 'approval', 'mode'},
}
```

Verified locally by calling `command_verdict` before/after the change:

| call | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `('memory', '')` | read | read |
| `('memory', 'pending')` | read | read |
| `('memory', 'reject all')` | **refused** | **control** |
| `('memory', 'approve <id>')` | refused | control |
| `('memory', 'approval on')` | refused | control |
| `('skills', 'reject x')` | control | control (unchanged) |
| `('skills', 'install x')` | refused | refused (unchanged) |

### Same gap for the other two commands named in that comment

`usage reset` and `suggestion
title: [Bug]: /memory approve|reject|approval refused as unsupported_command on desktop/local sessions — _CONTROL_ARGUMENTS has no memory entry
