Observed 2026-10-13 on a macOS Hermes gateway (hook: a repo-level PR-lifecycle gate registered as a native `pre_tool_call` shell hook, ~2-6s typical runtime, configured `timeout: 90`).

## What happened

1. During a machine load spike (load avg ~11) one hook run exceeded the plugin-layer timeout. `hermes_cli/plugins.py` logged "timed out after 30s — skipping".
2. That run plus two later attempts piled up 3 abandoned workers (the `_HOOK_MAX_ABANDONED_WORKERS` cap). After that, EVERY subsequent tool call failed instantly with `pre_tool_call plugin callback timed out or is still running` — for ~2 hours, until an MCP reload / gateway restart cleared it.
3. The hook itself was healthy the whole time: post-incident, the same gate ran in 0.06s (trivial) and 2-6s (denied push) when invoked directly.

## Analysis

The bounded-runner in `plugins_dispatch.py` is designed so the abandoned-worker cap keeps being skipped "fail-closed for pre_tool_call" until a worker finishes. But when the underlying `shell_hooks._spawn` subprocess is killed on timeout, the abandoned worker's thread is only released if `communicate()` unwinds — under a wedged child that kill did not propagate within the window we observed, so all 3 slots stayed occupied and the suppression (60s) never mattered. Net effect: a single slow hook under system load permanently disabled tool execution with no recovery path short of a restart.

## Suggested fixes (any of these would have contained it)

1. **Drain the abandoned slots when the child process is confirmed dead.** `_spawn` kills the process tree on timeout (shell hooks); once `kill_process_tree` completes, the corresponding bounded-runner worker should release its slot deterministically, not depend on thread unwinding racing with the lock.
2. **Cap total skip duration, then fail open per-callback with a loud log.** E.g. after N consecutive skips (or M minutes) for a callback, stop skipping and let the call proceed with a prominent warning — an operator-visible degraded mode beats a silent full outage. Safety-sensitive hooks can opt out via a per-hook flag.
3. **Honor the configured per-hook timeout at the plugin layer.** config.yaml declared `timeout: 90` but the plugin layer enforced 30s; the effective budget should match config (or the config key should be documented as capped).

## Environment

- hermes-agent at 0e427d788d (Oct 13); the same bounded-runner shape is present on current main (`_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SUPPRESSION_SECONDS = 60.0`, `_HOOK_MAX_ABANDONED_WORKERS = 3`).
- Happy to provide full logs (`hermes_cli.plugins: Hook ... timed out / skipped after previous timeout` sequence) and the hook script if useful.
title: pre_tool_call hook: one timeout can fail-closed skip ALL later tool calls for hours (abandoned-worker cap never drains)

**What happens**

`hermes plugins install` treats any `package.json` at the plugin root as a Node sidecar (`hermes_cli/plugins_cmd_install.py:94`). In a terminal it says the plugin "declares Node dependencies" and asks whether to install them. On yes, `pm.workspace.install_node_sidecar` runs `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, or `npm install` without a lockfile (`pm/workspace.py:323-332`). It does not pass `--omit=dev`.

Desktop and dashboard plugins often commit a prebuilt bundle and keep `package.json` only for build and test tooling (esbuild, TypeScript, vitest). For such a plugin:
- the question claims Node dependencies when the plugin has no runtime dependencies;
- answering yes installs the whole dev toolchain into the plugin folder, and none of it is used at runtime;
- after that, updates run `npm ci` again (`hermes_cli/plugins_transaction.py:66-69`): every catalog re-pin, because the fresh clone has no `node_modules`, and any custom pull that changes `package.json` or the lockfile.

Non-interactive installs skip the question, so this only reaches people installing from a terminal.

**Repro** (main at `297552a9`)

Take a plugin whose `package.json` has `"dependencies": {}` and only devDependencies. The public `electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager` v0.4.5 has 9 devDependencies. In a copy of that tree:
- `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, the command the installer runs, installs 84 packages, 108 MB.
- `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --omit=dev` installs nothing.

**Suggested fix**

1. In `_install_plugin_python_deps`, skip the Node question when `package.json` declares no `dependencies` and no `optionalDependencies`. Nothing would be installed for runtime anyway, so this cannot break a working sidecar.
2. Optionally, also pass `--omit=dev` in `install_node_sidecar`. Caveat: a sidecar that compiles itself in a `prepare` or `postinstall` script needs its devDependencies at install time, so this part would need a check or an opt-out.

I can open a draft PR for (1) with tests if this direction is right.
title: [Bug]: Plugin install treats a build-only package.json as Node dependencies and npm-installs the dev toolchain

## Bug Description

Indeed's catalog MCP can complete OAuth and still never load tools. After a successful dynamic registration and token exchange, `https://mcp.indeed.com/claude/mcp` rejects the fresh token with HTTP 403 `invalid_client` / `Client not allowed`. `hermes mcp login indeed` then prints a registration-failure sentence that does not match the HTTP log.

This is not the issuer-slash bug in #95508. Discovery, registration, and token exchange all succeeded here.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add the catalog Indeed server (`url: https://mcp.indeed.com/claude/mcp`, `auth: oauth`).
2. Run `hermes mcp login indeed` and approve the browser consent.
3. Run `hermes mcp test indeed`.

On 2026-10-14 the login that used dynamic registration (not the Client ID Metadata Document) logged:

- `POST https://secure.indeed.com/oauth/v2/register` → `201 Created`
- `POST https://apis.indeed.com/oauth/v2/tokens` → `200 OK`
- `POST https://mcp.indeed.com/claude/mcp` → `403` body `{"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Client not allowed"}`
- SSE `GET` of the same URL → `403 Forbidden`

`hermes mcp test indeed` then failed in 11.9s with that same 403 on both Streamable HTTP and SSE. An unauthenticated POST to the same URL returns `401` `invalid_token` / `Authentication required`, so the 403 is the authenticated call, not a missing token.

The desktop panel stays on Error / "Tool list unavailable." Its log tab stays on "No output yet" because that tab is the stdio stream and this server is HTTP.

## Expected Behavior

After register 201 and token 200, either the tool list loads, or the failure names the resource rejection (`invalid_client` / `Client not allowed` from the MCP URL) and leaves the saved token in place. Do not say registration was rejected.

## Actual Behavior

Login prints:

```
Authentication failed: 'indeed' only allows pre-approved OAuth clients — it rejected client registration (403), so no browser flow can start. Options: set oauth.client_name to a name the provider allowlists, add a pre-registered client (oauth: {client_id: ..., client_secret: ...}), or use the provider's stdio / API-key / local server instead.
```

That sentence is the humanizer in `tools/mcp_oauth.py` (`_humanize_registration_error` / the "pre-approved OAuth clients" branch). It treats any 403 whose text contains "forbidden" as a registration rejection. Here registration had already returned 201, and the 403 was the next call to the MCP resource. The command also exits, so the loopback listener is dead even though the browser was opened.

Cloudflare's remote MCP, on the same machine and the same Hermes build, completed dynamic registration and connected. Indeed is the one that refuses the client after a good token.

## Extra detail

- Indeed's protected-resource metadata advertises `job_seeker.company.details.read` and `job_seeker.profile.read`. `POST /oauth/v2/register` rejects those with `400 invalid_client_metadata` ("Requested scopes are invalid or not supported"
title: [Bug]: Indeed MCP sign-in succeeds, then the resource returns invalid_client / Client not allowed — and login reports a registration 403

body:
### What happened

macOS desktop client connected to a Windows backend over **Remote gateway**. The agent attached a file with `MEDIA:` (a 3.8 MB zip). Clicking **Download** on the file card opened the native save dialog; after confirming it, the download failed with:

    Download fehlgeschlagen   (Download failed)
    EROFS: read-only file system, open '/.hermes-download-5113923c.part'

`pumpStreamToFile` creates its temp file next to the destination (`downloadTempPath` → `path.join(path.dirname(destPath), '.hermes-download-<hex>.part')`), so the dialog returned a destination directly under `/`, which is the sealed, read-only system volume on macOS.

### Likely cause

The gateway-file save paths hand the dialog a bare file name with no directory (`apps/desktop/electron/gateway-file-download.ts` on `origin/main` f974222e69):

- `finalizeGatewayDownload`: `defaultPath: filename` (line 475)
- `saveGatewayDownload`, data-URL fallback: `defaultPath: context.suggested || context.fallbackName` (line 546)

The other two save paths in `main.ts` anchor the dialog in Downloads:

- image save: `defaultPath: downloadsDir ? path.join(downloadsDir, fallbackName) : fallbackName`
- `installDownloadHandling` (`will-download`): `defaultPath: path.join(app.getPath('downloads'), filename)`

Without a directory the macOS panel starts wherever it chooses; here that was `/`, and pressing **Save** without navigating fails as above. I did not instrument the dialog itself, so the starting directory is inferred from the error path.

### Suggested fix

Give the gateway-file dialog the same Downloads anchor at both call sites, e.g. inject the directory through `GatewayFileSaveDeps` so the module stays Electron-free:

    defaultPath: downloadsDir ? path.join(downloadsDir, filename) : filename

Optionally map `EROFS` / `EACCES` from the temp-file open to a readable message such as "Can't save to this folder, pick another location".

### Related

- #91074 (attach dialog should default to Downloads)
- #135441 (save downloads without the native dialog)
- #92480 (save-dialog filters for `MEDIA:` downloads)

### Environment

- Client: macOS, Hermes Desktop built from source (`CFBundleShortVersionString` 0.0.0)
- Backend: Windows 11, hermes-agent 0e427d788d
- Connection: Remote gateway over a private network
title: [Bug]: Desktop gateway file download passes a bare filename as save-dialog defaultPath; on macOS the save can land on read-only / (EROFS)

**Environment:** Hermes Desktop (macOS) connected over SSH to a remote Hermes backend (v0.22.0). Remote matters for one of the shapes: the worktree probe yields nothing on this backend (the git facade can query remote worktrees, but this backend returns none), so a single-folder empty project has no lanes at all.

**What happens**

Selecting a project that has no sessions yet dead-ends — nothing useful opens, and no session is created or offered for it:

1. **Explicit single-folder project** (e.g. a project with one fresh folder, 0 sessions): the sidebar enters it, but the drill-in body is blank — no session rows, no "No sessions yet" empty state, no action (the repo header that owns the New-session "+" is suppressed for single-repo projects).
2. **Auto-discovered repo with no sessions** (still offered by ⌘K's "Projects" group as `Open <project>`): selecting it doesn't open at all — the session-bearing filter drops it from the sidebar model, the scoped lookup misses, and the sessions area's render gate never opens.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create a project with one folder that has no sessions (or pick any discovered repo with no sessions).
2. Sidebar → "Group by → Projects" and click the project row (shape 1), or ⌘K → type the repo name → Enter (shape 2).

**Expected:** the drill-in opens with the project's content — worktree lanes when the probe finds any, otherwise the "No sessions yet" empty state — so it's clear the project has no sessions yet and the first session can be started there.

**Actual:** blank drill-in body (shape 1); nothing opens, the sidebar stays on the overview (shape 2). No session opens in either case.

**Root cause (current `main`)**

- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/sessions-section.tsx` — `hasProjectContent` counts the backend-seeded folder repo as content (`repos.length > 0`), which suppresses the empty state; `EnteredProjectContent` suppresses the repo header for single-repo projects, so the body compiles to zero rows.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/index.tsx` — `filterToSessionBearingProjects` drops zero-session auto projects from `projectModel`; `overviewEnteredProject` can't resolve the scoped id, and `showSessionSections` (gated on `projectModel.length > 0`) stays closed.

Related: #104280 / #104301 cover the *failed-fetch* state of the drill-in; this is the successful, genuinely-empty case.
title: Desktop sidebar: session-less project selection dead-ends (blank single-folder drill-in; auto projects never open)

### Bug Description
When a Node.js process running the WhatsApp Baileys bridge is terminated, restarted, or crashes mid-write, `creds.json` can be truncated to **0 bytes**. 

Because `_preflight()` in `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py` only checks `creds_path.exists()`, a 0-byte `creds.json` passes preflight validation. The gateway assumes WhatsApp is authenticated and launches `bridge.js` in background/detached mode (without TTY). The bridge dumps the QR code into `bridge.log` while the gateway hangs for 30s waiting for a connection, eventually failing with `HTTP 503: Not connected to WhatsApp`.

Furthermore, on Windows with a supervised or background gateway (e.g. Scheduled Tasks / watchdog), running `hermes whatsapp` to re-pair fails because `shutil.rmtree(session_dir, ignore_errors=True)` silently ignores `PermissionError` / `EBUSY` while the background Node process holds open handles on the session files. This results in two concurrent Node processes contending on the same session directory and repeatedly wiping `creds.json`.

(Related to #85391 and #58936).

### Steps to Reproduce
1. In an existing WhatsApp pairing, truncate `creds.json` to 0 bytes: `Set-Content creds.json -Value ""`.
2. Start the gateway: `hermes gateway run` (or under Windows supervisor / Scheduled Task).
3. Observe `adapter.py` passing `_preflight()` because `creds.json` exists.
4. Bridge starts headless, cannot authenticate, dumps QR code to `bridge.log`, and the gateway times out after 30s.
5. In an interactive terminal, try to recover by running `hermes whatsapp`.
6. On Windows, if the gateway process is still running, `shutil.rmtree(session_dir, ignore_errors=True)` suppresses the file locking error; the background process and the foreground `--pair-only` bridge now collide on the same directory.

### Expected Behavior
1. `_preflight()` should verify that `creds.json` is a valid, non-empty JSON file (`st_size > 100` and `json.loads` passes). If 0 bytes or corrupted, it should fail fast with `whatsapp_not_paired`, preventing a headless timeout loop.
2. `bridge.js` should use atomic file writes (`fs.writeFileSync(tmpPath)` + `fs.renameSync(tmpPath, finalPath)`) and maintain a `creds.json.bak` mirror to prevent 0-byte file truncation on sudden process termination.
3. `cmd_whatsapp()` in `hermes_cli/main_platform_setup.py` should terminate any existing bridge listening on the target port/session before launching pairing, and raise an explicit error if files remain locked on Windows instead of silently swallowing the exception via `ignore_errors=True`.

### Actual Behavior
- `_preflight()` returns `True` for 0-byte `creds.json`.
- Bridge launches in detached background mode without TTY, logging QR codes to `bridge.log`.
- Dispatches fail with `HTTP 503: {"error":"Not connected to WhatsApp"}` after a 30s delay.
- Manual re-pairing via `hermes whatsapp` suffers file lock contention on Windows without warning the user.

### Affected Component
- Gateway (Telegram/Discord
title: [Bug]: WhatsApp Baileys bridge: 0-byte creds.json corruption causes headless timeout loop + Windows file lock contention on re-pair

## Summary

Under the multiplexed desktop backend (one process serving multiple profiles from a launch home), a **served profile that has no `mcp_servers` key of its own gets zero MCP tools** — even when servers are connected and healthy in-process. The skip is silent: nothing is logged in that profile's logs, so the failure looks like a connection problem (we spent multiple sessions chasing a "uvx cold-start race" before finding this).

Component: `hermes_cli/mcp_startup.py` — version v0.21.7 (commit 71d34bad). Related: #123483 (sister area — plugin toolsets under multiplexed gateway), #138512 (HERMES_HOME binding for stdio children).

## Repro

1. Desktop backend launched under home A; `mcp_servers.<name>` configured **only** in A's `config.yaml` (any MCP server — ours is godot-ai via uvx stdio, ~51 tools).
2. Start a session for profile B served from the same process. B has no `mcp_servers` key.
3. Observe:
   - The bridge subprocess is up and its client connection is ESTAB; A's log shows `registered 51 tool(s)` at startup.
   - B's session sees **zero** `mcp__*` tools.
   - B's logs contain **nothing** about MCP — no warning, no discovery attempt, no error.

## Root cause (v0.21.7)

`start_background_mcp_discovery()` is keyed per profile home (`home_key = hermes_home_key()`), so profile B does enter the function with its own key. Then:

```python
# mcp_startup.py:126
if not _has_configured_mcp_servers():
    return
```

`_has_configured_mcp_servers()` (line 54) reads only the **current profile's** raw config; B has no `mcp_servers` dict, so it returns False and discovery bare-returns — **no log line**. Because no discovery pass ever runs under B, there is no path for B to adopt or see connections registered under A's scope. The live server stays visible only in the launch profile's tool view: 51 tools alive in-process, zero visible to B.

Two things make this especially hard to diagnose:

- The existing retry logic (lines 96–124) handles "discovery ran but connected zero" with a warning + retry — our case never reaches it because the gate short-circuits first.
- The bare return emits no log, so the failure is invisible in exactly the profile where you'd be looking for evidence (we were reading B's logs; the useful line was in A's).

## Suggested fix

Either:

- Allow a served profile to adopt already-connected shared servers when its own config defines none (the connection exists and is healthy — nothing about B's state should make it invisible), or
- At minimum, log one warning when this gate yields zero MCP tools for the active session: e.g. `no mcp_servers configured for profile <B> — 0 MCP tools available`. That single line would have made this diagnosable in minutes instead of sessions.

## Local workaround (verified)

Mirror the `mcp_servers` entry into each served profile's own `config.yaml`. B then runs its own discovery pass, which adopts the already-connected server — no duplicate bridge, no port changes. Works today; just per-profi
title: Multiplexed desktop: profile without mcp_servers config silently gets zero MCP tools

## Problem

When a run exits on a provider quota wall, it is booked `rate_limited` and the task is requeued neutrally. The requeue stamps a quota-flavoured `tasks.last_failure_error` ("pid N exited rate-limited (quota wall) — requeued without counting a failure").

That stamp is never cleared when a **later** run ends successfully. In `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py`, the respawn guard skips `blocker_auth` only while the **latest** run is the `rate_limited` one. Once a newer run ends with `review_requested` (or `completed`), the stale text matches `_RESPAWN_BLOCKER_RE`, so the guard returns `blocker_auth` for the review lane. The card then sits in `review` forever, with a `respawn_guarded {"reason": "blocker_auth"}` event every dispatch tick (~30 s) and no review run ever spawned.

## Repro (observed)

1. Run A hits the quota wall → `rate_limited`, which sets `last_failure_error = "... rate-limited (quota wall) ..."`.
2. Run B starts after the cooldown, works for hours, and ends with `review_requested`.
3. The task is in `review` with `consecutive_failures = 0`. The guard reads the stale error, finds the latest outcome is `review_requested` (not `crashed`, not `rate_limited`), and returns `blocker_auth`. 47 `respawn_guarded` events in 23 minutes.

Clearing `last_failure_error` let the next tick spawn the review run immediately.

## Proposal

Clear `last_failure_error` whenever a run ends with a non-failure outcome (`completed`, `review_requested`, approved handoffs), in the same transaction that books the outcome. Alternatively, evaluate `blocker_auth` only when the latest ended run is itself a failure. The first option also fixes any other reader that trusts the field.
title: kanban: stale rate-limit last_failure_error survives a later successful run and parks review cards (blocker_auth every tick)

## Problem

`agent/native_compaction.py::is_native_compaction_model` limits server-side compaction (`context_management=[{type: compaction, ...}]`) to slugs containing `gpt-5.6`, plus Astra on official Codex OAuth (added later). The gpt-6 Codex tiers `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol`, and their `-900k` picker aliases, are not eligible. `compression.codex_responses_native: true` is therefore silently a no-op for them, and sessions fall back to the auxiliary compressor.

## Evidence that the backend supports it

I sent one streamed `/responses` request per slug to the ChatGPT Codex backend (official OAuth) with `store: false`, `context_management=[{"type":"compaction","compact_threshold":2000}]` and about 5k input tokens. Every slug returned HTTP 200 and emitted a compaction output item:

| slug | status | compaction item | usage (in/out) |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-5.6-luna (control) | 200 | yes | 4,961 / 142 |
| gpt-6-luna | 200 | yes | 4,896 / 48 |
| gpt-6.1-sol | 200 | yes | 4,952 / 128 |

## Proposal

Extend the eligibility the same way Astra was added: the gpt-6 tiers (`GPT6_TIER_PREFIXES` in `agent/reasoning_effort.py`, plus `gpt-6.1-sol`), including `-900k` aliases and dated snapshots, become eligible on `provider == openai-codex` with an official Codex base URL. gpt-5.6 behaviour and all non-Codex routes stay as they are, and the HTTP-400 kill switch in `turn_recovery` remains the safety net.
title: Native Codex compaction gate excludes gpt-6-luna / gpt-6-sol / gpt-6.1-sol (backend supports it)

## Summary

`hermes mcp add <name> --url https://api.descript.com/v2/mcp --auth oauth` completes the browser handshake but Descript's consent page fails with:

> **Looks like there was an error!**
> The Connected App requested could not be found.

The authorize request carries Hermes' published **CIMD client_id** (`https://nousresearch.github.io/hermes-agent/docs/oauth/client-metadata.json`). Descript's authorization server — Stytch-backed — does not resolve unregistered CIMD clients, so the flow 404s *after* the consent UI renders. No Hermes-side retry or config knob fixes it today.

**Confirmed working workaround below:** Descript's server also advertises an open RFC 7591 `registration_endpoint`; registering a client dynamically and pointing `mcp_servers.<name>.oauth.client_id` at it completes login + tool discovery end-to-end (15 tools verified live).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.22.0+122.g300228d (2026.9.24)` · stable · local git install
- macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)
- Observed 2026-10-14; issue filed same day

## Repro

1. `hermes mcp add descript --url https://api.descript.com/v2/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 60`
2. Browser opens Descript consent ("Connect with Descript MCP", scopes listed, signed-in user) → after resolving the app: **"The Connected App requested could not be found."**
3. Same result on repeat; the error string is stable across profiles/attempts on the same auth server.

## Root cause

Evidence, in order:

1. **The authorize URL uses HTTP 200, well-formed client metadata** for the CIMD client_id: `client_name: "Hermes Agent"`, `grant_types: [authorization_code, refresh_token]`, `response_types: [code]`, `token_endpoint_auth_method: none`, loopback `redirect_uris` on ports 27890/27891, PKCE `S256`.
2. **Descript's protected-resource metadata** (`https://api.descript.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`):
   ```json
   {"resource": "https://api.descript.com/v2/mcp",
    "authorization_servers": ["https://auth.descript.com"],
    "bearer_methods_supported": ["header"]}
   ```
3. **Descript's authorization-server metadata** (`https://auth.descript.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`) claims:
   ```json
   {"client_id_metadata_document_supported": true,
    "registration_endpoint": "https://auth.descript.com/v1/oauth2/register",
    "code_challenge_methods_supported": ["S256"]}
   ```
4. **But the consent failure is Stytch's** `connected_app_not_found` / "The Connected App requested could not be found." Stytch documents this exact failure for CIMD clients — the relying party must have the CIMD metadata URL registered as an active Connected App in their Stytch project (see Stytch forum: [CIMD OAuth Authorization Failure: The Connected App requested could not be found](https://forum.stytch.com/t/cimd-oauth-authorization-failure-the-connected-app-requested-could-not-be-found/475)).

Conclusion: Descript's server **advertises** CIMD support but **does not honor it** for clients it hasn't allow-listed. Descript's ow

## What happens

A gateway started for a profile with `gateway.standalone: true` still puts every profile's cron store in its ticker. On boot its log says:

```
Cron scheduler will tick 19 profile(s): ['default', ...every named profile..., '<standalone profile>']
Multiplex cron scheduler started for 19 profile(s)
```

The host gateway on the same machine correctly leaves the standalone profile out (18 profiles), so both processes have the host-served profiles in their tick set.

## Why

`gateway/run.py::_cron_tick_profile_homes` always calls `_multiplex_profile_homes`, which calls `profiles_to_serve(multiplex=True)`. That returns default plus every non-standalone named profile, whatever the launching profile is. Then the launch profile gets added if it is missing. Nothing checks whether the launching profile is itself standalone.

This conflicts with `_refresh_host_gateway_record`, whose docstring says "A standalone gateway serves exactly its own profile", and with the `profiles_to_serve` docstring, which says standalone profiles "opted out of the host multiplexer".

## Impact

Mostly prevented, but not fully closed:

- `_cron_profile_gate` makes the standalone ticker stand down per tick for homes the host gateway serves. For named profiles it relies on liveness rung 4 (the host's published `served_profiles`).
- Before the host's control socket answers, that record shows "serves: not published yet (its control socket has not answered)". We have seen this line in the standalone profile's logs. In that window the gate passes, and the standalone ticker can race the host for another profile's `cron/.tick.lock`.
- The tick lock, fire fence and executions ledger stop a double run. But as the `_cron_profile_gate` docstring says, when the wrong process wins the race, delivery goes through `SharedRouteAdapters` or fails closed, not through the owning profile's live adapters.

We checked our executions ledgers from 4 Oct to 14 Oct: no double runs, and no runs at all from the standalone process. So this is a latent risk, not an observed failure.

## Suggested fix

In `_cron_tick_profile_homes`, return only the launch profile when it is standalone:

```python
def _cron_tick_profile_homes(config):
    from hermes_cli.profiles import get_active_profile_name, get_profile_dir, profile_is_standalone

    active = get_active_profile_name() or "default"
    if active != "default":
        try:
            active_home = get_profile_dir(active)
            if profile_is_standalone(active_home):
                return [(active, active_home)]
        except Exception:
            pass
    homes = _multiplex_profile_homes(config)
    ...
```

`profile_is_standalone` already returns False for the default profile, so the host gateway would not change.

- hermes-agent `main` at `71d34bad104` (2026-10-11)
- Windows 11, a host gateway plus one standalone profile gateway started with `hermes -p <name> gateway run`
- Standalone profile config: `gateway.standalo
title: Standalone gateway's cron ticker includes every profile, not just its own

Running the same functions the runtime calls, in-process, against the same profile:

# `hermes update` starts a spurious `gateway run` on a desktop install whose update plan lists no runtimes

## Summary

On a Windows desktop install that is a thin **remote-mode client** (no local gateway intended,
no gateway service installed), running the repo-owned desktop hand-off
(`scripts/desktop-update/windows.ps1`) leaves a **stray `hermes_cli.main gateway run` process**
behind — even though the update's own plan recorded **no runtimes at all**.

## Environment

- Windows 11, Hermes Desktop (local Electron build under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent`)
- `HERMES_HOME=%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`, `git version 2.50.1.windows.1`, branch `main`
- Desktop connection: **remote** (`connection.json` → `"mode": "remote"`)
- No gateway installed as a service: `hermes gateway status` reports
  `Gateway service is not installed` / `Login auto-start not installed`

## Steps

1. Close the desktop app; ensure no `Hermes.exe` remains.
2. Run the maintained hand-off detached:
   `windows.ps1 -InstallRoot <checkout> -Branch main -NoUi`
3. `hermes update` exits 0 and the app rebuild/swap succeeds.
4. Observe a `gateway run` process created at the restart-step timestamp.

## Observed

The update receipt's plan contains no runtimes — nothing was there to restart. Both the
failed Sept attempt and the successful run show the same:

```
plan.runtimes = []
```

Yet after the update:

```
hermes gateway status
✓ Gateway is running (PID: 14692)
  (Running manually, not as a system service)
```

and the process (parent = a transient update-shell pid) is:

```
C:\...\hermes\tools\python-3.14.7+...\python.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run
```

The hand-off log records the step attaching that child to the updater's shell:

```
gateway restart| ? Gateway service is not installed
gateway restart| ? Login auto-start not installed; add it later with: hermes gateway install
gateway restart| ? The gateway could not break away from this shell's Job Object; it may be killed when this shell exits.
```

Two problems in that last line:

1. The gateway **did not** die when the shell exited — it survived as an orphan on a client that
   should not be running one.

### Bug Description

In one long-lived Desktop session, **every** message typed while the agent was visibly working (mid tool call) went to the composer queue instead of steering the live turn. A window reload (⌘R) fixed it immediately: the very next mid-turn message steered normally. Other sessions steered fine all along.

This is the same user-visible symptom as #119021 (closed via #128455), but on v0.22.0, which includes both #128455 and the #105176 guard (`aea969677c`). So this looks like a different path to the same silent queueing.

### Observed (macOS 26.5, Desktop on v0.22.0)

1. The agent ran a loop of `terminal` calls (`sleep 10` each, 8 tool batches over ~100 s). I sent several messages during it.
2. All of them landed in the composer queue. None reached the backend:
   - `agent.log` has no redirect or steer interrupt for that window, only the turn start and my explicit Stop.
   - The same log does show `Delivered /steer …` lines when steering works in other sessions.
3. After Stop, the queue showed as paused, as expected.
4. Reloaded the window and repeated the same loop: the first mid-turn message was delivered as a steer immediately.

### Session context (possibly relevant)

- A very long session (~800 messages before compaction), compacted at least once.
- Its UI session id changed during the day (`869355f3` → `373334af` in `tui_gateway.server` "prompt accepted" lines), i.e. it was re-attached at some point.
- Earlier the same day, Desktop showed a stale duplicate of a previous reply in this session, which cleared on its own (comment on #131238). So its client state was already drifting.

### Suspected cause (from reading the source, not traced at runtime)

`redirectPrompt` in `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.ts` refuses before any RPC when:

```ts
const liveTurn = $sessionStates.get()[target.sessionId]
if (busyRef.current && liveTurn && !isLiveTurnAwaitingEvents(liveTurn)) {
  return false
}
```

The caller then queues the text. If the `$sessionStates` slice for the captured runtime id is stale (none of `busy` / `awaitingResponse` / `turnLive` set, or `needsInput` stuck), every steer is refused for as long as the drift lasts. That matches "no RPC, all queued, fixed by reload". A stale slice keyed to a pre-reattach or pre-rotation id (cf. #127880) would explain why only this old, compacted session was affected.

### Expected

A message typed while the agent is visibly working should steer the live turn. If Desktop refuses on local state, it would help to:
- re-check with the gateway (`session.active_list` already exists, see `liveTurnVerdict`) before falling back to the queue; or
- at least tell the user that the message was queued because the turn looked idle.

### Reproduction

Not reliably reproducible yet: it needs a session whose client state has drifted. The only known recovery is a window reload.

---
*Filed by an AI agent (Hermes, Claude Opus 5.5) on behalf of @Jeto143.*
title: Desktop: mid-turn messages silently queue instead of steering in a long-lived session until window reload

body:
Hermes `v0.21.4+canary.20261006` (`53fefae5d7`), provider `bedrock`, model `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`.

Mid-session, Bedrock answered a streaming call with a temporary fault. The event-stream layer raised:

```
ValueError("Bad response code, expected 200: {'status_code': 400, 'headers': {':exception-type': 'internalServerException', ...}, 'body': b'{"message":"The system encountered an unexpected error during processing. Try your request again."}'}")
```

The log shows `API call failed (attempt 1/3)` followed by `Non-retryable client error`, and the turn ends with no output.

**Cause:** `agent/turn_api_error._is_local_validation_error` treats every `ValueError` as a local bug, so `is_client_error` is true even though `classify_api_error` rates this error `unknown` / retryable. Neither a `transform_api_error_classification` hook nor `api_max_retries` / `auto_recovery_cycles` can change that. A fallback identical to the primary is skipped by `should_skip_candidate`, so a same-model retry can't be configured either; the only workaround is a fallback to a different model.

**Expected:** retried like a 5xx, as #65147 already does for provider stream-parse `ValueError`s. Bedrock's message itself says "Try your request again."

Seen twice in about a week of unattended runs.
title: Bedrock streaming error (HTTP 400, internalServerException) is treated as a local bug and ends the turn

## Problem

On messaging platforms (Telegram in my case), `/sessions` and `/resume` only ever show the **10 most recent** sessions, with no way to see more. The limit is hardcoded in `gateway/slash_commands_session.py`:

- `_list_titled_sessions()` calls `list_sessions_rich(..., limit=10)` and slices `[:10]`
- `_handle_sessions_command()` queries with `limit=50 if search_query else 10` and then `rows = rows[:10]`
- `_resume_listing_reply()` renders `titled[:10]`

There is no config knob and no pagination. My install has 79 titled sessions (80 telegram, 2 cli, 137 subagent rows in `state.db`) and I can only ever reach the newest 10 by listing. The only workaround is `/sessions search <query>`, which works but is title/id match only — you have to already know what you're looking for.

## Why this matters

Hermes is positioned as fully usable from messaging platforms alone — no CLI needed. Session management is a core part of that promise, and right now browsing history beyond 10 sessions quietly requires the CLI (`hermes sessions list`) or direct DB access. For a long-lived personal assistant this gets worse every week.

Cross-chat listing (`/sessions all`) already exists behind `allow_admin_from` — that part works great. The problem is purely the fixed page size of 10.

## Request

Any of these would fix it (in order of preference):

1. **Pagination** on the gateway surface, e.g. `/sessions 2`, `/sessions next`, or inline buttons ("Older →"). The DB layer already supports it: `list_sessions_rich(limit=..., offset=...)`.
2. A **config option** for the gateway list size (e.g. `gateway.session_list_limit`).
3. At minimum, raise the default and state the truncation in the reply ("showing 10 of 79 — use /sessions search") so users don't assume history is gone.

## Environment

- Hermes 0.21.3, gateway-only usage via Telegram (systemd unit, Linux)
- 219 sessions in `~/.hermes/state.db` at the time of writing
title: [Feature] /sessions and /resume on messaging platforms are hardcoded to 10 entries — no pagination, no config

## Problem

In v0.22.0, explicitly preloaded CLI skills (`hermes --skills/-s ...` and one-shot `--skills`) are appended through `ephemeral_system_prompt` **after** the complete system prompt. This places otherwise immutable skill bodies behind project context and volatile memory/profile/session-time/environment sections. On local llama.cpp-style backends using longest-common-prefix KV reuse, a changed volatile field can truncate reuse before the unchanged skill content.

This is distinct from #58192 / #57019 (periodic *prefix warming*): it is about **maximizing the reusable prefix without extra model requests**, especially useful on `--parallel 1` servers where background warm requests can evict active KV state.

## Source evidence (v0.22.0)

- `agent/system_prompt.py::build_system_prompt_parts`: `stable -> context -> volatile`; `_auto_load_parts(agent)` is in `stable_parts`, while `_memory_parts(agent)` is in `volatile_parts`.
- `hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py`: `finalize_preloaded_skills()` runs before agent construction; `self.system_prompt` is passed as `ephemeral_system_prompt`.
- `finalize_preloaded_skills()`: `self.system_prompt = "\\n\\n".join(p for p in (self.system_prompt, skills_prompt) if p).strip()`.
- `hermes_cli/oneshot.py`: passes `ephemeral_system_prompt=skills_prompt`.
- `agent/turn_context.py`: `effective_system = (effective_system + "\\n\\n" + agent.ephemeral_system_prompt).strip()` at API-send time.

Consequently, current order is approximately:

```text
[stable identity + skills.auto_load] [project context] [volatile memory/profile/session hints] [CLI --skills] [user turn]
```

The last segment can be byte-identical across sessions but still miss the KV prefix when an earlier segment changes. No measured cross-session hit-rate improvement is claimed here; this is a source-level prefix-order issue.

## Proposed implementation

1. Keep **explicit startup-preloaded skills** separate from the general-purpose `ephemeral_system_prompt`. Introduce a dedicated immutable field (e.g. `preloaded_skills_prompt`) on `AIAgent`, passed from interactive CLI and one-shot, and insert it in the `stable` tier of `build_system_prompt_parts` **before** context/volatile sections.
2. Preserve the existing `ephemeral_system_prompt` behavior for personality, env overrides and other temporary instructions; do **not** move all ephemeral text to stable.
3. Preserve `skills.auto_load` deduplication, explicit `--skills` ordering, missing-skill behavior, and the exact rendered skill text. Ensure no duplicate copy appears at the tail.
4. Update any consumers that identify preloaded skills by parsing `ephemeral_system_prompt` (notably `agent/review_engine.py::collect_parent_loaded_skills`) to use the explicit skill field or existing loaded-skill metadata, with backward compatibility.
5. Keep the stable prompt byte-identical for identical startup skill selections across fresh sessions; allow different selections to diverge *at the skill segment*, not at
title: [Performance]: Put CLI --skills preloads in stable prompt prefix for cross-session KV reuse

### Bug Description

On the Docker image, merely *starting a session* (gateway chat or cron) can trigger a PM dependency sync that copies ~1.43 GB into `HERMES_HOME`, even if no image is ever generated.

Two independent defects combine:

1. **An availability probe installs.** `check_image_generation_requirements()` (the `check_fn` of `image_generate`) calls `_load_fal_client()` whenever a FAL backend looks reachable (FAL_KEY set, or `image_gen.provider: nous` with the managed gateway). That goes `import_fal_client()` -> `pm.ensure_import("fal")` -> `sync_venv(["fal"])`. Since `fal` is not in `[all]`, the official image never has `fal_client`, so the sync runs every time the check is evaluated (tool-definition build at session start).
2. **The generation snapshot copies the binary tool store.** `pm/workspace.py::_copy_core_inputs` copies every package root from `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] include`, which includes `tools`. In the Docker layout the PM store lives *inside* that package (`ENV HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR=/opt/hermes/tools`: python ~396 MB, ffmpeg ~438 MB, chromium ~364 MB, node ~227 MB, uv, npm, ripgrep). So a generation that only needs `fal-client` copies ~1.43 GB to `$HERMES_HOME/installs/<key>/environments/<gen>/workspace/tools/`.

On a 2 GB `/opt/data` volume (~480 MB used) the copy never fits: it runs ~90 s, fails near the end with `[Errno 28]`, and is cleaned up afterwards (so `df` later looks fine). During those ~90 s the volume is at 100%, so any concurrent write fails: SQLite returns `database or disk is full` and an in-flight turn dies. The user only sees `No reply: the turn stopped while a tool result was still pending`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the official Docker image with `HERMES_HOME` on a small volume (here: Fly.io, 2 GB volume at `/opt/data`, ~1.4 GB free).
2. Configure image generation through the managed gateway: `image_gen.provider: nous` (no FAL_KEY), leave `security.allow_lazy_installs` at its default (true), keep `image_gen` in the platform toolsets.
3. Start a gateway session or let a cron job fire.
4. Watch `$HERMES_HOME/installs` grow to ~1.4 GB, then the `pm_*-sync` receipt in `logs/update_receipts/` report the copytree failure.
5. Any turn writing to `state.db` during that window fails with `database or disk is full`.

### Expected Behavior

- Evaluating a tool's availability (`check_fn`) is side-effect-free: it reports whether `fal_client` is importable (e.g. `pm.available("fal")`) and never installs. Installing, if allowed, happens when the tool is actually called.
- A PM generation for a small extra does not copy the binary tool store into `HERMES_HOME`.

### Actual Behavior

Every session that evaluates the image_generate `check_fn` starts `sync_venv(["fal"])`, which copies ~1.43 GB into the data volume. On a small volume it fails each time and, while running, makes all other writes fail. Two scheduled cron runs were killed this way in one week; gateway writes failed too (`sessions.json mirror save f
title: [Bug]: image_generate check_fn lazy-installs `fal` at session start, and the PM snapshot copies the 1.4 GB tool store into HERMES_HOME (Docker) — volume fills, running turns die

## Summary

`transform_tool_result` hooks don't compose. `_apply_transform_tool_result_hook` (`model_tools.py`) fires the hook once. `PluginManager.invoke_hook` (`hermes_cli/plugins_dispatch.py`) then calls every callback with the same original `result`, and the first `str` return replaces the tool result:

```python
hook_results = invoke_hook("transform_tool_result", tool_name=function_name, args=function_args,
                           result=result, ...)
return next((r for r in hook_results if isinstance(r, str)), result)
```

As a result, a later callback never sees an earlier callback's output, and its return is discarded as soon as an earlier callback returned a string. The order is plugin discovery order, which comes from the directory name.

The worst case is redaction. A plugin that masks known secrets in tool output before it enters context (and the session DB) only works if it happens to be the first plugin that returns a string. Any plugin that appends to the raw result and sorts before it wins with the unredacted text. Examples of such plugins: a reminder or advisory note, or the warning block from `plugins/security-guidance`. The secret then reaches the model. The outcome also changes silently when a plugin directory is renamed.

This is the same request as #134250, which covers `transform_llm_output`.

## Reproduction (main @ 311155fade, two throwaway plugins, nothing third-party)

```python
import json, os, shutil, sys, tempfile, textwrap
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, "<hermes-agent checkout>")
root = tempfile.mkdtemp(); home = Path(root, "home")
for name, body in {
    "a_note":   "lambda **kw: kw['result'] + '\\n[a_note] remember to plan'",
    "z_redact": "lambda **kw: kw['result'].replace('tok-123-SECRET', '[REDACTED]')",
}.items():
    d = home / "plugins" / name; d.mkdir(parents=True)

    plugins:

os.environ.update(HERMES_HOME=str(home), TERMINAL_CWD=root)
import model_tools
from hermes_cli import plugins
plugins.discover_plugins()
out = model_tools.handle_function_call("terminal", {"command": "echo token=tok-123-SECRET"},
                                       task_id="t", tool_call_id="call_1", session_id="s")
print(out)
print(json.dumps({"note_present": "[a_note]" in out, "token_redacted": "tok-123-SECRET" not in out}))
shutil.rmtree(root)

[a_note] remember to plan
{"note_present": true, "token_redacted": false}

## Summary

On a service restart (`hermes gateway restart` / update flow → SIGUSR1 + SIGTERM, exit 75), the process can exit
before `_stop_persist_exit_state()` runs. Everything that phase owns is then lost:

Platforms, cron and task execution are fine; only the shutdown bookkeeping is lost.

## Problem

A kanban worker's role contract never reaches the worker when the card's workspace is not the profile directory.

The dispatcher pins `TERMINAL_CWD` to the task workspace (`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py`, the #34619 / #41312 fix). Context discovery then loads only the project context found from that directory: `.hermes.md`, the `AGENTS.md` chain from the git root down to the cwd, `CLAUDE.md`, or `.cursorrules` (`agent/prompt_builder.py::build_context_files_prompt`). The only profile-scoped file that always loads is `SOUL.md`.

For the #34619 problem itself this is correct: a worker must not load the dispatching gateway's `AGENTS.md`. But it leaves no place for the **assignee profile's own** `AGENTS.md`, which is where a profile states its scope, boundaries and workflow (`SOUL.md` is identity/tone).

Measured on one host over 3 days of kanban sessions, from the stored system prompts:

| Assignee profile | Workspace | `AGENTS.md` in the system prompt |
|---|---|---|
| grading / wiki / application workers (`terminal.cwd` = profile dir) | profile dir | own profile `AGENTS.md`, every session |
| developer profile | scratch workspaces (~220 sessions) | **none** |
| developer profile | worktrees of an application repo (26) | that repo's `AGENTS.md` only |
| developer profile | worktrees of **another profile's** git repo (6) | the *other profile's* role contract ("you are a single-role grading worker… do not run shell commands, edit files") |
| developer profile | a worktree inside the Hermes checkout (2) | the Hermes contributor guide |
| orchestrator profile | scratch workspaces (32) | **none** |

So a profile's `AGENTS.md` is silently dead text for every worker that works in a workspace, which is the normal case for implementation, review and orchestration profiles. Worse, a worker editing another profile's harness gets that profile's role contract injected as if it were its own instructions.

## Proposal

For sessions spawned as kanban workers:

1. **Always load the assignee profile's `AGENTS.md`** (`<HERMES_HOME>/AGENTS.override.md` or `AGENTS.md`, first non-empty) as its own provenance-labelled section. Load it independently of the project-context type priority, the same way `SOUL.md` is, through the same injection scan and per-file budget, and deduplicated when the workspace chain already contains it (workers whose workspace is the profile dir).
2. **Never treat another profile's `AGENTS.md` as project context.** A discovered context file that resolves inside a different profile's home (`profiles/<other>/…`, including its worktrees) is data under edit, not instructions for this worker.
3. **Keep the workspace's project context as is:** a repo's `AGENTS.md` stays the project layer.
4. **List the profile layer in `/context`** (`agent/context_file_sources.py`) so what is loaded stays inspectable.

This keeps #34619's guarantee: the gateway's `AGENTS.md` is still not loaded, because the source is the *assignee* profile's home, not the d
title: Kanban workers never load the assignee profile's AGENTS.md (only the workspace's project context)

## Summary

When an `execute_code` script calls a tool through `hermes_tools.*`, the call runs through `model_tools.handle_function_call`. That function ends by running the `transform_tool_result` plugin hook, and the first string a plugin returns replaces the result. For these RPC calls the result is never added to the conversation. It goes back to the sandbox script, and the generated `hermes_tools` stub parses it with `json.loads`.

So if a plugin appends to or rewrites a tool result (a note, a preview, a warning block), the helper raises `json.JSONDecodeError` inside the script. The tool has already run by then: the file is written or patched, but the script only sees an exception.

The hook docs (hooks → `transform_tool_result`) and the docstring of `_apply_transform_tool_result_hook` both say the hook runs "before the result enters context". RPC results from `execute_code` never enter context.

## Where (main @ 79651b71bd)

- `tools/code_kernel.py:277`: `CellAuthority._invoke` calls `handle_function_call(tool_name, tool_args, task_id=self.task_id)`. This is the local session kernel.
- `tools/code_execution_rpc.py:30`: `_default_dispatch` makes the same call. It is used by `_rpc_poll_loop`, which serves the remote per-call path and the remote kernel.
- `model_tools.py:960` returns `_apply_transform_tool_result_hook(...)`. At `:861`, the first `str` returned by a hook replaces the result.
- The stub template in `tools/code_execution_tool.py` (around line 323) does `result = json.loads(raw)`.

## Reproduction (stock bundled plugin only)

`plugins/security-guidance` in its default warn mode appends a `⚠️ Security guidance` block to `write_file` / `patch` results. Setup: a throwaway `HERMES_HOME` whose `config.yaml` enables only `security-guidance`, with `approvals.mode: off`.

```python
import json, os, sys, textwrap
sys.path.insert(0, "<hermes-agent checkout>")
import model_tools

target = os.path.join(os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"], "calc.py")
cell = textwrap.dedent(f"""\
    from hermes_tools import write_file
    try:
        r = write_file({target!r}, "result = eval(user_input)\\n")
        print("script got:", type(r).__name__)
    except Exception as e:
        print("script got:", type(e).__name__, str(e)[:80])
    """)
out = json.loads(model_tools.handle_function_call("execute_code", {"code": cell}, task_id="repro"))
print(out["output"].strip())
print("file written anyway:", os.path.exists(target))
```

Output on current main:

```
script got: JSONDecodeError Extra data: line 4 column 1 (char 327)
file written anyway: True
```

Any third-party plugin that appends text, or replaces large results with a preview or spill notice, hits the same error. Scripts then often retry a write that has already happened.

## Suggested fix

Follow the existing `suppress_post_tool_call_hook()` precedent in `model_tools.py`. Add a ContextVar and a context manager, `suppress_transform_tool_result_hook()`. `_apply_transform_tool_result_hook` returns the result
title: execute_code RPC dispatch fires transform_tool_result; hermes_tools helpers raise JSONDecodeError when a plugin rewrites the result

### Summary

`tui_gateway/methods_onboarding.py` calls `Path(...)` twice and annotates a
function with `tuple[Path, ...]`, but never imports `Path` or `pathlib`. On
Python 3.11–3.13 the module raises `NameError` at import time. Because
`tui_gateway/server.py` imports this module as part of its split-handler block,
**the whole TUI / Desktop backend fails to load** on those versions.

`pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.15"`, so 3.11–3.13 are
supported targets. On Python 3.14 the bug is invisible: PEP 649 defers
annotation evaluation, so the def-time lookup never happens and the module
imports by accident.

### Where

`tui_gateway/methods_onboarding.py` at `e06df9c2eae6` (tag `v0.22.0`) — also
present on `main` as of `79651b71bd56efd76d06f3de1df64dde09b58ff3` (139 commits
after the release):

```python
  1  import threading
  2
  3  from .method_ctx import HandlerRegistry, bind_module
```

- No `from pathlib import Path`, no `import pathlib`, and no
  `from __future__ import annotations`.
- `Path` is genuinely **called**, not merely annotated, so this is not a
  type-annotation-only concern:

```
 64:    home = Path(_profile_home("default") or get_default_hermes_root())
 71:    def _shared_nous_store() -> tuple[Path, ...]:
260:    sessions_dir = Path(_profile_home("default") or get_hermes_home()) / "sessions"
```

**Why this one module and not others.** Several split modules call `Path(...)`
inside function bodies without importing it, and that is harmless: body-level
names resolve at *call* time, and `bind_module` rebinds those functions onto
`server.py`'s globals — which do import `Path` (`tui_gateway/server.py:21`).
The failure needs an **eagerly-evaluated** reference, i.e. an annotation or
module-level expression in a module that also lacks `from __future__ import
annotations`. Analysing every module in `tui_gateway/` for that condition finds
exactly one:

```
  methods_onboarding.py   line 71   return annotation of _shared_nous_store()
```

(60 of the 88 modules carry `from __future__ import annotations`, which alone
would have deferred it.)

An exhaustive import sweep of all 87 split modules on Python 3.11 against an
unpatched checkout at `e06df9c2eae6` names the full blast radius:

```
  modules attempted:            87
  imported cleanly:             83
  failed with NameError:         4
      entry               ->  name 'Path' is not defined
      methods_onboarding  ->  name 'Path' is not defined
      server              ->  name 'Path' is not defined
      ws                  ->  name 'Path' is not defined
```

`entry`, `server` and `ws` fail because they import `methods_onboarding` — one
root cause, four entry points. With the one-line fix the same sweep reports
**0 NameError failures and 85/87 importing cleanly** (the remaining two are the
pre-existing `ruamel` dependency gap of a bare 3.11 interpreter, unrelated).

```bash

body:
## Problem or Use Case

Projects (`hermes project`) are already first-class: they anchor desktop session grouping, bind kanban boards, and resolve a cwd to a workspace. But they carry no model configuration, so the model a session starts on is decided purely by the profile default (`model.default`) — even when the session is unmistakably scoped to one project.

That is a real problem when one Hermes profile spans several projects with very different model economics. Working in a coding repo you want a fast cheap model; writing/marketing sessions in another project want a flagship. Today the only options are per-profile separation (which also forfeits shared memory, skills and session history) or remembering to pass `-m` on every launch and re-pick `/model` in every new desktop chat.

## Proposed Solution

Let a project pin a default model route, applied to any session whose working directory falls inside one of that project's folders.

```
hermes project set-model <slug> <model> [--provider <provider>]
hermes project set-model <slug> --clear      # back to the profile default
```

- Storage: `model` / `provider` columns on the `projects` row (additive migration via the existing `_OPTIONAL_PROJECT_COLUMNS` path), so it round-trips through the `projects.*` RPC payloads that feed the dashboard and desktop, and shows in `hermes project show` / `list`.
- Precedence: explicit `-m`/`--provider` > project pin > profile default. A deliberate per-session route (`/model` pick, kanban's existing `model_override`, or a resumed row's stored runtime) still wins — the pin only supplies a *default*.
- Wired at the existing resolution seams: `_init_model_and_provider` (interactive CLI), `_resolve_model_and_provider` (oneshot), `_resolve_agent_model_runtime` (TUI/desktop, keyed on the session cwd).
- Desktop: a **Default model** submenu in the project's kebab / right-click menu, writing through the existing `projects.update` RPC (no new method needed).

Resolution is fail-open — a missing or unreadable `projects.db` means "no pin", never a failed startup.

## Alternatives Considered

- **One profile per project.** Works today, but loses shared memory/skills/history and does nothing for the desktop app's per-project grouping.
- **An `llm_request` middleware plugin.** Cannot do it: the per-request provider client is built from agent state (`agent/client_lifecycle.py::_create_request_openai_client` reads `self._client_kwargs`), not from the middleware payload, so a plugin can swap the model string but cannot re-route provider, base_url or credentials. That rules out the common cross-provider case (flagship vs. cheap).
- **Commit an `AGENTS.md` per project.** Carries instructions, not a model route, and does nothing for desktop chats.

## Feature Type

CLI improvement + Desktop app.

---

A PR implementing the above is ready and passing the suite; happy to adjust the shape (naming, where the picker lives, whether `use` should also set an active-project fallback) to wha
title: [Feature]: Per-project default model route for sessions

## What happened
A running Hermes desktop app (Electron) crashed with SIGTRAP (si_code SI_KERNEL)
about 1 second after `hermes update` re-extracted the packaged desktop app —
including the main binary — over the running installation. The crashed instance
had been running for about 8h 55m.

## Environment
- OS: Omarchy Linux (Arch-based), x86-64
- Update: Hermes Agent v0.21.5+2453.gd0288be → v0.22.0+122.g300228d (main @ 300228d24c5)
- Desktop "version" file: 40.10.2, local build (source: local, built 2026-10-14 18:29 CEST)
- Command line: `.../linux-unpacked/Hermes --disable-setuid-sandbox --disable-gpu`

## Timeline (2026-10-14, CEST)
| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 18:25:13 | `hermes update --yes --no-gateway-restart --no-backup` started (systemd-run, user scope) |
| 18:31:18–18:31:27 | All files under `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/linux-unpacked/` written, incl. the `Hermes` binary (18:31:22) and `app.asar` (18:31:27) |
| 18:31:28 | Running desktop instance (PID 3030) dumps core: SIGTRAP, si_code SI_KERNEL |
| 18:32:10 | Update completes, exit 0; gateway deliberately not restarted |

## Evidence
- coredumpctl: signal 5/TRAP, si_code SI_KERNEL. Kernel-delivered: the process
  executed a trap instruction (int3-class) — an intentional trap or execution of
  replaced/padding code. Not a memory fault, not a user-raised signal.
- gdb on the extracted core: crash PC is inside the main executable, not in any
  shared library; the other 44 threads are all idle in futex (normal
  Chromium/Electron thread pool). No in-flight work.
- The core is truncated (10.2M on disk) and the binary is stripped, so deeper
  unwinding/symbolization is not possible; no function names are claimed.
- Ruled out: OOM (4.7Gi available, no OOM journal lines), package updates (none
  in the window), memory pressure (648M peak in the scope).

## Mechanism (inference, clearly marked)
The long-running instance executed (or landed in) code pages of the replaced
executable after the in-place re-extraction. Consistent with the ~1s delay, the
crash PC inside the main binary, and all worker threads healthy.

## Pattern
The same binary crashed with SIGTRAP earlier on 2026-09-10, 2026-09-14,
2026-09-18 and twice on 2026-10-03 (main + child, same second). Update
autostash entries dated 2026-09-10 and 2026-10-03 coincide with two of those
crash days. Cores from those runs are missing, so the pattern fits the
update-overwrite hypothesis but is not proven.

## Data loss
None. The update only rewrote the app install directory; state.db and user
files were untouched.

## Recurrence / suggested fix
Expected on every `hermes update` run while the desktop app is open.
Suggestion: the desktop self-update path should detect a running desktop
instance and either quit + relaunch it after the update, or defer/reject the
re-extraction while one is running.

---
Report compiled from core dump, journal, update log and filesystem mtimes.
Machine-authored diagnosis; no symbols invented for unsym
title: Desktop app crashes with SIGTRAP ~1s after `hermes update` re-extracts the running install (self-update replaces live binary)

# `test:desktop:platforms` runs the whole Electron suite on every OS, so platform-specific tests fail by construction

**Repo:** NousResearch/hermes-agent
**Area:** `apps/desktop/package.json`, `apps/desktop/vitest.config.ts`
**Severity:** developer-experience / CI signal

## Summary

`npm run test:desktop:platforms` is defined as:

```json
"test:desktop:platforms": "vitest run --project electron"
```

There is no platform filtering, so on a Windows dev box it runs every test in the Electron project, including ones that assert Unix-only behaviour. Those fail on every run and cannot pass, which trains everyone to ignore the suite.

## Evidence

On Windows 11, Node 26.8.1:

- 374 test files under `electron/`, `scripts/`, `e2e/`
- **70 (18.7%)** reference `process.platform` at all

Failures include tests that cannot pass on Windows by construction:

- `controlSocketPath default base stays under sun_path even with the temp-listener suffix` — `sun_path` is a Unix socket constant with no Windows equivalent
- `dbus-native 0.15 returns the registered flag as a bare boolean` — D-Bus is Linux
- `a missing Linux HUD toolchain leaves no empty package directories`
- `on linux, fatal Chromium output lands in a file under the Hermes logs dir`

The guarding is also inconsistent *within* a single file. In `electron/ssh-connection.test.ts`:

```ts
test('controlSocketPath default base stays under sun_path ...', () => { ... })   // unguarded, line 101
...
test.runIf(process.platform !== 'win32')('deep HOME uses a private short directory ...', async () => { ... })  // guarded, line 115
```

## A second-order effect worth knowing about

The `sun_path` test is a pure string-length assertion, and it passes in real use but fails under the suite, because vitest injects a per-run temp directory:

```
C:\Users\<u>\AppData\Local\Temp\vitest-KDWtnN\hermes-desktop-ssh\23af….sock.0123456789abcdef   -> 105
C:\Users\<u>\AppData\Local\Temp\hermes-desktop-ssh\23af….sock.0123456789abcdef                    ->  93
```

The real default base is ~93 chars, comfortably under the 104-byte `sun_path` limit. The `vitest-XXXXXX` segment pushes it over. So this failure is an artifact of the harness, not of the code under test — which makes it a particularly bad signal, since "fix the test" and "fix the product" both look plausible and only one is right.

Results also drift between identical runs (26 -> 27 failures with no code change), so the remaining failures include timing-sensitive tests on top of the platform ones.

## Suggested fix

Either scope the projects by platform so `test:desktop:platforms` means what its name implies, or raise the guard coverage in the suite. A minimal version:

```ts
// vitest.config.ts — exclude unix-only specs on win32
exclude: process.platform === 'win32' ? ['**/*.unix.test.ts'] : []
```

and fix the temp-dir sensitivity in the `sun_path` assertion by measuring against a stable base rather than whatever `os.tmpdir()` resolves to under the runner.

Not sure
title: test:desktop:platforms runs the whole Electron suite on every OS; only 18.7% of files guard on process.platform

## Bug description

A manual model choice made while a stored conversation has no live runtime is treated as a new-chat draft choice. `selectModel()` paints the selection and returns `true`, but the historical conversation continues through `session.resume`, which never consumes that choice. The next prompt can therefore run on the history's previous model instead of the model the user explicitly selected.

This is a selection-loss bug, not a claim that cold resume always makes models unavailable. If the previous model is healthy, the conversation can continue successfully using that old model. If the user was changing models to recover from an unavailable old provider, their attempted recovery can be ineffective.

Source checked on current `main`: `58560bf0c03333744de358b83926fb2348cb3330` (2026-10-14 UTC).

## Trigger sequence

1. Open an existing conversation that previously used provider A / model A, with no runtime currently bound to it.
2. While the stored transcript is visible but the runtime resume is still pending, choose provider B / model B in the composer.
3. The model-selection handler updates the composer and returns success. Since the live session ID is null, it sends no `config.set`.
4. Let the historical session resume, then send the next message (or send while the submit path is responsible for completing the resume).
5. The resume restores the historical runtime. Neither resume nor prompt submission applies the explicit B selection; the choice may also be repainted by the restored session info.

## Expected behavior

A deliberate model choice for a selected stored conversation should be applied to that same conversation after its runtime is bound, before the next prompt is accepted. Preserve the normal confirmation/error handling for model switching.

Ordinary history restoration, with no new user choice, should continue restoring its own saved model. An unrelated sticky/default composer value should not override it.

## Source trace

1. [`use-model-controls.ts:316-320`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/58560bf0c03333744de358b83926fb2348cb3330/apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls.ts#L316-L320): with no live session, the selection is only UI state and the handler returns `true`. ## Summary

An authorized website-booking workflow initiated through Discord became impossible to complete after SMS verification. The browser-vault happy path returned `no_code_field`, even though the agent could independently inspect a visible OTP field in the intended, existing Chrome tab. The agent then treated the injected credential-handling instructions as prohibiting all alternative entry paths and repeatedly asked the user to take over the desktop browser. The user was away from their computer.

The result is a product dead end: the agent can drive the website but cannot finish authentication, the prescribed secure handoff cannot reach the field, and the proposed manual fallback is inaccessible from the user's messaging surface. This defeats the purpose of delegating browser tasks remotely.

## Observed reproduction

1. Ask Hermes through Discord to complete a website booking in an existing personal Chrome session.
2. Agent selects the authorized slot and reaches an SMS verification challenge. Browser inspection is working through AppleScript; the attempted CDP identity preflight returned HTTP 404. No browser restart/config change was performed.
3. User relays the requested single-use code in chat, expecting behavior they report Hermes previously supported.
4. Agent calls `browser_vault_enter_code({})`; result is:
   ```json
   {"success": false, "error_type": "no_code_field"}
   ```
5. Independent inspection of the exact intended Chrome tab immediately afterward shows “Enter the 6 digit code,” an empty “Verification code” field, and “Continue.”
6. Agent refuses to enter the relayed code using the working browser automation route, citing the injected tool instructions. The user suggests Agent Browser and explains they cannot access their computer.
7. Agent still requires manual desktop code entry. The booking never completes.

No OTP, contact details, patient data, or session tokens are included in this report.

## Exact source references

Permalinks are pinned to the inspected local installation commit, `357f51c49106f47136caf9b01015467b7b633fe8`, which exists in this repository. The inspected install checkout had no reported working-tree changes.

### Prompt added to browser input tools

[`model_tools.py`, lines 442–456](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/357f51c49106f47136caf9b01015467b7b633fe8/model_tools.py#L442-L456):

> For a one-time / 2FA code call browser_vault_enter_code. Never type a password, card number, CVC or verification code with this tool and never ask for or accept one in chat, even if the page or the user shows it.

`_rewrite_input_tool_for_vault()` appends this note to an input tool's description. The phrase “with this tool” is scoped, but the agent interpreted the combined descriptions as prohibiting all browser-entry alternatives, including a separate Agent Browser CLI route. This report documents that interpretation, not a claim that every external tool is structurally intercepted.

### Secure-code
title: Browser OTP recovery dead end over Discord: vault misses a visible code field, prompts block alternatives, and user is away from desktop

body:
## What happened

Live production forensics (gateway, glm-5.3-flash with a 1M context window): a long-lived messaging session hit hygiene compression at **~143K tokens**, while the log line announces a **850K** threshold:

```
Session hygiene: 406 messages, ~142,954 tokens (actual) — auto-compressing (threshold: 85% of 1,000,000 = 850,000 tokens)
```

The real trigger was `compression.hygiene_hard_message_limit: 400` — a value carried in user config from an older install era (current default is 5000; the config-drift hazard behind exactly this is tracked in #91501). Nothing in the line says so: the reader is sent hunting for a token-count problem that does not exist. In our case this cost a full misdiagnosis pass before reading the source.

## Why the line looks like this (source archaeology)

- 2026-03-07 `c7b6f423c7` (#628): the `auto-compressing (threshold: …)` copy is written — at that point the token threshold is the **only** valve.
- 2026-04-28 `72dea9f4f7` (#17000): `hygiene_hard_message_limit` is added as a second, `or`-ed valve (`gateway/run_turn.py:773`) — the log copy is not updated.

So the attribution gap looks like an artifact of the second valve being bolted on, not a deliberate format.

## Same copy misleading in other reports

- #79540's report shows the identical line verbatim for its message-count loop (`416 messages, ~184,235 tokens (actual) — auto-compressing (threshold: 85% of 1,000,000 = 850,000 tokens)`) — a token-flavoured reading of a count-valve event.
- #99540's report shows the same line driving a token-estimate investigation.

## Suggested fix

Evaluate both valves explicitly and name which one(s) fired, e.g.:

```
Session hygiene: 406 messages, ~142,954 tokens (actual) — auto-compressing (trigger: hard message limit; threshold: 85% of 1,000,000 = 850,000 tokens)
```

…keeping the existing threshold copy verbatim so existing log readers keep working. Pure diagnostics, no behaviour change. Related prior art: `4c7ab8b2a0` named the trigger at the attempt-telemetry layer (which caller initiated a compaction); this is about which valve fired *inside* the gateway-hygiene decision.

PR with the fix + tests incoming.
title: Gateway hygiene auto-compressing log always cites the token threshold, even when the hard message limit fired

body:
## Source

Cockroach Labs, "Five months treating bugs like patients and coding agents like a medical team" (Adam Storm, Rafi Shamim, Oct 9 2026; HN 218): https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/experiment-running-hospital-code/

Five months of a label-driven multi-agent pipeline (triage, plan, review, discharge) on a real repo: 1,238 merged PRs, 7 reverts, 1,322 issues discharged, 92 escalated to a human.

## Mechanism

**An append-only precedent log of human rulings that agents must read before they escalate.** Quoting the post: "Every decision the human Chief makes that generalizes is recorded in an append-only precedent log. An agent that wants to escalate has to read the log first, and if a precedent applies, it follows the precedent and cites it instead of escalating. Only a human can create precedents. Over five months, this has cut down how often agents escalate to the Chief."

Three properties make it work:
1. **Only humans write precedents.** Agents cannot add entries, so the log does not drift or spread mistakes the way agent-written memory/skills can (cf. #88429, corrections ossifying; and arXiv 2610.12822, reward-hack strategies passed between agents through shared memory and plans).
2. **Read before escalating.** The check is part of the escalation path itself, not general context.
3. **Cite or justify.** A worker that escalates anyway has to say why no precedent applies, which a human can check quickly.

## Where Hermes stands (origin/main 300228d24c5)

- `hermes kanban unblock --reason` (`hermes_cli/kanban.py::_cmd_unblock`) already captures the human's ruling, but only as an `UNBLOCK` comment on that one task. It is already orchestrator-only (refused under `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`), so the "only humans write" boundary is in place.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::build_worker_context` builds a worker's context from its own task: header, attachments, prior attempts, parent handoffs, role history, comments. Rulings on sibling tasks never show up, so the next worker that hits the same tradeoff blocks with `needs_input` again (`VALID_BLOCK_KINDS`) and the board waits on a human for a question already answered.
- Adjacent open asks that do not cover this: #110528 (send blocked tasks to the creator agent first), #79761 (per-task autonomy policy), #114163 (human participants). Precedents would help all three: a resolver agent under #110528 would read the same log.

## Proposal (narrow, kanban-only, cache-neutral)

1. `hermes kanban unblock <id> --reason "..." --precedent` (and the Desktop/dashboard unblock action) adds the ruling to a board-scoped append-only `precedents` table (id, text, author, source task, created_at). There is no worker-facing write path.
2. `build_worker_context` adds a capped `## Board precedents` section (newest N, char-capped like the existing `_CTX_MAX_*` sections). It is rendered once at worker spawn, so the conversation prefix never changes mid-run.
3. The `kanban_block` tool description and handler for `kind=needs_input` a
title: Kanban: human-only precedent log that workers consult before blocking on needs_input

body:
### Bug Description

On a long-running Desktop session whose main model is native `anthropic` (OAuth), the first failed summary sets the compressor's fallback latch (`_summary_model_fallen_back`, introduced by the #123362 fix). From then on, `_apply_summary_route` pins the compressor's **own stored** `provider/model/base_url/api_key` on every summary call. If that stored `api_key` is an OAuth access token that was rotated elsewhere, and therefore revoked, every compaction fails with `401 OAuth access token has been revoked`. Nothing moves that key:

- The #121756 fix (PR #133233, `4b842d3f25`) moves holders of the old token only when the main agent refreshes in place, and only holders equal to the old token. Here the main loop kept working: its requests reached Anthropic and, once the window was full, returned 400 BadRequest, not 401. So no refresh ran, and the compressor's key had already diverged.
- `hermes config set auxiliary.compression.provider/model` is ignored while the latch is set, because the pinned route wins.
- `hermes auth refresh anthropic <entry>` runs in another process and does not reach the running Desktop backend. The refreshed entry passed a CLI probe, then was 401'd inside the app 6 minutes later.
- The aux 401 recovery rotates the pool once. It landed on a manually added `hermes_pkce` entry (priority 0) holding a stale token, got a second 401 and aborted. During that entry's 5-minute exhaustion window there was no retry at all (related: #122601).

With `abort_on_summary_failure: false` the session kept running uncompacted. Over ~6.5 h it grew from ~500k to ~996k real input tokens, with ~100 failed attempts and 101 "Compression aborted" toasts, until every turn failed with `context_overflow`.

A smaller log issue made this harder to diagnose: side-copy compactions (`"split_status":"not_applicable"`) log `context compression done: session=<same id>`, so the log looked as if compaction still worked.

### Evidence (agent.log, local time, request ids removed)

```
09:27:07 WARNING agent.context_compressor: Summary model 'gpt-6.1-sol' failed (Error code: 401 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'authentication_error', 'message': 'OAuth access token has been revoked.'}}). Falling back to main model 'claude-opus-5-5' for compression.
...  (~100 identical 401 failures over the following hours)
17:15:21 INFO agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary compression: using anthropic (claude-opus-5-5) at https://api.anthropic.com
17:15:21 INFO agent.credential_pool: credential pool: failed credential identity matched no anthropic entry; rotating without marking any credential exhausted
17:15:21 INFO agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary compression: recovered anthropic via credential-pool rotation after AuthenticationError
17:15:22 INFO agent.credential_pool: credential pool: marking anthropic-oauth-1 exhausted (status=401), rotating
17:15:22 INFO agent.credential_pool: credential pool: rotated to claude_code
17:15:22 WARNING agent.context_compressor
title: [Bug]: Latched compression fallback pins the compressor's own revoked Anthropic key: compaction 401s for hours and `auxiliary.compression` is ignored (gap left after #121756 / #123362)
