### Bug Description

`tests/conftest.py::_hermetic_environment` deletes `HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS` before every test (it is listed in `tests/_fixtures/env_filter.py::_HERMES_BEHAVIORAL_VARS`). By then `agent.redact` has already read it: `agent/redact.py:97` evaluates `_REDACT_ENABLED = os.getenv("HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS", "true")...` at import, and test modules import `agent.redact` at collection time, before any fixture runs.

So when pytest is launched from a shell that has redaction off, redaction stays off for the whole run. `security.redact_secrets: false` is bridged to `HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS=false`, so every `hermes chat -q` / kanban-worker shell of such a profile exports it, and the terminal tool's subprocesses (including pytest) inherit it. Four tests that do not pin the flag themselves then fail locally while CI is green:

- `tests/tools/test_file_tools.py::TestSecretFileReadRedaction::test_read_file_of_hermes_config_masks_opaque_token`
- `tests/tools/test_file_tools.py::TestSecretFileReadRedaction::test_search_in_hermes_home_masks_opaque_token`
- `tests/tools/test_approval.py::TestApprovalPromptRedaction::test_callback_receives_redacted_command`
- `tests/tools/test_approval.py::TestApprovalPromptRedaction::test_execute_code_pending_fallback_redacts_script`

The trap is already known in the suite. #99562 pinned the flag in `tests/cron/test_cron_incidents.py` for exactly this reason, and `tests/gateway/test_signal.py` and `tests/gateway/test_standalone_send_redaction.py` carry the same comment. 14 test files pin `agent.redact._REDACT_ENABLED = True` themselves. Every new redaction test has to remember to do it; the four above do not.

### Steps to Reproduce

On `main` @ 0e427d78:

```bash
env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" LANG=C.UTF-8 HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS=false \
  python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
  tests/tools/test_file_tools.py::TestSecretFileReadRedaction \
  tests/tools/test_approval.py::TestApprovalPromptRedaction
# 4 failed, 1 passed

env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" LANG=C.UTF-8 \
  python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
  tests/tools/test_file_tools.py::TestSecretFileReadRedaction \
  tests/tools/test_approval.py::TestApprovalPromptRedaction
# 5 passed
```

### Expected Behavior

Same result as CI. The hermetic fixture already makes the launch shell's `HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS` irrelevant for code that reads the variable at call time; the import-time snapshot should not be the exception.

### Actual Behavior

4 failed: the opaque 40-char fixture token in `TestSecretFileReadRedaction` and the `sk-proj-…` fixture key in `TestApprovalPromptRedaction` come back in cleartext (`assert '<token>' not in '<output>'`).

### Affected Component

Other (test suite isolation)

### Debug Report

N/A: test-suite isolation bug, no runtime component. The reproduction above is self-contained.

### Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)

### Python Version

3.14.7 (pytest 9.1.1)

### Hermes Version

`main` @ 0e427d78 (2026-10-14)

### Roo
title: [Bug]: pytest from a shell with security.redact_secrets: false fails 4 redaction tests: agent.redact's import-time snapshot escapes the hermetic env scrub

body:
## Feature description

The kanban dispatcher decides part of a worker's capability surface at spawn time, through command-line parameters and code paths that bypass the assignee profile's own configuration. The profile cannot decline them. It can only fight them afterwards, where a counter exists at all.

Spawn-time injections in current `main`:

| Injection | Where | Profile control today |
|---|---|---|
| Card-level skills: one `--skills <name>` per entry in `task.skills`, chosen by whoever created the card | `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py` `_worker_argv` (`for sk in task.skills`) | none |
| `sdlc-review` force-loaded on every review-lane claim | `kanban_db_dispatch.py:2476-2479` | only `kanban.review_dispatch: false`, which turns off review dispatch entirely; `skills.disabled` breaks the review run instead (#99251) |
| `kanban` toolset force-appended for every dispatcher-owned worker | `model_tools.py:320-324` | `agent.disabled_toolsets: [kanban]`, which works only because disabled toolsets are subtracted last; this is a counter-measure, not a setting |
| `--toolsets` pin resolved by the dispatcher | `_resolve_worker_cli_toolsets` (`kanban_db_dispatch.py:3071-3089`) | indirect |
| `-m` / `--provider` / `--reasoning` from per-card overrides (`kanban set-model`, `reasoning_effort`) | `_worker_argv` | none |
| `KANBAN_GUIDANCE` protocol text, injected whenever the show tool is present | `agent/agent_init.py:1134-1136` | only by removing the toolset |

Each of these is harmless while nobody uses it. But each is a channel through which a card author (an orchestrator agent, or any profile holding `kanban_create`) or the dispatcher itself adds instructions, tools or model choices to another profile's run. To keep the worker's context clean, an operator has to disable or override every one of them pre-emptively, not just the ones in use.

## Motivation

We run worker profiles whose contract is enforced by their tool and skill surface, not by prompt text (see #138448). Concrete effects:

- **Review runs:** the dispatcher adds `sdlc-review` to every review run. That skill teaches the built-in kanban lifecycle tools, so a profile that deliberately replaces those tools gets the text back through the skill.
- **Card skills:** an orchestrator agent copies its own choice of skills onto every card it creates. The assignee profile has no allowlist, so a mistake there loads an implementation procedure into a review run, or the reverse.
- **Kanban toolset:** the forced `kanban` toolset is removable only through the subtract-last rule. Nothing documents that rule as the supported way to opt out, so it can change in any update.

The principle we would like Hermes to adopt: **the assignee profile is authoritative over its own capability surface.** The dispatcher may propose; the profile's config decides.

## Proposed solution

An opt-in, per-profile worker policy, defaulting to today's behaviour:

```yaml
kanban:
  worker_policy:
    task_skills: all          #
title: [Feature]: kanban dispatcher injects skills, toolsets and model overrides into workers at spawn — make the assignee profile authoritative (opt-in worker_policy)

body: ### Summary After a session is auto-compacted several times, the desktop transcript stops short of the end: the newest rows (including the final answer) are never shown, even when scrolling to the very bottom. The backend/DB is correct — a direct API read returns those rows. ### Environment - Hermes desktop 0.21.7 (commit 71d34ba), macOS 15.8.1 - Custom provider (deepseek), long agentic session (1009 DB rows), auto-compacted 3x ### Backend is fine (excluded) `GET /api/sessions//messages?limit=120&order=latest&include_compacted=true` returns: first id = 12518, … , last id = 12637, last content = "## 步骤 6 调优收尾——完成 …" (the final answer) `pagination.order` = "latest" (echoed correctly). So the tail-paging contract the front-end relies on is satisfied by the backend. ### Front-end symptom (the bug) Scroll to the very bottom of that session's transcript → the last visible row is "shadow 从 −1.16 → +1.09 … 加轮数到 5:" (timestamp 20:18, ≈ id 12512); ~125 newest rows (id ~12513–12637) are missing. Recovery behavior (this is the useful clue): - Closing and reopening the session tab → still broken. - Clicking / switching to another session and back → still broken. - Fully quitting and restarting the desktop app → FIXED. So the ordering/tail is cached in run-time state and only rebuilt on a cold start. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Long agent task that auto-compacts the context several times. 2. Let it finish (final answer written to DB). 3. Open the session, scroll to the bottom → newest rows absent. 4. Reopen the tab / switch sessions → still absent. 5. Quit and relaunch the desktop app → order/rows correct again. ### Suspected front-end area (not pinned to a line) Run-time tail-state cache / hydration merge. Inspected and appear correct, so the defect is likely in how the hydrated tail is cached or merged across re-renders: - apps/desktop/src/api/sessions.ts (getLatestSessionMessages, pageHonorsLatestOrder, LATEST_SESSION_MESSAGES_LIMIT=120) - apps/desktop/src/store/transcript-tail.ts - apps/desktop/src/app/chat/transcript-backfill.ts - apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/{hydration,reconciliation}.ts - apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/list.tsx ### Expected Scrolling to the bottom always shows the newest rows (final answer last), regardless of compaction count, without needing an app restart.

body:
## Problem

The `discord` / `discord_admin` toolsets are default-off (`_DEFAULT_OFF_TOOLSETS` in `hermes_cli/tools_config.py`, deliberate security opt-in). That part is fine. The problem is that nothing on the path a user actually walks tells them the tool exists or how to turn it on.

When the toolset isn't loaded, `gateway/session.py` (~L338) injects this platform note:

> You are running inside Discord. You do NOT have access to Discord-specific APIs — you cannot search channel history, pin messages, manage roles, or list server members. Do not promise to perform these actions. If the user asks, explain that you can only read messages sent directly to you and respond.

That reads as a hard capability limit. The agent repeats it to the user ("I can't do that"), when the real answer is "this is one command away."

## Repro (observed today)

- `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` set, gateway running on Discord
- `platform_toolsets.discord` is an explicit list without `discord`/`discord_admin`
- `known_builtin_toolsets.discord` *does* list `discord` and `discord_admin`, so the checklist offered them once and they're now treated as declined (`_enable_recently_shipped_toolsets` skips them)
- User asks in a Discord thread whether the tool needs to be added to config. The agent only has the "you do NOT have access" note to go on, and has to read the source to find out it's an opt-in toolset

## Proposed fix

1. **Reword the fallback note** for the case where the bot token is present but the toolset is off. Something like: "Discord server tools (`discord`, `discord_admin`) are installed but not enabled for this platform. If the user asks for channel history, member search, threads, pins, or roles, tell them to run `hermes tools enable --platform discord discord` (and `discord_admin` for server management), then restart the gateway." Keep the current hard-no wording only for the no-token case.
2. **Discoverability in `hermes gateway setup` / Discord setup:** once the token validates, offer to enable `discord` (core: fetch_messages, search_members, create_thread) with a one-line explanation, and leave `discord_admin` as a separate prompt.
3. **Docs:** the Discord messaging page should say explicitly that the tools are opt-in, and give the enable command.

## Related

- #96056: per-turn preamble promises reply/react/pin that the core toolset doesn't have (the inverse failure: over-promising when loaded)
- #2020: make platform notes configurable
- #35527: `hermes-discord` composite silently dropping discord tools (closed)
title: Discord: fallback platform note says 'no Discord API access' instead of pointing at the opt-in discord toolset

body:
## Bug

The `discord` and `discord_admin` tools are off on the Discord gateway unless `config.yaml` has an explicit `platform_toolsets.discord` list. If you run the gateway with a working `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` and no `platform_toolsets.discord` entry, the agent gets neither tool. Nothing tells the user this, and the docs say the opposite.

## Repro (main @ 1f6c02c07c)

- `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is set and valid. Calling the module directly works: `_list_guilds` returns the server, and `_detect_capabilities` returns `{'has_members_intent': True, 'has_message_content': True, 'detected': True}`.
- `platform_toolsets` lists `cli`, `telegram` and `webhook`, with no `discord` key.
- Resolution for discord:

```python
from hermes_cli.tools_config import _get_platform_tools
from hermes_cli.config import load_config
s = _get_platform_tools(load_config(), "discord")
"discord" in s, "discord_admin" in s   # (False, False)
```

## Cause

`hermes_cli/tools_config.py`:

- `_DEFAULT_OFF_TOOLSETS` contains `discord` and `discord_admin`.
- `_default_off_toolsets(platform, explicitly_configured)` keeps both stripped from the implicit `hermes-discord` expansion. Only an explicitly saved list lets them through (added by the fix for #35527 / #60553).
- `_first_install_flow` seeds the checklist with `current_enabled - _DEFAULT_OFF_TOOLSETS`, so a fresh setup also starts with both unchecked.

Default-off as a security opt-in is a reasonable choice. The bug is that nothing surfaces it.

## Docs say otherwise

- `website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md`: "Active on the `hermes-discord` toolset" for both tools, and "`hermes-discord` adds `discord` and `discord_admin` on top of `hermes-cli`".
- `website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md`: "Registered on the `hermes-discord` platform toolset". It also lists actions the tool doesn't have. `discord` is said to have `send_message`, `react`, `fetch_channel`, `list_channels`, but its real core set is `fetch_messages`, `search_members`, `create_thread`. `discord_admin` is said to have create/edit/delete channels, timeouts, kicks and bans, but its real set is list guilds/channels/roles, server/channel/member info, pins, delete message, add/remove role.

## Impact

People argue from the docs that gateway users "already have" Discord tooling. In practice they only have it after hand-writing a full `platform_toolsets.discord` list or ticking the boxes in `hermes tools`. Writing that list also pins every other toolset for the platform, so the user has to copy the whole default set across.

## Suggested fix

1. Docs: state that both toolsets are default-off on Discord and show how to enable them. Fix the action lists so they match `_ACTION_MANIFEST`.
2. Surface it: when the Discord adapter is connected with a valid token and both toolsets are resolved off, print one line at gateway startup and in `hermes doctor` pointing at `hermes tools`.
3. Optional: give an additive way to opt in (e.g. `discord.tools_enabled: true`) so enabling these
title: Discord gateway: discord/discord_admin tools silently off without explicit platform_toolsets.discord; docs say they're active

body:
## Feature description

Two related capabilities, so that a workflow contract can be enforced through the tool surface instead of through prompt text:

1. **Per-tool selection in profile config.** Allow and deny lists at tool granularity, alongside the existing toolset-level `toolsets` / `agent.disabled_toolsets`, for example `agent.disabled_tools: [<tool>, ...]` (and optionally `agent.enabled_tools`). It would be applied in `model_tools._select_tool_names` after toolset resolution, using the same subtract-last rule that `disabled_toolsets` already has.
2. **Kanban tools and kanban guidance that depend on the run's step.** A dispatcher-owned worker should receive only the lifecycle tools valid for the lane its run was claimed from, and `KANBAN_GUIDANCE` should describe only those tools:
   - **Implementation-step claim** on a board or task that requires review: no completion tool. The worker finishes by requesting review or by blocking.
   - **Review-step claim:** the verdict tools only, with no request-review tool.

## Motivation

Today a profile can only take or drop whole toolsets. Every dispatcher-spawned worker gets all kanban lifecycle tools (`tools/kanban_tools.py:83-96`; `model_tools.py:320-324` force-adds the `kanban` toolset). `KANBAN_GUIDANCE` (`agent/prompt_builder.py:266`) teaches every worker both "complete" and "request review", whatever its lane or the board's policy.

So "this card must be reviewed before done" exists only as prose, and prose loses to context. Observed on one board over 14 days:

- **Implementer completed its own card.** The card body described a reviewer whose verdict tool is the completion tool. The implementer applied that text to its own run and completed without review (details in #122966).
- **Reviewers re-implemented.** 7 review-step runs called request-review on the card they were reviewing instead of giving a verdict.

Hiding a tool is stronger than refusing it. A refused tool still sits in the schema and the guidance, which keeps the forbidden path in the model's context. For agent workflows that context pollution is the actual failure mode.

## Proposed solution

- `agent.disabled_tools` / `agent.enabled_tools` (per profile), subtracted last, with no `HERMES_*` env var.
- The step at claim time is already recorded (`claimed` event `source_status`). Expose it to the kanban `check_fn`s (or set it in the worker env at spawn), and gate each lifecycle tool on it plus an opt-in policy flag such as `kanban.require_review_before_done` (#122966).
- Build `KANBAN_GUIDANCE` from the tool names the session actually has, so it never names a tool the worker lacks.

## Alternatives considered

- **Current local workaround:** `agent.disabled_toolsets: [kanban]` on the worker profile, which also suppresses `KANBAN_GUIDANCE` because injection is keyed on the presence of the show tool. A plugin then supplies a step-specific replacement toolset that calls `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py` directly. It works, but it duplicates the
title: [Feature]: per-tool selection in profile config + step-aware kanban lifecycle tools and guidance (enforce workflow contracts by tool surface, not prompt text)

## Summary
In Desktop, the "+" button on a git group header in the sidebar ("New session in master") starts the session in the git root. If a Project's primary folder is a subfolder of that repo, the Project's folder is ignored.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.22.0+119 (2026.9.24), Desktop, Linux, install method: git
- Named profile in a multi-profile setup
- Sidebar: Group by -> Projects

## Project configuration (`hermes project show customer-x`)
```
customer-x  [p_xxxxxxxx]
  name:    Customer X - Engagement
  primary: /home/user/work/customers/customer-x/engagement
  folders:
    * /home/user/work/customers/customer-x/engagement
```
`/home/user/work/customers/customer-x` is a git repo (branch `master`, no commits). `engagement` is a plain subfolder of it, with no `.git` of its own.

## Reproduction
1. Create a git repo at `customers/customer-x` (no commits needed).
2. Create a Project whose only folder is `customers/customer-x/engagement`.
3. In the sidebar, click "+" on the `master` group header ("New session in master").

## Expected
The new session starts in the Project's primary folder, `.../customer-x/engagement`.

## Actual
The session starts in the repo root, `.../customer-x`. The workspace, the Files pane and the loaded context files (`AGENTS.md`) come from the parent folder.

## Workaround
Use "+ New session" on the Project row in the sidebar. The session then starts in the primary folder.

## Likely cause
The group header uses the auto-discovered git root as the new session's cwd. It does not check for a Project whose folder sits inside that repo.

## Impact
The session loads the wrong context files and file scope. This matters when several engagements sit under one customer repo, because context can leak between them.

## Possibly related
#96834, #66686, #40297
title: Desktop: "New session in <branch>" group-header button ignores the Project's primary folder inside that repo

body:
### Bug Description

`hermes update` (git install, stable channel) fails at channel resolution when the `gh` CLI resolves to any PATH wrapper that prints to stdout:

```
✗ Could not resolve the stable source channel: No published stable release could be verified: Invalid header value b'Bearer mise ~/.config/mise/config.toml tools: gh@2.102.0\ngho_***'. No update was applied.
```

The captured `gh auth token` output contained a line of wrapper noise ahead of the token; the embedded newline makes the `Authorization` header invalid, and the update aborts — even though the credential ladder's anonymous rung would have succeeded.

### Environment

- Arch Linux (Omarchy), Hermes v0.21.7 (git install), stable channel
- `gh` 2.102.0, installed via mise behind omarchy's `omarchy-mise-install` wrapper pattern: `mise use -g "gh" || exit 1` / `exec mise x "gh" -- "gh" "$@"`
- No `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` env vars set, so the updater takes the `gh auth token` rung

### Root cause (code path)

1. `hermes_cli/github_api.py::github_token()` uses the raw stdout of `gh auth token` as the token (result cached per process).
2. In the updater's sanitized environment, `gh` resolves to the mise wrapper above. Since mise 2026.10.x, `mise use -g` prints a summary line to stdout, so the capture is `mise ~/.config/mise/config.toml tools: gh@2.102.0` + newline + the real token. (Omarchy fixed their own wrappers with `mise use -g --quiet` in omacom/omarchy#6940 and added a regeneration migration — but any stdout-printing shim or hook, mise or otherwise, triggers this.)
3. `hermes_cli/source_check.py::_request_with()` builds `Authorization: Bearer <captured>`; `http.client` raises `ValueError: Invalid header value …` while sending, before any bytes hit the wire.
4. `source_check.py::_request()` falls back to anonymous only for `urllib.error.HTTPError` with code 401 — the header-build `ValueError` is not an `HTTPError`, so it propagates and `_resolve_stable` reports it as "No published stable release could be verified", failing the whole update closed.

This is the same ladder-robustness family as #134335 (stale token 403 never falls back to anonymous; Desktop update check) and #13970 (token validation accepts arbitrary strings), but a distinct failure mode: the token is malformed at capture time, so no request is ever attempted and no fallback ever engages.

### Impact

Any wrapper/hook that emits stdout around a resolved CLI (mise/asdf shims, direnv-style hooks, corporate wrappers) breaks `hermes update` and update checks on every run, despite a working anonymous fallback (GitHub's 60 req/hour per address is plenty for a release lookup). Affects both the CLI updater and Desktop update checks, which share the ladder.

### Suggested hardening (either or both)

1. `github_token()`: take the last non-empty line of the capture and require a GitHub token shape (`gh[a-z]_[A-Za-z0-9]+` / `github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]+`); anything else is treated as no token, letting the ladder continue
title: [Bug]: updater sends raw `gh auth token` stdout as the Bearer token — any stdout-printing wrapper breaks every update with "Invalid header value"

## Bug description

Changing a Cron job's model in the official Desktop editor leaves an existing per-job `base_url` override untouched. This can turn a valid job into one that saves successfully but is rejected at execution time. Selecting the default-model option has the same problem: `provider` and `model` are cleared, while the old endpoint remains.

Checked against current `main`, `0e427d788d253630d38a3a51cd76849e73cd6925` (2026-10-14).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two named custom providers, `custom:old` and `custom:new`, with different endpoints. Make `custom:new` the profile default. For an isolated fixture, use `https://old.example.invalid/v1` and `https://new.example.invalid/v1` with dummy credentials.
2. Start with a valid agent Cron job containing:
   ```json
   {
     "provider": "custom:old",
     "model": "old-model",
     "base_url": "https://old.example.invalid/v1"
   }
   ```
   This can be created through the existing Cron API/tool with an explicit endpoint matching its provider.
3. Open the job in Desktop's Cron editor, choose a model from `custom:new`, and save.
4. Run the job. The saved record has the new provider/model but still has the old `base_url`.
5. Alternatively, choose the default-model option and save. The record now has `provider: null` and `model: null`, but the same old `base_url` remains.

## Actual behavior

The runtime guard correctly refuses the inconsistent record before creating the agent:

- Switching to the other provider: `base_url 'https://old.example.invalid/v1' is not allowed for provider 'custom:new'`.
- Selecting the default: `base_url override requires an explicit provider`.

The old endpoint is not exposed by this model picker, so saving a seemingly valid model choice does not repair the job.

## Expected behavior

An explicit model/provider change should leave a coherent executable route. Clear an obsolete endpoint override when replacing the binding, or expose and validate it as part of that operation. Selecting the default should genuinely restore the default route. Unrelated edits should preserve an intentionally unchanged override.

## Source trace

- [`cronEditorUpdates()`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/0e427d788d253630d38a3a51cd76849e73cd6925/apps/desktop/src/app/cron/cron-job-model.ts#L135-L158) updates only `model` and `provider` for the model selection.
- [`update_job()`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/0e427d788d253630d38a3a51cd76849e73cd6925/cron/jobs.py#L2122) merges those updates into the stored record, retaining `base_url`.
- [`_guard_job_credential_exfil()`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/0e427d788d253630d38a3a51cd76849e73cd6925/cron/scheduler_prompt.py) then rejects the retained endpoint/provider combination.

Related: #108423 concerns missing validation on API mutations. This report concerns a valid existing job becoming inconsistent through an ordinary Desktop model selection; the runtime guard should remain intac
title: [Bug]: Desktop Cron model changes retain stale base_url and fail at runtime

body:
## Problem

On messenger platforms there is no way to tell that a reply was produced through MoA:

- `/moa <prompt>` (one-shot) sends **no acknowledgment** on success — the gateway handler (`gateway/run_inbound.py`, `_hm_cmd_moa`) silently re-dispatches the prompt with a one-turn MoA override; only a prepare-failure message is shown.
- The reply is generated by the aggregator acting as the model, so it is indistinguishable from a normal single-model reply — no prefix, footer, or annotation.
- The MoA display events (`moa.reference`, `moa.progress`, `moa.phase`, `moa.aggregating`) are rendered by richer surfaces (CLI/TUI/Desktop), but the messenger gateway path does not handle them, so chat users see nothing.
- The only indirect evidence is timing: the turn takes much longer, with just the generic long-running "still working" heartbeat.

Net effect: users cannot verify that MoA actually ran, and an explicit `/moa` invocation with no acknowledgment/answer marker reads like a silent no-op.

## Repro (observed on v0.21.7, Telegram via the gateway)

1. Send `/moa <short question>` in a Telegram chat.
2. Watch the conversation: no acknowledgment appears; after a long pause the answer arrives as a normal message with no MoA marker.
3. Any preset change (models, reference count) stays invisible on the surface — replies remain unmarked.

## Why it matters

- A MoA turn is slower and costs extra reference calls; users verifying that a preset is actually in effect have no feedback loop without host-side log access.
- Experimenting with presets is guesswork when you cannot tell which replies ran through MoA.
- It makes `/moa` feel broken on chat platforms.

## Proposed behavior (suggestions, not prescriptive)

A lightweight, persistent indicator tied to the turn on messenger surfaces, e.g.:

- a small marker on the reply itself (e.g. `🧩 MoA · <preset> · N refs` as a footer or prefix), and/or
- a one-line notice when a MoA turn starts (could reuse the existing `moa.phase` / `moa.aggregating` events), and/or
- a reaction on the invoking message.

Terse by design — users do not need reference bodies on chat, only the fact that MoA ran. Config-gated is fine; on-by-default for explicit `/moa` invocations would cover the main case.

## Related

- #71243 — MoA reference fan-out gives zero UI feedback (in-flight progress / hang-vs-slow, mostly CLI/TUI)
- #97737 — open PR: compact `🧩` progress markers for MoA on the messenger gateway (transient in-turn progress; opened 2026-08-29). Complementary but different: this request is about the reply/turn **remaining identifiable after the fact**.
- #97674 / #97251 — Desktop-side MoA visibility (fan-out display, preset roles)

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.7 (2026.9.24), stable channel, git install
- Platform: Telegram via the gateway
- MoA preset: default (4 reference models + aggregator)
title: [Feature]: show a visible MoA marker on messenger replies (e.g. Telegram)

**Problem**

With `WHATSAPP_REQUIRE_MENTION=true`, the WhatsApp adapter drops group messages that don't mention the bot in `_should_process_message` (`gateway/platforms/whatsapp_common.py`). They are never stored, so when someone later asks the agent "what did we agree on?", it has no context.

Telegram already solves this: with `TELEGRAM_OBSERVE_UNMENTIONED_GROUP_MESSAGES`, unmentioned chatter is appended to the group session as `observed` rows without dispatching, and `gateway/run.py` passes it as a separate context-only block when the bot is addressed (`_uses_telegram_observed_group_context`).

**Proposal**

Add the same opt-in to WhatsApp, e.g. `WHATSAPP_OBSERVE_UNMENTIONED_GROUP_MESSAGES`, limited to allowed groups.

One difference we hit while implementing it downstream: Telegram strips the sender (`user_id=None`) to share the group session and relies on the chat-scoped allowlist (`TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS`) for authorization. WhatsApp has no chat-scoped grant in `authz_mixin._GROUP_CHAT_ENV`, so stripping the sender makes the gateway reject the mention. What worked for us was keeping the sender on the event and making `build_session_key` use one session per group for observed WhatsApp groups (instead of `group_sessions_per_user`).

The observed-context marker in `run.py` is Telegram-specific ("observed Telegram group context"); a platform-neutral marker would make this cleaner.

**What we tested** (Hermes 0.21.5, Baileys bridge, real number): unmentioned messages stored and not answered; a mention answered using the stored conversation; an unrelated question answered without summarizing the chatter; DMs and non-allowed numbers unaffected.

Happy to share our patch or open a PR if this direction fits.
title: WhatsApp: observe unmentioned group messages (parity with TELEGRAM_OBSERVE_UNMENTIONED_GROUP_MESSAGES)

## Bug description

On macOS, Kanban recorded two resumed worker runs as `crashed` / `protocol_violation` and respawned them while their corresponding native Hermes model sessions continued making tool calls. The overlapping sessions wrote into the same scratch workspaces; successful CLI recovery evidence appeared concurrently, and terminal board calls from the older owner were rejected after ownership changed.

This report is based on existing logs and read-only SQLite snapshots. No new reproduction, forced cron execution, OOM experiment, local kernel patch, or configuration repair was performed for this report. Local personal paths, project names and task/session identifiers are anonymized below.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `0.21.6+763.g1fd1827`, installed commit `1fd18277267152893a8a24792b79213e7ca3f899`.
- macOS `26.7.1`, build `25G241`.
- Claude Code `2.1.296`; Hermes native delegating drivers, with persisted external CLI sessions.
- Hermes Desktop/agent terminal, one already running gateway hosting the embedded dispatcher.
- Gateway reports singleton dispatcher lock held; interval 60 seconds, max_in_progress 3, max_in_progress_per_profile 1.
- Two independent synthetic scratch cards, one per developer profile; no product inheritance, production data or deployment.

## Historical setup / observed sequence

1. Embedded gateway dispatcher was already running. A foreground `hermes kanban dispatch --json` launched two initial scratch workers. Their first claims were later replaced by gateway-owned claims (45/46 -> 47/48); this is not asserted to be safe or recommended orchestration.
2. The actual scratch failures were observed: empty Claude `--print` stdin exited 1 with the input-required validation error; another Claude invocation reported an actual Edit permission denial and left the synthetic file unchanged.
3. The existing cron job was manually invoked once via `hermes cron run <job>` and wrote Ruling/ANSWER, then unblocked both cards. It also caused recorded resumed worker spawns. The synchronous terminal invocation eventually hit its 180-second tool timeout; its execution receipt later became UNKNOWN. The chronology below independently verifies the card effects and distinguishes that interrupted command from natural cron execution.
4. Gateway booked the first resumed runs as protocol violations, immediately replaced them, and the original native sessions continued after the board runs ended.

## Timestamped evidence

All times are 2026-10-14, Europe/Warsaw / CEST, UTC+02:00.

| Event | Synthetic task A: empty input | Synthetic task B: Edit denial |
|---|---|---|
| First actual block | 15:01:54 (run 47) | 15:03:02 (run 48) |
| Recorded ANSWER / unblock | 15:06:08 | 15:06:09 |

# Plugin API gap: per-dispatch tool-call correlation

Out-of-tree plugins need a documented, nullable correlation value for the current tool dispatch. A fresh nested `registry.dispatch` must not inherit or consume its parent's value. The value may expose the existing task, session, tool-call, turn, and API-request labels, plus a new dispatch-attempt ID and a digest of the final arguments.

This is correlation metadata only. It should not be documented as authenticated agent identity, human approval, or authorization to perform a protected operation.

## Current limitation

A plugin can store the middleware payload in a plugin-local context variable, but that value is tied to the wrapping callback rather than to each registry dispatch. A fresh unwrapped dispatch nested inside that callback can observe and consume it before the intended handler runs. Passing only `task_id` and `session_id` to the handler does not identify the dispatch boundary. A profile label or approval digest is not a principal credential.

A minimal isolated reproduction has 11 tests: 10 pass and 1 fails. The failure is the fresh nested dispatch consuming the parent correlation. The handler still denies the operation, so this is a context-delivery bug rather than demonstrated authorization bypass. An isolated generic prototype fixed the reproduction, but local core patches are intentionally not being deployed; the capability needs to arrive through Hermes itself.

## Acceptance

- An unmodified Hermes release exposes the observation through the documented plugin context.
- A standalone plugin test shows that a fresh nested dispatch sees no inherited attempt, while the intended wrapped dispatch sees its own.
- Existing narrow tool handlers remain compatible.
- The change contains no product- or deployment-specific logic.
title: Plugin API: provide per-dispatch tool-call correlation

body:
## 问题与使用场景

希望能在当前对话中固定所选模型和供应商，明确选择“宁可等待或报错，也不要自动换模型”。

实际使用中的困扰是：用户为复杂任务选择某个模型后，遇到网络波动或供应商暂时不可用，自动 fallback 可能让备用模型继续回答。即使有切换通知、下一轮会尝试恢复主模型，这一轮任务也已不再由用户指定的模型完成。对重视能力一致性的任务，可用性并不应自动优先于模型选择。

这里的“降档”是用户对所选备用模型能力的判断，并不是所有 fallback 都一定更弱。网络波动是用户反馈的场景，本 Issue 没有附带受控网络故障复现实验，也不把所有回退归因于网络。

现有 `/model` 可以进行会话级切换，但“选择主模型”与“严格禁止回退”是两种不同需求。

## 建议方案

增加会话级 **模型锁定 / 严格模式**，并通过聊天命令及模型选择界面暴露：

- 锁定当前会话的具体 `provider + model`；使用自定义供应商时，保留其已解析的 endpoint 路由，避免同名模型被路由到另一供应商。
- 可考虑 `/model <provider>:<model> --lock`，并提供解锁入口（例如 `/model --unlock`）。**这些是建议语法，不是现有命令。**
- 桌面模型选择器可加“锁定本会话模型／禁止自动回退”开关；CLI、TUI 和消息网关聊天应有一致语义。
- 锁定只覆盖当前会话，不能通过清空全局 fallback 链实现；其他会话仍可按已有策略自动回退。
- 遇到临时错误，允许对同一锁定路由进行有界重试；耗尽重试后明确提示失败，保留对话上下文，供用户重试或主动解锁。
- 即使是配额耗尽、鉴权失败或模型不可用，也不能在锁定模式下擅自切换模型；应给出可操作的错误说明。
- `/status` 和模型状态显示锁定状态、请求的模型及实际服务模型；不要让备用模型的回答仍显示为锁定模型。
- 会话恢复及进程重启后保留该会话的锁定状态；新会话继续遵循原有默认策略。

建议优先复用现有 session API 的 `require_model_lock` / `confirmed_runtime_lock` 机制，而不是另建一套独立锁定规则。

## 验收建议

1. 配置主模型 A 和备用模型 B，在会话 S1 开启锁定，S2 保持默认。
2. 对 A 注入受控连接失败、超时或 503：S1 仅重试 A，失败后报错，B 的调用次数为 0；S2 仍可按原策略回退到 B。
3. A 恢复后，S1 可以继续在 A 上完成任务；锁定状态不会被失败清除。
4. 恢复会话或重启后，S1 仍保持锁定；解锁后才重新允许自动回退。
5. 验证配额、鉴权和模型不存在等永久错误，也不会绕过锁定。

首期请求范围为**当前对话主模型**。辅助模型和显式指定的子任务模型具有各自用途，先保持其独立策略并清楚说明边界，不要求本功能把所有辅助调用强制改成同一模型。

## 已考虑的替代方案

- 全局清空 fallback 链：影响其他会话及无人值守任务，粒度太粗。
- 每次只用 `/model` 切回所需模型：不能阻止同一轮任务中途再次回退。
- 增加回退前重试或回退通知：有帮助，但通知不等于用户同意换模型。
- 直接调用带 `require_model_lock` 的 session API：部分底层机制已存在，但普通聊天用户需要在对话入口操作，而非自行构造 API 请求。

## 相关 Issue 与官方文档

- #128488：显式指定模型的 API 请求仍可能继承 fallback 链，并错误标注响应模型。本请求主要关注聊天内可操作的会话级严格模式，而非仅修复 OpenAI-compatible API。
- #136049：临时 CPA 错误的重试策略。本请求不要求普通回退策略永远等待，而是提供用户可选的严格模式。
- [Slash Commands](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/slash-commands)
- [Fallback Providers](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/fallback-providers)

## 环境与范围

本机 CLI 核验版本：`Hermes Agent v0.22.0+119.g0e427d7`，Windows，消息网关聊天场景。该版本信息来自 `hermes --version`；不据此断言正在运行的每个进程都是同一版本。

类型：聊天／消息网关改进、配置选项、可靠性。此 Issue 为功能请求，不是已经完成的实现或测试报告。
title: [Feature]: 支持对话内锁定模型，失败时明确报错而不是自动回退（session model lock / no fallback）

body:
### Bug Description

Apple Mail and iOS Mail attach files with `Content-Disposition: inline; filename=...` rather than `attachment`. The Email adapter treats every inline `text/plain` / `text/html` part as body, so:

1. An attached `.txt` / `.log` / `.html` file never reaches the agent: it is not cached as an attachment ("summarize the attached notes" arrives with no file and no error). Other types (`.csv`, `.pdf`, images) do arrive.
2. When the body is HTML-only (common from Apple Mail), the attached text file is picked as the body: the agent reads the file's contents in place of what the user wrote.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. From Apple Mail / iOS Mail, send the Hermes mailbox a message with a `.txt` file attached.
2. Ask it to summarize the attachment.

Minimal: a `multipart/mixed` message with a plain body and a part `Content-Type: text/plain`, `Content-Disposition: inline; filename=meeting-notes.txt`. `_parse_fetched_message` returns no attachment for it. With an HTML-only body instead, `body` is the file's text.

### Expected Behavior

The file is cached as an attachment like any other, and the body is the user's message.

### Actual Behavior

The file is dropped; with an HTML-only body, the file's text replaces the message body.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

Not from a live mailbox: reproduced on current `main` (0e427d788d) with `EmailAdapter._parse_fetched_message` on an `email.message.EmailMessage` built with `add_attachment(..., disposition="inline", filename=...)`.

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.14

### Hermes Version

main @ 0e427d788d

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`plugins/platforms/email/adapter.py`: `_extract_attachments` skips any part that is not `attachment` when it is inline `text/plain`/`text/html`, without checking for a filename; `_first_body_part` only skips `attachment` parts, so an inline text file can be chosen as the body.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Treat an inline part with a filename as an attached file in both places; inline parts without a filename stay body parts.

body:
## Context

I run **several real companies** on one Hermes Desktop (separate legal entities, credentials, inboxes, and standing rules). Bot Mode currently treats **one Bot = one profile = a full Hermes home** (`SOUL.md`, `memories/`, skills, `.env`, `state.db`, cron). That isolation is valuable. It does not match how we actually need to staff work.

I compared this to **Grok Bot / OpenMausBot + BotMRR**: a **catalog of small teams** (typically 2–4 named roles + Markdown playbooks). Installing a team creates lightweight roles in one app; a different project is often a **thread/folder**, not another full agent home. A catalog of ~18 teams already encodes ~60 role slots; that library can grow to hundreds. Mapping each catalog role onto a Hermes profile would mean **hundreds of full homes**.

This is a product/architecture question, not a bug report.

Related (not the same request): #97333 (preset profiles), #106201 (spawn-location overlay — cloning a whole profile is too heavy for “same agent, other folder”).

## What is unclear in Hermes today

1. **Two different “profiles” are collapsed into one primitive.**
   - *Business / tenant:* company A vs company B must not share memory, API keys, Telegram tokens, or “who we are legally.”
   - *Persona / desk role:* inside one company, Scout vs Envoy vs Ledger (or programmer vs SEO) need different **souls and refusals**, but they often should share the company’s keys, project rules, and some memory.

   Docs say “never point two writers at one home” (memory compounds) and “a Bot is a profile.” There is no documented layer for “many souls inside one business” without cloning the whole home.

2. **Clone / Duplicate is the wrong operation for a team template.**
   Duplicate copies SOUL, skills, and memory into a new directory. That is a second **person**, not “same company, other desk.” Messaging channels are stripped (correct for tokens). There is still no “install this 4-role desk under company X.”

3. **Bulk edits do not exist (or are undocumented).**
   If I must change a standing refusal, a skill, or a model pin across 20 programmer-like bots — or across all bots of one company — I am left to hand-edit N copies of `SOUL.md` / `skills/`. After that, copies drift. How are we supposed to patch souls, skills, and related policy **in mass**?

4. **The roster and runtime are sized for a handful of specialists.**
   Search / sections / Hide help a list, but Warm Bot Backends default to 3 live processes; group chats cap at 2–6 members. That is a **crew**, not a **catalog of desks** across several companies.

5. **Skills vs souls are easy to confuse and don’t replace a team package.**
   A skill is “how to do a job.” A soul is “who I am and what I must never do.” Catalog roles are mostly **souls + playbooks**. Hermes skills are per-profile copies when cloned, so a library of roles still explodes into N trees.

## Where Hermes could beat Grok Bot / Mausbot (if this layer existed)

These are already Hermes strength
title: Bot Mode: business isolation vs persona bots, bulk SOUL/skill edits, and catalog-scale teams (vs Grok Bot / OpenMausBot)

**Title**: Non-TTY environments: `hermes hooks accept` / `--accept-hooks` / `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1` don't accept hooks (direct allowlist write is the only working path)

**Environment**: Linux (Fedora), Hermes CLI, non-TTY session (script / cron / gateway-attached session) running `hermes hooks accept` or setting `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1`.

**Observed** (2026-10-06, reproduced on a fresh non-TTY shell): both officially documented acceptance paths are inert without a terminal — the hook still reports `✗ not allowlisted` and `~/.hermes/shell-hooks-allowlist.json` is unchanged. The only path that lands an approval is appending `{"event": …, "command": …}` to the `approvals` array of that file directly. That path is not documented as supported, and the file carries no integrity check (signature/ownership), so an unattended process is pushed toward an undocumented write to the consent store.

**Impact**: in unattended / gateway scenarios, hooks that the operator has already approved cannot be landed through the official interface, forcing either the bypass (direct write) or dropping the approval — which breaks the fail-closed approval discipline. Silent no-op is the worst failure mode here: the command exits without making the consent effective.

**Suggested fixes**:
1. Make `--accept-hooks` / `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1` actually take effect in non-TTY sessions, or fail loudly with a clear error instead of silently doing nothing.
2. Either bless the allowlist file as a supported path and add integrity protection (signature/ownership check), or provide a supported CLI subcommand that writes it.
3. Document the correct acceptance flow for non-TTY / headless environments.

**Repro notes**: non-TTY execution → `hermes hooks list` shows no change after either official path; the allowlist file only changes when written directly.

Related: #100942 (non-TTY gateway allowlist has no entry → hook never registers), #133582 (cron sessions never register hooks), #109179 (hooks list/doctor don't say which allowlist file they read).
title: Non-TTY environments: `hermes hooks accept` / `--accept-hooks` / `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1` don't accept hooks (direct allowlist write is the only working path)

### Bug Description

A skill config value of `false` or `0` is shown as "(not set)". With a skill declaring `metadata.hermes.config` keys `deploy.dry_run` (default `true`) and `deploy.retries` (default `3`), and `config.yaml` setting `skills.config.deploy.dry_run: false` / `retries: 0`, invoking the skill injects:

```
[Skill config (from ~/.hermes/config.yaml):
  deploy.dry_run = (not set)
  deploy.retries = (not set)
]
```

The agent never sees the explicit setting and may fall back to the declared default (here a real deploy instead of a dry run). The "Skill Settings" section of `hermes config` shows the same "(not set)".

### Steps to Reproduce

1. A skill whose frontmatter declares `metadata.hermes.config` keys with a boolean or numeric value, e.g. `deploy.dry_run` (default `true`).
2. `config.yaml`: `skills: {config: {deploy: {dry_run: false, retries: 0}}}`.
3. Invoke `/deploy`, or run `hermes config`.

### Expected Behavior

`deploy.dry_run = False` and `deploy.retries = 0`; "(not set)" only for keys with no value.

### Actual Behavior

Both are shown as "(not set)".

### Affected Component

Skills (skill loading, skill hub, skill guard)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

Not from a live session: reproduced on current `main` (0e427d788d) through `build_skill_invocation_message("/deploy")` and `hermes_cli.config._show_skill_settings` with a temp HERMES_HOME.

Windows 11

main @ 0e427d788d

## Summary

The desktop app re-downloads a file URL that is present in the conversation **once per
agent turn**, opening a native Save dialog each time. During a long agent run the dialogs
stack up — a user showed five of them open at once, all for the same file.

The agent produces the link once. Nothing on the server triggers these requests.

## Evidence

Web-server access log vs. the agent's own log for the same session. The agent's log is UTC,
the web server is UTC+3 — these are the same instants:

```
agent turn (agent.log, UTC)   12:08:12  12:08:20  12:08:25  12:09:07  12:09:14  12:09:29
GET /files/<name>.html (MSK)  15:08:12  15:08:20  15:08:25  15:09:07  15:09:14  15:09:29
```

31 downloads of the same signed URL (identical `md5=` query parameter) in roughly three
minutes, one per model call. Two distinct links were ever minted for that file — the repeats
all used one of them.

## Scope

Not specific to one machine. Across 20 instances, the number of repeats tracks how long the
agent keeps working after the link appears in the conversation:

| user | downloads | distinct links | max per link |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (long SEO sessions) | 40 | 5 | 17 |
| B | 20 | 5 | 5 |
| C | 6 | 2 | 4 |
| D, E (closed the chat) | 1 | 1 | 1 |

Users B and C are on agent **0.19.0**, user A on **0.21.5** — so this is not new in 0.21.
Desktop app versions seen: 0.17.0 and 0.17.6, both affected.

## Expected

A file URL in the message history is downloaded when the user asks for it, not on every
re-render of the conversation.

## Environment

- Desktop app 0.17.0 and 0.17.6 (Electron, Windows)
- Agent 0.19.0 and 0.21.5, remote gateway over HTTPS
- File links are signed URLs served by the agent: `/files/<name>?md5=…&expires=…`

## Notes

Possibly related: #135441 (option to save downloads without the native Save dialog) would
reduce the pain but not the repeated downloads themselves.

Happy to provide more log excerpts if useful.
title: [Bug]: Desktop re-downloads a file link from the conversation on every agent turn, stacking native Save dialogs

body:
## Summary

`hermes update` / Telegram `/update` fails deterministically on Ubuntu 24.04
(git 2.43.0) with:

```
✗ Could not resolve the stable source channel: Command '['git', 'merge-base',
'--is-ancestor', '<release-sha>', '<head-sha>']' timed out after 10 seconds.
No update was applied.
```

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/source_releases.py:_head_containing` runs
`merge-base --is-ancestor` as a read-only ancestry probe with `timeout=10`.
The checkout is a blobless partial clone, and `source_git_env()` sets
`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` — but that variable is only honored by git ≥ 2.44
(acknowledged in `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py` comments).

On git 2.43 (Ubuntu 24.04 stock), when the stable release lands on a commit
the clone never fetched, `merge-base` triggers an on-demand promisor fetch of
the missing history (~186 MB observed, network-bound). The 10s timeout kills
git mid-fetch, `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` escapes `_head_containing`, and
the update aborts.

Failure is deterministic per new stable release and retries never converge:
each killed probe orphans `tmp_pack_*` and the next run refetches from zero.

## Reproduction

1. git 2.43, partial clone (`blob:none`) of this repo
2. HEAD older than the latest published stable release
3. `hermes update --check`

## Suggested fix

Treat the timeout as "unknown relation" instead of letting it escape —
same semantics as the existing shallow-history / GitHub-unreachable paths:

```python
try:
    ancestry = run("merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, head).returncode
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    # Partial clone on git <2.44 ignores GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH: the probe
    # triggered an on-demand history download past the 10s timeout. The
    # relation is unknown; let the GitHub compare API below decide.
    ancestry = None
```

With this, timeout falls through to the existing
`_github_compare(commit, head, repository)` fallback which already handles
behind/diverged, and `merge-base` exit code `None` skips both `ancestry == 0`
and `ancestry == 1` branches correctly.

Verified on a live affected host: warm path 0.02s, timeout path now resolves
via compare API in ~10.6s with no exception, `hermes update --check` succeeds.

Alternative: make the probe pass `-c` config to disable lazy fetch on older
git, or bump git ≥ 2.44 on the host.
title: Update channel resolution times out on git <2.44: merge-base probe lazy-fetches history in partial clones

# Gap: core kanban auto-decomposer lacks an approval-gate concept

**Component:** kanban (auto-decomposer / dispatcher / worker preflight)
**Severity:** high — approval-pending work was executed without approver sign-off
**Reported by:** Valicen IT (deployment of Hermes Agent as a multi-agent operations system)

## Summary

A kanban card explicitly in an *awaiting human approval* state was auto-decomposed by the core auto-decomposer ~15 seconds after creation. The pending proposals were reworded into imperative work-order text and dispatched to executing workers, which then performed live write-class mutations against an external API with no approver approval anywhere in the lane.

## Reproduction (as observed in production, 2026-10-14)

1. A card was created with the human operator as assignee and body text stating the work is **pending the operator's approval** (three proposed ad-account mutations, dry-run first, "awaiting approval" language throughout).
2. ~15 s later the auto-decomposer decomposed it like an ordinary work card.
3. The three pending proposals were **reworded as "Execute the approved mutation" work orders** — the pending-approval semantics were inverted into imperative instructions, with no provenance of the pending state preserved.
4. Child cards were dispatched to executing workers. Two mutations were **executed on the live external account** (a Google Ads account) without the approver ever approving; the third was in flight at detection.

No card-level field, marker, or hook in the decomposer, dispatcher, or worker preflight caused any lane to re-check for an actual approval before write-class tool calls were permitted.

## The gap (core, not profile)

1. **No approval-gate concept in the auto-decomposer.** A card whose assignee is the approver and whose body marks the work as pending approval is decomposed like an ordinary work card.
2. **Gating semantics are lost in rewording.** The decomposer rewrites pending proposals as imperative work-order text, so downstream lanes see an instruction, not a pending approval. Provenance of the pending-approval state is not preserved.
3. **No lane re-checks for an actual approval before non-dry-run calls.** Neither decomposer, dispatcher, nor worker preflight verifies explicit approver approval before write-class tool calls are permitted.

## Recommended fixes

1. **Card-level approval-gate flag the decomposer honors.** An explicit marker (e.g. a first-line `APPROVAL-GATED` in the card body, or a structured task field such as `gated: approval`): the auto-decomposer must not decompose such cards, and the dispatcher must not spawn workers that could execute their content.
2. **Worker pre-mutation approval-verification hook for gated tool surfaces.** Before permitting write-class tool calls on a profile whose tools are approval-gated, require recorded approver approval (a named chat reply or an approval comment on the card); if absent, fail closed into a `needs_input` block naming the appr
title: Gap: core kanban auto-decomposer lacks an approval-gate concept

Hi — reporting a reproducible desktop bug (Windows 11) with a clean root-cause trace and a locally verified fix. A community PR previously proposed a fix for this (#111503, closed unmerged); the bug is still live on v0.22.0.

## Environment
- Hermes v0.22.0 (commit e06df9c2ea), Windows 11, 175% display scaling, single display
- Appearance: frosted glass mode, material=under-window, scope=**sidebar only**, intensity 10%, fade 0%
  (`%APPDATA%/Hermes/translucency.json`: `{"intensity":10,"fade":0,"mode":"glass","material":"under-window","scope":"sidebar"}`)
- Reproduced on both the packaged app and the dev pipeline (vite renderer + isolated user-data dir + CDP) — not build-specific.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Set translucent glass with scope = sidebar only.
2. Quit and relaunch the desktop app (cold launch).
3. Sidebar renders fully opaque — no glass.
4. Drag a window edge to resize (or toggle any translucency setting, or switch light↔dark) → glass instantly appears.
5. Restart again → broken again until any resize.

## Expected vs actual
- Expected: sidebar glass applies as soon as the sidebar is mounted.
- Actual: `--glass-rail-edge` is measured and set to `0px` before the sidebar exists, and nothing re-measures it when the sidebar mounts. The glass surface width stays 0 → the sidebar paints opaque until some resize event forces a re-measure.

## Evidence (fresh reproduction)
- Cold boot with CDP polling: `--glass-rail-edge` stuck at `0px` for the whole boot; **zero window resize events** during boot; a synthetic `resize` event flips it to `260px` (= sidebar width) instantly.
- With the fix below: the seam flips `0px → 260px` at the exact same poll tick as the rail appearing (no resize events involved at that point). The single resize seen shortly after is just the window restoring its saved size, long after the seam was already correct.

## Root cause (apps/desktop/src/store/translucency.ts, v0.22.0)
- `startRailTracking()` runs when glass activates (store module evaluation precedes React render) and calls `measureRailEdge()` immediately. The sidebar has not mounted yet, so the measure finds nothing and sets `--glass-rail-edge: 0px`.
- The only re-measure triggers are the `window` `resize` listener and a `ResizeObserver` on the (not yet found) rail. A `ResizeObserver` cannot discover an element it never observed — so a late-mounted or remounted sidebar is never picked up.
- Net effect: in sidebar scope the glass width is 0 until any resize event (settings changes / appearance toggles also re-enter the tracking path).

## Fix shape (validated locally)
- Ported from #111503, whose diagnosis matches exactly: while rail tracking is active, observe child-list changes on `documentElement` and check identity only — when the tracked rail is still connected, do nothing (no geometry reads; streaming/tint churn must not force layout); when the rail is missing or disconnected and a `[data-slot="sidebar"]` exists, re-measure. Dis
title: [Bug] Windows Desktop: sidebar-scoped glass stays opaque after a cold launch until a window resize or settings change

## Bug Description
`auxiliary.<task>.extra_body` is forwarded unchanged to every `fallback_chain` entry. When the primary is a local OpenAI-compatible server that needs a server-specific field (e.g. `chat_template_kwargs` for Qwen on vLLM/llama.cpp), and it is unreachable, the fallback to Anthropic fails with a 400. So the fallback never works in exactly the situation it exists for.

## Steps to Reproduce
```yaml
providers:
  mylocal:
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:18000/v1   # nothing listening
    model: some-qwen
auxiliary:
  explain_command:
    provider: mylocal
    model: some-qwen
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:18000/v1
    extra_body:
      chat_template_kwargs:
        enable_thinking: false
    fallback_chain:
      - provider: anthropic
        model: claude-haiku-5-5
```
1. Stop the local server.
2. Trigger the task, e.g. "Explain" on a command approval in the desktop app (`llm.oneshot` → `run_oneshot(task="explain_command")`).

## Expected Behavior
The fallback request to Anthropic omits the primary's server-specific `extra_body` keys, and the explanation comes from Haiku.

## Actual Behavior
```
Couldn't explain: one-shot generation failed: Error code: 400 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'message': 'chat_template_kwargs: Extra inputs are not permitted'}}
```
Reproduced in isolation with throwaway `HERMES_HOME`s (local port unreachable vs. a stub server that logs request bodies):

| Config | Primary down → fallback | Primary up |
|---|---|---|
| task-level `extra_body` (above) | ❌ 400 from Anthropic | ✅ body carries `chat_template_kwargs` |
| same `extra_body` moved to `providers.mylocal.extra_body`, task `provider: custom:mylocal` | ✅ | ✅ body carries `chat_template_kwargs` |
| task-level `reasoning_effort: none` instead of `extra_body` | ✅ | ✅ |

The provider-level path already does the right thing: `_with_custom_endpoint_extra_body` resolves per destination, "so a fallback to another provider never inherits it". The task-level `extra_body` gets no such treatment.

## Suspected cause
`agent/auxiliary_client.py`: `_plan_fallback_candidate` → `_fallback_request_kwargs(..., effective_extra_body=...)` passes the primary's task-level `extra_body` to every candidate. On the Anthropic wire, `AnthropicAuxiliaryClient` forwards every non-`reasoning`/`response_format` key as passthrough (around L1775–1786), so `chat_template_kwargs` reaches `/v1/messages`.

Possible fixes, either would work:
- don't carry task-level `extra_body` onto a fallback whose provider/base_url differs from the primary unless the fallback entry declares its own `extra_body` (per-entry override), or
- strip known OpenAI-compat-only keys (`chat_template_kwargs`, …) on the Anthropic Messages passthrough, like `response_format` was handled in #100417.

## Workaround
Put the field on the provider entry (`providers.<name>.extra_body`) and reference it as `custom:<name>`, or use `reasoning_effort: none` if the server honours it.

## Environment
title: [Bug]: auxiliary.<task>.extra_body is forwarded to fallback_chain providers — chat_template_kwargs makes Anthropic fallback 400

## Bug Description

`_bounded_health_probe()` advertises a one-second route budget but can wait for the underlying health worker after that budget has expired. The timeout is caught **inside** a `ThreadPoolExecutor` context; leaving the context calls `Executor.__exit__ -> shutdown(wait=True)`.

This is a narrow follow-up to the optional health-probe mitigation in #57203 / #57254 / #68661, not a claim that all Desktop latency or SQLite problems have the same cause. I searched open/closed issues and PRs for `_bounded_health_probe`, executor cleanup and health deadlines; I did not find an existing report for this remaining context-manager wait.

## Affected Component

Dashboard/serve status route (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py`), optional HTTP Gateway health fallback.

## Environment

- Windows 11; CPython 3.14.7.
- Installed Hermes v0.22.0, commit `e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8`.
- The affected source is also present in current main observed at `0e427d788d253630d38a3a51cd76849e73cd6925`.
- Current `status.py` Git blob: `e58e429a063634dc819de8c74dc6821f98c11f25`; raw SHA-256: `15817402186f010fba182518ff5569700d84ac6437860cb9575465346283ba55`.

## Root Cause Analysis

[Current helper](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/0e427d788d253630d38a3a51cd76849e73cd6925/hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py#L248-L261):

```python
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as pool:
    future = pool.submit(_probe_gateway_health)
    try:
        return future.result(timeout=_GATEWAY_HEALTH_ROUTE_TIMEOUT)
    except concurrent.futures.TimeoutError:
        return False, None
```

The fallback return still exits the executor context. CPython's `Executor.__exit__` calls `self.shutdown(wait=True)`, so a running call is joined before the helper actually returns. The inner urllib timeout is not a route-level absolute deadline (e.g. it cannot make executor cleanup stop waiting for a delayed callee).

## Steps to Reproduce

The following is an **isolated original-function/dependency-seam test**, not a live HTTP/ASGI reproduction. It compiles the public source without importing/booting Hermes, uses its unchanged function CodeType and genuine stdlib threads, and supplies a finite event-blocking health dependency:

```python
import concurrent.futures, logging, pathlib, threading, time, types

path = pathlib.Path('hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py')
module = compile(path.read_bytes(), str(path), 'exec')
code = next(c for c in module.co_consts
            if isinstance(c, types.CodeType)
            and c.co_name == '_bounded_health_probe')
released = threading.Event()
probe = types.FunctionType(code, {
    'concurrent': __import__('concurrent'),
    '_probe_gateway_health': lambda: (released.wait(4.0), {'ok': True}),
    '_GATEWAY_HEALTH_ROUTE_TIMEOUT': 1.0,
    '_log': logging.getLogger('health-deadline-repro'),
})
timer = threading.Timer(1.35, released.set)
timer.start()
try:
    start = time.monotonic()
    result = probe()
    prin
title: [Bug]: /api/status one-second health fallback waits past its deadline in executor __exit__

# [Bug]: kimi-coding static catalog carries 8 retired ids and omits k3-256k — and k3-256k's context_length resolves to the wrong 256,000

## Bug Description

`hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py:204` lists 10 model ids for the `kimi-coding` provider. Only 2 of them appear in the endpoint's live roster. `k3-256k` is absent from the catalogue, and even when set manually in `config.yaml` its context window resolves to a **wrong** value.

## Evidence

Environment: Hermes Agent 0.21.7 (`71d34bad`), macOS 27.0.1 (Darwin 27.0.0 arm64), Python 3.14.7, `kimi-coding` configured with a valid coding-plan key (`KIMI_API_KEY` in `$HERMES_HOME/.env`).

Live authoritative roster — `GET https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/models` (2026-10-14) returns exactly 4 ids:

| id | context_length |
| --- | --- |
| `kimi-for-coding` | 1048576 |
| `kimi-for-coding-highspeed` | 262144 |
| `k3` | 1048576 |
| `k3-256k` | 262144 |

Static catalogue intersection with live roster = `{kimi-for-coding, kimi-for-coding-highspeed}` only.

- **Retired but still listed (8)**: `kimi-k3`, `kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k2.6`, `kimi-k2.5`, `kimi-k2-thinking`, `kimi-k2-thinking-turbo`, `kimi-k2-turbo-preview`, `kimi-k2-0905-preview`
- **Served but not listed (2)**: `k3`, `k3-256k`

Context-length resolution:

```python
from agent.model_metadata import get_model_context_length

get_model_context_length("k3-256k", base_url="https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1", provider="kimi-coding")
# Actual: 256000 (generic fallback)  —  Expected: 262144
```

`_ENDPOINT_SCOPED_CONTEXT` (`agent/model_metadata.py:593`) covers `k3` / `kimi-k3` / `kimi-k3-cot` but not `k3-256k`, so it falls through to the generic path, misses the models.dev lookup (the Kimi Code provider was renamed to `kimi-code-plan-*`), and lands on the 256,000 default.

## Verification trap for maintainers

This endpoint does **not** validate model ids. A request naming a non-existent model returns HTTP 200 with a normal completion, on both wires:

- OpenAI-compat: `POST https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/chat/completions` with `model: "fake-model-xyz"` → HTTP 200, `content: "PONG"`
- Anthropic: `POST https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/messages` with `model: "fake-model-xyz"` → HTTP 200

Any liveness check based on HTTP status, or a 1-token probe, will falsely "confirm" every retired id above. `GET /v1/models` is the only authority.

## Relation to existing reports

Catalogue-side overlap with #117909 / #87590 / #109895 / #105650; probe-side overlap with #127906.

**This report's increment**: the `k3-256k` context-length gap (not covered by #126224, which describes the opposite direction — `kimi-for-coding` being *under*-resolved) plus the id-validation trap above, which invalidates HTTP-status-based verification of this provider's catalogue.

## Requested

1. Land the catalogue fix so `k3` and `k3-256k` are selectable.
2. **Drop the 8 retired ids** — they are not in the live roster.
3. Add `k3-256k` → `262_144` to `_ENDPOINT_SCOPED_CONTEXT`.
title: [Bug]: kimi-coding static catalog carries 8 retired ids and omits k3-256k — and k3-256k's context_length resolves to the wrong 256,000

## Summary
Every `hermes chat` / profile CLI run prints `Warning: Unknown toolsets: messaging, moa, rl` when the user's `config.yaml` has these names under `platform_toolsets.cli`. The names appear to be left over from an older config (the list is written by `hermes tools` / migrations); they are not valid toolset names in the current `toolsets.py`, so the warning shows on every run and never goes away on its own.

## Observed
- Config (profile created by migration, `_config_version: 50`):
  ```yaml
  platform_toolsets:
    cli: [browser, clarify, code_execution, ..., messaging, moa, rl, ..., web]
  ```
- `chat -Q -q "say ok"` prints `Warning: Unknown toolsets: messaging, moa, rl`.
- Removing those three entries from `platform_toolsets.cli` makes the warning disappear; no other behaviour changed.

## Expected
Config migration should drop (or map) toolset names that no longer exist, or the warning should say which config key holds them and how to fix it. A warning that fires on every unattended run with no actionable hint also gets read as a tool restriction, which sent us debugging the wrong thing.

## Notes
Found while auditing a research profile. Seen on the default profile config too (same three names).
title: 'Unknown toolsets: messaging, moa, rl' warning on every run from stale platform_toolsets.cli entries

### Problem or Use Case

We run several agents on one kanban board. A worker writes a checkpoint comment before it stops, and the next worker picks the task up with `hermes kanban context <id>`.

`build_worker_context()` caps each comment at 2,048 characters (`_CTX_MAX_COMMENT_BYTES` in `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`), against 8,192 for the body and 4,096 for summary, error, metadata and result. `_ctx_cap` keeps the first 2,048 characters, so it is the end of the comment that goes, which in a checkpoint is usually the list of what is left to do. The next worker sees `… [truncated, N chars omitted]` and has to go back to `kanban show` for the rest, if it notices at all.

We first ran into this on 0.15.2; the caps are unchanged on main (0e427d7). The constants are named `_BYTES`, but `_ctx_cap` counts characters.

### Proposed Solution

- Cap the newest comment, or the newest few, at 8,192 characters (the same as the body) and leave older comments at 2,048. `_CTX_MAX_COMMENTS` already limits that section to the 30 most recent.
- Or make the per-comment cap configurable.

### Alternatives Considered

`hermes kanban show` prints comments in full, and that is our workaround today. But a worker has no reason to look past `context` unless it knows something was cut, and the marker is easy to miss in a long prompt. We could ask workers to stay under 2,048 characters, but the checkpoint is the one comment where the detail matters.

#109537 raises the body cap from 8K to 32K and leaves the comment cap unchanged.

### Feature Type

CLI improvement

### Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)
title: [Feature]: `kanban context` truncates each comment at 2,048 characters

### Bug Description

With no agent running, a photo (or other attachment) sent with the caption `/queue` or `/steer` and no other text gets the usage reply, and the attachment never reaches the agent. `/steer`'s reply even says "(no agent is running; sending as a normal message)", but nothing is sent.

While a turn is running, the same media-only `/queue` is accepted and queued with its photo (`_busy_queue_command`: "A /queue carrying media ... is valid with no prompt text"). So a screenshot queued just as the bot finishes its turn is lost.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Make sure the agent is idle in a Telegram chat.
2. Send a photo with the caption `/queue` (or `/steer`) and nothing else.

### Expected Behavior

The photo is sent to the agent as a normal turn, as an uncaptioned photo is, and as a busy `/queue` with that photo is queued.

### Actual Behavior

"Usage: /queue <prompt>" (or the idle `/steer` usage), and the photo is dropped. `/queue look at this` with the same photo works.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Debug Report

Not from a live bot: reproduced on current `main` (0e427d788d) through `GatewayRunner._handle_message` with an idle session and a `MessageEvent` carrying `media_urls`.

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.14

### Hermes Version

main @ 0e427d788d

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`gateway/run_inbound.py` `_hm_send_payload_as_turn` (idle `/queue` and `/steer`) returns the usage hint whenever the command text is empty, without looking at `event.media_urls`.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Show the usage hint only when there is neither text nor media; otherwise run the event (prefix stripped) as a normal turn.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
title: [Bug]: Idle /queue or /steer as a bare photo caption drops the photo and replies with usage

**Verified during a line-by-line audit (2026-10-14) of gateway/.** Quality is high overall (hmac.compare_digest everywhere, SSRF guards on most media paths, parameterised SQL). Two medium clusters worth fixing:

1. **MEDIUM — weixin media download redirects bypass SSRF/host allowlists** (`gateway/platforms/weixin.py:1124-1132`, `:371-382`): `_download_remote_media` runs `is_safe_url` once, then `_download_bytes` follows redirects by default (up to 10 hops) — an external URL can 302 to intranet/cloud-metadata. `_download_and_decrypt_media` checks the URL against `_WEIXIN_CDN_ALLOWLIST` but then downloads with a redirect-following session, so an allowlisted CDN host can bounce the request anywhere. This contradicts the per-hop re-validation standard in `relay/media.py` (`_RedirectPolicyHandler`) and `platforms/base.py`. Fix: `allow_redirects=False` or per-hop `is_safe_url`/allowlist re-check.

2. **MEDIUM — dynamic webhook subscriptions can self-grant script/cron/deliver** (`gateway/platforms/webhook.py:446-450`, `:392-411`): `_dynamic_route_allowed` validates secret/coalesce but does not restrict the high-privilege fields `script` (executes from scripts/), `cron_job`, `deliver_only`, `deliver`, `skills` — while `toolsets` is explicitly blocked from self-grant (GHSA-2fmg-cjqm-hhrj). If the agent can write `hermes webhook subscribe` payloads, `script`/`deliver` is a privilege surface equivalent to the blocked one. Fix: dynamic routes should ignore `script`/`cron_job`/`deliver*` exactly like `toolsets`.

Also (low): `authz_mixin.py:425-449` group `allow_from` non-empty grants without sender re-check (medium); `pairing.py` unlocked read-modify-write JSON; `control_socket.py` /tmp fallback TOCTOU + exception text in responses; `run_inbound_media.py:36-44` lexical `relative_to` traversal; quick-command `create_subprocess_shell` surface; `relay/media.py` and `qqbot/adapter.py` logging raw signed URLs; `whatsapp_cloud.py` downloads without the SSRF-safe client; `bluebubbles.py:580-588` empty-password compare_digest passthrough.
title: [Security] gateway: weixin media redirects bypass SSRF/CDN allowlist; dynamic webhook subscriptions can self-grant script/cron/deliver

body:
**Verified during a line-by-line audit (2026-10-14).** Three chained issues in pm/ where lock/state file values are used as path/env components without shape validation:

1. **HIGH — arbitrary directory deletion** (`pm/store.py:379-388`, `pm/install.py:289-292`): `lock.json` artifact `sha256` is concatenated into `fetch-{sha}` entry names with no `^[a-f0-9]{64}$ ` validation. A value like `../../../x` normalizes outside the store root; both `fetch_many`'s `shutil.rmtree(entry)` and `_remove_downloads` will then recursively delete attacker-chosen paths. Reproduced that normalization escapes the store root. Fix: fail-closed regex validation at `Lockfile.artifacts()`, and assert entry names are single path components before any remove.

2. **MEDIUM — process env injection** (`pm/lock.py:225-229`): `facts.json` `entry`/`env` used without the validation that `refresh_digests` applies — `entry` can traverse, and arbitrary `env` keys (LD_PRELOAD / DYLD_* / PATH) flow into every PM subprocess via `compose_env`. Fix: reuse the entry charset check and deny loader/path-class env keys.

3. **MEDIUM — https-only/loopback gate bypass** (`pm/downloader.py:49,62,293`): the loopback check is a string prefix test — `http://127.0.0.1:@evil.com/payload` passes (verified `startswith=True` while the real host is evil.com), allowing plaintext fetches to remote hosts. Fix: parse with `urllib.parse.urlsplit`, require scheme https and hostname in {127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost}, and reject userinfo.

Lower-severity siblings (filename traversal in `store.py:387`, generation parsing in `runtime.py:147-156`, `pm update --npm` missing `--ignore-scripts` in `cli.py:652`, publish race in `store.py:415-434`, `hash_url` scheme in `store.py:168-191`) can ride along in the same fix.
title: [Security] pm: lock.json sha256 not shape-validated -> path traversal to arbitrary rmtree (verified) + facts.json env injection + downloader loopback gate bypass

### Bug Description

A Telegram DM turn wedged for ~80 minutes with no reply and no log output after the `inbound message` line. The gateway process stayed healthy (Telegram polling, cron ticks, heartbeats all alive), so nothing recovered it. Later messages were silently queued behind the stuck turn (`Flushing text batch ...` with no `inbound message` line after it). Only a gateway restart cleared it, and the two user messages sent during the hang were lost.

Version 0.21.5, Windows 11, Python 3.14.7, single gateway, `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`, platform telegram.

### Evidence (gateway.log / agent.log, local time)

```
11:33:49 response ready ... (last good turn, session S)
11:34:41 background review of S done (last agent.log line for S)
12:01-12:08 cron job "weekly-retro": terminal(background=true, notify=true) launch call times out after 420.0s
12:10:50 cron delivery mirrored into telegram:<chat> session transcript
12:11:00 ERROR cron.scheduler: Job ...: agent resource teardown exceeded 10.0s; abandoning cleanup
12:18:34 inbound message: platform=telegram ... (344 chars, reply to the cron delivery)
         -> no `API call`, no `Turn ended`, no `response ready`, no row in state.db for this message
13:31:11 Flushing text batch ... (29 chars) -> queued, never logged as inbound
13:40    gateway_state.json: active_agents: 1, gateway_state: running; `hermes gateway status` OK
```

`gateway.log` and `agent.log` have no warning, no traceback and no watchdog line for the whole 80 minutes.

### Suspected cause (not proven: no stack dump was taken before restarting)

`_handle_message_with_agent` logs `inbound message` (`gateway/run_turn.py:2149`) and then awaits `_hmwa_resolve_session`, `_hmwa_prepare_turn` (session open, turn lease, transcript load, hygiene), and `hooks.emit("agent:start")` before it reaches `_run_agent`. The inactivity watchdog (`agent.gateway_timeout`, default 1800 s) is started only inside `_run_agent_start_turn_worker` (`run_turn.py:~3419`), so a stall in that pre-agent phase has no timeout at all and holds the session's running-agent sentinel forever. The 1800 s turn-lease wait (see #131578) would at least surface a "transient agent failure"; here nothing surfaced in 80 min, so the stall is somewhere without a bound.

Possibly related trigger: a cron agent that left an abandoned terminal/background session (same family as #137437: Windows background session, 420 s tool timeouts, then `agent resource teardown exceeded 10.0s; abandoning cleanup`). In this incident the cron teardown abandonment preceded the wedge by 7 minutes; the same abandonment also happened earlier the same day without a wedge, so it may only be a contributing factor.

### Expected

- The pre-agent phase of a turn should be bounded (or covered by the same inactivity watchdog), logging a wedged-turn stack dump and releasing the session when it expires.
- A message that arrives while the session is "busy" and is queued should produce a visible notice (busy a
title: [Bug]: Telegram turn wedges before the agent starts: no timeout, no reply, later messages silently queued (80 min)
