### Bug Description

`_carry_parent_timestamps` never fires on either in-place compaction path, because at both call sites it runs **after** the archive that deactivates every row it could use as a donor. Carried copies therefore fall back to `now_ts`, their `_display_dedupe_key` no longer matches the archived original, and `GROUP BY display_order` projects the same logical message twice.

The function's own docstring states the intent: *"Adopt the durable parent row's timestamp onto carried handoff rows so the re-inserted child row keeps the original's display identity (see `_display_dedupe_key`)."* It selects donors with:

```python
"SELECT id, role, content, timestamp, tool_call_id, tool_calls, tool_name FROM messages "
"WHERE session_id = ? AND active = 1 ORDER BY id"
```

But `hermes_state_messages.py::archive_and_compact` calls it *after* the archive:

```python
            else:
                conn.execute(_ARCHIVE_ACTIVE_SQL, (session_id,))   # active = 1 -> active = 0 for every row
            # Same identity carry as publish_compression_child (#59661): carried tail copies keep the
            # durable row's timestamp so display dedupe still collapses generations. Donors are active-only;
            # the rewound/archived originals above never donate, so this is a no-op for a clean compaction.
            self._carry_parent_timestamps(conn, session_id, compacted_messages)
            inserted, tool_calls_total = self._insert_message_rows(conn, session_id, compacted_messages)
```

`_ARCHIVE_ACTIVE_SQL` is `UPDATE messages SET active = 0, compacted = 1 WHERE session_id = ? AND active = 1`, so by the time the donor query runs, the map is empty **by construction**. The in-code comment already says so — *"this is a no-op for a clean compaction"* — but that no-op is exactly the bug: the copies it was written to protect are the ones that drift. `_archive_named_rows` (~L962-966) has the same order.

**Consequence.** A carried dict reaching the writer without a `timestamp` key — the normal shape for a message rebuilt from durable state rather than from a `_row_id`-carrying live dict — takes `now_ts` in `_insert_message_rows`:

```python
message_timestamp = _coerce_timestamp(msg.get("timestamp"), now_ts)
```

`_display_dedupe_key` includes `timestamp`:

```python
return _stable_tool_key(row) or (
    row["role"], dedupe_content, row["timestamp"], row["tool_call_id"], row["tool_calls"], row["tool_name"])
```

So the copy's identity (and `display_order`) differs from its archived original's. `_display_rows_from_conn` groups by `display_order` and `_DISPLAY_ACTIVE_CLAUSE` is `active = 1 OR compacted = 1`, which keeps the archived original visible — both rows project, and the message renders twice.

### Environment

- macOS 26.6 (desktop app), Hermes Agent checkout `97a9ae8ee5` (2026-10-11)
- `state.db` ~784 MB / 46,741 message rows / 1,217 sessions
- In-place compaction (`split_status=in_place_committed`), hermes-lcm driving `compress()`

### Steps
title: `_carry_parent_timestamps` is a no-op in both in-place compaction paths: the archive runs before its donor query, so carried copies drift to `now_ts` and one logical message renders twice

## Summary
The serve/cli startup paths now register shell hooks (#69825, #102681 fixed those), but the legacy `hermes dashboard` spawn — which is still what the Desktop app falls back to (`dashboard --no-open`) and can be pinned as a systemd unit ExecStart — hosts agent turns **in-process inside its uvicorn server** yet never calls `shell_hooks.register_from_config`. Result: every session served by that process runs with an empty hook registry.

## Evidence (current upstream main, not just our checkout)
- grep for register sites on origin/main finds them only in `cli.py`, gateway startup (`run_startup`), and `tui_gateway/server`; **no wiring at all** in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` / dashboard flow:
  `origin/main:agent/shell_hooks.py:4  |  origin/main:cli.py:3  |  origin/main:gateway/run_startup.py:4  |  origin/main:tui_gateway/server.py:2`

## Impact (observed live, two hosts side by side)
- Discord/gateway-served sessions fire approved hooks normally. Desktop/dashboard-hosted sessions on the same machine never do — no block/inject/audit output at all, even after `--accept-hooks` approval and a restart of both processes. Silent inertness is very hard to diagnose from user side (config looks correct in `hermes hooks list`, doctor clean).

## Workaround / proposed fix
- Modern spawn (`hermes serve`) registers within its flow — switching the unit would dodge this, but legacy dashboard fallback still hits it.
- Tested locally: mirror of `GatewayStartupMixin._register_config_hooks` added to `hermes_cli/web_server.py:_lifespan` (server-start-once point), +17 lines, never-raises try/except mirroring gateway startup shape; hooks fire immediately after restart for dashboard-hosted sessions. Caveat found while testing: it registers the launch profile's config only — per-profile agent construction may need its own call upstream.

Happy to PR this minimal fix if maintainers confirm scope (or prefer retiring the legacy spawn instead).
title: Legacy `dashboard` spawn never registers shell hooks — declarative config.yaml `hooks:` silently inert for Desktop-hosted sessions (follow-up to the serve/cli fixes in #69825/#102681)

### Summary

When a skill's auto-generated slash command is skipped (e.g. because it collides with a core
command), Hermes tells the user to use `/skill <name>` instead. That command does not exist:
there is no `CommandDef("skill")` in the command registry, and the `/skills` handler treats any
first argument as a Skills-Hub action. A colliding skill therefore has **no slash path at all**,
despite being advertised one.

### Reproduction

1. Take any skill whose name collides with a core command (e.g. a skill named `compact`).
   Observed log line:

   ```
   WARNING agent.skill_commands: Skill 'compact' generates slash command '/compact' which
   collides with a core Hermes command; skipping auto-registration. Use '/skill compact' instead.
   ```

2. Type `/skill compact` in the desktop composer.

3. Result:

   ```
   Unknown action: compact
   + the /skills Skills-Hub help panel (browse/search/install/...)
   ```

### Root cause

- `agent/skill_commands.py:441` returns advice `... use /skill {name}`;
- `agent/skill_commands.py:444-446` comment repeats the claim ("the skill stays loadable via
  /skill <name>");
- `agent/skill_commands.py:464-465` logs the same advice;
- but `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py:1689 handle_skills_slash` parses the first argument as a Hub
  action and prints `Unknown action: <name>` at line 1701 — it has no load-by-name branch;
- `hermes_cli/commands.py` has no `CommandDef("skill")` — the name is not a registry command;
- the gateway `command.dispatch` stage order (quick → plugin → bundle → skill → built-ins,
  `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`) finds nothing for `skill` and rejects with
  `4018 not a quick/plugin/bundle/skill command`.

A repo-wide search finds no `/skill <name>` loader — the only occurrences of the string are the
advice itself. The actual load path for a skill is its auto-generated `/<skill-slug>` command.

### Finding 2: the skill-command cache does not invalidate on disk changes

`agent/skill_commands.py:516-531 get_skill_commands()` caches per identity key
(platform, home, project) and returns the cached map whenever it exists — there is no
mtime/content check. Skills installed or edited while a backend is running never appear until
restart or an explicit `/reload-skills`. Observed timeline: skill installed 17:06–18:51, backend
up since 16:03 → `/alien-approach` rejected with 4018 at 21:37 → backend restart 22:33:59 →
command resolves. A directory-mtime (or content) tag on the scan cache — the way the plugin
projection already tags on plugin-name changes — would close this class.

### Related upstream work (searched 2026-10-13)

- #127976 — collision warning spam; quotes the same `Use '/skill <name>' instead.` advice but
  does not notice the advice itself is dead. This report adds that observation.
- #88064 — the auto-generated `/<skill>` invocation fails with the same
  `not a quick/plugin/bundle/skill command` text when `skills.external_dirs` poin
title: Skills: fallback advice points to non-existent `/skill <name>`; skill-command cache ignores disk changes until restart

body:
## Problem or Use Case

A Bot Mode room is a hub-and-spoke workspace: one coordinator Bot holds the context and dispatches, and specialists are pulled in by `@mention` when their domain is needed. Concretely, a 4-bot room (`chief`, `architect`, `inspector`, `research`) where the user wants `chief` to read every message and the other three to read only when named.

Today a room cannot express that. With no `@mention`, round 0 selects **every** member (`resolveGroupResponders`, `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-rounds.ts`), so each specialist pays a full model call to conclude the line is not theirs and answer `(pass)`. The only workaround is ceremony: prefix every message with `@chief` — and the moment the user forgets, the whole roster wakes again.

The waste is measurable: #98610 measured 122 no-op calls / 490 s / 8% of all model time in a five-bot room, all of it spent producing the word `(pass)`. But cost is not the ask. The ask is **control**: there is no way to say which member reads an unaddressed message in a room.

The closest existing primitive is the room hold (`holdDetection`, "Detect stop directives" in Group settings): the user can tell *individual* members to stop, and a held member stays quiet until it is mentioned again. It is per-member, manual, and re-armed by the next mention, so it cannot express "this room has one reader".

## Proposed Solution

An opt-in, **room-level** setting, stored on the room record beside `holdDetection`:

- `unmentioned: all (shipped default) | owner`, plus the owner member when `owner` is chosen.
- `all` is exactly today's behavior. A room that never opens the setting stores no field and behaves byte-for-byte as it does now.
- `owner` selects the configured member in round 0 when the user's message mentions nobody. An explicit `@mention`, a title mention, or `@everyone`/`@all` still wins exactly as today.
- Only turn **selection** changes. Watermarks, the delta each member reads on its own turn, round order, and every existing cap are untouched.
- Surfaces: a control in **Group settings** (next to "Detect stop directives") plus i18n; `website/docs/user-guide/bot-mode.md:165` updated — the bullet that currently reads "everyone responds when nobody is mentioned" is the line whose meaning changes.
- Shape: one resolver consulted inside `resolveGroupResponders` (still the single decision point today), the room field carried through `durableGroupChatRooms`, and behavior-contract tests for default / configured / mention-precedence / room-without-policy.
- Rooms may become gateway-hosted (#95163); the same selection contract should be reusable by the hosted driver, and #125258 already anticipates a host-declared `active_member_ids`.

Per-room limits (#92213) establish the storage semantics this would follow: absent inherits the shipped default, an untouched room stores nothing.

### The question this issue is really asking

Bot Mode group rooms got a standing ruling in #98610 (declined):

> Bot Mo
title: [Feature]: Bot Mode rooms — route unmentioned turns to a configured reader (opt-in, shipped default unchanged)

body:
## Feature Description

The Feishu adapter can **receive** real mentions but can never **send** one. Any `@Name` an agent writes in a reply goes out as literal text: the receiving instance's `require_mention` admission gate sees no mention entity and silently drops the message. In a multi-instance setup this deadlocks bot-to-bot group collaboration entirely.

## Why it matters (our production evidence)

We run 8 Hermes instances (one Feishu app per profile) in one shared group, exactly the setup `FEISHU_ALLOW_BOTS` + mention gating is designed for. Timeline verified today with the Feishu API and each profile's `state.db`:

1. A bot replies in the group with text containing `@平和` (another bot's display name). Feishu API shows the message with `mentions: []` — no mention entity, just characters.
2. The receiving gateway drops it (bot sender + no self-mention → admission fails). The drop is logged at DEBUG level, so it is invisible by default — it looks like "Feishu doesn't deliver bot messages", but the platform does deliver them; the gate is ours.
3. Across **5 weeks** of group traffic, not a single bot-authored message entered any other profile's conversation context. Humans in the group see the replies and assume the agents are talking to each other; they are not.

Root cause asymmetry: `FEISHU_ALLOW_BOTS=mentions/all` makes the **receiving** side mention-aware, but the **sending** side has no code path that maps `@Name` → `open_id` → `<at>` post element. Half a protocol is implemented.

## Proposed Solution

Native outbound mention resolution in the Feishu adapter, e.g.:

- a display-name → `open_id` map (config `feishu.bot_mention_map` or equivalent — note repo policy prefers `config.yaml` over new env vars),
- rewrite outbound `@Name` into an `at` post element (`{"tag":"at","user_id":...}`), keeping the current plain-text rendering when the name is unmapped,
- keep mentions alive through the markdown-table → plain-text fallback path instead of silently stripping them.

## Three open PRs already implement this

- #29662 — `FEISHU_MENTION_ALIASES` outbound conversion + several companion fixes (May 21, 2 review comments, then silence)
- #64234 — `@BotName` → `<at user_id>` conversion in outbound bodies (Jul 14)
- #124952 — `feishu.bot_mention_map` with placeholder pipeline, longest-first name matching, chunk-boundary handling, byte-identical output when unconfigured (Sep 27)

All three are open, non-draft, unmerged, with essentially no review movement. Rather than a fourth implementation, could maintainers evaluate merging one of these (or state which design is preferred so the others can be rebased onto it)? Happy to test any of them against our 8-instance group.

## Alternatives Considered

- Workaround we run today: a helper script calls the Feishu API directly with a real `<at user_id="...">` tag embedded, bypassing the Hermes outbound path. It works (verified end-to-end: `mentions: [1]` → message lands in the target profile's session), but
title: [Feishu] Outbound @Name is plain text, so mention-gated bots can never be addressed — bot-to-bot group collaboration is deadlocked (3 open PRs since May)

## Incident: gateway restart loop after unclean death strands cron; stale async-delegation delivery burns provider quota

Reporting a two-part outage observed 2026-10-13/14 on a Linux source install (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent`, profile `default`, systemd user service). One fix is in PR **#138342** (part 1); part 2 is analysis + the mitigation applied on the host.

### Part 1 — permanent restart loop after unclean death + recycled pid (fixed by #138342)

**What happened.** The host gateway was SIGKILLed at 22:20 (lifecycle ledger: *"exited UNCLEANLY (no exit path ran — SIGKILL / OOM / VM death)"*; the host was under memory pressure — 8.1 GB swap in use at the previous recorded death). It left its rendezvous record behind (`~/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/host-gateway.json`) carrying **neither `createTime` nor `startTime`** — the legacy format from before those fields existed. The dead gateway's **pid 1842 was recycled** by an unrelated process on the host (`/usr/bin/alloy`, a monitoring daemon).

Because `_same_incarnation` treats a missing `create_time` as a match, `liveness_is_proven()` proved the recycled pid "alive" forever. Every restart then dialed the recorded owner's control socket, got no answer, and refused to start with the *transient* verdict — the one the supervisor is told to retry:

```
окт 13 23:19:16 hermes[64031]: ⏳ A gateway already owns this host and has not published its served set yet.
окт 13 23:19:16 hermes[64031]:    PID 1842 (launched by profile 'default'; serves: not published yet (its control socket has not answered))
окт 13 23:19:23 systemd[1743]: hermes-gateway.service: Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 221.
```

**223 restart attempts in ~75 minutes**, each failing after ~8 s — while the cron scheduler (hosted by the gateway) was dead. All 11 scheduled jobs stalled from 22:20 until the record was cleared by hand at 23:35.

**Root cause.** The module's own invariant — *"the record proves an OWNER exists (PID + createTime)"* — holds only for records that actually carry `createTime`. For the legacy format the liveness check degrades to "is this pid number alive", which a recycled pid answers for a process unrelated to Hermes; the control-socket dial is the only real proof, and its failure was treated as the never-expiring boot race.

**Fix (PR #138342).** The "owner exists, served set unknown" verdict is now bounded **for unfalsifiable records only**: once the record's 90 s boot grace has expired with the socket still silent, the owner is treated as gone and the caller may take the host over. Records with incarnation proof keep the old behaviour (a wedged owner holds the host lock; takeover could not succeed anyway), and a fresh unprovable record keeps the boot-race verdict. 6 new unit tests cover the outage shape, the boot race, provable records, the happy path, and the `decide()`-level outcome.

### Part 2 — stale async-delegation completion re-runs a full turn and burns provider quota (analysis; mitigated
title: Gateway restart loop after unclean death + recycled pid strands cron; stale async-delegation delivery burns provider quota

### Summary

`delegate_task` children dispatched in one coordinator turn share that turn's `CredentialPool` object. When their Anthropic OAuth access token expires, each child's 401 recovery force-refreshes the shared entry, even when a sibling has already rotated it. Each refresh POST revokes the access token the siblings now hold. The children then trade `401 OAuth access token has been revoked` errors until each one reaches the 2-refresh cap and dies. The cap never resets inside a child's single long turn, and reaching it ends the session even when another pool row has room.

The per-request refresh bug in #118379 (PR #123361) killed two more sessions on the same day. I commented the evidence there. The patch below fixes both and includes tests.

### Environment

- Hermes `main` at `503a6b60e5` (2026-10-06), native Windows 11, gateway with Telegram.
- Provider `anthropic` (`anthropic_messages`, `claude-opus-5-5`). The credential pool holds 3–4 `hermes_pkce` OAuth rows (`fill_first`). Access tokens live 8 h.
- `agent.api_max_retries: 10`. Long `delegate_task` children: each is one turn lasting hours, and several children run from the same coordinator turn.

### What happened (2026-10-14, local time UTC+8, `logs/agent.log`, trimmed)

Three children (sessions `…_e25526`, `…_e7e9eb`, `…_44655e`) leased pool entry `562a87`. The first 401 was an ordinary expiry. All 14 later 401s were "revoked": each refresh by one child revoked the token the other two had just adopted. After every refresh the next call got a **429**, not a 401, so the refreshed key authenticated. The child then waited out `Retry-After` (600 s), and that wait is where the gaps come from.

```
13:49:47 ERROR chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 401 - … 'OAuth access token has expired. …'
13:49:48 INFO  [20261014_115550_e25526] run_agent: Credential auth failure — refreshed pool entry 562a87
13:49:49 ERROR chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 429 - … 'rate_limit_error' …
13:49:49 WARNING [20261014_115550_e25526] conversation_loop: Retrying API call in 600.0s (attempt 6/10) provider=anthropic …
13:50:03 ERROR chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 401 - … 'OAuth access token has been revoked.'
13:50:04 INFO  [20261014_115413_e7e9eb] run_agent: Credential auth failure — refreshed pool entry 562a87
13:50:05 WARNING [20261014_115413_e7e9eb] conversation_loop: Retrying API call in 600.0s (attempt 6/10) provider=anthropic …
13:56:23 ERROR … 401 … 'OAuth access token has been revoked.'
13:56:23 INFO  [20261014_115412_44655e] run_agent: Credential auth failure — refreshed pool entry 562a87
13:59:51 INFO  [20261014_115550_e25526] run_agent: Credential auth failure — refreshed pool entry 562a87
14:00:07 INFO  [20261014_115413_e7e9eb] run_agent: Credential auth failure — refreshed pool entry 562a87
14:06:26 INFO  [20261014_115412_44655e] run_agent: Credential auth failure — refreshed pool entry 56
title: [Bug]: delegate_task children sharing an Anthropic OAuth pool revoke each other's token on 401, then die at a refresh cap that never resets or rotates

### Bug Description

In the classic CLI, with native image input (a vision model, `/image` or a pasted image), `/history` prints the image turn as a Python list repr including the image's base64 data URL, e.g. `[{'type': 'text', 'text': 'describe this\n\n[Image attached at: …]'}, {'type': 'image_url', 'image_url': {'url': 'data:image/png;base64,iVBOR…`. With a real photo the 400-char preview is mostly base64 and the caption can be cut off. The `/resume` recap shows the same row as `describe this … [image]`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a model with native image input in the CLI.
2. Attach an image (`/image photo.png` or paste one) and send "describe this".
3. Run `/history`.

### Expected Behavior

`[You #1]` shows the text plus `[image]`, as the `/resume` recap does.

### Actual Behavior

The Python repr of the content-parts list, including the base64 data URL.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

Not from a live session: reproduced on current `main` (0e427d788d) by calling `HermesCLI.show_history` on a user row built by `build_native_content_parts`, as `_chat_stage_user_message` stores it.

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.14

### Hermes Version

main @ 0e427d788d

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`hermes_cli/cli_session_mixin.py` `show_history` previews `str(content)`; native image turns keep the parts list from `build_native_content_parts` (`hermes_cli/cli_chat_turn_mixin.py`) as the message content.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Use `_user_display_text` (`hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py`), which the `/resume` recap already uses for these rows.

## Summary

After upgrading to an environment that has `httpx2==2.12.0` (the pin Hermes carries for the `mcp` extra since `bc8545bd1a`, "bump httpx2/httpcore2 2.7.0 -> 2.12.0 for the audit advisories"), any HTTP MCP server whose `tools/list` response arrives as a **single SSE event larger than 1 MiB** becomes unconnectable.

The failure is deterministic, but the reported error is a red herring:

```
$ hermes mcp test <server>
  ✗ Connection failed (12.3s): SSE stream ended without a response
```

The real cause, swallowed by the MCP SDK, is:

```
httpx2.SSEError: Server-sent event exceeded the 1048576 byte limit.
```

Hermes then parks the server (`MCP server '<x>' failed initial connection after 3 attempts, parking until a reconnect is requested`), and the desktop Catalog shows "The server refused the connection." Nothing about the token, the URL, or the network is wrong.

## Root cause

1. `httpx2/_config.py` (2.12.0):

   ```python
   DEFAULT_MAX_EVENT_SIZE_BYTES = 1024 * 1024
   ```

   enforced in `httpx2/_sse.py::_SSEEventDecoder._check_size()`:

   ```python
   raise SSEError(f"Server-sent event exceeded the {self._max_event_size} byte limit.")
   ```

   `httpx2 2.9.1` (the last release below 2.12) has no `max_event_size` in `httpx2/_sse.py` at all, so this is a new hard cap, not a pre-existing one. It is still present in `httpx2 2.13.1`. No env var or config knob is documented for it, and `EventSource.__init__` just defaults to the constant.

2. `mcp 2.0.0` builds the SSE reader with the default limit and never passes one:

   `mcp/client/streamable_http.py` -> `event_source = EventSource(response)`

3. `mcp/client/streamable_http.py::_handle_sse_response` wraps the iteration in a bare `except Exception:` that only logs `SSE stream ended` at DEBUG, then synthesizes `MCPError(CONNECTION_CLOSED, "SSE stream ended without a response")`. So the `SSEError` never reaches Hermes, and at default log levels the user sees a generic "no response".

Net effect: with `httpx2==2.12.0` pinned, `max_event_size` is not reachable from Hermes or the SDK, and every MCP server with a >1 MiB single-event `tools/list` (large OpenAPI-backed servers, e.g. Cloudflare's `https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp?codemode=false`, which returns ~3,700 tools in one ~3.6 MB event) is dead on arrival.

## Why it shows up as a sudden break

It only manifests once the dependency environment is rebuilt. If the runtime already has an older `httpx2` (e.g. 2.7.0), the same MCP server connects fine; after an update that produces a fresh environment with 2.12.0, that server stops connecting with no config change on the Hermes or server side. Same tree, same `mcp==2.0.0`, different `httpx2` -> different outcome.

## Reproduction

1. Configure any HTTP MCP server whose `tools/list` is one >1 MiB SSE event. Public example:

   ```yaml
   mcp_servers:
     cf:
       url: https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp?codemode=false
   ```

2. `hermes mcp test cf` -> `Connection failed: SSE stream ended wit
title: httpx2==2.12.0's 1 MiB per-SSE-event cap silently breaks MCP servers with a large tools/list (reported as "SSE stream ended without a response")

## Environment

- Hermes Agent commit `41cd7b649d0980c57620035af736f91be10dae79` (2026-10-12)
- Windows 11, native (git-bash), Python 3.14.7

## Config

```yaml
model:
  default: "deepseek-v4.1-flash"
  provider: "opencode-go"
auxiliary:
  title_generation:
    provider: "nous"                     # Nous Portal
    model: "stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free"
    model_upgrade_enabled: true          # default
```

## Symptom

Some turns print:

```
⚠ Auxiliary title generation failed: HTTP 400: {"model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash"}
```

1. The model named in the error is the **main** model (`deepseek-v4.1-flash`), not the pinned aux model (`stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free`).
2. The response body is a bare `{"model": ...}` — matching the Nous Portal error envelope. `deepseek-v4.1-flash` is an opencode-go model; the Portal does not serve it (`GET https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/models` returns 423 ids, none matching).
3. Re-pinning `auxiliary.title_generation.{provider,model}` does **not** change the model name that gets sent: pointing it at opencode-go instead produces `{"model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash"}` / `Model is unavailable`.

=> the stage-2 upgrade appears to resolve the **provider from the pin** while keeping the **model name from the main route**.

## Frequency

Intermittent — roughly 3 of 6 identical CLI runs.

## Localization evidence

Disabling only the upgrade (`auxiliary.title_generation.model_upgrade_enabled: false`, instant derived title kept):

```bash
for i in 1 2 3; do hermes chat -q "回两字：测$i" 2>&1 | grep -icE "Auxiliary .* failed"; done
# 0
# 0
# 0
```

So the bug is in the stage-2 upgrade path — `agent/title_generator.py` (`_model_title_upgrade_enabled()`, the deferred upgrade thread → `agent.auxiliary_client.call_llm`) — not in the instant title derivation.

## Suspected code paths

- `agent/title_generator.py` — the upgrade thread's resolution of `auxiliary.title_generation` (are provider and model read from the same place?)
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py` — aux route resolution: does it fall back to the main model name even when the task is pinned?

## Related observation (likely a separate bug)

With the main provider set to opencode-go, any aux task left at `provider: "auto"` (= inherit the main model) returns:

```
HTTP 400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"MissingSessionID","message":"Request is missing x-opencode-session ..."}}
```

opencode-go requires the `x-opencode-session` header — verified directly against the endpoint: without it → `400 MissingSessionID`; with it → `200`. The header is attached only on the main conversation path (`agent/opencode_affinity.py`); the aux path does not attach it, so every aux task fails under opencode-go. Workaround: pin all aux tasks to another provider.

## Impact

Title regression (falls back to the derived title) plus log noise; the same route resolution may affect other aux tasks, so filing it here.
title: auxiliary.title_generation: stage-2 model upgrade sends the MAIN model name to the aux provider (intermittent HTTP 400)

## Summary

On Windows, a **catalog plugin's dependency never advances across `hermes update`**: each new PM generation is built by *seeding* the previous generation's `uv.lock`, and `uv` "retains its compatible versions", so a pin resolved once (here `hindsight-embed 0.10.2`) travels forward forever — even after a compatible fix (0.10.3, released 2026-10-08) ships. On this machine that means the Hindsight memory plugin's daemon can no longer start after any update that regenerates the environment, and memory tools fail until manual repair.

## Mechanism (read from the shipped code)

- `pm/packages.py` → `PackageSet.apply` (~l.460-476): reads prior facts, then
  `seed = Path(prior["resolved_lock"]) if members and prior.get("resolved_lock") else project / "uv.lock"` and calls
  `lock_and_sync(..., seed_lock=seed, frozen=repair or not members)`.
- `pm/workspace.py` → `lock_and_sync` (l.339-374): writes the **seed lock bytes** as the new workspace `uv.lock`
  (comment: *"uv retains its compatible versions"*), then `environment.sync(root, extras=extras, frozen=False)`.
- Net effect: a plugin requirement `hindsight-embed>=0.10.1,<1` resolved on 2026-10-02 (when 0.10.2 was latest) is
  re-carried by every later generation, because 0.10.2 still satisfies the specifier. The catalog plugin's own
  `pyproject.toml` comment explicitly anticipates picking up *"the release after 0.10.2"* — it never does.

Verified on the machine: generation built 2026-10-02 → `uv.lock` pins `hindsight-embed 0.10.2`; generation rebuilt by
the 2026-10-13 `hermes update` → the fresh `workspace/uv.lock` **again** pins `hindsight-embed 0.10.2` /
`hindsight-client 0.10.2` (facts.json chain: `resolved_lock` of the previous generation becomes the seed of the next).

## Impact (Windows 11, `local_embedded`)

1. `hindsight-embed 0.10.2` lacks `_strip_parent_interpreter_env`, so the plugin takes its legacy workaround path
   (`embedded.py::_start_daemon_in_clean_child`): spawn `sys.executable -c "<start snippet>"` with
   `PYTHONPATH`/`PYTHONHOME`/`VIRTUAL_ENV` stripped.
2. Under the current PM layout the plugin packages live in `installs/<id>/environments/<hash>/venv/site-packages`
   and are reachable in-process only via the PM-injected path; the scrubbed child interpreter therefore cannot
   import them:
   `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hindsight_embed'` →
   `RuntimeError: Failed to start the Hindsight daemon for profile 'hermes'`.
3. Every cold daemon start fails ⇒ `hindsight_recall` / `hindsight_retain` error for the session
   (`{"error": "Failed to search memory: Failed to start the Hindsight daemon for profile 'hermes'"}`),
   repeated until a manual repair: install `hindsight-embed>=0.10.3` into the current generation venv, provide an
   import path for the helper child, restart the daemon.

## Why it can't be repaired in place locally

Running `uv lock --upgrade-package hindsight-embed --upgrade-package hindsight-client` inside the generation

### Bug Description

**TL;DR: with `dashboard.public_url` declared, the browser login entries (`/login`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/native/authorize`) still allocate the host-only PKCE cookie on the request's own origin, while the OAuth callback is pinned to `public_url`. Opening any of those entries from loopback sets a cookie the callback can never read → `400 Missing PKCE state cookie`.**

Two pieces of the shipped code contradict each other:

1. `_redirect_uri()` treats the operator-declared `public_url` as the callback's complete authority:

   ```python
   public_url = _prefix_mod.resolve_public_url()
   if public_url:
       return f"{public_url}/auth/callback"
   ```

2. The PKCE cookie is **host-only** — `cookies.py::_common_attrs()` sets `httponly` / `samesite` / `path` and never `domain`.

So a login started on `127.0.0.1:9119` writes `__Host-hermes_session_pkce` for `127.0.0.1`, then hands the browser to the IDP with `redirect_uri=https://<public>/auth/callback`. The browser will not send a `127.0.0.1` cookie to `<public>`, so `auth_callback()`'s `read_pkce_cookie()` comes back empty and the request dies at:

```python
if not pkce_raw:
    _audit(request, AuditEvent.LOGIN_FAILURE, reason="missing_pkce_cookie")
    raise _http(400, "Missing PKCE state cookie")
```

### Why this is a code-level contradiction, not a deployment preference

`_redirect_uri()` already assumes the entire flow happens on `public_url`; the entries never enforce that. Nothing in `dashboard_auth` reconciles a loopback request origin with a declared `public_url` — `prefix.py` carries no loopback handling, and the only loopback logic in `routes.py` is `_validate_loopback_redirect_uri()` for RFC 8252 *native* callbacks, a different path.

That is also why the desktop app works on the same host while a browser does not: the native flow validates an RFC 8252 loopback `redirect_uri` and finishes on the loopback broker (origin-consistent), whereas the browser flow always posts back to `public_url`.

### Related but distinct

- `#126061` — PKCE cookie 10-minute TTL expiring mid-login.
- `#127100` — scheme detection behind a non-trusted proxy picking the wrong `SameSite`.
- `#101594` — MCP OAuth with a dead `public_url` origin (missing port).
- `#93981` / `#100438` — earlier `public_url`-forced-gating breakage for the desktop app.

None of them is the loopback-entry vs `public_url`-callback origin mismatch.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a reverse-proxied dashboard — e.g. `HERMES_DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_URL=https://dash.example.test:8443`, proxy → `127.0.0.1:9119`.
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:9119/login` in a browser on that host.
3. Pick a provider: the browser goes to the IDP with `redirect_uri=https://dash.example.test:8443/auth/callback`.
4. The IDP returns to `https://dash.example.test:8443/auth/callback` → `400 Missing PKCE state cookie`.

### Expected

A loopback navigation into a login entry should be moved onto the callback origin **before** the host-only PKCE cookie is alloc
title: [Bug]: Dashboard browser login from loopback dead-ends with "Missing PKCE state cookie" when public_url is set

### Problem or Use Case

`resolveEditor()` in `ui-tui/src/lib/editor.ts` is a mixed-world function: `env.PATH` and the
`platform` argument are simulated-world inputs, but candidate probing uses host-bound
`accessSync()`/`spawnSync()`. Its output can therefore be observably mixed-dialect — e.g. a
`win32`-joined candidate list returned for a `linux` target on a Windows host.

No caller consumes that difference today (production always passes `process.platform`; the two
production call sites are `openInEditor()` in `editor.ts` and the `resolveEditor` call in
`app/useComposerState.ts`), so this is latent, not a live bug. It is the remaining "two worlds"
seam in the terminal-setup path family that #79495 / #79497 closed everywhere else.

### Proposed Solution

Purify the function behind an injected probe:

1. Inject an `exists(path)` access probe (the same pattern as `fileOps`) instead of calling
   `accessSync` directly.
2. Select `delimiter` and the path module from the **target** platform when joining PATH entries
   and candidates.
3. Rewrite `editor.test.ts` fixtures as declarative exists tables with target-platform paths.

Acceptance criteria:

- `resolveEditor()` performs no direct host filesystem calls; the dialect of every produced path
  is determined by the target `platform` alone.
- `editor.test.ts` is green on both Windows and POSIX hosts without host-directory fixtures.
- Behavior at the two production call sites is unchanged (`process.platform` passthrough).

### Alternatives Considered

- **Literal `delimiter` swap with the current real-directory fixtures — rejected.** Windows drive
  letters are `:`-containing and the probe must hit a real filesystem; a delimiter patch is
  physically broken, not merely untested. (This is why #79497 documented the boundary instead of
  fixing it, and why the issue's "path syntax" wording must not be read that way.)
- **Leave as-is.** Works today because production always passes `process.platform`, but it is
  exactly the class of host dependence #79495 reported; leaving it invites the next
  host-dependent test failure.
- **No test may claim** a Windows host can simulate a POSIX PATH fixture with real host
  directories until the probe is injected.

### Feature Type

Developer experience (tests, docs, CI)

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)

N/A
title: [Feature]: Purify resolveEditor() with an injected exists probe (last mixed-world seam)

### Problem or Use Case

When a Hermes profile delegates work to another profile through Kanban, the handoff can become effectively invisible in the originating Desktop conversation. The coordinating profile may not visibly follow up, leaving the user unsure whether the work is queued, running, blocked, or finished.

As a user, I want to see:
- Which profile owns the delegated task and whether it has been picked up.
- How long it has been queued or running.
- The latest meaningful progress update or blocker.
- Whether the task needs my input or has failed.
- Whether the worker has finished but the coordinating profile has not yet reviewed and returned the result.

Currently, I have to switch to the Kanban board to investigate. Desktop has enough space to communicate this within the conversation, and already has a disclosure-based task/status area above the composer, including “Previous tasks.”

The originating profile should remain visibly accountable for bringing the result back. Worker completion alone does not mean my original request has been answered.

This is a product/design proposal for discussion. Missed coordinator follow-up is a reported symptom; its specific cause has not been reproduced or diagnosed here.

### Proposed Solution

Extend the existing above-composer task/status area with a session-scoped **Delegated work** section. Use the same interaction model rather than adding a separate monitoring pane.
Keep delegated work distinct from the local todo checklist, and do not bury active handoffs under “Previous tasks.”
### Suggested presentation
Illustrative display, not real task data:
```text
▾ Delegated work · 1 running · 1 needs input
  @research       Compare providers
                  Running 8m · Last update 40s ago
                  Checking API write capabilities
  @business-ops   Review invoice discrepancies
                  Needs input · Awaiting your decision
▸ Previous tasks
```
### Expected behaviour
- Keep a summary visible whenever the conversation has outstanding handoffs, even while the coordinating profile is idle.
- When collapsed, retain meaningful counts and attention states.
- Expand in place to show profile, task title, canonical status, elapsed time, last activity, and the latest meaningful milestone or blocker.
- Make “Open in Kanban” an optional secondary action, not a requirement for seeing progress.
- Distinguish “Result ready — awaiting coordinator” from “Reported back.” These can be presentation/acknowledgment states rather than new Kanban columns.
- Keep outstanding results visible until the coordinator reports back; move acknowledged/completed handoffs into collapsed history.
- Represent unavailable or stale data honestly. A heartbeat indicates liveness, not substantive progress; missing activity is not automatically failure.
- Avoid fabricated completion percentages, ETAs, and recurring unchanged-status chat messages.
### Suggested approach for discussion
Reuse canonical Kanban task state, timestam
title: [Feature]: Desktop: surface cross-profile delegated work in the conversation’s task/status area

### Bug Description

**TL;DR: `scan_sessions()` calls `list_sessions_rich()` without `include_archived=True`, so every archived session is invisible to the scanner.** Lifetime totals (`total_tool_calls`, `total_terminal_calls`, `total_errors`, …) and per-session maxima (`max_tool_calls_in_session`, …) only reflect the *unarchived* tail of the history. Unlocks are sticky in `state.json` while progress is recomputed on every scan, so the UI keeps rendering earned badges while their progress silently collapses back toward the threshold.

`archived` is a **sidebar visibility** flag. `_session_filter_where()` defaults to `include_archived=False` precisely so the session list does not show archived rows — the achievements scan inherited that default.

### Where

`plugins/hermes-achievements/dashboard/plugin_api.py` → `scan_sessions()`:

```python
sessions_meta = db.list_sessions_rich(limit=db_limit, include_children=True, project_compression_tips=False)
```

No `include_archived=True`, so `hermes_state_sessions.py::_session_filter_where()` appends `s.archived = 0`.

### Why #112273 does not cover this

#112273 fixed a *different* mechanism: message rows deactivated **inside** one session (rewind `active=0`, compaction `compacted=1`). That fix is the `include_compacted=True` argument to `get_messages()`. It never touches `sessions.archived`, which hides the **whole session** regardless of its message rows.

On the install where this was measured, archived sessions are not compression continuations at all — `end_reason = 'compression'` matches **0** of them. They are ordinary lifecycle ends:

| `end_reason` | sessions |
|---|---|
| `session_reset` | 169 |
| `startup_orphan_reap` | 125 |
| `cron_complete` | 121 |
| `agent_close` | 91 |
| `cli_close` | 69 |
| `(none)` | 56 |
| `ws_orphan_reap` | 12 |
| `tui_shutdown` | 4 |
| `webhook_complete` | 1 |
| `session_switch` | 1 |

### Measured impact

Real install, `state.db` (`hidden = 0`):

| Scope | Sessions | Σ `tool_call_count` |
|---|---|---|
| `archived = 0` — what the scan sees | **70** | **2,219** |
| `archived = 1` — invisible to the scan | **649** | **37,921** |
| total | 719 | 40,140 |

The snapshot served to the UI reported `scan_meta.sessions_total = 70` and a lifetime `total_tool_calls` in the low thousands, while the same payload kept 54/60 badges unlocked from `state.json`. The result is internally contradictory by construction: unlocked badges whose displayed progress sits below their own first tier.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable the bundled achievements dashboard.
2. Accumulate history, then let sessions end normally / archive old ones (`sessions.archived = 1`).

# 上报：auxiliary.title_generation 升级阶段间歇把「主模型名」发到 aux provider

**环境**：Hermes Agent `41cd7b6`（Mon Oct 12 01:43:33 2026），Windows 11 原生（git-bash），Python 3.14.7

## 复现配置

```yaml
model:
  default: "deepseek-v4.1-flash"     # 主模型
  provider: "opencode-go"
auxiliary:
  title_generation:
    provider: "nous"                  # Nous Portal
    model: "stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free"
    model_upgrade_enabled: true       # 默认值，问题在此路径
```

## 现象

部分 CLI 回合打印：

```
⚠ Auxiliary title generation failed: HTTP 400: {"model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash"}
```

三个可疑点：

1. 报错里的模型名是**主模型**（`deepseek-v4.1-flash`），不是 pin 的 aux 模型（`stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free`）。
2. 响应体是**光秃秃的 `{"model": ...}`** —— 与 Nous Portal 的错误信封一致；而 `deepseek-v4.1-flash` 是 opencode-go 的模型，Portal 上不存在（`GET https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/models` 列 423 个，无此 id）。
3. 把 aux 的 provider/model 改成 opencode-go 后，报错变成同一个模型的另一种 400（`{"model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash"}` / `Model is unavailable`），说明**换 pin 并不能改变被发出去的模型名**。

推断：stage-2 升级线程解析路由时，取的是 **pin 的 provider + 主模型的 name**，两者被拼到了一起。

## 频次

间歇 —— 同一命令连跑 6 次，约 3 次出现，其余干净（不是每次必现，也不是 pin 未生效）。

## 定位证据

把升级关掉（`auxiliary.title_generation.model_upgrade_enabled: false`，保留即时派生标题）后：

```bash
for i in 1 2 3; do hermes chat -q "回两字：测$i" 2>&1 | grep -icE "Auxiliary .* failed"; done
# → 0
# → 0
# → 0
```

即问题**确实在 stage-2 升级路径**（`agent/title_generator.py`：`_model_title_upgrade_enabled()` / 升级线程 → `agent.auxiliary_client.call_llm`），与即时派生标题无关。

## 建议排查点

- `agent/title_generator.py` 升级线程里对 `auxiliary.title_generation` 的解析（provider 与 model 是否来自同一处）
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py` 的 aux 路由解析：pin 生效时是否仍会回落到主模型名

## 相关观察（可能同源，另一个 bug）

主模型在 **opencode-go** 时，任何 `provider: "auto"`（= 继承主模型）的 aux 任务都会 400：

```
HTTP 400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"MissingSessionID","message":"Request is missing x-opencode-session ..."}}
```

opencode-go 强制要求 `x-opencode-session` 头（直连复测：不带该头 → 400 MissingSessionID；带上 → 200）。该头只在主对话路径由 `agent/opencode_affinity.py` 附上，**aux 路径不附**，于是 aux 在 opencode-go 下全灭。当前绕过办法是把 aux 全部 pin 到别的 provider（如 nous + 免费模型）。

## 影响

仅标题退化（回落到即时派生标题）+ 日志噪音；但同一套路由解析可能影响其它 aux 任务，故一并上报。
title: auxiliary.title_generation upgrade sends the main model name to the aux provider (intermittent HTTP 400)

### Bug Description

A cron run whose host process dies before `cron.scheduler._finalize_cron_session` runs keeps its session row at `ended_at IS NULL` / `title IS NULL` forever. The Desktop cron write gate re-reads that row before every send (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/submit.ts` → `refreshCronRunWriteGate` → `GET /api/sessions/{id}` → `cron_run_scheduler_owned`), sees no end stamp and no scheduler ownership, and refuses the message as a read-only transcript. Nothing ever closes the row: the gateway-side startup sweep only covers `('tui', 'desktop', 'subagent', 'unknown')` (`tui_gateway/session_reaper.py::_ORPHAN_SWEEP_SOURCES`), deliberately excluding `cron` — a cron row's lifecycle belongs to the scheduler, and the scheduler died with the process.

This is the sibling of #131433 / #132124: there a properly **closed** run loses its stamp on resume; here an **interrupted** run never gets one. PR #113342 records a shutdown-interrupted attempt as `interrupted` instead of `error` in the execution ledger, but it does not close the session row, so the read-only symptom stays.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Let a cron job start a run that is still in flight when the gateway shuts down (agent-mode jobs that run a few minutes are enough).
2. Stop the gateway (or let its drain time out).
3. Open that run from the Desktop Cron section.
4. Sending is refused with the read-only transcript notice; `state.db` shows the row with `ended_at IS NULL` and `title IS NULL`.

### Evidence (2026-10-14, Windows 11, single-backend install, v0.21.x)

`logs/gateway.log` — the shutdown that killed four in-flight runs:

```
13:05:20 INFO gateway.run: Received UNKNOWN as a planned gateway stop — exiting cleanly
13:08:20 INFO gateway.run: Shutdown phase: drain done at +180.08s (drain took 180.07s, timed_out=True, active_at_start=0, active_now=0, cron_at_start=4, cron_now=4, ...)
13:08:20 WARNING gateway.run: Gateway drain timed out after 180.1s with 0 active agent(s), 4 in-flight cron job(s), ...
13:08:20 WARNING gateway.run: Shutdown (post-interrupt): marked 4 in-flight cron job(s) interrupted: eacf7e98542f, 7d2b5b26a02c, 4307c63500e7, 215b35692183
13:12:49 INFO gateway.run: Starting Hermes Gateway...
```

`cron/executions.db` — all four attempts `unknown`:

```
Scheduler restarted after this execution's owner exited before a durable terminal state;
whether side effects ran is unknown.
```

`state.db` (`sessions`) — the four matching `cron_<job_id>_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>` rows:

```
cron_eacf7e98542f_20261014_130220 | title NULL | ended_at NULL | last activity 13:07
cron_7d2b5b26a02c_20261014_130213 | title NULL | ended_at NULL | last activity 13:07
cron_4307c63500e7_20261014_130227 | title NULL | ended_at NULL | last activity 13:07
cron_215b35692183_20261014_130220 | title NULL | ended_at NULL | last activity 13:07
```

Same database, 968 other cron rows carry `end_reason = 'cron_complete'` and 49 `'cron_incomplete_no_output'` — finalization works; these
title: [Bug]: a cron run killed by a gateway shutdown never gets its session row closed — the Desktop Cron view opens it read-only forever

body:
### Bug Description

With `MATTERMOST_REPLY_MODE=thread`, replies in **direct messages** are posted as thread replies, and when the user answers inside that thread the agent starts a **new session without any of the previous context**. The adapter seems to intend DMs to stay unthreaded, but only the inbound side does that.

**Inbound** (`plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py`, ~L569–571): a top-level DM post gets no `thread_id`, because of `not is_dm`:

```python
thread_id = post.get("root_id") or None
if not thread_id and self._reply_mode == "thread" and not is_dm and post_id:
    thread_id = post_id
```

**Outbound** (`_post_message`, ~L201–206): in thread mode the reply always gets a `root_id` from `reply_to`, including in DMs:

```python
if self._reply_mode == "thread":
    candidate = reply_to or (isinstance(metadata, dict) and (metadata.get("thread_id") or metadata.get("root_id")))
    if candidate:
        payload["root_id"] = await self._resolve_root_id(str(candidate))
```

The result in a DM:
1. The user's first message is handled in the DM session (no thread).
2. The agent's answer is posted as a thread reply under that message.
3. The user replies in the thread (where the conversation now visibly lives). That post has a `root_id`, so it gets `thread_id = root_id` and a **different session key**.
4. The agent answers without context ("I'm missing the context for that…").

In channels this doesn't happen, because the top-level post's id is used as `thread_id` from the start, so the follow-ups land in the same session.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Mattermost platform with `MATTERMOST_REPLY_MODE=thread`.
2. DM the bot: "can you read X?" It answers in a thread under the message.
3. Reply in that thread: "yes you can".
4. The agent has no context for step 2.

### Expected Behavior

One of:
- In DMs, replies are **not threaded** when `reply_mode=thread` (matching the inbound `not is_dm` logic), or
- the inbound and outbound sides use the same key, so a thread reply in a DM continues the DM session.

A separate setting (e.g. `MATTERMOST_DM_REPLY_MODE`) would also solve it: threads in channels, flat in DMs.

### Actual Behavior

DM answers are threaded, and follow-ups in that thread lose the conversation. The only workaround is `reply_mode=off`, which also removes threads in channels.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.7 (2026.9.24), upstream 71d34bad, official Docker image (s6), gateway mode
- Mattermost Team Edition 11.11.1, Collapsed Reply Threads on (default)

Possibly related, channel side: #4221.
title: [Bug]: Mattermost reply_mode=thread threads DM replies, and follow-ups in that thread lose the session context

body:
## Summary

The built-in API server (`/v1/chat/completions`) ignores the OpenAI-standard **top-level** `reasoning_effort` request field. It only reads reasoning control from the Hermes extension field `model_options`. Strict OpenAI-compatible clients that send the standard field — e.g. **Homarr's assistant** (Vercel AI SDK `openai-compatible` provider, which maps its reasoning toggle to top-level `reasoning_effort`) — therefore cannot turn thinking off, and the model keeps emitting reasoning tokens regardless of the client's toggle.

## Evidence

Homarr 2.5.2 assistant chat against the Hermes API server: the "reasoning off" toggle had no effect; the stream still carried `delta.reasoning_content`. Inspecting Homarr's shipped client (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`) shows it sends `reasoning_effort` as a top-level body field.

In `gateway/platforms/api_server.py`, `_request_agent_overrides()` copies only `body["model_options"]` into the agent overrides; `grep body.get("reasoning_effort")` across `gateway/` returns nothing.

Live probes against `:8642/v1/chat/completions` (same prompt, `stream:true`):

| request shape | reasoning deltas |
|---|---|
| (no reasoning control) | 22 |
| top-level `"reasoning_effort":"none"` (what Homarr sends) | 22 ← ignored |
| `"model_options":{"reasoning_effort":"none"}` (Hermes ext) | 0 ← honoured |

## Expected

A top-level `reasoning_effort` on an incoming Chat Completions request should be honoured like the `model_options` spelling, so standard clients can control thinking.

## Proposed fix (tested locally)

Fold the top-level field into `model_options` at the single request-parsing chokepoint, letting the existing decoder handle it. The Hermes `model_options` spelling and a structured `model_options.reasoning` block still win on a clash, so this only fills a gap the client left:

```python
# in _request_agent_overrides(), after the existing model_options copy:
top_level_effort = body.get("reasoning_effort")
if isinstance(top_level_effort, str) and top_level_effort.strip():
    opts = overrides.setdefault("model_options", {})
    if "reasoning_effort" not in opts and not isinstance(opts.get("reasoning"), dict):
        opts["reasoning_effort"] = top_level_effort.strip().lower()
```

After the change, the same probes give: baseline 22, top-level `none` → 0, top-level `low` → 22, `model_options` `none` → 0. Existing `test_api_server_reasoning_*` / `test_api_server_model_options_*` tests still pass (one pre-existing failure in `test_chat_completions_stream_forwards_agent_reasoning_callback` is a `home_io_guard` test-harness issue, unrelated — it fails identically without the change).

Version: v0.21.7 (rc.9, 46d7718a52).
title: [Bug]: API server ignores OpenAI-standard top-level reasoning_effort (Homarr assistant cannot disable thinking)

body:
On a gateway platform where several people talk to the same agent (a shared room bot), the persistent answers
to approval prompts write to the profile's shared config (checked at v0.21.6, 2026.9.24):

- "Always" on the `/new` / `/reset` / `/undo` confirmation saves `approvals.destructive_slash_confirm: false`
  into `config.yaml` (`gateway/run_busy.py`, `_run_confirmed_destructive_slash`), so after one participant
  chooses it, nobody in any room is asked again;
- "Always" on a dangerous-command approval adds the pattern to the profile's `command_allowlist`
  (`tools/approval.py`), again for every user and session of that profile.

That is the right behaviour for a single-owner agent, but on a shared bot it lets any room member widen what the
agent may do for everyone. We currently filter `/always`, `/approve always` and `/approve session` in our
platform plugin before they reach the core, which works but is brittle (every new alias or button has to be
caught there).

Proposal: a config switch, e.g. `approvals.allow_persistent: false` (or per platform), under which approval
prompts offer only Once/Deny and the persistent choices are refused. Related: #96703 (the MCP trust-gate card
renders Session/Always although they act as Once).
title: Multi-user gateways: option to disable persistent approval choices, so one participant cannot turn off confirmations for everyone

body:
On messaging gateways the reply to `/new` (session reset) always ends with a random tip:
`gateway/slash_commands_session.py` builds `_tip_line = t("gateway.reset.tip", tip=get_random_tip())`
unconditionally (checked at v0.21.6, 2026.9.24). There is no config key to suppress it.

The tips are written for the CLI/TUI (keys, commands, desktop features). On a shared team bot in a chat
platform most of them don't apply, and some point to slash commands that the deployment deliberately blocks for
room members, so the tip line reads as noise or as an invitation to try something that will be refused.

Proposal: a setting honored by the gateway reset reply, e.g. `display.tips: false`, or per platform
`display.platforms.<platform>.tips: false`. Default unchanged.
title: Gateway `/new` reply always appends a CLI tip; add a setting to turn it off

body:
## Problem or Use Case

On the WhatsApp Cloud adapter, every agent reply is sent as a reply to the triggering message, so the user's own text is quoted above each answer. In a 1:1 assistant conversation this adds visual noise to every single turn: the person sees their own message repeated before each reply.

In group chats the quote is useful. In direct messages it is not, and there is currently no way to turn it off.

## What I tried

- `display.platforms.whatsapp_cloud` with `tool_progress: off`, `interim_assistant_messages: false`, `long_running_notifications: false`, `busy_ack_detail: false`, `streaming: false` — the quoting remains.
- The adapter's `extra` options: `api_version`, `dm_policy`, `group_policy`, `group_sessions_per_user`, `health_path`, `reply_prefix`, `thread_sessions_per_user`, `webhook_host`, `webhook_path`, `webhook_port`. None covers it.
- Searched the docs and the repository for a `reply_to` / `quote` setting; found none.

As far as I can tell the anchor comes from the turn context (`run_turn_runner` passing `_progress_reply_to`) and reaches the adapter through `metadata.reply_to_message_id` (`_reply_to_from` in `gateway/platforms/whatsapp_cloud.py`).

## Proposal

An adapter setting, for example:

```yaml
platforms:
  whatsapp_cloud:
    extra:
      quote_inbound: always | groups_only | never
```

defaulting to `always` so nothing changes for existing deployments. `groups_only` would cover the common 1:1 assistant case.

## Version

2.0.0-rc.5 (0.21.5), WhatsApp Cloud adapter.
title: WhatsApp Cloud adapter: option to not quote the inbound message on every reply

body:
## What I see

In the Desktop app the same keystroke gives two different results, in two different conversations, at the same time.

In the Bot Chat, the permanent session bound to the bot and the one you land on when you click the bot, I press Enter while the agent is working and the message jumps into the running turn as a correction. Ctrl+Enter puts it in the queue.

In any other conversation Enter queues it instead, and nothing in the UI says the redirect was refused.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.7+758 (2026.9.24), upstream d97007c3
- Windows 11, Desktop app (Electron)
- git install at `C:\Users\39795\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent`

## Sessions where the steer landed

From `agent.log`, the mid turn delivery line shows up under three different session ids.

```
10:07:50  [20261009_105449_c5960c] Delivered /steer to agent after tool batch
14:11:35  [20261014_112620_176131] Delivered /steer to agent after tool batch
14:52:54  [20261014_144534_9fd33e] Delivered /steer to agent after tool batch
```

Two of those are ordinary chats, so the steer is not confined to the Bot Chat.

## What I traced

The Enter while busy path in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/index.tsx:392` computes `canSteer` and then calls `redirectPrompt` in `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.ts:796`. That function asks `captureSteeringSession()` for permission before it sends anything.

The check lives in `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/steering-session.ts`. Lines 62 to 77 define three refusals.

- `routeLeftSelection`, when the routed stored id sits outside the selected lineage
- `runtimeUnbound`, when a stored chat is selected but the live runtime has no binding at all
- `runtimeBoundElsewhere`, when this runtime is bound to a stored id outside the selected lineage

Any one of them returns null, `redirectPrompt` returns false, and `steerDraft` falls into its `keep()` path at `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-submit.ts:441`. That path calls `enqueueQueuedPrompt`, or puts the text back in the composer when there is no queue key yet. No toast, nothing in the renderer log, the words just become a queued item.

## Why the Bot Chat seems immune

The Bot Chat holds a stable identity. `activeSessionId` equals the selected stored session, the runtime binding map holds one entry pointing at itself, and the route agrees with the selection. All three refusals stay false, so it steers.

Other sessions accumulate bindings. A compression rotation, a rebuilt runtime, or a navigation that leaves route and selection disagreeing can put more than one stored id against the same runtime. Miss the check and the identical Enter key queues.

The refusals are guard rails against steering a conversation the user has moved away from, and the comments in that file say so. What the composer does not currently do is tell the user which path it took. From the outside the same key looks like it changed meaning between chats.
title: [Bug]: Enter-while-busy redirects in the Bot Chat and silently queues in other sessions

body:
### Problem or Use Case

Plugins have no supported way to set, read or clear a session's standing `/goal`.

Our use case is the plan-mode plugin (https://github.com/100yenadmin/hermes-plan-mode). After a user approves a plan, we want to offer "approve and keep going until done": the approved plan becomes a standing goal, with the plan's Verification section as the contract. Hermes' own judge, continuation turns, budget, `/goal` status and pause/clear controls then do the work. Neither Claude Code nor Codex links plan approval to goals, so this would be a Hermes-only strength.

What exists today (upstream main 0e427d788d; v0.21.6 behaves the same):
- There is no goal hook in `VALID_HOOKS` (`hermes_cli/plugins.py:109`) and no goal API on the plugin context.
- `register_command` rejects core command names, so a plugin cannot wrap `/goal` (`hermes_cli/plugins.py:658-660`).

We tried the two available routes on v0.21.6 with live CLI sessions, then traced the other surfaces in source:

1. **`ctx.inject_message("/goal …")`.**
   - On the classic CLI it runs as the real `/goal` command, and the goal is driven normally. We observed a judge-driven second turn.
   - Injected from `post_llm_call`, it takes the interrupt path, because `_agent_running` is still true (`hermes_cli/plugins_injection.py:21`). The CLI prints "New message detected, interrupting..." over a reply that has already finished, then runs the command.
   - On TUI/Desktop (`tui_gateway/plugin_inject.py:24-57`) and on the gateway (`gateway/run_plugin_injection.py:148`, `allow_gateway_control=False`), injected text reaches the model as plain text. This route is therefore CLI-only.
2. **Writing through `hermes_cli.goals.GoalManager(session_id).set(...)` from a hook** (internal API; we measured it and will not ship it).
   - TUI/Desktop and the gateway build a fresh manager every turn, so they would pick the goal up.
   - The classic CLI caches one manager per session id (`hermes_cli/cli_loops_mixin.py:479-515`), and `GoalManager` reads its state only in `__init__` (`hermes_cli/goals.py:1097-1100`).
   - Live result: the `state_meta` row is `active` with 0 turns used, but the CLI never continues it, and `/goal status` prints "No active goal". In the other direction, the CLI's next save from its stale manager would overwrite a goal written elsewhere, or undo a pause or clear written elsewhere.

On every route there is also no ownership. `GoalManager.set()` silently replaces any existing goal (`hermes_cli/goals.py:1168`), so a plugin cannot avoid clobbering a goal the user set themselves.

### Proposed Solution

Add a small plugin goal seam:
- `ctx.goals.get(session_id)` returns a read-only snapshot: objective, status, turns used and max, and owner.
- `ctx.goals.set(session_id, objective, *, contract=None, max_turns=None, owner=<plugin id>, if_absent=True) -> bool`. With `if_absent`, it refuses when an active or paused goal exists. The call is routed through the surface's own manager, or that mana
title: [Feature]: plugin goal seam (ctx.goals) — plugins cannot set, read or clear a standing /goal; the classic CLI ignores goals written outside its cached manager

body:
### Problem or Use Case

It's multiple steps to get input (text, URL, images, videos) into Hermes Desktop:

Copy item -> open Hermes Desktop -> select profile -> press new session -> paste -> submit

### Proposed Solution

## Summary
Add Hermes Desktop as a destination in the macOS share sheet, allowing users to share **text, URLs, images and videos** directly into a new Hermes session.
Confirming the share should open Hermes, create a new session and submit the shared content automatically—not just prefill the composer.
## Motivation
This would make Hermes accessible at the point where users encounter something they want help with: a webpage, selected text, screenshot, photo or video.
Instead of copying content, switching apps, creating a session and attaching files manually, the workflow becomes:
**Share → Hermes → optionally add an instruction → submit.**
Example uses:
- Share a webpage and ask for a summary.
- Share selected text and ask for an explanation or rewrite.
- Share a screenshot and ask for troubleshooting help.
- Share a photo or video and ask Hermes to describe or analyse it.
## Proposed MVP
- Hermes appears as a destination in the **macOS share sheet**.
- Accept text, URLs, images and videos.
- Provide an optional instruction field in the share interface.
- On confirmation:
  1. Open or bring Hermes to the foreground.
  2. Create a **new session**, rather than modifying an existing conversation.
  3. Transfer the content and attachments.
  4. Submit automatically and begin the agent response.
- Work whether Hermes is already running or closed.
- Ensure each confirmed share creates **one session and one submission**, even if delivery is retried.
## Proposed defaults
These are suggestions, open to feedback:
- Use the currently selected profile and backend connection.
- When no instruction is supplied, use a default such as: **“Summarize and explain this shared content.”**
- Treat confirmation in the share interface as authorization to submit; no second confirmation inside Hermes.
- Retain normal tool/action approvals. Shared content should be treated as input, not trusted instructions that override agent safeguards.
## Implementation considerations
The likely approach is a small native macOS Share Extension bundled with the desktop app, plus a handoff into Hermes’ session creation and attachment flow.
Areas to resolve:
- Extension packaging, signing and release integration.
- Reliable handoff during cold start and normal operation.
- Attachment lifetime and large-video handling.
- Uploading media when using a remote backend.
- Clear errors for unsupported media, size limits or unavailable connections.
- Avoiding duplicate submissions and accidental changes to existing sessions.
The goal is to reuse existing Hermes session, attachment and submission capabilities wherever possible.
## Acceptance criteria
Sharing text, a URL, an image or a short video should create a fresh session containing the content and start a response. This shou
title: [Feature]: Share to Hermes Desktop from the macOS share sheet

### Bug Description

When I open Hermes desktop app I get a black window. 

### Steps to Reproduce

Open Hermes Desktop on Omarchy.

Blank window only. 

### Expected Behavior

It should have opened the Hermes desktop app. 

### Actual Behavior

**Second reproduction — different GPU, distro and session type (Intel HD 4600, Omarchy/Arch, Wayland). Not NVIDIA- or Mint-specific.**

**Environment**
- Hermes Desktop built from source (Linux x64). Fails *identically* on two commits: `bd0affe5` (28 Sep — which had been rendering fine earlier the same day) and `main @ 8f817911` (13 Oct). Electron 40.10.2 on both.
- Omarchy 4.0.4 (Arch, Hyprland; Wayland plus XWayland), kernel `7.2.5-3-omarchy`. CPU Intel i7-4790K (Haswell: AVX2, no AVX-512), GPU Intel HD 4600 — no NVIDIA driver in play.
- Used as a remote client of a Hermes on another host over SSH: the connection itself succeeds every time.

**Symptoms (same chain as yours)**

```
[boot] Remote Hermes backend is ready
[renderer:main] webContents became unresponsive
Renderer failed to load: Error: ERR_FAILED (-2) loading 'file:///.../resources/app.asar.unpacked/dist/index.html'
[renderer:main] render-process-gone reason=crashed exitCode=132
[main] Uncaught exception: TypeError: Object has been destroyed
    at shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard (.../electron-main.mjs:70909:11)
    at focusWindow (.../electron-main.mjs:78971:7)
    at ensureMainWindow (.../electron-main.mjs:28006:5)
```

Kernel trap at the **same address on every crash** (30+ coredumps in one evening):

```
traps: Hermes[pid] trap invalid opcode ip:... in Hermes[6e26995,...]
coredumpctl: Signal: 4 (ILL) si_code: ILL_ILLOPN   #0 ... (Hermes + 0x6e27995)
```

`0x6e27995` sits inside a run of `int3` padding between functions, and the nearest symbol is in the same **c-ares region** you saw (`ares_dns_rr_get_ttl@@Base+...`), so the two offsets look like the same class of fault rather than two unrelated ones.

**Ruled out here (as far as I could test)**
- bundle integrity: 1,044 assets, every reference in `index.html` resolves, packaged copy byte-identical to the build output
- `/dev/shm` healthy (3.9 GB, mode 1777, empty); RAM and disk fine
- not GPU/ozone-specific: reproduces with `--ozone-platform=x11 --disable-gpu`; under native Wayland the window goes white rather than blank
- not a corrupted Electron artifact: the packaged Electron binary is byte-identical between the working and failing builds, and the cached Electron zip passes `unzip -t`
- not the app's caches: `Cache`, `GPUCache`, `Code Cache`, `Dawn*` moved aside — no change
- no dependency change in `apps/desktop` between the two commits (527 commits touched the app; `package.json` unchanged); the only native module is `node-pty`
- no AVX-512 in the binary or in the new HUD native helper; Chromium elsewhere on the same machine (Brave) renders fine, so the machine is not at fault
- **intermittent**: it rendered fine hours earlier on the same build, and previously opening blank once and relaun
title: [Bug]: Hermes Desktop blank window

### Problem or Use Case

Compression trigger settings are global to the profile, but a profile is usually reached from more than one surface. `compression.threshold` (ratio) and `compression.threshold_tokens` (absolute cap) are read once, at agent construction, and that read has no access to the surface being constructed:

- `agent/agent_init.py` — `_parse_compression_config(agent, _agent_cfg)` parses `_cfg_dict(_agent_cfg, "compression")`, i.e. the global section only.
- Its two neighbours on the same construction path *do* receive the surface: `_apply_display_config(agent, _agent_cfg, platform)` and `_init_memory(agent, _agent_cfg, skip_memory, platform, ...)`. `platform` is in scope at the call site; it is simply not passed to the compression read.

Consequence: an absolute cap set to stop long-context CLI work compacting early applies unchanged to a messaging surface whose context, models and habits are different — and the reverse. Today the only ways out are one profile per surface (duplicating skills, memory and credentials) or abandoning the cap.

The codebase already accepts that the trigger is not a single number: `compression.threshold` carries a documented raise-only floor of 0.75 for windows below 512K, and `compression.model_thresholds` varies the ratio per model. The missing affordance is the same thing keyed on the surface.

I searched open and closed issues and PRs and found nothing for platform- or channel-scoped compression thresholds. The nearest work is adjacent, not overlapping:

- per-model absolute caps — #87198
- session-scoped override (`/compthreshold`) — #98477
- `pre_compression` plugin hook — #93391
- reporting the effective trigger (`/new` banner, `/footer`, `hermes doctor`) — #130709, #124012

### Proposed Solution

A platform-scoped block, using the key shape already proposed for approvals in #88184:

```yaml
compression:
  threshold: 0.50            # global default, unchanged
  threshold_tokens: ~        # global default, unchanged

  platform_overrides:
    whatsapp:
      threshold: 0.35
      threshold_tokens: 60000
    slack:
      threshold_tokens: 200000
```

Resolution: the platform block wins, per key, over the global section; a platform block that sets only `threshold_tokens` still inherits the global `threshold`. No `platform_overrides` key means today's behaviour exactly, so this is additive and opt-in.

Scope of an implementation:

- Pass the surface into `_parse_compression_config` (available at its call site already) and merge `compression.platform_overrides.<platform>` over the global `compression` section before parsing.
- In-tree precedent for platform-keyed config is the top-level `platform_toolsets` mapping (see `cli-config.yaml.example`); `platforms.<name>.*` is the other convention in use. Either is fine — I have proposed it inside `compression` to keep one section per concern, but will follow whatever a maintainer prefers.
- Add the new key to `_CACHE_BUSTING_CONFIG_KEYS` in `gateway/run.py`
title: [Feature]: Per-platform compression thresholds (compression.platform_overrides.<platform>)

## Summary

Two distinct model ids render to the **exact same** label in the desktop model picker and the composer pill when the id carries a suffix *after* the variant tag. The user cannot tell the rows apart, and one of them may be an id the backend rejects — so "I keep selecting it and it keeps failing" becomes an unfixable-looking loop.

The variant-tag regexes in `model-status-label.ts` are anchored at the end of the id (`/-flash$/i`), so a trailing region/deployment segment consumes the anchor, the tag is never extracted, and the whole tail is title-cased into the name instead.

## Concrete case

Fireworks router ids (provider `fireworks`):

| model id | rendered label |
|---|---|
| `accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us` | `DeepSeek V4p1 Flash Us` |
| `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us` | `DeepSeek V4p1 Flash Us` |

Two different ids, one label. In the desktop model menu both appeared as adjacent rows reading **“DeepSeek V4p1 Flash Us”** with the same capability badge — while only one of them exists on the provider (the other returns HTTP 400 / 404 on use). The user repeatedly selected the wrong row and could not see why it kept failing.

The same anchoring also **loses** the variant tag that the unsuffixed sibling gets:

| model id | rendered label |
|---|---|
| `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash` | `DeepSeek V4p1 · Flash` |
| `accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us` | `DeepSeek V4p1 Flash Us` |

…so the region-suffixed id of the same family renders *without* the `Flash` tag, and the two rows differ only by a word that looks like part of the model name.

## Root cause

`apps/desktop/src/lib/model-status-label.ts`:

```ts
const VARIANT_TAGS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [RegExp, string]> = [
  [/-fast$/i, 'Fast'],
  [/-flash$/i, 'Flash'],
  [/-thinking$/i, 'Thinking'],
  [/-preview$/i, 'Preview'],
  [/-latest$/i, 'Latest']
]
```

`modelDisplayParts()` → `modelBaseId()` (slices at the last `/`) → `splitTrailingTags()` walks these regexes, each of which only matches at the end of the string. For `deepseek-v4p1-flash-us` nothing matches, `base` stays `deepseek-v4p1-flash-us`, and `prettifyBase()` title-cases it into `DeepSeek V4p1 Flash Us` — identical to what another id can produce.

## Expected

Ids that differ must render differently (this is the invariant the surrounding code already states for other cases). Suggested shape:

- treat a trailing region/deployment segment (`-us`, `-eu`, …) as a tag of its own, and
- extract variant tags at any trailing position (`…-flash-us` → `DeepSeek V4p1 · Flash Us`), so a suffixed id keeps the tag its sibling has.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.21.7+753.g1555b6f (2026.9.24) · stable` (install method: git)
- macOS 27.0.1 (Darwin 27.0.0), arm64
- Desktop (packaged app); provider `fireworks`

## Related

- #124884 — desktop model picker: `-flash` variant-tag classification is inconsistent and the tag mechanism has structural issues (this is a concrete insta
title: [Bug]: Two distinct model ids render to the identical label when the id carries a suffix after the variant tag (…-flash-us)
