## Summary

The desktop composer's model pick is sticky state that **cannot be cleared from any reachable UI surface**, and it silently overrides `model.default` on every new session. Once it holds a model the user no longer wants, every subsequent new chat inherits it — including a model the user never deliberately pinned.

This is the model-slot twin of #87036 (sticky `reasoning_effort` with no safety valve). The model slot has the same three properties — un-clearable, unvalidated, silently overrides `config.yaml` — plus a worse failure mode: a switch that **fails** leaves the pin exactly where it was, so the user's corrective action has no effect and no visible cause.

## Mechanism

`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/session-create-request.ts`:

```ts
// Omit model/provider unless the source is 'manual'.
const isManualSelection = getCurrentModelSource() === 'manual'

const selection = {
  ...
  model:    isManualSelection ? $currentModel.get().trim() : '',
  provider: isManualSelection ? $currentProvider.get().trim() : ''
}
```

So `model-source === 'manual'` is the sole gate: while it is set, every `session.create` ships that model as a session override, which beats `model.default` for the whole session.

`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls.ts`:

```ts
const prevSource = getCurrentModelSource()                      // :270
const paintSelection = () => { ... markComposerSelectionManual() }  // :273-277
const rollbackSelection = () => {                               // :294
  setCurrentModel(prevModel)
  setCurrentProvider(prevProvider)
  setCurrentReasoningEffortWire(prevWire)
  setCurrentModelSource(prevSource)                             // :300
}
```

`paintSelection()` marks the composer manual **before** the gateway call; on failure `rollbackSelection()` restores the model but also restores `prevSource` — which is `manual` whenever the composer was already pinned. The pin therefore survives every failed attempt, and nothing in the flow reports that an override is active.

## Why there is no way out

The only function that clears the pin is `followDefaultModel()` (`use-model-controls.ts:232` → `setCurrentModelSource('default')`), and it is reachable only through a menu item gated on:

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/app/shell/model-menu-panel.tsx:39
const pinnedDraft = view.kind === 'primary' && !activeSessionId && modelSource === 'manual'
```

i.e. it renders only in a **draft with no active session** — while the desktop calls `session.create` as soon as a chat is opened to paint the composer, so in practice the item is not reachable.

The other candidate, Settings → Model → Apply, only reaches the composer via `applySavedMainModel()` on a **successful** apply (`app/settings/model-settings.tsx:832`). When the pinned model is one the switch validator rejects (see the companion issue), the apply itself 400s, so `onMainModelChanged` never runs and the pin is never cleared. The two defects compose into a hard
title: [Bug]: Composer model pin is un-clearable — a failed switch leaves model-source=manual on the old model, and every new session then ships it

body:
## Summary

A model id that is explicitly configured as `model.default` — and therefore shown by the picker as the **current** selection — is rejected by the model-switch validator. The user can see the model, it answers fine on `/chat/completions`, and yet every attempt to select it fails with `not found in this provider's model listing`.

`_config_declares_model()` (`hermes_cli/model_switch.py`) already implements exactly the escape hatch this needs — *"A model declared in the user's `providers:`/`custom_providers:` config is accepted even when the remote /v1/models does not list it"* — but it does **not** consult `model.default`, even though that is the most explicit declaration a user can make.

## Concrete case

Provider `fireworks`, model `accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us` (an account-level Fireworks **router** id, not a catalogue model).

It is served correctly:

```
POST https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions
  {"model":"accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us", ...}
→ HTTP 200
```

It is reported as the current selection by the same endpoint the picker renders from:

```
GET /api/model/options
→ {"model":"accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us","provider":"fireworks", ...}
   providers[fireworks].is_current = true
```

But selecting it fails:

```
POST /api/model/set  {"scope":"main","provider":"fireworks","model":"accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us"}
→ HTTP 400
  {"detail":"Model `accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us` was not found in this provider's
    model listing.\n  Similar models: `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash`,
    `accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k3-fast`, `accounts/fireworks/routers/glm-5p3-fast`"}
```

(Also observed from the desktop renderer as `模型切换失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: Model ... was not found in this provider's model listing.`)

## Why the validator can't find it

`_validate_live_listing()` checks two sources and the id is in neither:

- Fireworks' inference `/v1/models` (both `api.` and `us.api.`) returns **20** ids, containing three router ids (`routers/glm-5p2-fast`, `routers/kimi-k3-fast`, `routers/glm-5p3-fast`) and **no** `deepseek` router.
- The curated catalogue (`_PROVIDER_MODELS`) / models.dev carry 10 Fireworks router ids, none region- or deployment-suffixed.

So the id is genuinely absent from every listing — while being a first-class, addressable resource on the inference endpoint.

## Workaround (verified)

Declare the id under the provider's `models:` map so `_config_declares_model()` accepts it:

```bash
hermes config set 'providers.fireworks.models.accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us.context_window' 1048576
```

```yaml
providers:
  fireworks:
    models:
      accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us:
        context_window: 1048576
```

Result: the identical `POST /api/model/set` returns **200**; a genuinely bogus id (`accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us`) still return
title: [Bug]: A model named by model.default is rejected by the model-switch validator — _config_declares_model() never consults model.default

## Summary

Switching the model from the desktop composer while the session is still a **draft** (opened but no prompt sent yet) does not persist. The switch itself is applied in-place and logged as success, but the durable marker write fails on a SQLite foreign key, so the session keeps its old model — and the next `session.info` repaints the old model over the user's choice.

Net effect: the user sees "switch succeeded" (no error toast) and then the model silently reverts.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Desktop app, open a **new chat** (draft — do not send anything yet).
2. Open the model menu and pick a different model.
3. Observe: no error is surfaced.
4. Send a prompt, or inspect the session.

## Actual

`agent.log` shows the switch applied:

```
14:35:39,848 run_agent: OpenAI client created (switch_model, shared=True) ... model=accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us
14:35:39,853 agent.agent_runtime_helpers: Model switched in-place: accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash (fireworks) -> accounts/fireworks/routers/deepseek-v4p1-flash-us (fireworks)
14:35:39,883 WARNING tui_gateway.server: failed to persist model switch marker
```

with the traceback:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../tui_gateway/server.py", line 1861, in _append_model_switch_marker
    entry["_row_id"] = db.append_message(
        session_id=target, role="user", content=marker, display_kind="model_switch",
        message_uid=stamp_message_uid(entry))
  File ".../hermes_state_messages.py", line 421, in append_message
  ...
sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed
```

The session row is never updated (`sessions.model` / `model_config.model` still hold the pre-switch model), and the next `session.info` publishes the old model back to the composer/pill.

The same switch performed **after** the first prompt succeeds and persists normally (the row exists by then), which is what makes this a draft-only, order-dependent trap.

## Expected

Either:
- the marker write should be deferred/skipped when the target session has no row yet (the row is created lazily on the first prompt — the marker can be attached then), or
- if the durable write genuinely cannot happen, the in-place switch should not be reported as successful.

Silently applying a switch that cannot be persisted — and then letting `session.info` revert the UI — is worse than refusing it.

## Root cause (as far as I could trace it)

`tui_gateway/server.py:_append_model_switch_marker()` (line ~1823, write at ~1861) calls `db.append_message(session_id=target, ...)`. `target` comes from `_submit_row_target_key(session)`. Desktop drafts deliberately have **no DB row** (`session.create` does not persist a row for an empty draft — see the comment in `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` about drafts leaving "Untitled" litter), so `append_message` violates the `messages.session_id -> sessions.id` foreign key.

The `except Exception` around the block downgrades this to a WARNING, so the failur
title: [Bug]: Switching models in a draft session fails to persist — _append_model_switch_marker hits FOREIGN KEY constraint failed and the switch silently reverts

## Bug Description

After the desktop backend crashed and respawned (2026-10-13 22:36 local, UTC+8), **every assistant message rendered twice in the desktop UI across all conversations** — including conversations created *after* the crash — while the canonical store (`state.db` → `messages`) contained exactly **one** row per message. Separately, one long-running conversation accumulated **26 transcript rows that exist twice with byte-identical `message_uid` values**, inserted in a single batch roughly 90 minutes after the affected messages were first written.

Restarting the desktop app cleared the doubled rendering and no new duplicate rows have appeared since, which points at the crash-recovery/reconnect path rather than at the store itself.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (desktop app, Electron)
- Hermes Agent: `v0.21.7+509.g4957bbd (2026.9.24)`, install dir `D:\Program Files\Hermes\hermes-agent`
- Model/provider context: `glm-5.3-flash` via a custom `chat_completions` endpoint (provider-side stream truncation was raging the same evening — believed to be the *trigger* of the crash, not the bug itself)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 22:35:21 | Last heartbeat of backend `default@host:38112` (`gateway_heartbeats` table) |

## Summary

A transcript rewrite releases the whole `skill_view` repeat-view dedup bucket, even for skills whose full result is still verbatim in the rewritten transcript. The next repeat view of such a skill returns the full body again, so the context carries two identical copies.

## Evidence

Measured on one week of gateway sessions (Telegram/Discord, Claude and GPT routes), counting each tool call id once:

- 266 repeat `skill_view` calls returned a full body while the earlier full result of the same skill and file was still present in the persisted transcript.
- 195 of them followed a proactive tool-result prune, 24 a compaction, 39 a gateway restart, and 8 had no rewrite found.
- Duplicated bodies were about 3.9M characters. Re-reading them on later requests until the next compaction cost an estimated $240/week at cached-input prices on this installation.

## Cause

`_reset_read_dedup_caches()` runs after a committed proactive prune, a micro-compaction splice, a compaction, and a native checkpoint. It calls `reset_skill_view_dedup(task_id)`, which drops every entry for the task. A prune or splice usually demotes only some tool results, so entries for results it kept are released too.

## Expected

Release only the entries whose full result the rewrite demoted or removed. Keep the stub for results that are still verbatim in context.

Related: #132177 (stub served after its result was pruned), #112763, #98206. The fix must keep their release behavior.
title: skill_view dedup releases entries whose full result survives a transcript rewrite

body:
## Problem

With NeMo Relay managed execution on (only when shared metrics, `telemetry.shared_metrics.enabled`,
or a Relay plugin configuration is active; both are off by default), every chat-completions stream
runs on a new private event loop, and `ManagedLlmStream._provider_stream` reads each provider chunk
with `asyncio.to_thread(next, sync_stream)`: two cross-thread wake-ups per chunk. NeMo Relay 0.10.0
already processes chunks on the calling event loop when it can, so this executor hop now causes
most of the managed path's cross-thread traffic: about 6 of its 7 context switches per chunk.

- **Per-chunk cost.** A managed stream costs 1.6 ms of CPU and 7 context switches per chunk, against
  0.8 ms and 1 without Relay. A gateway runs each turn on its own thread, and once enough streams
  overlap the process falls behind. With 5 sessions streaming about 200 chunks/s each, chunks reach
  Hermes 269 ms late at p50 (682 ms at p99), where without Relay they arrive in 0.4 ms. At 50
  concurrent streams they arrive 5.6 s late at p50 (11 s at p99). That matches #120380 (replies sit
  unread in socket buffers while the stale watchdog stays quiet, because chunks still trickle in),
  although we have not confirmed that the reporter had managed execution on.
- **A close race (#132048).** Closing the stream while the off-loop `next()` is still running raises
  `ValueError: generator already executing`. Three open PRs patch it on the sync path (#132059,
  #132064, #132080).

## Approach

Each `AIAgent` owns one long-lived asyncio loop (`agent/relay_llm_agent_loop.py`). Relay's pipeline and
an `AsyncOpenAI` twin of the request client both run on it, so the worker thread that drives the
stream reads the socket itself: no executor hop per chunk, and no sync generator for a close to race.

- **Scope.** Managed chat-completions streams whose request-slot client is a plain `openai.OpenAI` on
  Hermes's own keepalive transport. The build ladder records those clients (`has_async_twin`).
  Provider-supplied, Gemini-native, MoA, Bedrock-signed and injected clients keep today's path, as do
  unmanaged streams. There is no config flag.
- **Same client, async.** The twin is built from the request slot's kwargs snapshot through the same
  kwargs phases as the sync client, now shared in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers_openai_client.py`:
  credentials including token providers, configured headers, TLS verify, proxies and the
  served-model hook. If the twin cannot be built, the request streams on the sync client.
- **Request-slot ownership rules.** One stream holds the loop at a time; a concurrent stream on the
  same agent gets a private loop, as today. Stop, the stale watchdog, the late-connect re-abort and
  the delegation drain only `shutdown()` the twin's sockets from their own threads. Every close runs
  on the loop while no stream holds it, and `release_clients()` and `close()` tear the loop down. Each
  stream gets its own default executor, shut down on release, so n

## Bug Description

The Desktop's port-announcement waiter has a grace path (added by #122206) that is supposed to re-arm the 90 s deadline while the backend is finishing an owed `source-completion-pending` update tail — the `hermes: finishing an interrupted source update...` / `hermes: completing source-update dependencies...` banners. The tail legitimately runs minutes, far past the 90 s cold-start budget.

But `venv_sync` prints those banners to **stderr** (`print(..., file=sys.stderr)`), while `waitForDashboardPort` only tests them against `child.stdout`. The grace therefore never arms, and a healthy backend that is mid-repair (or whose tail + relaunch merely crosses 90 s) is killed at the deadline and the repair re-runs on every launch.

This is distinct from the marker-lifecycle issue in #127284 and from the pipe issue in #96280: even with a perfectly readable stdout pipe, the banner never reaches the stdout listener because it is written to the other FD.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows self-managed source install with `source-completion-pending` armed (any interrupted/failed `hermes update`, e.g. a desktop packaging step that fails on a network error).
2. Confirm dependencies are current (`pm.venv_is_current(project_root=root)` → `True`), so the launch re-enters the tail via `if not current or pending.is_file():`.
3. Launch the Desktop (its Electron parent spawns `hermes serve`).
4. Backend prints `hermes: finishing an interrupted source update...`, then runs the tail before `serve` binds/announces.
5. At ~90 s Electron logs `Timed out waiting for Hermes backend port announcement (90000ms)`, kills the child, and the next launch repeats.

## Expected Behavior

While the banner indicates a completion is in progress, the deadline should be re-armed (5-minute window, 30-minute cap, as #122206 intended), so the backend can finish and announce its port.

## Actual Behavior

The grace never triggers. The failure message is the bare form — note the missing `while an update completion was in progress` suffix that the same code path appends when `completionInProgress` is true:

```
[hermes] hermes: finishing an interrupted source update...
[hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Timed out waiting for Hermes backend port announcement (90000ms)
[hermes] Error: Timed out waiting for Hermes backend port announcement (90000ms)
```

`completionInProgress` is never set because it is only set inside `onData`, and `onData` is attached only to `child.stdout`.

## Root Cause

`hermes_cli/venv_sync.py`:

```python
# line ~499
print("hermes: completing source-update dependencies...", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
# line ~514
print("hermes: finishing an interrupted source update...", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
```

`apps/desktop/electron/backend-ready.ts` (`waitForDashboardPort`, at `d97007c32d`):

```ts
const SOURCE_COMPLETION_BANNER_RE = /finishing an interrupted source update|completing source-update dependencies/
...
function onData(chunk) {
  ...
  if (SOUR
title: [Bug]: Desktop kills a healthy backend at the 90s port-announcement deadline during an owed update tail — #122206 grace watches stdout, but venv_sync prints the banner to stderr

### Bug Description

When an agent run fails during a streamed `/v1/chat/completions` request (`stream: true`), the final SSE chunk carries the raw error text in `error.message` and `hermes.error`, without the redaction the other API paths apply. A provider error containing a credential (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...`) is masked in the non-streaming reply, the `X-Hermes-Error` header and both `/v1/responses` paths (#37733), but sent verbatim to the client when streaming.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the API server.
2. Have the agent run fail with an error text containing a key, e.g. a result `{"failed": true, "error": "provider auth failed OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-..."}` or a raised exception with that text.
3. `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `"stream": true`.

### Expected Behavior

The key is redacted (`OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-pro...`), as with `"stream": false`.

### Actual Behavior

The last `chat.completion.chunk` contains the full key in `error.message` and `hermes.error`.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

Not from a live provider: reproduced on current `main` (0e427d788d) through the real `_handle_chat_completions` → `_run_agent` with a stubbed agent returning / raising that error.

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.14

### Hermes Version

main @ 0e427d788d

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`gateway/platforms/api_server_openai_routes.py` `_write_sse_chat_completion` builds `err_msg` from `_result_flags(result)` or `str(agent_error)` and writes it into the finish chunk directly; the non-streaming branch of `_handle_chat_completions` passes the same value through `_redact_api_error_text` first.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Pass `err_msg` through `_redact_api_error_text` in the streaming branch too.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
title: [Bug]: Streamed /v1/chat/completions sends unredacted agent error text (keys) in the final chunk

## Summary

In the Desktop composer, the same slash command commits in two different shapes depending on whether its name is typed in full:

* **name typed in full** → committed as a **pill/chip**, and for argument-taking commands the **argument step never opens** (the popover closes instead);
* **name picked from a partial list** → committed as **plain text**, and the argument list stays open as intended.

The cause is a single character: `SlashCommandCompleter._completion_text()` appends a trailing space to an exact command-name match, and the desktop's "an argument is already part of this command" check is a whitespace scan over the serialized item.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a Desktop chat and click into the composer.
2. Type `/compress` (full name) — the popover shows `/compress`.
3. Press **Enter** (or Space) — the command is committed as a pill, caret after a trailing space.
4. Clear the composer and type `/com` — the popover lists `/compose`, `/compress`, `/compact`.
5. Arrow to `/compress` and press **Enter** — committed as plain text `/compress `, no pill.

Same command, two shapes, decided by whether the name was complete when it was accepted.

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/commands_completion.py` → `SlashCommandCompleter._completion_text()` (line ~338):

```python
# Replacement text; exact matches get a trailing space (else prompt_toolkit hides the
# menu on a no-op replacement) — except _PICKER_COMMANDS.
exact = cmd_name == word and cmd_name not in SlashCommandCompleter._PICKER_COMMANDS
return f"{cmd_name} " if exact else cmd_name
```

So `complete.slash` returns the completion text **with a trailing space** whenever the typed word is an exact match — for every command except `_PICKER_COMMANDS` (`model`, `skin`, `personality`):

| request | items returned |
|---|---|
| `/com` | `compose`, `compress`, `compact` |
| `/compres` | `compress` |
| `/compress` | `compress ` |
| `/personality` | `personality` (picker command → no trailing space) |

Desktop side: `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-slash-completions.ts` `toItem()` (line ~296) does `const command = commandText(entry.text)`, so that space rides into `metadata.command` / `metadata.rawText` as `/compress `.

Then `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-trigger.ts` `replaceTriggerWithChip()`:

```ts
const expandsToArgs = trigger.kind === '/' && !trigger.inline && !serialized.includes(' ') && argumentMode !== null   // ~line 373
const slashKind = !expandsToArgs && trigger.kind === '/' ? slashChipKindForItem(item) : null                         // ~line 379
const keepTriggerOpen = starter || (expandsToArgs && argumentMode !== 'text')                                         // ~line 380
```

`serialized.includes(' ')` is meant to detect "the user already picked an argument" (e.g. `/personality alice`), but the completer's trailing space makes a bare command look like it already has one → `expandsToArgs` is false → a pill is emitted and the popover closes in
title: [Bug][Desktop]: a fully-typed slash command commits as a pill and skips its argument step (completer's trailing space defeats the expands-to-args gate)

## Feature Description

Persist the composer status-stack collapse state (per session, or at minimum stop resetting it on every store-driven remount) so a manually-collapsed Tasks/todo group stays collapsed across tool ticks.

## Motivation

Today `StatusSection` (`apps/desktop/src/components/chat/status-section.tsx:37`) keeps collapse in bare `useState(defaultCollapsed)`, and the todo group passes `defaultCollapsed={false}` (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/status-stack/index.tsx:293`). Every `tool.start`/`tool.complete` store write remounts the stack and snaps the group back open — even seconds after the user collapsed it. For long todo lists this eats ~half the composer dock on every tick.

This is the cosmetic half of the focus/scroll-yank loop filed alongside (same tick also blurs the composer via `onPointerDownCapture` at `status-stack/index.tsx:373` and shifts the thread anchor). Even with the focus half fixed, the re-pop alone is worth filing: visibility should be a user choice, matching the files-panel precedent (#67286 / #65375 — reactive unhide must not expand a user-collapsed rail).

## Proposed Solution

- Key each `StatusSection` collapse by group type + session and persist it (nanostore or localStorage), or lift collapse state above the remount boundary so tool ticks can't reset it.
- Default todo groups collapsed (or remember last user choice); expanding stays a click away.

## Alternatives Considered

- Cap the stack height only — helps screen space but the group still re-opens and re-renders every tick.
- Leave as-is — the current behavior trains users not to collapse, since collapse never sticks.
title: [Feature]: Desktop composer status stack — persist Tasks/todo collapse across tool ticks

## Bug Description

On Hermes Desktop `c70332f` (v0.21.7+494, Windows, Desktop bundle rebuilt from same source), all three of these persist mid-turn on every assistant turn:

1. **Composer caret loss** — typing in the input while a tool call starts drops the caret / clears the visible draft. Typing resumes only after re-clicking. Matches #84058 exactly (still open).
2. **Scroll yank** — reading scrolled-up history while streaming pulls the viewport back down. #78486 / #96160 closed via #115326 (`b46f2448f7`, in this build per `git merge-base`), so this reads as a regression or incomplete fix.
3. **Tasks panel re-pop focus yank** — the composer status stack above the input re-opens/expands the todo group on every tool tick, stealing focus/scroll.

Repro: send a long tool-heavy prompt, scroll up to read + type in the composer simultaneously. All three fire within the same tick.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.7+494.gc70332f (2026.9.24), source `c70332f888`, Desktop exe rebuilt Oct 14 from same source (verified `hermes-build.json` + exe mtime)
- Windows 10, single main pane, no tiles

## Mechanism (from local source at c70332f)

The scroll yank and focus yank share one root: the todo group in the composer status stack.

- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/status-stack/index.tsx:293` — todo groups render with `defaultCollapsed={group.type !== 'todo'}`, i.e. **todos default expanded**. Worse, `StatusSection` (`apps/desktop/src/components/chat/status-section.tsx:37`) holds collapse in `useState(defaultCollapsed)` with **no persisted key** — every remount (each `tool.start`/`tool.complete` store write re-renders the stack) resets your manual collapse back to expanded.
- Same file, line 373: the stack root has `onPointerDownCapture={() => blurComposerInput()}` — any pointer interaction with the stack **blurs the composer input**. Combined with the remount-expand above, the stack growing upward pushes the dock, the thread re-measures `--composer-measured-height`, and `use-stick-to-bottom` reads the layout shift as viewport motion.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/focus.ts:730-770` (`focusComposerInput`) already skips `el.focus()` when `document.activeElement === el` — but nothing re-asserts focus after the blur, so the caret stays gone until you click back.

So the tick is: tool event → stack remount → todo section snaps open (losing your collapse) → dock grows → thread scroll anchor shifts → composer blurred. Three symptoms, one loop.

## Suggested fix

1. Persist todo-group collapse per session (or default todos collapsed) so tool ticks don't re-expand.
2. Scope `blurComposerInput` to explicit dismiss chrome, not the whole stack root — or re-focus the composer after passive store-driven re-renders.
3. Stabilise the dock height contribution so stack growth doesn't shift the thread anchor mid-stream.

## Related

- #84058 (caret loss — still open, same tick)
- #85691 (ghost-buffer loop — same path)
- #78486 / #96160 (closed by #115326, in thi

## The capability exists; only the entry point is missing

`tui_gateway/methods_groups.py` registers 18 group-chat methods — `groups.create`, `groups.send`, `groups.list`, `groups.state`, `groups.rename`, `groups.log`, `groups.disband`, `groups.promote`/`demote`, `groups.stop`/`retry`/`approve`, `groups.replicate`/`replica_state`, `groups.peer.invite`/`revoke`/`register`, `groups.capabilities`.

`groups.create` is already shaped for programmatic use:

```python
@_room_method("groups.create", code=5111, room_code=4110, service_code=4123, ...)
def _(rid, params: dict, service) -> dict:
    """Create a hosted room idempotently; authority is this gateway's stable install identity."""
    room = service.create_room(room_id=..., name=..., members=...)
```

Idempotent, with a stable authority — exactly what an automated caller wants.

But there is **no CLI subcommand** for any of it. `hermes_cli/subcommands/` has nothing, and the tests reach the methods in-process (`srv._methods["groups.create"](...)` in `tests/tui_gateway/test_groups_methods.py`). The only external path is the TUI gateway's WebSocket JSON-RPC.

## The ask

A thin CLI surface over the methods that already exist:

```
hermes groups list [--json]
hermes groups create --name "Build Room" --members ceo,sanju,ruthcfo [--room-id UUID]
hermes groups send --room <id> --message "..."
hermes groups disband --room <id>
```

No new capability, no new storage, no new auth — `_api_server_key()` already resolves `API_SERVER_KEY` from the routed profile's secret scope, so the authorization story is unchanged. This is a front door onto a service Hermes already ships and already persists (`ui_meta["hermes-bots-groups"]`, with the revision CAS the gateway enforces).

## Why it matters outside Desktop

Bot Mode group chats are one of the most distinctive things Hermes has — *"a one-chat-per-agent roster with avatars, routines, group chats, and bot-to-bot messaging"*, and memberships sync across machines. Right now they can only be created by a human clicking in Desktop.

Concretely: I maintain [bot-forge](https://github.com/BkashJEE/hermes-bot-forge) (community catalog). Its `create_team` builds a lead plus specialists in one call and writes the roster into the lead's memory — but it cannot put that team in a room, so the user has to recreate the group by hand immediately afterwards. A plugin that creates five Bots for a job should be able to give them the room they are meant to talk in.

More generally this is the difference between group chats being a Desktop feature and being a Hermes feature: cron jobs, setup scripts, provisioning flows and headless installs all currently have no way to reach them.

## What I explicitly did not do

I found the persistence — `~/.hermes/profile.yaml` → `ui_meta["hermes-bots-groups"]`, rooms keyed `id:<uuid>` with `name`/`roomId`/`members[]`/`holdDetection`, and `_ui_meta_revisions` as the counter — and deliberately **did not** write it from a plugin. The gateway advances
title: Feature: CLI surface for Bot Mode group chats (groups.create / list / send already exist, Desktop-only)

## Bug Description
When the gateway is installed as a **system** service on a root deployment (e.g. WSL2, containers) and the unit file has no explicit `User=` line, the read-only command `hermes gateway status` crashes with a `ValueError` coming from the unit *install* path, instead of reporting service state.

The error message suggests "pass `--run-as-user root` to override" — but `hermes gateway status` does **not** accept that flag (it only exists on `hermes gateway install`), so the suggested workaround is unavailable on the command that crashes.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. WSL2 (or any root-run host) with `systemd=true`
2. Gateway installed as a system service: `hermes gateway install --system --run-as-user root`
   → unit at `/etc/systemd/system/hermes-gateway.service` with no explicit `User=` line, `enabled` + `active`
3. Run `hermes gateway status`

## Expected Behavior
Status reports the service state. `systemctl status hermes-gateway` works fine and shows `enabled`/`active`.

## Actual Behavior
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "hermes_cli/gateway.py", line 5677, in _cmd_status
    systemd_status(deep, system=system, full=full)
  File "hermes_cli/gateway.py", line 3915, in systemd_status
    if not systemd_unit_is_current(system=system):
  File "hermes_cli/gateway.py", line 3272, in generate_systemd_unit
    username, group_name, home_dir, uid = _system_service_identity(run_as_user)
  File "hermes_cli/gateway.py", line 2743, in _system_service_identity
    raise ValueError(
        "Refusing to install the gateway system service as root; pass --run-as-user root to override (e.g. in LXC containers)"
    )
ValueError: Refusing to install the gateway system service as root; pass --run-as-user root to override (e.g. in LXC containers)
```
(Traceback from v0.22.0; line numbers may shift slightly between builds.)

## Root Cause (from local source reading)
`systemd_unit_is_current(system=True)` does a drift check by comparing the installed unit against a freshly generated one:
- `_read_systemd_user_from_unit()` returns `None` when the unit has no explicit `User=` line
- `generate_systemd_unit(system=True, run_as_user=None)` → `_system_service_identity(None)` resolves the username to the *current* user (`root`)
- the root guard — which belongs to the **install** path — fires during a **read-only** status check

Suggested fix: on the read-only drift-check path, don't run the install-time identity guard (e.g. skip the "outdated" comparison when the target user can't be determined, or pass the resolved current user explicitly so the guard is satisfied). Also, the error message's "pass `--run-as-user root`" hint should not be shown for commands that don't accept that flag.

## Workaround
Check state with `systemctl status hermes-gateway` / `systemctl is-enabled hermes-gateway` directly.

## Environment
- OS: WSL2 (Ubuntu), Hermes running as root, systemd enabled (`/etc/wsl.conf` `[boot] systemd=true`)
- Version: Hermes Agent v0.22
title: [Bug]: hermes gateway status crashes on root system-service installs (read-only status hits the install-path root guard)

# Bitwarden secret source not applied in `chat -q` when bootstrap token is already in parent environment

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: **v0.21.7+753.g1555b6f (2026.9.24) · stable**
- OS: Linux
- Profile: custom profile with `secrets.bitwarden.enabled: true`, `bws` 2.0.0 (installed via `hermes secrets bitwarden install`), Bitwarden US Cloud, project with a secret named `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `override_existing: yes` (default).

## Repro

The Bitwarden secret source is enabled and works in direct processes, but is silently skipped in `chat -q` when the bootstrap token is already present in the parent shell environment.

**Fails** (bootstrap token exported in parent shell, e.g. after `source ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/.env`):

```bash
env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN hermes -p <profile> chat -q 'Run: [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] && echo PRESENT || echo ABSENT'
# -> ABSENT
```

**Works** (bootstrap token NOT in parent shell):

```bash
env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN -u BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN hermes -p <profile> chat -q 'Run: [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] && echo PRESENT || echo ABSENT'
# -> PRESENT
```

## Evidence that the dotenv load itself still happens

With a dummy bootstrap token in the parent environment, the subprocess sees the **real** token from the profile `.env` (so `load_hermes_dotenv` runs with `override=True`), yet the resolved secret is still not applied:

```bash
BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN=dummy-xyz-123 hermes -p <profile> chat -q 'Run: echo "${BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN:0:9}"'
# -> prints the real token prefix from .env, not "dummy-xyz"
```

Direct Python invocation on the same profile home applies the source correctly:

```python

sys.path.insert(0, "<hermes-agent source>")
from hermes_cli.env_loader import load_hermes_dotenv
load_hermes_dotenv(hermes_home="/home/user/.hermes/profiles/<profile>")
# -> "Bitwarden Secrets Manager: applied 1 secret", os.environ has CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN

The presence of the bootstrap token (`BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN`) in `os.environ` **before** the dotenv load appears to skip the `_apply_external_secret_sources(home_path)` pass in `load_hermes_dotenv` (`hermes_cli/env_loader.py`, around line 543) — while the dotenv layer itself loads normally.

The docs (https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/secrets/bitwarden) state: *"Every time hermes (or the gateway, or a cron job) starts, after ~/.hermes/.env has loaded, Hermes calls bws secret list ... and sets the returned keys into os.environ."* The presence of the bootstrap token in the parent environment should not change whether the source pass runs — it is the token the source itself consumes.

Silent failure mode: users who export the bootstrap token in their shell (a natural setup, and required for cron/headless per the docs) lose all resolved secrets in `chat -q` with no warning at startup. Secrets resolve only when the token comes exclusively from the profile `.env`.

   cd /home/hermes/hermes
   docker compose pull hermes
   docker compose up -d --force-recreate hermes
3. Container recreated successfully, landed on v0.22.0 (e06df9c2).
4. hermes doctor, hermes gateway status, hermes mcp list, hermes cron doctor now all print the "install out of sync" warning.
5. /opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python3 -c "import yaml" → ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'
6. /opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python3 -m pip --version → No module named pip (no package manager available in the venv to self-fix)
7. Re-ran docker compose pull && up -d --force-recreate again — pulled the same image (no-op, same commit e06df9c2), issue persists identically. Not a caching artifact — appears baked into the published :latest image itself.

Impact
- hermes-telemetry (community plugin, uses import yaml / PyYAML) silently fails to read its budget.yaml config, which caused its setup wizard to re-trigger and silently overwrite an existing custom budget configuration with defaults ($5/day, $100/month) without any visible error to the user in normal chat/CLI usage — only surfaced when manually inspecting the file and running the plugin's own CLI directly.
- Unclear what else in the broader plugin ecosystem might rely on PyYAML (vs. Hermes core's own ruamel.yaml, which hermes doctor confirms is present and fine).

Environment
- Install method: Docker (nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest)
- Version: v0.22.0 (2026.9.24), upstream commit e06df9c2
- Python: 3.14.7 (bumped from 3.13.5 in the prior v0.21.x image)
- Host: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, Docker 29.8.1

Expected behavior
Either:
(a) the docker image's venv should be fully in sync with uv.lock at publish time (no manual rebuild should ever be needed for an end user pulling :latest), or
(b) if PyYAML genuinely isn't a core dependency, plugins that need it should declare it so it gets installed as part of hermes plugins install, and/or the "install out of sync" warning should include actionable repair steps that work from inside a docker-managed install (since there's no pip/uv available there to self-heal).
title: v0.22.0 docker image: venv out of sync with uv.lock, breaks plugins requiring PyYAML (e.g. hermes-telemetry)

## Summary

On macOS, `psutil.Process(pid).create_time()` is corrected by
`psutil._psosx.adjust_proc_create_time`, which adds `INIT_BOOT_TIME - boot_time()`.
`INIT_BOOT_TIME` is captured when psutil is first imported. macOS steps `kern.boottime` by
seconds over time; we observed a single +1.93 s step while debugging. A gateway that has run
for days therefore reads every *other* process's start time shifted by the accumulated drift,
while a freshly started CLI process reads its own start time with no shift.

`cron/executions.py:recover_interrupted_executions`, run from the ticker every 300 s, compares
the owner's recorded `process_started_at`, written by the CLI process, with the gateway's
current reading through `start_time_fingerprints_match(..., tolerance=200)`. Once the gateway's
drift exceeds 2 s, every externally owned execution looks like a dead owner. The row becomes
`unknown` with "Scheduler restarted after this execution's owner exited…". The CLI's later
`finish_execution` cannot update the row, so `hermes cron run` prints `Ran now: failed.` even
though the run completed, `last_status=ok`, and delivery succeeded.

Scheduled runs are not affected: their rows carry the gateway's own `process_id`, which the
reaper skips.

## Evidence (macOS, gateway pid started 2026-10-02, observed 2026-10-14)

- `gateway_state.json` `start_time`, which the gateway computes for itself: `179095099400`.
  A fresh process reads the same pid as `179095098700`. The difference is exactly 700 (7.00 s).
- Setting `psutil._psosx.INIT_BOOT_TIME = psutil.boot_time() - 7.0` in a fresh process
  reproduces `179095099400` exactly.
- Manual runs were reaped mid-run on 09-27, 09-28 (x2), 10-06 and 10-14. All of them later
  finished and delivered normally. Right after a gateway restart on 09-29, manual runs of up to
  498 s completed normally.

## Repro

1. On macOS, keep a gateway running long enough for `kern.boottime` to drift by more than 2 s
   from its value at gateway start. Comparing `gateway_state.json` `start_time` with a fresh
   `get_process_start_time(gateway_pid)` shows the drift.
2. Run `hermes cron run <agent-job>` with a job that takes longer than one 300 s reap interval.
3. The execution row turns `unknown` mid-run, and the CLI prints `Ran now: failed.`

## Possible fixes

1. Read an unadjusted creation time for fingerprints, for example the platform
   `_proc.create_time(monotonic=True)` on macOS/BSD, so that every process computes the same
   value.
2. Or normalize the reading in the comparing process, by subtracting its own
   `INIT_BOOT_TIME - boot_time()` before comparing.
3. Or, for cross-process owner checks only, widen the tolerance in proportion to the observed
   boot-time drift, rather than using a fixed 2 s.

Option 1 also helps the other users of `start_time_fingerprints_match`, such as gateway pid
records and sibling-liveness checks, which compare readings taken by processes of different
ages.

---
Environment: macOS (Apple silicon), Python
title: macOS: gateway dead-owner reaper marks a live `hermes cron run` execution `unknown` once psutil's boot-time correction drifts past 2 s

### Bug Description

On messaging platforms, `/resume` and `/sessions` fail for a session title containing an apostrophe. `/resume Mom's birthday plan` replies "⚠️ Could not parse `/resume` arguments: No closing quotation. Use quotes around titles with spaces…" instead of resuming the session; `/sessions Mom's birthday plan` and `/sessions search don't` fail the same way. The hint is misleading: spaces work unquoted (`/resume Project A Plan` resumes), only the `'` breaks it. The classic CLI's `/resume` takes the raw text and resumes such a session.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Title a session `Mom's birthday plan` (or let one be auto-titled with an apostrophe).
2. In a gateway chat (Telegram, Discord, Slack, …) send `/resume Mom's birthday plan`.

### Expected Behavior

The session is resumed, as `/resume Project A Plan` is, and as the CLI does.

### Actual Behavior

The parse-error reply above. `/sessions search don't` returns the same error.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Debug Report

Not from a live bot: reproduced by calling `GatewayRunner._handle_resume_command` / `_handle_sessions_command` on current `main` (1f6c02c07c) with a real `SessionDB`.

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.14

### Hermes Version

main @ 1f6c02c07c

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`gateway/slash_commands_session.py` `_handle_resume_command` and `hermes_cli/session_listing.parse_session_listing_args` (used by `/sessions`) split the argument with `shlex.split`, which raises "No closing quotation" on the apostrophe.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Keep `shlex.split` (quotes still group words) and fall back to a plain whitespace split when the quoting is unbalanced, as `/reasoning` already does in `gateway/run_config_loaders.py`.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
title: [Bug]: gateway /resume and /sessions fail on a session title with an apostrophe (No closing quotation)

## Bug Description
A background `delegate_task` subagent session was bound to the SAME Telegram thread as its parent session. After the parent went idle waiting for background results, the user's subsequent messages in that thread were routed to the subagent instead of the main agent — so the user ended up "talking to a subagent" that denied being one, then admitted it.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a Telegram DM thread (thread `54287`), ask the main agent to do work.
2. Tell it to use subagents (e.g. "Just use your own subagents..."). Main agent calls `delegate_task` with 2 tasks in background mode (`delegation_id deleg_f449adfb`, children `sa-0`, `sa-1`), ends turn with "I'll report back when they land."
3. Parent session stays open but idle awaiting background completion.
4. User sends further messages in the SAME Telegram thread.
5. Those messages land in the child session `20261014_040222_5d0bcc` (whose `parent_session_id` = parent, but whose `thread_id` = `54287`, identical to parent) instead of the parent session.

## Expected Behavior
- Child/delegated sessions should NOT inherit the parent's chat/thread binding.
- User messages in the parent thread should always route to the parent (main) agent.
- Background completion results should re-enter the parent session; the parent session should not end with `session_switch` while background children are still running.

## Actual Behavior
- Child session row: `id=20261014_040222_5d0bcc`, `parent_session_id=20261014_020931_3881b279`, `thread_id=54287` (same as parent). Second child `20261014_040222_281f84` has `thread_id=NULL` — inconsistent.
- Parent session ended `session_switch` at 04:19 while children ran until 04:20; completion summaries never re-entered the parent conversation.
- User messages from 04:39–04:44 (e.g. "Am I talking to a subagent right now?") were recorded in the child session. The subagent first denied being a subagent ("First time I'm seeing that question"), then conceded ("yes, I'm a delegated worker, and no, I can't see the main chat's history").
- The stale child session remains open and bound to the thread, so further user messages keep routing to it.

## Environment
- Gateway: Hermes Agent (Telegram surface, DM thread)
- Main session: `20261014_020931_3881b279` ("Host apps on cluster with CLI access")
- Child sessions: `20261014_040222_5d0bcc` (wordcraft StorageBackend worker), `20261014_040222_281f84` (k8s harness worker)
- Delegation: `deleg_f449adfb`, live transcripts under `~/.hermes/cache/delegation/live/deleg_f449adfb/`
- Suggested severity: high — breaks the core expectation that the user always talks to their own agent; subagent has no main-chat history and misrepresents itself.

## Additional Context
Verified via `state.db` sessions/messages tables and delegation live-transcript logs. Happy to provide redacted rows/logs on request. Workaround applied locally: none yet — child session still open/bound at time of filing.
title: Bug: delegated subagent session inherits parent's Telegram thread binding, user ends up talking to subagent

### Bug Description

`agent/anthropic_adapter.py` falls back to a hard-coded `_CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION_FALLBACK = "2.1.74"` whenever `_detect_claude_code_version()` cannot read `claude --version`. `_get_claude_code_version()` then caches that value for the whole process lifetime (`_claude_code_version_cache`), and it is sent as the OAuth identity `user-agent: claude-code/<version> (external, cli)`.

Anthropic gates newer models on the reported Claude Code version. `claude-opus-5-5` requires >= 2.1.280, so a process that has fallen back sends `claude-code/2.1.74`. Every Opus 5.5 request on that process is then rejected with `400 invalid_request_error ... error_code: claude_code_version_too_old`, on every OAuth account. Sonnet 5 still passes, so the failure is easy to miss. On a long-lived gateway it lasts until the next restart.

`main` still has the same constant (checked 2026-10-14, `main` @ d97007c32d, line 243). #106414 raises it to 2.1.280 and adds a floor. That fixes today's value, but the constant is still hard-coded and will drift again; the review on that PR points this out ("the hardcoded fallback will drift the way prime-agent's did").

### Steps to Reproduce

Detection falls back in any of these cases. All were measured with the real `_detect_claude_code_version()` in a separate process:

1. No candidate found: `HOME` points elsewhere and `PATH` is minimal (`env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/some/other/dir ...`). `_claude_code_candidates()` returns `[]` and the result is `2.1.74`.
2. `claude --version` output format changes so that the first token does not start with a digit (e.g. `Claude Code v2.1.300`). Result: `2.1.74`.
3. The binary hangs for more than 5 s (timeout). Result: `2.1.74`, and the first OAuth request also waits 5 s.
4. Non-zero exit code, a broken or removed binary (e.g. a pruned `~/.local/share/claude/versions/<v>` that `~/.local/bin/claude` still links to), or fork failure. All of these are swallowed by `suppress(Exception)`. Result: `2.1.74`.

Then build an OAuth client:

```python
import agent.anthropic_adapter as a
a._claude_code_candidates = lambda: []          # simulate case 1
c = a.build_anthropic_client("sk-ant-oat01-...")
c.default_headers["user-agent"]                  # 'claude-code/2.1.74 (external, cli)'
```

Any `claude-opus-5-5` request with that client returns 400 `claude_code_version_too_old`.

### Expected Behavior

A transient detection failure should not silently downgrade the identity below a version the same machine has already reported successfully.

### Actual Behavior

The identity drops to `claude-code/2.1.74` for the rest of the process. The only signal is the 400 on Opus 5.5, and nothing is logged at detection time.

### Affected Component

Agent core: `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` (`_detect_claude_code_version`, `_get_claude_code_version`), Anthropic OAuth route.

### Hermes Version

`main` @ d97007c32d (2026-10-14). Also present in 71d34bad10.

### Root Cause Analysis

- The fallback is a static
title: [Bug]: Claude Code OAuth identity falls back to stale 2.1.74 when `claude --version` detection fails — claude-opus-5-5 then 400s (claude_code_version_too_old) for the process lifetime

### Description

The native task-card lane (since #85476) publishes `_TaskCardState.visible_tasks()`, the 8 most recently started tasks (`task_order[-8:]` in `gateway/run_turn_runner.py`). A status change to an older task is applied to the state but never sent to `send_native_task_card_progress`. When a turn issues 9 or more parallel tool calls, the first ones finish outside that window, and the card keeps the "in progress" status it last received for them.

### Steps to Reproduce

On `main` (`d97007c32d`):

```python
from gateway.run_turn_runner import TurnRunner

card = TurnRunner._TaskCardState(adapter=None)
for n in range(9):
    card.apply_event({"type": "tool.started", "tool_call_id": f"call-{n}", "tool_name": "web_search"})
card.apply_event({"type": "tool.completed", "tool_call_id": "call-0", "tool_name": "web_search"})
print([task["id"] for task in card.visible_tasks()])
# ['call-1', ..., 'call-8']: the frame published for call-0's completion does not contain call-0
```

### Expected Behavior

Every status change reaches the adapter, so each task ends in its final state on the card.

### Actual Behavior

`call-0`'s completion is never published.

### Proposed Fix

Remember which tasks changed since the last successful native publish and send the ones outside the window along with it. PR to follow.
title: [Bug]: Slack native task cards: a tool that finishes after 8 newer tool calls started stays "in progress"

**Where:** `gateway/platforms/whatsapp_cloud.py` (checked on `main` at d97007c32d and tag v2026.9.24): `_normalize_allow_ids` and `_entry_matches`.

```python
return {re.sub(r"\D", "", entry.split("@", 1)[0]) or entry for entry in ids}
...
bare = re.sub(r"\D", "", str(target).split("@", 1)[0]) or target
return bare in self._normalize_allow_ids(entries) or super()._entry_matches(entries, target)
```

**Problem:** since the 2026 WhatsApp usernames rollout, the Cloud API's `messages[].from` (and `contacts[].wa_id`) can carry a business-scoped user id (BSUID, `CC.<alphanumeric>`, e.g. `DE.1A2B3C4D5E`) instead of a phone number. `sender_id = raw_message["from"]` (around L835 / L1014) then goes through the digit-only normalisation, and so do allowlist entries. Two different BSUIDs whose digits are the same in the same order become the same bare id:

```
DE.1A2B3C4D5E -> 12345
DE.12345ABCDE -> 12345
```

So an allowlist that names one user's BSUID admits any sender whose BSUID shares its digit projection. The same applies to the interactive-tap check (`_dispatch_interactive_reply` -> `_is_dm_allowed`), which gates approval buttons. The odds for a long random BSUID are small, but the comparison is wrong by construction, and short digit projections (a BSUID that is mostly letters) collide easily. Entries also lose their country prefix, and a BSUID with no digits at all falls back to its raw form, so the matcher treats two id types inconsistently.

**Suggested fix:** normalise only values that are phone ids (strip `+`, spaces and `@...` JID suffixes, then require `^[1-9][0-9]{5,14}$`); compare anything shaped like a BSUID (`^[A-Z]{2}\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,128}$`) byte for byte, case-sensitive; never cross-match a BSUID against a phone entry. Also consider reading the BSUID from `contacts[].user_id` / `from_user_id` when `from` is a phone number, so an operator can allowlist by BSUID once users hide their numbers. A regression test with the two ids above would pin it.

Context: found while designing an owner-only WhatsApp line for a self-hosted Hermes; we compare exactly on our side in the meantime. Happy to open a PR if useful.
title: whatsapp_cloud: allowlist strips every non-digit, so business-scoped user ids (BSUIDs) can collide

## Summary

Since the `todo` → `todo_list` and `process` → `process_manage` renames, the ACP adapter still keys on the old names:

1. **No plan update is ever sent.** ACP clients' native task panel (`sessionUpdate: "plan"`) stops updating.
2. **Both tools lose their curated rendering.** Kind, start content and result formatting fall back to the generic path. `process_manage` is reported as kind `other` instead of `execute`.

## Where it happens

`acp_adapter/events.py` (`make_step_cb`) and `acp_adapter/server.py` (`_history_replay_updates`) emit the plan only for the old name:

```python
if tool_name == "todo" and (plan_update := _build_plan_update_from_todo_result(result)) is not None:
```

`acp_adapter/tools.py` registers `todo` / `process` only, in `TOOL_KIND_MAP`, `_POLISHED_TOOLS`, `_COMPLETION_FORMATTERS` and `_START_CONTENT_BUILDERS`.

## Accepting the new name in the step callback is not enough

When `todo_list` is deferred behind `tool_search`, the model calls it through the `tool_call` bridge. The step callback reads names from the assistant's wire `tool_calls` (`_previous_tool_round`), so it sees `tool_call`, never `todo_list`. History replay has the same problem: the stored assistant `tool_calls` carry `tool_call`, while the tool row's `tool_name` is `todo_list`.

`tool.completed` is the one place that sees the unwrapped name: `agent/tool_executor.py` emits it after `_unwrap_tool_search_call`.

## Reproduction

1. Run `hermes acp` with tool discovery on, so non-core tools sit behind `tool_search`.
2. Ask for a multi-step task tracked with the todo tool (e.g. "make a 10-step todo list, then complete each step, marking it completed").
3. Observe the session updates: `todo_list` tool calls arrive, but no `sessionUpdate: "plan"` does. On 0.21.0, with the old `todo` name, the plan was emitted.

## Expected

One plan update per completed `todo_list` call, carrying the full list. Curated start/result rendering for `todo_list` and `process_manage`, same as before the rename.

## Environment

Hermes v0.21.7 (`71d34bad`) and current `main` (`d97007c32d`), via `hermes acp`, Linux.

## Proposed fix

PR to follow:
- Send the plan from `close_tool_call`, on `tool.completed`, using `tools.todo_tool.is_todo_tool_name`.
- Keep the step-callback emission only on its fallback path, where it closed the call itself.
- In history replay, also check the stored `tool_name`.
- Register the new names in the four tables, keeping the old names for replayed transcripts.
title: ACP: no plan update for todo_list (todo → todo_list rename), and none at all through the tool_call bridge

## Bug Description
After a compaction, `_ensure_compressed_keeps_last_assistant_reply` re-adds the just-delivered assistant reply when the engine's output dropped it. `_reply_insertion_index` is meant to pick "the chronologically correct slot". It can instead place the reply **after tool rows that followed it** in the original transcript.

This happens when:
- the reply's first follower was dropped; and
- a later row has the same role and text (for example a second "continue" sent during a tool loop).

The in-place commit then persists that order, and the transcript reloads it (`ORDER BY id`). A context engine that tracks its rows in transcript order sees a stored row reappear after rows stored later than it. We hit this with a plugin context engine: from then on, each compaction pass stopped without making progress.

## Steps to Reproduce and Actual Behavior
This is pure host code: no engine, no database, no network. It reproduces on v0.21.7, and `agent/conversation_compression_reply_anchor.py` is byte-identical on main (d97007c32d, 2026-10-14).

```python
from agent.conversation_compression_reply_anchor import _ensure_compressed_keeps_last_assistant_reply

def tc(i): return {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": f"call_{i}", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "arguments": "{}"}}]}
def tr(i): return {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": f"call_{i}", "content": f"result {i}"}
U0 = {"role": "user", "content": "start the task"}
A  = {"role": "assistant", "content": "here is the plan; starting now"}
F  = {"role": "user", "content": "continue"}
F2 = {"role": "user", "content": "continue"}
original   = [U0, A, F, tc(1), tr(1), F2, tc(2), tr(2)]
compressed = [{"role": "user", "content": "[summary of earlier turns]"}, tc(1), tr(1), dict(F2), tc(2), tr(2)]
ins = _ensure_compressed_keeps_last_assistant_reply(original, compressed, session_id="repro")
print([m["role"] for m in compressed], next(i for i, m in enumerate(compressed) if m is ins))
```

Actual: the reply goes in at index 3, giving `[summary, call_1, result_1, REPLY, "continue", call_2, result_2]`. In the original, `call_1` and `result_1` came **after** the reply.

## Expected Behavior
The reply must never be placed after a surviving row that originally followed it. Here, the only slot that respects the original order is index 1, directly before `call_1`. That slot is next to an assistant tool-call row. Under the function's own rule ("strict alternation beats recovery"), it should therefore skip the reinsertion. The reply stays readable on disk.

## Root Cause and Existing Safe Seam
`_reply_insertion_index` walks the followers in order and returns at the **first follower that matches anything**. For a text row, the match is the **last** text match in `compressed`. That choice is deliberate: it avoids binding to an older identical "ok"/"thanks".

When the first follower (`F`) was dropped, its last text match is the later twin `F2`. That index is returned even thou
title: [Bug]: Compaction re-adds the delivered reply after tool rows that followed it (follower with a later text twin)

body:
### Problem or Use Case

A plugin that needs to act on the audio Hermes actually delivers has no hook for it. Example: provenance or AI-disclosure receipts for generated speech (record the sha256 of the delivered file with provider, model and voice, so anyone holding the clip can later check it was declared synthetic). With Fish Audio now an official TTS plugin, generated speech is a growing share of output, and disclosure of synthetic audio is becoming a requirement for some deployments (EU AI Act Art. 50).

Today no documented hook fires after a TTS file is produced. `post_tool_call` fires after `text_to_speech` / `fish_speak`, but its payload (`tool_name`, `args`, `result` JSON string, `duration_ms`, `status`) has no absolute path of the file that will be delivered, no byte length, provider, model or voice id. When delivery re-encodes to Opus for voice bubbles (#133133), the file sent is not the one the tool returned, so a hash taken from the tool result would not match what users receive.

### Proposed Solution

An observe-only hook, `post_tts_file`, mirroring the proposed `post_transcription` (#100991) on the other side of speech:

- Fires once, after the audio file that will actually be delivered has been written, including the Opus re-encode when that is what the platform sends. Call sites: `text_to_speech` in `tools/tts_tool.py`, and plugin TTS providers after their file is final.
- `ctx.register_hook("post_tts_file", callback)`; `**kwargs`; return value ignored; exceptions logged; a timeout fails open. The callback cannot replace, block or delay the audio.
- Fields: `path` (absolute path of the delivered file), `byte_length`, `provider` (e.g. `fish-audio`), `model` (or null), `voice_id` (or null), `tool_name`, `tool_call_id`, `session_id`, `reencoded` (bool, true when `path` is the post-re-encode file).
- Streaming playback with no stable file: not fired (documented), so no consumer has to guess.

### Alternatives Considered

- Hashing from `post_tool_call`'s result: guesses a path and misses the re-encode, so the hash can be of the wrong bytes.
- Wrapping `register_tts_provider` in a plugin: changes the speech path, which a disclosure plugin should never touch.
- Watching the audio cache directory: racy and platform-specific.

### Scope

Small: one hook name in `VALID_HOOKS`, two call sites, docs on the observer-hooks and hooks pages, and a test that the hook fires with the delivered path and that a raising or slow callback does not affect delivery.

### Contribution

Happy to send the PR if this shape works for you. We maintain `invinoveritas-receipts` (in the plugin catalog), which would be its first consumer, as an opt-in, off-by-default speech receipt.
title: [Feature]: post_tts_file observer hook (fires with the delivered audio file)

## Bug Description

Hermes Desktop's **Settings → Gateway → Hermes Cloud** sign-in never completes discovery of hosted Cloud agents.

Selecting **Hermes Cloud** and clicking **Sign in to Hermes Cloud** opens an in-app window that loads the public Nous Portal **marketing/overview** page (`// OVERVIEW` / "Everything to Power Hermes Agent" / **SEE PLANS**), already showing the user as signed in (account chip). There is no authorize/continue control, no agent picker, and no handshake back to Desktop.

The hosted Cloud instance is healthy and visible in the browser Portal (**Cloud / Manage Agents**, status Online / Running). Desktop never lists it. The Sign in button remains on the Gateway page after the popup.

This is distinct from #92852 (Privy "cannot authorize more than one account") and #73495 (cold-start cookie race hiding agents). Here the OAuth/discovery window never leaves the Portal landing page.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an existing Hermes Cloud instance on the same Nous Portal account (visible at portal.nousresearch.com → Cloud / Manage Agents).
2. Open Hermes Desktop on the **Local** backend.
3. Settings → **Gateway**.
4. Select **Hermes Cloud** as connection mode.
5. Click **Sign in to Hermes Cloud**.
6. Observe the popup.

## Expected Behavior

The popup completes Portal/Privy authorization for Desktop, then Desktop discovers hosted agents and lets the user pick one (e.g. the existing Cloud instance) as the gateway.

If the user is already signed into Portal in that window, discovery should continue automatically — not dump them on the public marketing page.

## Actual Behavior

- Popup title: **Nous Portal**
- Content: overview/marketing landing ("Everything to Power Hermes Agent", **SEE PLANS**), user already signed in
- No agent list, no "Use gateway", no completion of the Desktop Cloud connection
- Gateway settings still show **Sign in to Hermes Cloud** afterward
- Worked around only by chatting with the Cloud agent in the **browser** dashboard, not Desktop

## Environment

## Title
`[Bug]: Cron turn aborted on transient SQLite write lock without retry, and session finalization crashes with unhandled RuntimeError`

## Description

### Environment
- **Platform:** Linux / Docker container (`hermes gateway run --replace`)
- **Version:** v0.21.5 / v0.21.6 (`image: nousresearch/hermes-agent@sha256:...`)
- **Storage:** SQLite `state.db` (WAL mode)

### Summary
When a cron job executes concurrently with another Hermes process writing heavily to `state.db` (e.g. an active multi-turn peer-DM session or maintenance task):
1. **No Retry on Transient Write Lock:** The cron turn aborts with:
   ```
   RuntimeError: ⚠️ No reply: the turn was stopped because session storage was busy (another Hermes process was writing to the state database). Your message should already be saved — please send it again in a moment.
   ```
   The scheduler immediately treats this turn abort as fatal without any backoff or retry, causing the entire scheduled fire to fail. For low-frequency jobs (e.g. weekly `0 9 * * 1`), a 2–3 minute transient write lock causes a 7-day outage of scheduled deliverables.
2. **Session Cleanup Escalation Cascade:** During cleanup in `_finalize_cron_session`, `_set_cron_session_title` is invoked through `_bounded` (`/opt/hermes/cron/scheduler.py:1456`). If the database lock persists beyond `cleanup_timeout_seconds` (default 10.0s), `_bounded` sets `self._disabled = True` and raises `TimeoutError`. The exception handler in `_finalize_cron_session` catches the timeout, but its fallback logic immediately calls:
   ```python
   getattr(_session_db, "get_next_title_in_lineage", lambda b: b)(f"cron {job_id}")
   ```
   Because `_bounded` already disabled finalization, this invocation immediately raises:
   ```
   RuntimeError: session finalization disabled after prior cleanup failure
   ```
   This unhandled exception escapes `run_job`, leaving the cron session un-finalized and recording a misleading cleanup error instead of the underlying cause.

### Reproduction & Traceback

1. Run a long-running multi-turn agent session on the gateway that holds write transactions on `state.db`.
2. Simultaneously trigger a scheduled cron job whose execution attempts to write session messages or token accounting to `state.db`.
3. When the 60s patience expires, `hermes_state.py` raises `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked`.
4. Observe the turn abort and resulting stack trace in `errors.log`:

```
2026-10-12 09:06:03,176 ERROR cron.scheduler: Job 'Weekly Planning Check-in' failed: RuntimeError: ⚠️ No reply: the turn was stopped because session storage was busy (another Hermes process was writing to the state database). Your message should already be saved — please send it again in a moment.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/hermes/cron/scheduler.py", line 2530, in run_job
    final_response = _final_response_from_result(result, job_id, job_name, AIAgent)
  File "/opt/hermes/cron/scheduler.py", line 2017, in _final_respons
title: `[Bug]: Cron turn aborted on transient SQLite write lock without retry, and session finalization crashes with unhandled RuntimeError`

# Tool-progress repeat counter corrupts the Telegram code fence → backticks render escaped/literal

**Repo:** NousResearch/hermes-agent · **Version:** 0.21.7 (commit 71d34bad, image built 2026-10-12) · **Platform:** Telegram (MarkdownV2) · **Regression vs:** v0.20.x image built 2026-07-02

## Summary

When the same tool-progress line repeats consecutively, the gateway appends the repeat counter to the
**whole fenced block string**, which lands on the closing fence line:

```
💻 terminal
```
ssh -F /opt/data/home/.ssh/config fed...
``` (×4)
```

A fence line with trailing text is not a valid closing fence. The Telegram adapter's `format_message`
protects fenced blocks with an **anchored** closing fence, so the region no longer matches, falls
through to the MarkdownV2 escaper, and the backticks are sent escaped — the user sees mangled/literal
backtick runs instead of a code block ("the code fence looks like two backticks instead of three").

## Where

- Writer: `gateway/run_turn_runner.py`
  - `_progress_emit()` → `progress_queue.put(("__dedup__", msg, count))` (and the native path:
    `sc.on_tool_progress(f"{msg} (×{ctx.repeat_count[0] + 1})")`)
  - `_progress_absorb()` → `st.progress_lines[-1] = f"{base_msg} (×{count + 1})"` — `base_msg` is the
    entire multi-line fenced block, so the suffix is appended after the closing ```
- Reader: `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` → `format_message()` fence protection regex:
  `r'(?m)^((?:(?!```)[^\n])*)(```[^`\n]*\n)([\s\S]*?)(^[ \t]*```)[ \t]*\r?$'`
  the closing group `(^[ \t]*```[ \t]*\r?$)` cannot match ```` ``` (×4) ````

The counter fires readily because `_progress_terminal_blocks()` truncates each command to
`tool_preview_length` (default 40) chars — different commands sharing a prefix (e.g. repeated
`ssh -F …`, `grep -rn …`) produce **identical** previews and are treated as repeats.

## Verification (run in the container)

```python
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("tg", "/opt/hermes/plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py")
tg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(tg)
A = tg.TelegramAdapter; obj = A.__new__(A)
good = "💻 terminal\n```\nssh -F /opt/data/home/.ssh/config fed...\n```"
bad  = "💻 terminal\n```\nssh -F /opt/data/home/.ssh/config fed...\n``` (×3)"
print(repr(A.format_message(obj, good)))   # unchanged → renders as <pre> ✓
print(repr(A.format_message(obj, bad)))    # '\`\`\` … \`\`\` \(×3\)' → escaped literal backticks ✗
```

Fence-region match count with the adapter's own regex: `good` → 1, `bad` → 0.

## Why it is a regression

- v0.20.x adapter used the loose `r'(```(?:[^\n]*\n)?[\s\S]*?```)'`, which matched regardless of
  trailing text after the closing fence — the counter stayed harmless text.
- 0.21.7 replaced it with the anchored version (per its comment, to support lead-in prose and
  indented/nested fences). New parser, long-standing writer form → the defect surfaced.

## Suggested fix

The adapter already normalis
title: Tool-progress repeat counter corrupts the Telegram code fence → backticks render escaped/literal

### Problem or Use Case

When running several Hermes sessions in terminal tabs or panes, I'd like to see which session is working, waiting for input, finished, or failed without opening each one.

Hermes already has OSC 9 notifications and Warp's OSC 777 events in `hermes_cli/terminal_notify.py`. Could the interactive CLI/TUI also report its state through the terminal-independent [Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status)? Supporting terminals could then show persistent status indicators without parsing Hermes output.

### Proposed Solution

Emit OSC 7501 reports from the actual session lifecycle, with a stable app identifier such as `app=hermes`:

- `idle` while awaiting a new instruction.
- `working` during generation and tool execution.
- `blocked:kind=permission` for approvals, `blocked:kind=question` for clarification, and `blocked:kind=auth` when an interactive login or credential prompt prevents progress.
- Resume `working` after the blocking prompt is resolved.
- `done` when the response is ready, `error` when the turn fails and stops, and `idle` on user cancellation.

For example: `ESC ] 7501 ; state=working:app=hermes ESC \\`.

Please gate emission to an interactive terminal, keep escapes out of redirected output, JSON, logs, and gateway/API responses, and provide a way to disable reporting. Any optional `msg`/`title` should follow the specification's base64, control-character, and size rules. Progress can be omitted when unknown.

Follow the protocol's lifecycle rules: preserve completed/failed results as appropriate, avoid stale working/blocked status after cancellation, and don't send an unscoped `state=clear` on shutdown because it clears every record in the terminal.

### Alternatives Considered

Existing bells/OSC 9 alerts and Warp OSC 777 events help with notifications, but don't expose the same portable set of persistent states. Window titles and screen-output matching require heuristics. A skill can't reliably report all session transitions, especially cancellation and approval waits.

### Feature Type

CLI improvement

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines), subject to lifecycle integration requirements.

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Duplicate Check

Searched open and closed issues/PRs for `7501`, `OSC7501`, `OSC 7501`, and `program status protocol`, and checked the current source at `d97007c32d6340f7ba79ac1dfb5773cc00846448`. No matching implementation or request found. Related notification work: #101320 (OSC 9 / Warp OSC 777).
title: [Feature]: Support OSC 7501 Program Status Protocol in the CLI/TUI

# Feedback: weaker goal persistence and increased human supervision in daily use

A long-term Hermes user reports a decline in practical goal completion. Previously, assigning a clear goal usually led to finished work. Recently, the user has needed repeated prompts, corrections, status checks, and manual redirection to keep authorized work moving. The experience feels less persistent despite a newer underlying model.

## Concrete recent example

An authorized research task covered several jurisdictions, with completion criteria, checkpoints, a substantial runtime allowance, and instructions to preserve existing work. The worker stopped after an initial pass while its own receipt marked the assigned research incomplete. A later user status request exposed that work had stopped. The supervising agent then restarted the unfinished research with more explicit continuation instructions.

This example is observed workflow behavior. Prior versions have not been compared under identical conditions. Custom agent and project instructions are active, so their interaction with the model and runtime needs investigation.

## Expected behavior

Once a scoped goal is authorized, continue useful permitted work until the acceptance criteria are met or a genuine blocker is reached. Recover from operational failures where possible, preserve resumable checkpoints, and report partial completion accurately. Avoid making the user repeatedly supervise routine continuation. Explain an actual permission boundary clearly instead of presenting an agent's discretionary judgment as a software prohibition.

## Runtime

Python.

Please investigate goal persistence and premature stopping across model decisions, prompt instructions, context handling, worker orchestration, and completion handling. Evaluate completed user goals and required human interventions, including whether passing tests and polished final reports mask unfinished requested work.

This report excludes private transcripts, personal identifiers, device and operating-system information, software and model identifiers, version numbers, client data, credentials, local machine paths, and financial information.
title: Feedback: weaker goal persistence and increased human supervision in daily use

## Summary

In an interactive Telegram DM, two terminal commands requiring human execution approval blocked for the full ~300-second window with `BLOCKED: Command timed out without user response`. The person at the other end reports seeing **no Approve/Deny card** during either attempt. The commands did not execute. Ordinary inbound and final outbound Telegram messages in that same DM worked.

This is a request to trace the missing approval-delivery boundary, **not** a request to auto-approve commands or weaken the guard.

## Reproduction observed

1. In a Telegram DM using the gateway, ask the agent to run an authorized, approval-gated command.
2. The local tool call enters smart approval review; the agent log records `Auxiliary approval: using openai-codex (gpt-6-sol)`.
3. In two separate attempts on 2026-10-13 (about 15:35 and 15:43 UTC), no approval card was visible in the DM according to the user. Each attempt ended about five minutes later with the timeout above.
4. The bounded gateway INFO log shows normal DM inbound and final-response sends around those windows, but no approval-card send or Telegram acknowledgement entry. Absence of such an INFO line **does not prove** that a card was never submitted; the current instrumentation does not establish which boundary failed.

A separate read-only diagnostic command later encountered the same timeout; it was not run. No command was retried after an explicit block, and no approval bypass was used.

## Environment and limits

- Gateway platform: Telegram DM (private chat; identifiers omitted).
- Installed Hermes source checkout at `dce1e9b37581dd62e480a9064dc04a709c2940d3`; clean when checked. Running gateway was active during the attempts. Source identity of the running process has **not** been independently pinned, so source analysis below is not runtime proof.
- `approvals.mode: smart` was inferred from the observed auxiliary approval step; effective configuration was not dumped or independently verified.
- The actual command and product context are deliberately omitted. Do not ask for tokens, full env, raw gateway logs, private chat text or a live risky replay to diagnose this.

## Expected / actual

Expected: send an actionable approval card to the originating DM, or fail closed promptly and truthfully if delivery is definitively impossible. Ambiguous send acknowledgements should remain fail-closed without duplicate cards.

Actual: no card seen by the user, then a five-minute tool timeout. We cannot yet distinguish a missing notifier, unscheduled send, adapter failure, incorrect Telegram destination/thread, a delivered-but-unseen message, or another boundary.

## Suggested investigation

Correlate structural events for one request across terminal gate → per-session notifier registration/invocation → gateway-loop schedule → Telegram `send_exec_approval` send result/message ID → approval wait/settlement. Log only bounded stage/status/correlation data; no command contents or personal identifier
title: [Bug]: Telegram DM execution approval card unseen; terminal times out without consent
